api/Egami.Analysis.AlphaCompare.html.title: Enum AlphaCompare | Egami
api/Egami.Analysis.AlphaCompare.html.summary: Enum AlphaCompare Namespace Egami.Analysis Assembly Egami.dll How Compare(Raster, Raster, CompareOptions?) and Difference(Raster, Raster, DifferenceStyle, DifferenceOptions?) treat alpha. public enum AlphaCompare Fields Premultiplied = 0 Colors are multiplied by their alpha before they are compared, so two fully transparent pixels are equal whatever color is stored under them: what a viewer sees. ImageMagick 7's compare works this way too. Straight = 1 The stored channels are compared as they are, so a different color under a transparent pixel counts. Examples // Every cheap metric in one pass, per channel and overall, on the 0 to 1 scale; SSIM on request. CompareResult result = Raster.Compare(expected, actual, new CompareOptions { Ssim = true, Fuzz = 0.02f }); Console.WriteLine($"PSNR {result.Overall.Psnr:F1} dB, SSIM {result.Overall.Ssim:F4}, {result.DifferentPixels} pixels off by more than 2%"); bool sameLook = result.Overall.Psnr >= 40;

api/Egami.Analysis.PerceptualHash.html.title: Class PerceptualHash | Egami
api/Egami.Analysis.PerceptualHash.html.summary: Class PerceptualHash Namespace Egami.Analysis Assembly Egami.dll 64-bit perceptual hashes: images that look alike get hashes a few bits apart, however they were compressed or resized, so the Distance(ulong, ulong) between two hashes says how alike two pictures are. Store the hashes as keys to find near-duplicates. public static class PerceptualHash Inheritance object PerceptualHash Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // Find near-duplicate photos: hash each once, store the 64-bit keys, and call a pair a duplicate within about 10 bits. ulong a = PerceptualHash.Dct(original), b = PerceptualHash.Dct(copy), c = PerceptualHash.Dct(other); bool duplicate = PerceptualHash.Distance(a, b) <= 10; bool unrelated = PerceptualHash.Distance(a, c) > 10; string key = a.ToString("x16", System.Globalization.CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); Remarks Both hashes look at the first frame's brightness only, after flattening it onto white. The bits are in reading order, the first in the most significant bit, so hash.ToString("x16") matches the hex string of Python's imagehash. Methods Dct(Raster) Returns the DCT hash (pHash style; Zauner 2010): the image's brightness reduced to 32 × 32, a 2D DCT-II, and one bit per coefficient of the top-left 8 × 8, set when it is above the median of those coefficients without the DC term. It survives recompression, resizing and small brightness changes; pairs of unrelated photos are about 32 bits apart. public static ulong Dct(Raster image) Parameters image Raster The image. Returns ulong The hash. Exceptions ArgumentNullException image is null. ObjectDisposedException The image has been disposed. Difference(Raster) Returns the difference hash (dHash; Krawetz 2013): the image's brightness reduced to 9 × 8, and one bit per pair of horizontal neighbours, set when the right one is brighter. Faster than Dct(Raster) and a little less robust. public static ulong Difference(Raster image) Parameters image Raster The image. Returns ulong The hash. Exceptions ArgumentNullException image is null. ObjectDisposedException The image has been disposed. Distance(ulong, ulong) Returns the number of bits in which two hashes differ (their Hamming distance), 0 to 64. public static int Distance(ulong a, ulong b) Parameters a ulong One hash. b ulong The other. Returns int The distance: 0 to about 10 for the same picture, around 32 for unrelated ones.

Returns Barcode The barcode, with no human-readable text. Examples // The smallest compact or full-range symbol with at least 23 % error correction; no quiet zone needed. Returns Barcode The barcode. Examples // The smallest compact or full-range symbol with at least 23 % error correction; no quiet zone needed. Barcode ticket = Barcode.Aztec("EG1234 BER-MUC 2026-10-19 SEAT 12A DOE/JANE"); // More error correction for a ticket that gets folded, or a fixed compact size. Barcode robust = Barcode.Aztec("EG1234 BER-MUC", new AztecOptions { ErrorCorrectionPercent = 50 }); Barcode compact = Barcode.Aztec("EG1234", new AztecOptions { Compact = true, Layers = 2 }); // A rune: one value from 0 to 255 in an 11 x 11 core. Barcode rune = Barcode.AztecRune(42); Exceptions ArgumentException The text is empty or does not fit in a symbol. Returns Barcode The barcode. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is not 0 to 255. Code128(string, Code128Options?) Makes a Code 128 barcode (ISO/IEC 15417). The code sets A, B and C, and the changes and shifts between them, are picked to give the shortest symbol; runs of digits go in pairs in code set C. Returns Barcode The barcode, with the text as its human-readable text (control characters shown as spaces). Examples // The shortest mix of code sets A, B and C; the digits go in pairs. Barcode code = Barcode.Code128("ORDER-1180042", new Code128Options { Height = 40 }); using Raster<Gray8> image = code.ToRaster(pixelsPerModule: 2); Exceptions ArgumentException The text is empty, longer than 1000 characters, or has a character above 255. Code39(string, Code39Options?) Makes a Code 39 barcode (ISO/IEC 16388): digits, capital letters, space and - . $ / + %. Other ASCII characters are written as Full ASCII pairs when FullAscii allows it. public static Barcode Code39(string text, Code39Options? options = null) Parameters text string The text. options Code39Options The check character, Full ASCII, wide ratio and height, or null for Default. Returns Barcode The barcode, with the text (and a check character, when there is one and the text is not Full ASCII) as its human-readable text. Examples // Capitals, digits and a few symbols; lowercase switches to Full ASCII on its own. Barcode part = Barcode.Code39("PART-0042", new Code39Options { CheckDigit = true }); Console.WriteLine(part.HumanReadableText); // PART-0042 and its mod 43 check character Exceptions ArgumentException The text is empty, longer than 1000 characters, or has a character Code 39 cannot hold. Create(BarcodeFormat, string) Makes a barcode of a format chosen at run time, with that format's default options, for callers that store the format with the data. It calls the format's own factory, such as Qr(string, QrOptions?) or Ean13(string, EanUpcOptions?). public static Barcode Create(BarcodeFormat format, string text) Parameters format BarcodeFormat The symbology. text string The text or digits. Returns Barcode The barcode. Examples // Labels from a table that stores each barcode's format with its data. (BarcodeFormat Format, string Data)[] rows = [ (BarcodeFormat.Ean13, "590123412345"), (BarcodeFormat.Code128, "SHIP-0042"), (BarcodeFormat.Qr, "https://inexin.github.io/Egami/"), ]; foreach ((BarcodeFormat format, string data) in rows) { Barcode barcode = Barcode.Create(format, data); using Raster<Gray8> image = barcode.ToRaster(pixelsPerModule: 3); } Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException format is not a BarcodeFormat. ArgumentException The text does not suit the format or does not fit in a symbol. DataMatrix(IReadOnlyList<Gs1ElementString>, DataMatrixOptions?) Makes a GS1 Data Matrix symbol: FNC1 first and the element strings, separated by FNC1 where their AIs need it. public static Barcode DataMatrix(IReadOnlyList<Gs1ElementString> elements, DataMatrixOptions? options = null) Parameters elements IReadOnlyList<Gs1ElementString> The element strings, from Parse(string). options DataMatrixOptions The shape, or null for Default. Returns Barcode The barcode, with the element strings in their human-readable form as its text. Examples // Square by default; the encodation modes are switched for the fewest codewords. Barcode part = Barcode.DataMatrix("PN 4711-0815 / LOT 2026-10"); // A narrow label: rectangular sizes, the DMRE ones too. Barcode narrow = Barcode.DataMatrix("PN 4711-0815 / LOT 2026-10", new DataMatrixOptions { Shape = DataMatrixShape.Rectangle, AllowDmre = true, }); // GS1 Data Matrix, as on medicine packs. Barcode pack = Barcode.DataMatrix(Gs1.Parse("(01)09501101530003(17)261231(10)AB12(21)XYZ")); Exceptions ArgumentException There are no element strings, or they do not fit in the largest allowed symbol. DataMatrix(ReadOnlySpan<byte>, DataMatrixOptions?) Makes a Data Matrix symbol from bytes, without an ECI. public static Barcode DataMatrix(ReadOnlySpan<byte> data, DataMatrixOptions? options = null) Parameters data ReadOnlySpan<byte> The bytes, at most 3116. options DataMatrixOptions The shape, or null for Default. Returns Barcode The barcode, with no human-readable text. Examples // Square by default; the encodation modes are switched for the fewest codewords. Barcode part = Barcode.DataMatrix("PN 4711-0815 / LOT 2026-10"); // A narrow label: rectangular sizes, the DMRE ones too. Barcode narrow = Barcode.DataMatrix("PN 4711-0815 / LOT 2026-10", new DataMatrixOptions { Shape = DataMatrixShape.Rectangle, AllowDmre = true, }); // GS1 Data Matrix, as on medicine packs. Barcode pack = Barcode.DataMatrix(Gs1.Parse("(01)09501101530003(17)261231(10)AB12(21)XYZ")); Exceptions ArgumentException There are no bytes, or they do not fit in the largest allowed symbol. DataMatrix(string, DataMatrixOptions?) Makes a Data Matrix ECC 200 symbol (ISO/IEC 16022) from text. The six encodation modes are switched for the fewest codewords. Text in ISO 8859-1 is written as it is; other text is written as UTF-8 with ECI 26 before it. public static Barcode DataMatrix(string text, DataMatrixOptions? options = null) Parameters text string The text, at most 3116 characters. options DataMatrixOptions The shape, or null for Default: square. Returns Barcode The barcode. Examples // Square by default; the encodation modes are switched for the fewest codewords. Barcode part = Barcode.DataMatrix("PN 4711-0815 / LOT 2026-10"); // A narrow label: rectangular sizes, the DMRE ones too. Barcode pack = Barcode.DataMatrix(Gs1.Parse("(01)09501101530003(17)261231(10)AB12(21)XYZ")); Exceptions ArgumentException The text is empty or does not fit in the largest allowed symbol. Ean13(string, EanUpcOptions?) Makes an EAN-13 barcode (ISO/IEC 15420), such as a GTIN-13 or an ISBN. Twelve digits get their check digit added; thirteen are checked. With a Font, the first digit is drawn left of the symbol and the others between the guard bars, which reach down into the text line. public static Barcode Ean13(string digits, EanUpcOptions? options = null) Parameters digits string 12 or 13 digits. options EanUpcOptions The add-on and height, or null for Default. Returns Barcode The barcode, with the 13 digits (and the add-on after a space) as its human-readable text. Examples // A book: the ISBN as EAN-13, its check digit added, and the price as an EAN-5 add-on. Barcode book = Barcode.Ean13("978020137962", new EanUpcOptions { AddOn = "52495" }); // Fitted into a rectangle, with the digits between the guard bars. using Raster<Rgba8> label = Raster.Create(400, 200, Rgba8.White); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = label.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.DrawBarcode(book, new RectF(10, 10, 380, 180), Rgba8.Black, new BarcodeDrawOptions { Font = font }); } // A UPC-A number written in its short UPC-E form. Barcode small = Barcode.UpcE("042100005264"); Exceptions ArgumentException The text is not 12 or 13 digits, or the check digit is wrong. Ean8(string, EanUpcOptions?) Makes an EAN-8 barcode (ISO/IEC 15420) for small packages. Seven digits get their check digit added; eight are checked. public static Barcode Ean8(string digits, EanUpcOptions? options = null) Parameters digits string 7 or 8 digits. options EanUpcOptions The add-on and height, or null for Default. Returns Barcode The barcode, with the 8 digits (and the add-on after a space) as its human-readable text. Examples // A book: the ISBN as EAN-13, its check digit added, and the price as an EAN-5 add-on. Barcode book = Barcode.Ean13("978020137962", new EanUpcOptions { AddOn = "52495" }); // Fitted into a rectangle, with the digits between the guard bars. using Raster<Rgba8> label = Raster.Create(400, 200, Rgba8.White); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = label.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.DrawBarcode(book, new RectF(10, 10, 380, 180), Rgba8.Black, new BarcodeDrawOptions { Font = font }); } // A UPC-A number written in its short UPC-E form. Barcode small = Barcode.UpcE("042100005264"); Exceptions ArgumentException The text is not 7 or 8 digits, or the check digit is wrong. FromModules(BarcodeFormat, BarcodeModules, string?) Makes a barcode from modules you already have, with the quiet zone of its format's standard. public static Barcode FromModules(BarcodeFormat format, BarcodeModules modules, string? humanReadableText = null) Parameters format BarcodeFormat The symbology the modules are. modules BarcodeModules The modules: a linear symbol for the linear formats, a 2D grid for the others. humanReadableText string The text to print under the symbol, or null. Returns Barcode The barcode. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException format is not a BarcodeFormat. ArgumentException The modules are linear for a 2D format, or a 2D grid for a linear one. Gs1Code128(IReadOnlyList<Gs1ElementString>, Code128Options?) Makes a GS1-128 barcode: Code 128 with FNC1 first and the element strings after it, an FNC1 after each one whose AI has no predefined length unless it is the last. public static Barcode Gs1Code128(IReadOnlyList<Gs1ElementString> elements, Code128Options? options = null) Parameters elements IReadOnlyList<Gs1ElementString> The element strings, from Parse(string) or Create(string, string). options Code128Options The bar height, or null for Default. Returns Barcode The barcode, with the element strings in their human-readable form as its text. Examples // Each element string is checked: the AI, the length, the GTIN's check digit, the date. IReadOnlyList<Gs1ElementString> elements = Gs1.Parse("(01)09501101530003(17)261231(10)AB12"); Barcode label = Barcode.Gs1Code128(elements); // Mistakes say what is wrong. if (!Gs1.TryParse("(01)09501101530004", out _)) { Console.WriteLine("(01) has a wrong check digit"); } Exceptions ArgumentException There are no element strings, or more than 1000 characters. Gs1Code128(string, Code128Options?) Makes a GS1-128 barcode from element strings in their human-readable form, such as (01)09501101530003(10)AB12. public static Barcode Gs1Code128(string elements, Code128Options? options = null) Parameters elements string The element strings, each AI in parentheses; see Parse(string). options Code128Options The bar height, or null for Default. Returns Barcode The barcode. Examples // Each element string is checked: the AI, the length, the GTIN's check digit, the date. IReadOnlyList<Gs1ElementString> elements = Gs1.Parse("(01)09501101530003(17)261231(10)AB12"); Barcode label = Barcode.Gs1Code128(elements); // Mistakes say what is wrong. if (!Gs1.TryParse("(01)09501101530004", out _)) { Console.WriteLine("(01) has a wrong check digit"); } Exceptions FormatException The text is not valid element strings; the message says which and how. ArgumentException There are more than 1000 characters. Itf(string, ItfOptions?) Makes an Interleaved 2 of 5 barcode (ISO/IEC 16390) from digits; an odd number of digits gets a leading zero, as the symbology holds pairs. public static Barcode Itf(string digits, ItfOptions? options = null) Parameters digits string The digits. options ItfOptions The wide ratio, bearer bars and height, or null for Default. Returns Barcode The barcode, with the digits it holds as its human-readable text. Examples // A GTIN-14 on a carton: the check digit is added, and bearer bars frame the symbol. Barcode carton = Barcode.Itf14("1540014128876"); using Raster<Gray8> image = carton.ToRaster(pixelsPerModule: 3); // Plain Interleaved 2 of 5 with a 2:1 wide ratio and no bearers. Barcode itf = Barcode.Itf("0123456789", new ItfOptions { WideRatio = 2 }); Exceptions ArgumentException The text is empty, longer than 1000 characters, or has a character that is not a digit. Itf14(string, ItfOptions?) Makes an ITF-14 barcode (GS1): a GTIN-14 as Interleaved 2 of 5, framed by bearer bars. Thirteen digits get their check digit added; fourteen are checked. public static Barcode Itf14(string digits, ItfOptions? options = null) Parameters digits string 13 or 14 digits. options ItfOptions The wide ratio, bearer bars and height, or null for Default. Returns Barcode The barcode, with the 14 digits as its human-readable text. Examples // A GTIN-14 on a carton: the check digit is added, and bearer bars frame the symbol. Barcode carton = Barcode.Itf14("1540014128876"); using Raster<Gray8> image = carton.ToRaster(pixelsPerModule: 3); // Plain Interleaved 2 of 5 with a 2:1 wide ratio and no bearers. Barcode itf = Barcode.Itf("0123456789", new ItfOptions { WideRatio = 2 }); Exceptions ArgumentException The text is not 13 or 14 digits, or the check digit is wrong. Pdf417(ReadOnlySpan<byte>, Pdf417Options?) Makes a PDF417 symbol from bytes, without an ECI. public static Barcode Pdf417(ReadOnlySpan<byte> data, Pdf417Options? options = null) Parameters data ReadOnlySpan<byte> The bytes. options Pdf417Options The columns, error level and compact form, or null for Default. Returns Barcode The barcode, with no human-readable text. Examples // About three times as wide as tall, error level from the standard's table for the amount of data. Barcode ticket = Barcode.Pdf417("PASSENGER DOE/JANE FLIGHT EG1234 SEAT 12A GATE B17"); // Six data columns and error level 5, or the compact form for a narrow space. Barcode wide = Barcode.Pdf417("PASSENGER DOE/JANE", new Pdf417Options { Columns = 6, ErrorLevel = 5 }); Barcode compact = Barcode.Pdf417("PASSENGER DOE/JANE", new Pdf417Options { Compact = true }); Exceptions ArgumentException There are no bytes, or they do not fit in a symbol. Pdf417(string, Pdf417Options?) Makes a PDF417 symbol (ISO/IEC 15438) from text, in text, numeric and byte compaction chosen run by run. Text in ISO 8859-1 is written as it is; other text is written as UTF-8 with ECI 26 before it. Each row is 3 modules tall. public static Barcode Pdf417(string text, Pdf417Options? options = null) Parameters text string The text. options Pdf417Options The columns, error level and compact form, or null for Default. Returns Barcode The barcode. Examples // About three times as wide as tall, error level from the standard's table for the amount of data. Barcode ticket = Barcode.Pdf417("PASSENGER DOE/JANE FLIGHT EG1234 SEAT 12A GATE B17"); // Six data columns and error level 5, or the compact form for a narrow space. Barcode wide = Barcode.Pdf417("PASSENGER DOE/JANE", new Pdf417Options { Columns = 6, ErrorLevel = 5 }); Barcode compact = Barcode.Pdf417("PASSENGER DOE/JANE", new Pdf417Options { Compact = true }); Exceptions ArgumentException The text is empty or does not fit in a symbol. Qr(IReadOnlyList<Gs1ElementString>, QrOptions?) Makes a GS1 QR Code: FNC1 in first position and the element strings after it, separated where their AIs need it. public static Barcode Qr(IReadOnlyList<Gs1ElementString> elements, QrOptions? options = null) Parameters elements IReadOnlyList<Gs1ElementString> The element strings, from Parse(string). options QrOptions The level, version and mask, or null for Default. Returns Barcode The barcode, with the element strings in their human-readable form as its text. Examples // Level M, raised to Q or H when that fits in the same size; segments chosen for the fewest bits. Barcode link = Barcode.Qr("https://inexin.github.io/Egami/"); // A fixed size and level, for a layout that must not change. Barcode fixedSize = Barcode.Qr("ORDER-1180042", new QrOptions { Version = 3, ErrorCorrection = QrErrorCorrection.H }); // Bytes as they are, and GS1 element strings with FNC1. Barcode bytes = Barcode.Qr([0x45, 0x67, 0x61, 0x6D, 0x69]); Barcode gs1 = Barcode.Qr(Gs1.Parse("(01)09501101530003(10)AB12")); using Raster<Gray8> image = link.ToRaster(pixelsPerModule: 4); Exceptions ArgumentException There are no element strings, or they do not fit in the symbol. Qr(ReadOnlySpan<byte>, QrOptions?) Makes a QR Code from bytes, written in byte mode (and numeric and alphanumeric where shorter) without an ECI. public static Barcode Qr(ReadOnlySpan<byte> data, QrOptions? options = null) Parameters data ReadOnlySpan<byte> The bytes. options QrOptions The level, version and mask, or null for Default. Returns Barcode The barcode, with no human-readable text. Examples // Level M, raised to Q or H when that fits in the same size; segments chosen for the fewest bits. Barcode link = Barcode.Qr("https://inexin.github.io/Egami/"); // A fixed size and level, for a layout that must not change. Barcode fixedSize = Barcode.Qr("ORDER-1180042", new QrOptions { Version = 3, ErrorCorrection = QrErrorCorrection.H }); // Bytes as they are, and GS1 element strings with FNC1. Barcode bytes = Barcode.Qr([0x45, 0x67, 0x61, 0x6D, 0x69]); Barcode gs1 = Barcode.Qr(Gs1.Parse("(01)09501101530003(10)AB12")); using Raster<Gray8> image = link.ToRaster(pixelsPerModule: 4); Exceptions ArgumentException There are no bytes, or they do not fit in the symbol. Qr(string, QrOptions?) Makes a QR Code (ISO/IEC 18004) from text. The text is split into numeric, alphanumeric, byte and Kanji segments that give the fewest bits. Text in ISO 8859-1 is written as it is; text that Shift JIS holds is written in Shift JIS, its kanji in Kanji mode; other text is written as UTF-8 with ECI 26 before it. public static Barcode Qr(string text, QrOptions? options = null) Parameters text string The text. options QrOptions The level, version and mask, or null for Default: level M, raised while it fits. Returns Barcode The barcode. Examples // Level M, raised to Q or H when that fits in the same size; segments chosen for the fewest bits. Barcode link = Barcode.Qr("https://inexin.github.io/Egami/"); // A fixed size and level, for a layout that must not change. Barcode fixedSize = Barcode.Qr("ORDER-1180042", new QrOptions { Version = 3, ErrorCorrection = QrErrorCorrection.H }); // Bytes as they are, and GS1 element strings with FNC1. Barcode bytes = Barcode.Qr([0x45, 0x67, 0x61, 0x6D, 0x69]); Barcode gs1 = Barcode.Qr(Gs1.Parse("(01)09501101530003(10)AB12")); using Raster<Gray8> image = link.ToRaster(pixelsPerModule: 4); Exceptions ArgumentException The text is empty or does not fit in the symbol. ToPath(float, BarcodeDrawOptions?) Returns the symbol as one path: a rectangle per run of dark modules in a row, all filled with the nonzero rule. The quiet zone's top-left corner is at the origin, so with the quiet zone on the symbol starts at QuietZone modules in. Linear bars are Height modules tall. No text is included. public Path ToPath(float moduleSize = 1, BarcodeDrawOptions? options = null) Parameters moduleSize float The width of a module in path units; 1 by default. options BarcodeDrawOptions The quiet zone and bar width reduction, or null for Default. Returns Path The path. Examples // One path, a rectangle per run of dark modules; the quiet zone's corner is at the origin. Path path = qr.ToPath(moduleSize: 4); string svg = path.ToSvg(); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException moduleSize is not positive and finite. ToRaster(int, BarcodeDrawOptions?) Renders the symbol black on white, each module a square of whole pixels, with the quiet zone around it and, when Font is set, the human-readable text under it. Linear bars are Height modules tall. public Raster<Gray8> ToRaster(int pixelsPerModule = 1, BarcodeDrawOptions? options = null) Parameters pixelsPerModule int The width of a module in pixels; 1 by default. options BarcodeDrawOptions The quiet zone, bar width reduction (rounded to whole pixels) and font, or null for Default. Returns Raster<Gray8> The raster, which the caller disposes. Examples // Black on white, 4 pixels a module, quiet zone included. using Raster<Gray8> image = qr.ToRaster(pixelsPerModule: 4); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException pixelsPerModule is not positive, or the raster would be too large. UpcA(string, EanUpcOptions?) Makes a UPC-A barcode (ISO/IEC 15420). Eleven digits get their check digit added; twelve are checked. With a Font, the first and last digits are drawn outside the symbol, and their bars reach down with the guard bars. public static Barcode UpcA(string digits, EanUpcOptions? options = null) Parameters digits string 11 or 12 digits. options EanUpcOptions The add-on and height, or null for Default. Returns Barcode The barcode, with the 12 digits (and the add-on after a space) as its human-readable text. Examples // A book: the ISBN as EAN-13, its check digit added, and the price as an EAN-5 add-on. Barcode book = Barcode.Ean13("978020137962", new EanUpcOptions { AddOn = "52495" }); // Fitted into a rectangle, with the digits between the guard bars. using Raster<Rgba8> label = Raster.Create(400, 200, Rgba8.White); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = label.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.DrawBarcode(book, new RectF(10, 10, 380, 180), Rgba8.Black, new BarcodeDrawOptions { Font = font }); } // A UPC-A number written in its short UPC-E form. Barcode small = Barcode.UpcE("042100005264"); Exceptions ArgumentException The text is not 11 or 12 digits, or the check digit is wrong. UpcE(string, EanUpcOptions?) Makes a UPC-E barcode (ISO/IEC 15420), the zero-suppressed form of UPC-A. It takes the six UPC-E digits (number system 0), the number system (0 or 1) and the six digits, those and the check digit, or a UPC-A number of 11 or 12 digits, which is compressed to UPC-E. public static Barcode UpcE(string digits, EanUpcOptions? options = null) Parameters digits string 6, 7 or 8 UPC-E digits, or 11 or 12 UPC-A digits. options EanUpcOptions The add-on and height, or null for Default. Returns Barcode The barcode, with the number system, six digits and check digit (and the add-on after a space) as its human-readable text. Examples // A book: the ISBN as EAN-13, its check digit added, and the price as an EAN-5 add-on. Barcode book = Barcode.Ean13("978020137962", new EanUpcOptions { AddOn = "52495" }); // Fitted into a rectangle, with the digits between the guard bars. using Raster<Rgba8> label = Raster.Create(400, 200, Rgba8.White); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = label.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.DrawBarcode(book, new RectF(10, 10, 380, 180), Rgba8.Black, new BarcodeDrawOptions { Font = font }); } // A UPC-A number written in its short UPC-E form. Barcode small = Barcode.UpcE("042100005264"); Exceptions ArgumentException The text is not 6, 7, 8, 11 or 12 digits, the number system is not 0 or 1, the check digit is wrong, or a UPC-A number has too few zeros to compress.

api/Egami.Barcodes.BarcodeDrawOptions.ht.summary: Class BarcodeDrawOptions Namespace Egami.Barcodes Assembly Egami.Barcodes.dll How DrawBarcode(Canvas, Barcode, RectF, Paint, BarcodeDrawOptions?), ToPath(float, BarcodeDrawOptions?) and ToRaster(int, BarcodeDrawOptions?) draw a barcode. public sealed record BarcodeDrawOptions : IEquatable<BarcodeDrawOptions> Inheritance object BarcodeDrawOptions Implements IEquatable<BarcodeDrawOptions> Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A 0.33 mm module (the X dimension) in points, with the text under the bars and 0.05 mm taken off each bar // for ink spread. The quiet zone's top-left corner goes at (36, 36). float module = 0.33f / 25.4f * 72; page.DrawBarcode(code, new Vector2(36, 36), module, Rgba8.Black, new BarcodeDrawOptions { Font = font, BarWidthReduction = 0.05f / 25.4f * 72, }); Properties BarWidthReduction Gets how much narrower each dark bar or module is drawn, in output units (pixels for ToRaster(int, BarcodeDrawOptions?)), to make up for ink spreading on a printer; 0 by default. Half is taken off each side. 2D modules shrink in height too. It changes drawing only, never the modules. public float BarWidthReduction { get; init; } Property Value float Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is negative or not finite. Default Gets the defaults: quiet zone on, no bar width reduction, no text. public static BarcodeDrawOptions Default { get; } Property Value BarcodeDrawOptions Font Gets the font for the human-readable text under the bars (HumanReadableText), or null, the default, to draw no text. Its size is in output units. ToPath(float, BarcodeDrawOptions?) draws no text. public Font? Font { get; init; } Property Value Font? QuietZone Gets a value indicating whether the symbol's quiet zone (QuietZone) is kept clear around it; true by default. Readers need it; turn it off only when the space around the symbol is blank anyway. Linear symbols have it at the left and right only. public bool QuietZone { get; init; } Property Value bool

api/Egami.Barcodes.BarcodeFormat.html.summary: Enum BarcodeFormat Namespace Egami.Barcodes Assembly Egami.Barcodes.dll A barcode symbology, or a set of them: Format and Format hold one, and Formats any combination. [Flags] public enum BarcodeFormat Fields All = Matrix | Linear Every symbology. Aztec = 8 Aztec Code (ISO/IEC 24778); no quiet zone, as its finder is in the middle. Code128 = 16 Code 128 and GS1-128 (ISO/IEC 15417), linear; quiet zone 10 modules. Code39 = 32 Code 39 (ISO/IEC 16388), linear; quiet zone 10 modules. DataMatrix = 2 Data Matrix ECC 200 (ISO/IEC 16022); quiet zone 1 module. Ean13 = 128 EAN-13 (ISO/IEC 15420), linear; quiet zone 11 modules. Ean8 = 256 EAN-8 (ISO/IEC 15420), linear; quiet zone 7 modules. Itf = 64 Interleaved 2 of 5 and ITF-14 (ISO/IEC 16390), linear; quiet zone 10 modules. Linear = Code128 | Code39 | Itf | Ean13 | Ean8 | UpcA | UpcE The linear symbologies. Matrix = Qr | DataMatrix | Pdf417 | Aztec The 2D symbologies. None = 0 No symbology. Pdf417 = 4 PDF417 (ISO/IEC 15438); quiet zone 2 modules. Qr = 1 QR Code (ISO/IEC 18004); quiet zone 4 modules. UpcA = 512 UPC-A (ISO/IEC 15420), linear; quiet zone 9 modules. UpcE = 1024 UPC-E (ISO/IEC 15420), linear; quiet zone 9 modules. Examples // Modules from another encoder become a barcode with the quiet zone of their standard: 4 modules for QR. api/Egami.ChromaDownsampling.html.title: Enum ChromaDownsampling | Egami
api/Egami.ChromaDownsampling.html.summary: Enum ChromaDownsampling Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll How chroma is reduced to the chroma resolution when a raster converts to a subsampled YuvRaster. public enum ChromaDownsampling Fields Average = 0 Averages with the filter that matches the siting: a 2 × 2 box for centered chroma, a [1, 2, 1] filter across co-sited columns or rows. Edges repeat the last sample. Fast = 1 Takes the chroma of the top-left pixel of each block, with no filter. Examples using Raster photo = Raster.Load("duck.png"); // The defaults filter chroma by its siting both ways; Nearest and Fast trade edge quality for speed. YuvConvertOptions fast = new() { Upsampling = ChromaUpsampling.Nearest, Downsampling = ChromaDownsampling.Fast }; using YuvRaster<byte> yuv = YuvRaster.FromRaster(photo, ChromaFormat.Yuv420, YuvColor.Bt601Limited, options: fast); using Raster<Rgba8> back = yuv.ToRaster<Rgba8>(fast);

api/Egami.ChromaUpsampling.html.title: Enum ChromaUpsampling | Egami
api/Egami.ChromaUpsampling.html.summary: Enum ChromaUpsampling Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll How chroma is brought up to luma resolution when a YuvRaster converts to RGB. public enum ChromaUpsampling Fields Bilinear = 0 Interpolates between neighboring chroma samples, honoring the siting: the 3:1 triangle filter JPEG and WebP decoders use for centered chroma, and the average of the two neighbors between co-sited samples. Nearest = 1 Repeats each chroma sample over the luma samples it covers. Faster, with visible color fringes on edges. Examples using Raster photo = Raster.Load("duck.png"); // The defaults filter chroma by its siting both ways; Nearest and Fast trade edge quality for speed. YuvConvertOptions fast = new() { Upsampling = ChromaUpsampling.Nearest, Downsampling = ChromaDownsampling.Fast }; using YuvRaster<byte> yuv = YuvRaster.FromRaster(photo, ChromaFormat.Yuv420, YuvColor.Bt601Limited, options: fast); using Raster<Rgba8> back = yuv.ToRaster<Rgba8>(fast);

NColor = 3 Two to fifteen inks of an n-colour output profile (ICC's 2CLR to FCLR), such as a hexachrome or seven-colour press: ChannelCount says how many, and ColorantNames names them. ColorProfile web = ColorProfile.Srgb; ColorProfile wide = ColorProfile.DisplayP3; ColorProfile hdr = ColorProfile.Rec2100Pq; // ...and Create makes any other RGB encoding from primaries and a transfer function. ColorProfile camera = ColorProfile.Create(ColorPrimaries.AdobeRgb, TransferFunction.Gamma(2.2), "Camera RGB"); Console.WriteLine($"{camera.Name}: {camera.Model}, HDR {camera.IsHdr}, same as Adobe RGB: {camera.IsEquivalentTo(ColorProfile.AdobeRgb)}");

api/Egami.Colors.ColorTransform.html.summary: Class ColorTransform Namespace Egami.Colors Assembly Egami.dll A conversion from one color encoding to another, compiled once and then applied to spans of pixels of any type. Reusable and safe to share between threads. Transforms are cached per EgamiContext, so creating the same one again is cheap. public sealed class ColorTransform Inheritance object ColorTransform Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A transform is compiled once (and cached), then applied to spans of any pixel type, in place or into another type. ColorTransform transform = ColorTransform.Create(ColorProfile.DisplayP3, ColorProfile.Srgb, new ColorTransformOptions { Intent = RenderingIntent.Perceptual }); Rgba8[] pixels = [new(255, 0, 0, 255), new(0, 128, 255, 128)]; transform.Apply<Rgba8>(pixels); RgbaF32[] wide = new RgbaF32[pixels.Length]; transform.Apply<Rgba8, RgbaF32>(pixels, wide); // float types keep values outside 0..1 Remarks Pixels are read in the source encoding's model and written in the target's: RGB pixel types give and take red, green and blue; gray types their gray value; CMYK types (Cmyk8, Cmyk16) their inks. A pixel type of another model is converted to the encoding's model numerically first, as PixelConvert would (an RGB pixel's gray is its luma), and results land in it the same way. Alpha is carried over unchanged, and is opaque when the source has none. 8-bit RGB, BGR, RGBA, BGRA, gray, gray-alpha and CMYK pixels take a fast path; other types go through floats, so float and half types keep values outside 0..1 (as wide-gamut and HDR conversions produce) and integer types are clamped. Exceptions ArgumentNullException An argument is null. Returns the rendition of baseImage for a display with headroom (its peak over SDR white, linear; null for the map's full HDR capacity): linear RgbaF16 with 1.0 as SDR white (203 cd/m²), in the base image's primaries, with MaxContentLightLevel set from the map's largest boost. The display headroom, 1 or more, or null for full HDR. Returns Raster<RgbaF16> The rendition. The caller disposes it. Examples // As stored: the SDR base image, with the gain map in the metadata. using Raster sdr = Raster.Load("ultrahdr.jpg"); GainMap? map = sdr.Metadata.GainMap; // null for a plain JPEG // The HDR rendition for a display 4x as bright as SDR white: linear half floats, 1.0 = SDR white. using Raster<RgbaF16> hdr = Raster.Load<RgbaF16>("ultrahdr.jpg", options: new ReaderOptions { Hdr = new HdrDecode { Headroom = 4 } }); // The same from a raster in hand, at the map's full capacity. using Raster<RgbaF16> full = map!.Apply(sdr); Exceptions ArgumentNullException baseImage is null. Examples // Color values in the models apps ask for, from and to pixels, and between each other. Rgba8 orange = new(240, 128, 32, 255); HslColor hsl = HslColor.From(orange); // hue 28°, saturation 0.87, lightness 0.53 LabColor lab = ColorConvert.Convert<HslColor, LabColor>(hsl); // through XYZ OklchColor oklch = OklchColor.From(orange); YCbCrColor jpeg = YCbCrColor.From(orange); // BT.601 full range, as JPEG YCbCrColor video = YCbCrColor.From(orange, YuvMatrix.Bt709, YuvRange.Limited); // Color difference: CIEDE2000 on Lab, distance on Oklab. double deltaE = lab.DeltaE2000(LabColor.From(new Rgba8(235, 130, 40, 255))); // Whole rows at once, from any pixel type and encoding. Rgba8[] pixels = [orange, new(10, 20, 30, 255)]; OklabColor[] row = new OklabColor[pixels.Length]; ColorConvert.FromPixels<Rgba8, OklabColor>(pixels, row); ColorConvert.FromPixels<Rgba8, OklabColor>(pixels, row, ColorProfile.DisplayP3); // the same pixels read as Display P3 Methods From(Rgba8) Returns the value of an sRGB pixel; alpha is ignored. public static abstract TSelf From(Rgba8 color) Parameters color Rgba8 The pixel. Returns TSelf The value. Returns TSelf The value. FromXyz(XyzColor) Returns the value for an XYZ color (D65, white Y = 1). public static abstract TSelf FromXyz(XyzColor xyz) Parameters xyz XyzColor The color. Returns TSelf The value; components may fall outside their usual range for colors outside sRGB. IsCloseTo(TSelf, float) Returns whether every component of the two values differs by at most tolerance. bool IsCloseTo(TSelf other, float tolerance = 0.0001) Parameters other TSelf The other value. tolerance float The largest difference allowed in a component. Returns bool true if they are that close. ToRgba8() Returns the color as an opaque sRGB pixel, each channel clamped into range. Rgba8 ToRgba8() Returns Rgba8 The pixel. ToRgbaF32() Returns the color as an opaque sRGB pixel, unclamped, so colors outside sRGB keep channels outside 0..1. RgbaF32 ToRgbaF32() Returns RgbaF32 The pixel. ToXyz() Returns the color as XYZ (D65, white Y = 1). XyzColor ToXyz() Returns XyzColor The color.

api/Egami.Colors.IccProfileClass.html.summary: Enum IccProfileClass Namespace Egami.Colors Assembly Egami.dll What an ICC profile describes, from its header's class field. public enum IccProfileClass Fields Abstract = 6 An effect from PCS to PCS (abst). Egami does not convert with these. ColorSpace = 5 A color space such as a working space (spac). DeviceLink = 4 A link from one device space straight to another (link). Egami does not convert with these. Display = 2 A display (mntr); most RGB profiles in images. Input = 1 An input device such as a camera or scanner (scnr). NamedColor = 7 A list of named colors (nmcl). Egami does not convert with these. Output = 3 An output device such as a printer (prtr); most CMYK profiles. Unknown = 0 A class Egami does not know. Examples // IccData reads a profile's header and tags; it never throws, and says what was wrong with a damaged one. api/Egami.Colors.RenderingIntent.html.title: Enum RenderingIntent | Egami
api/Egami.Colors.RenderingIntent.html.summary: Enum RenderingIntent Namespace Egami.Colors Assembly Egami.dll How a color conversion handles colors the target cannot show, with the ICC numbering (0 to 3). public enum RenderingIntent Fields AbsoluteColorimetric = 3 Keep in-gamut colors exact, without adapting the white point (paper white shows as it measures). Perceptual = 0 Compress the whole gamut to fit, keeping relations between colors; uses the profile's perceptual tables. RelativeColorimetric = 1 Keep in-gamut colors exact relative to each white point and clip the rest. Saturation = 2 Keep colors vivid rather than exact; uses the profile's saturation tables. Examples // IccData reads a profile's header and tags; it never throws, and says what was wrong with a damaged one. IccData icc = IccData.Parse(bytes); Console.WriteLine($"{icc.Description}: version {icc.Version}, {icc.ProfileClass}, {icc.DataSpace} to {icc.ConnectionSpace}, damaged: {icc.IsDamaged}"); foreach (IccTag tag in icc.Tags) { Console.WriteLine($" {tag.Signature} ({tag.Type}), {tag.Data.Length} bytes"); } // ColorProfile.FromIcc makes an encoding from it: a matrix profile gets its primaries and curve, so an ICC profile written // for Display P3 is equivalent to the built-in. ColorProfile profile = ColorProfile.FromIcc(icc); bool isP3 = profile.IsEquivalentTo(ColorProfile.DisplayP3);

api/Egami.Colors.ToneMapping.html.title: Enum ToneMapping | Egami
api/Egami.Colors.ToneMapping.html.summary: Enum ToneMapping Namespace Egami.Colors Assembly Egami.dll How HDR light above reference white is brought into the 0..1 range of an SDR encoding. public enum ToneMapping Fields Bt2390 = 0 The EETF of ITU-R BT.2390: a Hermite knee in PQ space, applied to max(R, G, B) so hue holds, that leaves darker tones alone and rolls highlights off smoothly to reference white. For photos and video frames. Clip = 2 Clamps to 1. For tests, and for callers doing their own mapping. Reinhard = 1 Extended Reinhard on max(R, G, B), with its white point at the source peak: simple and predictable. Examples // HDR to SDR tone maps by default (BT.2390, source peak from the file's mDCV/cLLI, else 1,000 cd/m²). using Raster<Rgb8> web = hdr.ConvertColor<Rgb8>(ColorProfile.Srgb); // Or choose the curve and peak; Clip turns tone mapping off. using Raster<Rgb8> soft = hdr.ConvertColor<Rgb8>(ColorProfile.Srgb, new ColorTransformOptions { ToneMapping = ToneMapping.Reinhard, SourcePeakNits = 4000 }); // Linear HDR pixels (1.0 = reference white, 203 cd/m²) can be tone mapped in place. using Raster<RgbaF32> linear = hdr.ConvertColor<RgbaF32>(ColorProfile.LinearSrgb, new ColorTransformOptions { ToneMapping = ToneMapping.Clip }); linear.Apply(ops => ops.ToneMap(ToneMapping.Bt2390, sourcePeakNits: 1000));

api/Egami.Colors.TransferFunction.html.title: Class TransferFunction | Egami
api/Egami.Colors.TransferFunction.html.summary: Class TransferFunction Namespace Egami.Colors Assembly Egami.dll How a color space encodes light: the curve from stored values to linear light and back. Single values use exact double arithmetic; rows of floats use a vectorized form within 1e-5 of it (PQ rows use the double form), the same on every CPU with or without SIMD. public sealed class TransferFunction : IEquatable<TransferFunction> Inheritance object TransferFunction Implements IEquatable<TransferFunction> Inherited Members object.Equals(object, object) object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Examples // A transfer function decodes stored values to linear light and back; HDR curves put reference white at 1.0. double linear = TransferFunction.Srgb.ToLinear(0.5); // 0.214 double nits = TransferFunction.Pq.ToLinear(0.75) * 203; // a 75% PQ signal is about 983 cd/m² float[] row = [0f, 0.25f, 0.5f, 1f]; TransferFunction.Srgb.ToLinear(row, row); // a whole row at once, in place Remarks Linear 1.0 is the encoding's reference white. For PQ and HLG that is 203 cd/m² (ITU-R BT.2408), so HDR highlights are values above 1. PQ covers 0 to 10,000 cd/m², about 0 to 49.3. HLG decodes for a 1,000 cd/m² display with system gamma 1.2, which puts its reference white (a 75% signal) at 1.0; single values and rows apply its OOTF to each value as for a gray color, and the full OOTF, which depends on the color's luminance, is applied by color conversion. The SDR curves are extended to negative values by mirroring (f(−x) = −f(x)), as CSS Color 4 does, and to values above 1 by their own formula. PQ and HLG treat negative values as 0. api/Egami.Colors.html.title: Namespace Egami.Colors | Egami
api/Egami.Colors.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Colors Classes ColorConvert Converts between color values (IColorValue<TSelf>), through XYZ D65, and between rows of pixels and color values. ColorPrimaries The chromaticities of an RGB color space's red, green and blue primaries and of its white. With a transfer function they make a ColorProfile. ColorProfile What a raster's numbers mean: the color model, the primaries and white point, and the transfer function. Immutable; the built-ins cover the common encodings, and Create(ColorPrimaries, TransferFunction, string?) makes any other RGB encoding. ColorTransform A conversion from one color encoding to another, compiled once and then applied to spans of pixels of any type. Reusable and safe to share between threads. Transforms are cached per EgamiContext, so creating the same one again is cheap. ColorTransformOptions How a color conversion maps colors: the rendering intent, black point compensation, and for HDR sources, tone mapping, the source peak and reference white. Colorant A named ink: a process ink, a spot colour or a technical ink, with how it looks for backends that cannot print it. Names are matched exactly (ordinal, case-sensitive), as PDF matches them; the names Cyan, Magenta, Yellow and Black always mean the process inks, as in PDF's DeviceN. Two colorants are equal when their names are. GainMap An HDR gain map: a small image that, with GainMapInfo, turns an SDR base image into its HDR rendition (or the reverse). Read from Ultra HDR, ISO 21496-1 and Apple JPEG files into GainMap; written back by the JPEG writer. Immutable, so rasters can share it. GainMapInfo How a gain map turns its base image into another rendition, in ISO 21496-1's terms: for a gain map sample g (0 to 1) after gamma, the log2 boost is lerp(GainMapMin, GainMapMax, g), applied as (base + OffsetSdr) × 2^(boost × weight) − OffsetHdr, where the weight rises from 0 at a display headroom of HdrCapacityMin to 1 at HdrCapacityMax. Boosts and capacities are log2 values. GainMapOptions How Create(Raster, Raster?, GainMapOptions?) and GainMap make a gain map (HDR Design question 10). The defaults are libultrahdr's: a full-size map with a gain for each of red, green and blue, gamma 1, encoded at quality 95. HdrMetadata What an HDR file says about the display it was mastered on and the light levels in it (SMPTE ST 2086 and CTA-861.3, as PNG's mDCV and cLLI chunks store them). Tone mapping takes its source peak from here. Luminances are in cd/m². IccData A parsed ICC profile (ICC.1, versions 2 and 4): the header fields, the description and copyright text, and every tag with its bytes. Read-only; FromIcc(IccData) turns it into an encoding that conversion can use. InkColor A colour given as inks: named colorants with tints, as PDF's Separation and DeviceN colours, plus the appearance other backends draw. An ink canvas paints each named ink's plate; an RGB canvas, SVG or a raster without the ink draws Appearance. Immutable. InkSet The inks a printed page uses, fixed when an ink raster is made: the process inks of an output profile, then named spot and technical inks, at most MaxInks in all. Colours naming an ink the set lacks are drawn through their appearance into the process inks, as PDF does for a device without that colorant. Immutable: WithSpot(string, InkAppearance?, ColorantKind) and WithDisabled(string) return a new set. TransferFunction How a color space encodes light: the curve from stored values to linear light and back. Single values use exact double arithmetic; rows of floats use a vectorized form within 1e-5 of it (PQ rows use the double form), the same on every CPU with or without SIMD. Structs Chromaticity A CIE 1931 chromaticity: the x and y coordinates of a color with its brightness left out. CmykColor A CMYK color: ink amounts 0 to 1, 0 being no ink, by the plain formula (K = 1 − max(R, G, B), C = (1 − R − K) / (1 − K)) on encoded sRGB. Real inks need a print profile: From(Rgba8, ColorProfile, ColorTransformOptions?) converts through one. ColorCodePoints The ITU-T H.273 code points that PNG's cICP chunk, AVIF and JPEG XL use to name a color encoding: colour primaries, transfer characteristics, matrix coefficients and the full-range flag, kept exactly as stored so codes Egami does not know round-trip. GainMapValues A value for each of red, green and blue; a one-channel gain map has the same three. HslColor An HSL color: hue, saturation and lightness of encoded sRGB, as CSS hsl() defines them. HsvColor An HSV (HSB) color: hue, saturation and value of encoded sRGB, as color pickers use them. IccTag One tag of an ICC profile: its signature, the type signature its data starts with, and the data. InkAppearance How an ink looks at full tint where it cannot be printed: on an RGB canvas, in SVG, in a proof of a raster without its plate, or drawn into the process inks of a raster that lacks it. A process CMYK colour, an sRGB colour or a Lab colour, as PDF's alternate colour spaces allow. InkTint One ink of an InkColor and its tint. LabColor A CIE Lab* color relative to D50, as ICC and CSS Color 4 define Lab. LchColor A CIE LCh color: the polar form of LabColor (D50), with chroma and hue instead of a and b. OklabColor An Oklab color (Björn Ottosson, 2020): a perceptual space built on linear sRGB, where equal distances look about equally different and hues stay put when lightness or chroma changes. CSS Color 4's oklab(). OklchColor An Oklch color: the polar form of OklabColor, CSS Color 4's oklch(). XyzColor A CIE 1931 XYZ color relative to D65 white (Y = 1 for white), CSS Color 4's XYZ; ToD50() adapts it. YCbCrColor A Y'CbCr color: luma and two chroma differences of encoded sRGB, scaled as 8-bit codes / 255: at full range chroma is centered on 128 / 255, as JPEG and H.273 store it, so a byte reads as value × 255. The members without options use BT.601 at full range, as JPEG does; overloads take a YuvMatrix and YuvRange, from the coefficient table planar YUV images share. Interfaces IColorValue<TSelf> A color value in one color model, convertible to and from CIE XYZ (D65) and sRGB pixels, so ColorConvert can convert between any two models and between pixels and values. Enums ColorModel Whether a color encoding has three RGB channels, one gray channel, four CMYK inks, or the inks of an n-colour press. ColorantKind What a colorant is for, as PDF and ICC name inks. GainMapFormat Where a gain map's metadata came from. IccProfileClass What an ICC profile describes, from its header's class field. InkAppearanceKind The colour model an InkAppearance is given in. RenderingIntent How a color conversion handles colors the target cannot show, with the ICC numbering (0 to 3). ToneMapping How HDR light above reference white is brought into the 0..1 range of an SDR encoding.

api/Egami.Css.CssMarginBox.html.summary: Enum CssMarginBox Namespace Egami.Css Assembly Egami.Css.dll The sixteen page-margin boxes around a page's content (CSS Paged Media 3 section 5.1), clockwise from the top left. public enum CssMarginBox Fields BottomCenter = 10 @bottom-center. CssPageStyle appendix = cascade.CascadePage(new CssPage("appendix", IsFirst: false, IsLeft: false)); bool isTurned = CssPageSize.TryParse(appendix.Page.GetValueText("size")!, out CssPageSize turned); bool landscape = turned.Orientation == CssPageOrientation.Landscape; // true: 297mm by 210mm

BadString = 5 A string cut off by a newline. BadUrl = 7 An unquoted url(...) with characters it may not contain. Cdc = 14 -->. Cdo = 13 <!--. Colon = 15 :. Comma = 17 ,. CssCascadeOptions Options for building a CssCascade. CssCascadedStyle The cascaded style of an element: the winning declaration of each property, with its origin. CssComponentValue A CSS Syntax 3 component value: a preserved token, a function or a simple block. Declarations, preludes and values are lists of these. ToString() serializes back to CSS text. CssComputedStyle An element's computed style, as far as CSS defines it generically: CSS-wide keywords resolved, inheritance applied, custom properties and var() substituted. Values stay component values; the consumer parses each property by its type (and resolves relative units, percentages and currentcolor). CssFontFace The descriptors of an @font-face rule (CSS Fonts 4), parsed. Invalid descriptors keep their defaults. CssFontFaceRule An @font-face rule. CssFontSource One source of an @font-face src descriptor: a URL with its format and technologies, or a local font. CssFunction A function: its name and its arguments up to the closing parenthesis. CssImportRule An @import rule. Egami.Css does not fetch it: the consumer may load the sheet and pass it to the cascade. CssLayerRule An @layer rule: a statement naming layers, or a block of rules. Cascade layers are not implemented: the cascade treats the rules inside a layer block as ordinary rules in their place. CssMatrixTransform matrix(a, b, c, d, e, f). CssNamespaces The namespace prefixes selectors may use (svg|rect, [xlink|href]) and the default namespace for type selectors, as @namespace rules declare them. Prefixes are case-sensitive. CssPageMarginRule A page-margin rule inside @page, such as @bottom-center { content: counter(page) }. CssPageRule An @page rule (CSS Paged Media 3): page selectors, the declarations for the page context (size, margin, padding, border, background, inherited text properties) and its page-margin rules. api/Egami.DecodeStatus.html.summary: Enum DecodeStatus Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll Where a RasterDecoder stands, as Status reports it. public enum DecodeStatus Fields Completed = 3 Every frame has been read. Examples // Decode while the bytes arrive, a chunk at a time, as from a download. using RasterDecoder decoder = RasterDecoder.OpenIncremental(); Raster<Rgb8>? band = null; foreach (ReadOnlyMemory<byte> chunk in file.Chunk(4096).Select(c => new ReadOnlyMemory<byte>(c))) { decoder.Append(chunk.Span); if (decoder.HeaderRead) { band ??= Raster.Create<Rgb8>(decoder.Info.Width, 16); int rows; while ((rows = decoder.ReadRows(band)) > 0) { rowsSoFar += rows; // the rows finished so far; an interlaced file shows RenderPreview instead } } } decoder.EndOfInput(); while (decoder.ReadRows(band!) is int rest and > 0) { rowsSoFar += rest; } band?.Dispose();

api/Egami.DiagnosticLevel.html.title: Enum DiagnosticLevel | Egami
api/Egami.DiagnosticLevel.html.summary: Enum DiagnosticLevel Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll How much an EgamiDiagnostic matters. Maps one to one onto the Debug, Information and Warning log levels. public enum DiagnosticLevel Fields Debug = 0 Detail for someone chasing a problem, such as a safety limit about to throw or the band count of a parallel decode. Info = 1 A notable decision Egami made for the caller, such as the format detected or the factor picked for a scaled decode. Warning = 2 A problem Egami recovered from, or something lost on purpose, such as a bad checksum read leniently or alpha dropped when saving JPEG. Every Warning raised by a load is also in Warnings. Examples // Info and Debug events are off unless asked for; below the level they are never even formatted. EgamiContext verbose = EgamiContext.Default with { Diagnostics = d => seen.Add(d), DiagnosticLevel = DiagnosticLevel.Debug, }; using Raster image = Raster.Load("duck.jpg", verbose, new ReaderOptions { MinimumSize = new Size(100, 100) }); foreach (EgamiDiagnostic d in seen) { Console.WriteLine($"{d.Level,-7} {d.Id}: {d.Message}"); }

Get one from StartDiagnostics() at the start of a call (format plug-ins use Diagnostics) and dispose it when the call ends. When the context has no handler it is a shared instance that does nothing, so reporting costs one check. public sealed class DiagnosticReporter : IDisposable Inheritance object DiagnosticReporter Implements IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A decoder outside Egami (a video demuxer, a format plug-in's own entry point) reports through the same handler, with the // same level filter and the same cap of 10 per id per call. GdiPlus = 1 As measured from GDI+'s SmoothingMode.AntiAlias and HighQuality: 8 by 4 point samples a pixel, at eighths across and quarters down from its top-left corner, so coverage comes in 32 steps. A sample on a shape's left or top edge is inside and one on its right or bottom edge is outside. api/Egami.Drawing.Canvas.html.summary: Class Canvas Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll A surface to draw paths, shapes, strokes and images on, through a current transform and clip. The canvas itself is abstract: RasterCanvas<TPixel> draws into pixels, and other backends (a PDF page, a recorder) keep the calls as vectors. Every public call is checked and tracked here (the transform, the clip bounds, the save stack) and then ends in exactly one protected On hook, which is all a backend overrides; hooks added in later versions get default bodies, so adding them never breaks a backend. Coordinates are float pixels, y down; the pixel at (0, 0) covers the square from 0 to 1. Calls draw when they are made. A canvas is for one thread at a time; one large call may still spread its rows over several cores. public abstract class Canvas : IDisposable Inheritance object Canvas Implements IDisposable Derived InkCanvas PictureRecorder RasterCanvas<TPixel> SvgCanvas Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Extension Methods CanvasBarcodeExtensions.DrawBarcode(Canvas, Barcode, RectF, Paint, BarcodeDrawOptions?) By default a sprite without a color is a DrawImage(Raster, RectF, RectF, SamplingOptions?, Paint?) under its transform, and a tinted one a two-triangle textured OnDrawMesh(Mesh, Paint, BlendMode, ReadOnlySpan<GradientStop>) call, one sprite at a time. protected virtual void OnDrawAtlas(Raster image, ReadOnlySpan<SpriteTransform> transforms, ReadOnlySpan<RectF> sources, ReadOnlySpan<RgbaF32> colors, BlendMode colorBlend, SamplingOptions sampling, Paint? paint) Parameters image Raster The sprite sheet. transforms ReadOnlySpan<SpriteTransform> Where each sprite goes. sources ReadOnlySpan<RectF> Each sprite's part of the image. colors ReadOnlySpan<RgbaF32> One color per sprite, or empty. colorBlend BlendMode How a sprite combines with its color. sampling SamplingOptions How the image is sampled. paint Paint The blend mode, opacity and antialiasing, or null. Examples // Pack the sprites once, then draw thousands of them in one call: each with its own place, turn, scale and tint. using SpriteSheet sheet = SpriteSheet.Pack([spark, star], new SpritePackOptions { Padding = 1 }); Random random = new(7); SpriteTransform[] transforms = new SpriteTransform[2000]; RectF[] sources = new RectF[transforms.Length]; RgbaF32[] tints = new RgbaF32[transforms.Length]; for (int i = 0; i < transforms.Length; i++) { Rect frame = sheet.Frames[i % 2]; sources[i] = frame; transforms[i] = SpriteTransform.FromRotationScale( scale: 0.3f + random.NextSingle(), degrees: random.NextSingle() * 360, position: new Vector2(random.NextSingle() * 320, random.NextSingle() * 200), anchor: new Vector2(frame.Width / 2f, frame.Height / 2f)); tints[i] = new RgbaF32(1, 0.5f + (random.NextSingle() / 2), random.NextSingle(), 0.8f); } using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // Plus adds the sprites up, as light does. canvas.DrawAtlas(sheet.Image, transforms, sources, tints, BlendMode.Modulate, paint: new SolidPaint(Rgba8.White) { BlendMode = BlendMode.Plus }); } OnDrawEncodedImage(EncodedImage, RectF, RectF, SamplingOptions, Paint?) Draws part of an encoded image into a local rectangle; the source lies inside the image. A PDF backend can embed a JPEG's bytes as they are. By default the image is decoded once and drawn with OnDrawImage(Raster, RectF, RectF, SamplingOptions, Paint?). protected virtual void OnDrawEncodedImage(EncodedImage image, RectF source, RectF destination, SamplingOptions sampling, Paint? paint) Parameters image EncodedImage The image. source RectF The part to draw, inside the image. destination RectF Where it goes, in local coordinates. sampling SamplingOptions How it is sampled. paint Paint The blend mode, opacity and antialiasing, or null for source-over. Examples // A backend overrides hooks; the base class has already checked the arguments and tracks the transform and clip bounds. // This one writes SVG elements, keeping rectangles as rectangles and strokes as stroke settings. public sealed class SvgCanvas(float width, float height) : Canvas(width, height) { private readonly System.Text.StringBuilder _body = new(); public string Document => $"<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" width=\"{Width}\" height=\"{Height}\">{_body}</svg>"; protected override void OnDrawRect(RectF rect, Stroke? stroke, Paint paint) => _body.Append(FormattableString.Invariant($"<rect x=\"{rect.X}\" y=\"{rect.Y}\" width=\"{rect.Width}\" height=\"{rect.Height}\" {Style(stroke, paint)}/>")); protected override void OnDrawPath(Path path, Stroke? stroke, Paint paint) { System.Text.StringBuilder d = new(); int p = 0; foreach (PathVerb verb in path.Verbs) { int count = verb switch { PathVerb.Quad => 2, PathVerb.Cubic => 3, PathVerb.Close => 0, _ => 1 }; d.Append(verb switch { PathVerb.Move => "M", PathVerb.Line => "L", PathVerb.Quad => "Q", PathVerb.Cubic => "C", _ => "Z" }); foreach (Vector2 point in path.Points.Slice(p, count)) { d.Append(FormattableString.Invariant($"{point.X},{point.Y} ")); } p += count; } _body.Append(System.Globalization.CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, $"<path d=\"{d}\" {Style(stroke, paint)}/>"); } protected override void OnClipPath(Path path, ClipOp op, bool antialias) { // Clips would become <clipPath> elements; this sketch leaves them out. } protected override void OnDrawImage(Raster image, RectF source, RectF destination, SamplingOptions sampling, Paint? paint) { // An image would be embedded as a PNG data URI. } private string Style(Stroke? stroke, Paint paint) { Rgba8 c = paint is SolidPaint solid ? solid.Color.ToRgba8() : Rgba8.Black; string color = $"#{c.R:x2}{c.G:x2}{c.B:x2}"; string transform = Matrix.IsIdentity ? "" : FormattableString.Invariant($" transform=\"matrix({Matrix.M11} {Matrix.M12} {Matrix.M21} {Matrix.M22} {Matrix.M31} {Matrix.M32})\""); return stroke is null ? $"fill=\"{color}\"{transform}" : FormattableString.Invariant($"fill=\"none\" stroke=\"{color}\" stroke-width=\"{stroke.Width}\" stroke-linecap=\"{stroke.Cap.ToString().ToLowerInvariant()}\"{transform}"); } } OnDrawImageLattice(Raster, Lattice, RectF, SamplingOptions, Paint?) Draws an image through a lattice; the lattice fits the image. By default each cell is an OnDrawImage(Raster, RectF, RectF, SamplingOptions, Paint?) call of its part of the image, sampled only inside that part, and each fixed-color cell an OnDrawRect(RectF, Stroke?, Paint) call; a PDF backend gets one image per cell this way. Examples using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // An Android .9.png: its one-pixel border marks what stretches. The corners stay sharp at any size. LatticeCellKind[] kinds = [.. Enumerable.Repeat(LatticeCellKind.Default, 9)]; kinds[4] = LatticeCellKind.FixedColor; RgbaF32[] colors = new RgbaF32[9]; colors[4] = new RgbaF32(0.95f, 0.95f, 0.9f, 1); canvas.DrawImageLattice(frame, new Lattice([8, 16], [8, 16]) { CellKinds = kinds, CellColors = colors }, new RectF(150, 70, 140, 40)); } OnDrawImageMask(Raster, RectF, Paint, SamplingOptions) Paints through an image mask. "" : FormattableString.Invariant($" transform=\"matrix({Matrix.M11} {Matrix.M12} {Matrix.M21} {Matrix.M22} {Matrix.M31} {Matrix.M32})\""); return stroke is null ? $"fill=\"{color}\"{transform}" : FormattableString.Invariant($"fill=\"none\" stroke=\"{color}\" stroke-width=\"{stroke.Width}\" stroke-linecap=\"{stroke.Cap.ToString().ToLowerInvariant()}\"{transform}"); } } OnDrawPicture(Picture, Matrix3x2, Paint?, bool) Draws a recorded picture. By default it calls OnRestore(). protected virtual void OnRestoreLayer() OnSave() Called by Save() after the state is pushed. protected virtual void OnSave() OnSaveLayer(LayerOptions) Called by SaveLayer(LayerOptions?) after the state is pushed; DeviceClipBounds is already limited by the options' bounds. The raster backend allocates the layer; a PDF backend would begin a transparency group. By default it calls OnSave(), so a backend without layers draws their contents directly. protected virtual void OnSaveLayer(LayerOptions options) Parameters options LayerOptions How the layer is merged. Examples using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // Group opacity: the overlapping circles fade as one shape, with no darker overlap. canvas.SaveLayer(0.5f); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(80, 100), 60, new Rgba8(200, 30, 30, 255)); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(140, 100), 60, new Rgba8(200, 30, 30, 255)); canvas.Restore(); // A group blended with Multiply and blurred as a whole; the layer grows by the blur's reach, so nothing is cut. canvas.SaveLayer(new LayerOptions { BlendMode = BlendMode.Multiply, Filter = ops => ops.Blur(4) }); canvas.FillRect(new RectF(180, 40, 90, 120), new Rgba8(40, 120, 220, 255)); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(225, 100), 30, Rgba8.White); canvas.Restore(); } OnSetMatrix(Matrix3x2) Called whenever the transform changes, with the new transform (also Matrix). protected virtual void OnSetMatrix(Matrix3x2 matrix) Parameters matrix Matrix3x2 The transform from local to device coordinates. RasterizeFallback(Action<Canvas>, float) Draws one call into a temporary raster instead, for a backend that cannot express it (a blend mode or paint its format lacks): the result covers the device clip bounds at scale device pixels per unit and holds what the call draws, clipped to those bounds, over transparency; the backend then draws it as an image. Skia's PDF backend falls back the same way. A paint's Blur, whose sigma is in device units, is scaled with the raster, so it keeps its size. A layer's filter and backdrop chains run on the raster's pixels as they are: a chain with sizes in pixels (a blur radius, an offset) should be built for the scale. protected FallbackImage? RasterizeFallback(Action<Canvas> draw, float scale = 1) Parameters draw Action<Canvas> The call, made on a raster canvas set up with this canvas's transform. scale float Raster pixels per device unit, such as 300 / 72 for a PDF page at 300 dpi. Returns FallbackImage The image and the device rectangle it covers, or null when the clip is empty. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException scale is not positive and finite. Examples // A canvas draws onto a raster. api/Egami.Drawing.PathBuilder.html.summary: Class PathBuilder Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll Builds a Path one command at a time. Arcs, ovals and round corners become cubic curves as they are added, so a path holds only lines, quadratics and cubics. A line or curve with no contour open starts one at the last contour's start (or the origin), as SVG and Skia do. Building takes time in proportion to the points added; ToPath(FillRule) copies them, so the builder can go on or be reused. public sealed class PathBuilder Inheritance object PathBuilder Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A path is built once and never changes, so it can be drawn many times and from many threads. Path heart = new PathBuilder() .MoveTo(150, 60) .CubicTo(150, 30, 100, 20, 90, 60) .CubicTo(80, 100, 130, 130, 150, 160) .CubicTo(170, 130, 220, 100, 210, 60) .CubicTo(200, 20, 150, 30, 150, 60) .Close() .ToPath(); canvas.FillPath(heart, Rgba8.Red); // SVG's arc command, and the even-odd rule: an inner contour becomes a hole. api/Egami.Drawing.PathEffect.html.summary: Class PathEffect Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll Turns one path into another before it is filled or stroked: dashes, rounded corners, trimming, jitter, shapes stamped along the path, hatching. Effects are immutable, so one can be shared and reused; Then(PathEffect) and Plus(PathEffect) combine them. api/Egami.Drawing.PathMeasure.html.summary: Class PathMeasure Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll Measures a path: the length of each contour, and the point, direction and pieces at any distance along it. Lengths are exact to about 1e-4 units, curves included: each curve's length is integrated by adaptive Gauss–Legendre quadrature, and a distance is turned back into a point on the curve by Newton steps, so long curves do not gather the errors of a flattened outline. Contours of zero length are left out, as Skia's SkContourMeasureIter leaves them. Measuring is done once, here; the queries are cheap and safe from many threads. public sealed class PathMeasure Inheritance object PathMeasure Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // Measure a path: its length, and a point and direction at any distance, curves included. Path arrow = Path.Polygon([new(-6, -4), new(0, 0), new(-6, 4)]).Transform(contour.GetMatrix(contour.Length)); Path middle = contour.GetSegment(contour.Length / 3, 2 * contour.Length / 3); Constructors PathMeasure(Path, bool) Initializes a new instance of the PathMeasure class. public PathMeasure(Path path, bool forceClosed = false) Parameters path Path The path. forceClosed bool Whether to measure open contours as if closed, with the line back to their start. api/Egami.Drawing.PathOp.html.summary: Enum PathOp Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll How Op(Path, PathOp, float) and Combine(IEnumerable<Path>, PathOp, float) combine the areas of two paths: Skia's five operations. public enum PathOp Fields Difference = 0 The first area without the second. Intersect = 1 Where both areas are. ReverseDifference = 4 The second area without the first. Union = 2 Where either area is. Xor = 3 Where exactly one of the areas is. Examples // A frame: one round rectangle cut out of another, kept as curves, so a PDF or SVG backend writes it exactly. Path frame = Path.RoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(0, 0, 200, 140), 24)) .Difference(Path.RoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(20, 20, 160, 100), 12))); // Many shapes in one pass, applied left to right; overlaps and self-intersections removed; an area grown by 4 units. api/Egami.Drawing.PathVerb.html.summary: Enum PathVerb Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll One drawing command of a Path; the comment on each says how many points it takes. public enum PathVerb : byte Fields Close = 4 Closes the contour with a line back to its start; takes no point. api/Egami.Drawing.PixelGeometry.html.summary: Enum PixelGeometry Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll The order of a display's color subpixels, which LCD text edging needs to know. public enum PixelGeometry Fields BgrHorizontal = 2 Blue, green and red stripes from left to right. BgrVertical = 4 Blue, green and red stripes from top to bottom. RgbHorizontal = 1 Red, green and blue stripes from left to right, the common LCD layout. RgbVertical = 3 Red, green and blue stripes from top to bottom, as on a rotated display. Unknown = 0 Not known: LCD edging falls back to grayscale. Examples // Small text for a screen: light hinting (vertical only), quarter-pixel origins (the default) and, for an RGB display // the image will not leave, LCD edging. var screen = new Font(face, 13) { Hinting = FontHinting.Light, Edging = FontEdging.Lcd }; using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = image.CreateCanvas(new CanvasOptions { PixelGeometry = PixelGeometry.RgbHorizontal })) { canvas.DrawText("Crisp caption", new Vector2(8, 24), screen, Rgba8.Black); // A face matched for bold italic it lacks is emboldened and slanted, unless AllowSynthesis is off. var synthetic = new Font(face, 13) { Synthesis = FontSynthesis.Bold | FontSynthesis.Italic }; canvas.DrawText("Synthetic bold italic", new Vector2(8, 48), synthetic, Rgba8.Black); }

api/Egami.Drawing.PixelOffset.html.summary: Enum PixelOffset Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll Where a canvas puts its pixel centres, for paths and unhinted text: GDI+'s PixelOffsetMode. public enum PixelOffset Fields Half = 0 Whole coordinates fall on pixel edges and pixel centres at half coordinates: Egami's default, GDI+'s Half. A clip that is a pixel-aligned rectangle stays a rectangle; any other clip becomes a coverage mask over the clip's bounds. A call whose area exceeds 256 KiB of destination rows spreads its rows over up to MaxParallelism cores, with the same pixels at any core count. Examples // Pack the sprites once, then draw thousands of them in one call: each with its own place, turn, scale and tint. using SpriteSheet sheet = SpriteSheet.Pack([spark, star], new SpritePackOptions { Padding = 1 }); Random random = new(7); SpriteTransform[] transforms = new SpriteTransform[2000]; RectF[] sources = new RectF[transforms.Length]; RgbaF32[] tints = new RgbaF32[transforms.Length]; for (int i = 0; i < transforms.Length; i++) { Rect frame = sheet.Frames[i % 2]; sources[i] = frame; transforms[i] = SpriteTransform.FromRotationScale( scale: 0.3f + random.NextSingle(), degrees: random.NextSingle() * 360, position: new Vector2(random.NextSingle() * 320, random.NextSingle() * 200), anchor: new Vector2(frame.Width / 2f, frame.Height / 2f)); tints[i] = new RgbaF32(1, 0.5f + (random.NextSingle() / 2), random.NextSingle(), 0.8f); } using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // Plus adds the sprites up, as light does. canvas.DrawAtlas(sheet.Image, transforms, sources, tints, BlendMode.Modulate, paint: new SolidPaint(Rgba8.White) { BlendMode = BlendMode.Plus }); } Remarks Each sprite is two textured triangles filled on its own; the sheet's texels are prepared once for the whole call. Draws an image through a lattice; the lattice fits the image. By default each cell is an OnDrawImage(Raster, RectF, RectF, SamplingOptions, Paint?) call of its part of the image, sampled only inside that part, and each fixed-color cell an OnDrawRect(RectF, Stroke?, Paint) call; a PDF backend gets one image per cell this way. The raster backend draws the cells as one mesh instead, so they meet without seams. protected override void OnDrawImageLattice(Raster image, Lattice lattice, RectF destination, SamplingOptions sampling, Paint? paint) Parameters image Raster The image. lattice Lattice The grid. destination RectF Where the image goes, in local coordinates; not empty. sampling SamplingOptions How the image is sampled. paint Paint The blend mode, opacity and antialiasing, or null. Examples using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // An Android .9.png: its one-pixel border marks what stretches. The corners stay sharp at any size. (Raster inner, Lattice lattice, Rect? padding) = NinePatch.FromAndroid(file); canvas.DrawImageLattice(inner, lattice, new RectF(10, 10, 180, 48)); inner.Dispose(); // A nine-patch from a plain image: the 8-pixel corners keep their size, the edges and center stretch. canvas.DrawImageNinePatch(frame, new Rect(8, 8, 8, 8), new RectF(10, 70, 120, 40)); // A lattice can leave cells out or fill them with a color: here the center becomes a flat panel. LatticeCellKind[] kinds = [.. Enumerable.Repeat(LatticeCellKind.Default, 9)]; kinds[4] = LatticeCellKind.FixedColor; RgbaF32[] colors = new RgbaF32[9]; colors[4] = new RgbaF32(0.95f, 0.95f, 0.9f, 1); canvas.DrawImageLattice(frame, new Lattice([8, 16], [8, 16]) { CellKinds = kinds, CellColors = colors }, new RectF(150, 70, 140, 40)); } Remarks The cells are one mesh, each cell's triangles textured from a copy of its part of the image, so samples stay inside the cell as in Skia and neighboring cells still meet without seams; fixed-color cells are part of the same mesh. OnRestore() Called by Restore() after the state is popped; Matrix and DeviceClipBounds are already the restored ones. protected override void OnRestore() OnRestoreLayer() Called by Restore() for a state saved by SaveLayer(LayerOptions?), after it is popped, so Matrix and DeviceClipBounds are those the layer was started with: the raster backend merges the layer through that clip. By default it calls OnRestore(). protected override void OnRestoreLayer() Remarks Filters the layer, multiplies it by its soft mask, and merges it with its opacity and blend mode through the restored clip. OnSave() Called by Save() after the state is pushed. protected override void OnSave() OnSaveLayer(LayerOptions) Called by SaveLayer(LayerOptions?) after the state is pushed; DeviceClipBounds is already limited by the options' bounds. The raster backend allocates the layer; a PDF backend would begin a transparency group. By default it calls OnSave(), so a backend without layers draws their contents directly. protected override void OnSaveLayer(LayerOptions options) Parameters options LayerOptions How the layer is merged. Examples using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // Group opacity: the overlapping circles fade as one shape, with no darker overlap. canvas.SaveLayer(0.5f); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(80, 100), 60, new Rgba8(200, 30, 30, 255)); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(140, 100), 60, new Rgba8(200, 30, 30, 255)); canvas.Restore(); // A group blended with Multiply and blurred as a whole; the layer grows by the blur's reach, so nothing is cut. canvas.SaveLayer(new LayerOptions { BlendMode = BlendMode.Multiply, Filter = ops => ops.Blur(4) }); canvas.FillRect(new RectF(180, 40, 90, 120), new Rgba8(40, 120, 220, 255)); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(225, 100), 30, Rgba8.White); canvas.Restore(); } Remarks Allocates the layer over the options' bounds inside the clip, grown by the filter's reach (the whole bounds, or the raster, when the reach is unknown), and starts it transparent, as a copy of the backdrop, or as the filtered backdrop. Inside the layer the clip is the layer's rectangle: the clip of this call applies once, when the layer is merged.
