api/Egami.Drawing.html.title: Namespace Egami.Drawing | Egami
api/Egami.Drawing.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Drawing Classes Annotation A link or a destination for DrawAnnotation(RectF, Annotation): what a document backend writes, and pixels never show. BlendPaint Two paints combined pixel by pixel with a blend mode, as Skia's blend shader: Source is blended onto Destination, and the result is what this paint draws. Each part keeps its own LocalMatrix and Opacity (its blend mode, blur and dithering are not used), inside this paint's own local matrix. Canvas A surface to draw paths, shapes, strokes and images on, through a current transform and clip. The canvas itself is abstract: RasterCanvas<TPixel> draws into pixels, and other backends (a PDF page, a recorder) keep the calls as vectors. Every public call is checked and tracked here (the transform, the clip bounds, the save stack) and then ends in exactly one protected On hook, which is all a backend overrides; hooks added in later versions get default bodies, so adding them never breaks a backend. Coordinates are float pixels, y down; the pixel at (0, 0) covers the square from 0 to 1. Calls draw when they are made. A canvas is for one thread at a time; one large call may still spread its rows over several cores. CanvasOptions Settings for a raster canvas. ColorMatrixPaint Another paint with a color matrix run on its colors, as Skia's color-filtered shader: each color, unpremultiplied, goes through the matrix, is clamped to 0 to 1 and is premultiplied again. WithColorMatrix(ColorMatrix) makes one. ConicalGradient A gradient between two circles, as the HTML canvas's createRadialGradient, Skia's two-point conical gradient and a PDF type 3 shading define it: for each t, the circle whose center and radius are t of the way from the start circle to the end one; a pixel takes the largest t whose circle passes through it with a radius of at least 0. It covers a focal point inside a circle (a start radius of 0), one circle inside the other, and cones drawn on one side only. ContourMeasure One measured contour of a PathMeasure. Distances run from 0 at the contour's start to Length at its end; distances outside are clamped to them, as in Skia. CustomPaint A paint whose colors come from C# code: override Shade(int, int, Span<PremulRgbaF32>, in Matrix3x2) to fill a row of premultiplied float colors. Rows are shaded in parallel bands, so Shade(int, int, Span<PremulRgbaF32>, in Matrix3x2) must be thread-safe and must give a pixel the same color whichever band or thread asks; then the result is the same at any core count. A backend that keeps vectors, such as a PDF page, cannot run C# and draws the call through its raster fallback instead. Derive a record class from it. DashPattern The dashes of a stroke: lengths of drawn and skipped stretches in turn, in path units, and where in the pattern each contour starts, as PDF's d, SVG's stroke-dasharray and stroke-dashoffset, and Skia's dash effect define them. An odd number of lengths repeats once to make an even one, as SVG says, and a pattern whose lengths add up to 0 draws a solid line. Each dash is an open piece of the path that follows its curves and gets the stroke's caps; the pattern starts afresh on each contour. DrawingExtensions Ways into a canvas from Egami's rasters and operation chains. EncodedImage An image kept as its file's bytes, such as a JPEG, for DrawImage(EncodedImage, RectF, SamplingOptions?, Paint?): a backend that can store the bytes as they are, as a PDF page stores a JPEG as DCTDecode, gets them through OnDrawEncodedImage without decoding and encoding again; every other backend draws the decoded pixels. The bytes are probed when the image is made and decoded at most once, on first need. Immutable and thread-safe. FallbackImage A drawing call rendered into pixels by Canvas.RasterizeFallback, for a backend to place as an image. FontExtensions Glyphs and text as Paths in canvas units, y down, for clipping, stroking or measuring them as shapes. GlyphCache The process-wide cache of glyph coverage masks the raster canvas draws small text from: one mask per typeface (each variation position its own), glyph, device em size, axis scales, subpixel phase, edging, hinting and synthesis, for glyphs up to 256 device pixels per em under a scale-and-translate transform. Masks hold one byte per pixel, or three for LCD edging. Bigger, rotated or skewed glyphs fill as paths and are not cached. Masks are rendered by the same rasterizer as paths and drawn at the same rounded positions either way, so the cache changes speed, never pixels. Shared by every canvas on every thread; least recently used masks go first when the budget is spent. Gradient A paint whose color changes along a line, around a center or between two circles by its stops. Each pixel center maps back through the canvas transform and LocalMatrix to a position t along the gradient, which Tile brings into 0 to 1 and the stops turn into a color. On 8-bit targets t picks one of 1024 colors made once per paint; float and 16-bit targets mix the stops exactly. GradientInterpolation How a gradient mixes its stops: the color space, as CSS Color 4 defines them, and for Oklch the way around the hue circle. ImagePaint An image as a paint: shapes are filled with the image's pixels, pixel (0, 0) covering the paint-space square from 0 to 1, under LocalMatrix and the canvas transform. TileX and TileY say what lies past its edges, so it tiles as a pattern, and Decal leaves the outside transparent, as image masks and stencils need. When the paint shrinks the image, sampling reads the nearest smaller level of a MipChain. InkCanvas A canvas that draws into an InkRaster's plates: printing inks instead of RGB. It shares RasterCanvas<TPixel>'s rasterizer, clips and layers, so shapes, strokes and text cover exactly the same pixels; where the RGB canvas blends colours, this one sets each plate. A paint's Ink prints its inks by name (inks the raster lacks through their appearance into the process inks); RGB colours, gradients and images convert into the process inks through RgbSource and the ink set's profile. InkCanvasOptions How an InkCanvas turns colours that are not inks into its process inks. Lattice A grid over an image for DrawImageLattice(Raster, Lattice, RectF, SamplingOptions?, Paint?), as Skia's lattice: the x and y divisions cut the image into columns and rows that alternate fixed and stretchable, starting with fixed, so a division at the image's left or top edge makes the first column or row stretchable. Fixed columns and rows keep their size when the destination is large enough and shrink in proportion when it is not; stretchable ones share what is left. A nine-patch is the lattice with two divisions each way. LayerOptions How a layer started by SaveLayer(LayerOptions?) is merged at the matching Restore(): filtered, masked, faded by Opacity and blended into what lies below with BlendMode, through the clip. A layer is what PDF calls a transparency group. LcdFilter The five-tap filter LCD text spreads each subpixel's coverage with, across the subpixel and its two neighbours on each side. The weights add up to 256. A wider filter has softer colour fringes; a narrower one is sharper and more coloured. LinearGradient A gradient along a line: t is 0 on the line through Start square to it, and 1 through End. MarkedContent A tag that brackets a run of drawing for a document backend, as PDF's marked content (BMC, BDC and EMC): a structure element of tagged PDF (a paragraph, a heading, a figure), an artifact such as a page number, or a span with replacement text. Mesh Triangles with an optional color, texture coordinate or value at each vertex, for DrawMesh(Mesh, Paint?, BlendMode, ReadOnlySpan<GradientStop>): Gouraud-shaded triangles, textured triangles (a paint mapped through the texture coordinates) and PDF's free-form and lattice-form shadings (one value per vertex, mapped through gradient stops). Immutable: the constructor copies what it is given. NinePatch An image with its Lattice, as Android's nine-patch (.9.png) files hold them. NoisePaint Procedural noise as a paint. Fractal(float, float, int, int, Size?) and Turbulence(float, float, int, int, Size?) follow SVG 1.1's feTurbulence step by step (its random table, lattice and gradients), so the pixels match Skia's noise shaders and browsers within rounding; Simplex(float, int, int, Size?) is smoother and can tile. Each of the four channels is its own noise, straight alpha included. The noise lives in paint coordinates: it scales and turns with the canvas transform and LocalMatrix. Paint What a drawing call puts on the canvas, and how it combines with what is there: the colors (from the subclass), the BlendMode, an Opacity, whether edges are antialiased, and for shapes an optional Blur. The kinds are SolidPaint, the gradients (LinearGradient, RadialGradient, ConicalGradient, SweepGradient), ImagePaint, NoisePaint, BlendPaint, ColorMatrixPaint and CustomPaint. A color converts to a solid paint where a paint is expected. A paint is an ITextPaint, so a paragraph's text style can carry it. A paint other than a solid one has its own coordinates: LocalMatrix maps them into the canvas's local coordinates, so a gradient or an image turns and scales with the canvas transform, and further with its own matrix. Patch A curved four-sided surface with a color, value or texture coordinate at each corner, for DrawPatch(Patch, Paint?, BlendMode, ReadOnlySpan<GradientStop>): PDF's Coons and tensor-product patch shadings (types 6 and 7) and Skia's drawPatch. The surface's parameters u (left to right) and v (top to bottom) run from 0 to 1; corner data is interpolated bilinearly in them. Immutable. Corners are in the order top-left (u 0, v 0), top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left. A Coons patch's 12 points go clockwise from the top-left corner, as Skia's: the top curve left to right (points 0 to 3), the right curve down (3 to 6), the bottom curve right to left (6 to 9) and the left curve up (9, 10, 11, 0). A tensor patch's 16 points are its net row by row, top row first, each row left to right. Path An outline of contours made of lines, quadratic and cubic Bézier curves, with the FillRule that says which points it covers when filled. A path never changes after it is built, so one path can be drawn from many threads and kept by any canvas backend. Coordinates are float pixels, y down. Build one with PathBuilder or a shape helper such as Circle(Vector2, float). PathBuilder Builds a Path one command at a time. Arcs, ovals and round corners become cubic curves as they are added, so a path holds only lines, quadratics and cubics. A line or curve with no contour open starts one at the last contour's start (or the origin), as SVG and Skia do. Building takes time in proportion to the points added; ToPath(FillRule) copies them, so the builder can go on or be reused. PathEffect Turns one path into another before it is filled or stroked: dashes, rounded corners, trimming, jitter, shapes stamped along the path, hatching. Effects are immutable, so one can be shared and reused; Then(PathEffect) and Plus(PathEffect) combine them. Apply one with Apply(PathEffect), or set it on Effect to have the canvas apply it before stroking. The set is Skia's: dash, corner, trim, discrete, 1D path, 2D line and 2D path effects, composed and summed. PathMeasure Measures a path: the length of each contour, and the point, direction and pieces at any distance along it. Lengths are exact to about 1e-4 units, curves included: each curve's length is integrated by adaptive Gauss–Legendre quadrature, and a distance is turned back into a point on the curve by Newton steps, so long curves do not gather the errors of a flattened outline. Contours of zero length are left out, as Skia's SkContourMeasureIter leaves them. Measuring is done once, here; the queries are cheap and safe from many threads. Picture Recorded canvas calls, from a PictureRecorder or Load(Stream, EgamiContext?): replay them on any canvas with DrawPicture(Picture, Matrix3x2?, Paint?, bool) or Playback(Canvas), fill shapes with them through a PicturePaint, render them with ToRaster<TPixel>(float, CanvasOptions?, EgamiContext?), or keep them in an .egdr file with Save(Stream). Replay is always vector, so a picture stays sharp at any scale. Immutable, and safe to replay on several threads and canvases at once. PicturePaint A Picture as a paint: a tiling pattern, the shape of PDF's and SVG's tiling patterns and Skia's picture shader. The Tile rectangle of the picture, in its own coordinates, is repeated by TileX and TileY under LocalMatrix and the canvas transform. The raster backend renders one tile at the device scale the paint is drawn at and keeps it with the picture, so a pattern stays sharp when zoomed and is rendered once for repeated fills at one scale. A tile is at most 4096 pixels a side. PictureRecorder A canvas that records instead of picture: every hook call is kept with its arguments, and Finish() returns them as an immutable Picture to replay on any canvas, at any scale, as often as needed, as Skia's SkPictureRecorder. Any code that draws on a Canvas can draw into it. Paths, paints, images and nested pictures are kept by reference: images must not change while the picture is in use. RadialGradient A gradient in circles around a center: t is the distance from Center divided by Radius. RasterCanvas<TPixel> The raster backend: a canvas that draws into a raster's pixels, with exact-area antialiasing, blended through Egami's Compositor in the pixel type's own precision. A clip that is a pixel-aligned rectangle stays a rectangle; any other clip becomes a coverage mask over the clip's bounds. A call whose area exceeds 256 KiB of destination rows spreads its rows over up to MaxParallelism cores, with the same pixels at any core count. A layer from SaveLayer(LayerOptions?) is premultiplied in the raster's class (PremulRgba8 for 8-bit rasters, PremulRgbaF32 for deeper ones) and covers only its bounds inside the clip, grown by its filter's reach; its memory comes from the raster's EgamiContext and is released at Restore(). ShadowOptions The light and colors of DrawShadow(Path, ShadowOptions?), after Skia's shadow model (the Material Design one): a shape lifted Elevation above the canvas casts an ambient shadow, blurred by its height, and a spot shadow from a round light at LightPosition, moved away from the light and blurred by the light's size. SoftMask A mask made by drawing, as a PDF soft mask: Draw runs on a canvas of its own with the layer's transform and clip, and its alpha, or its luminosity over Backdrop, through the optional Transfer curve, multiplies the layer. A luminosity mask of a white shape on black shows the layer only inside the shape. SolidPaint One color everywhere, with straight alpha. The color keeps float precision, so float and 16-bit targets get it in full; values outside 0 to 1 are kept on the paint, and the blend clamps them as Egami's Compositor does. Stroke How a path is outlined: the pen's width, caps, joins and miter limit. The settings travel with the drawing call as data, so a vector backend can write them as they are (PDF's w, J, j and M). The pen is applied in the canvas's local space and then transformed, so a non-uniform scale gives an elliptical pen, as in PDF, SVG and Skia. SvgPathException Thrown by ParseSvg(ReadOnlySpan<char>, FillRule, bool) when SVG path data breaks the grammar. SvgPathFormat How ToSvg(SvgPathFormat?) writes SVG path data. SweepGradient A gradient around a center, as Skia's sweep gradient and CSS's conic-gradient: t goes from 0 at StartAngle to 1 at EndAngle, in degrees clockwise (on a y-down screen) from the positive x axis. TextOnPathOptions How ShapeOnPath(Font, string, Path, TextOnPathOptions?) lays text along a path. Structs CornerRadii The x and y radius of each corner of a RoundRect, clockwise from the top-left. A radius below 0 counts as 0, and a corner with either radius 0 is square. GradientStop One color of a gradient at a position along it, from 0 (the start) to 1 (the end). Two stops at the same offset make a hard edge: the later one applies from that offset on. A gradient whose first stop is after 0 or whose last is before 1 repeats the nearest stop's color to the end, as CSS does. MaskBlur A Gaussian blur of a shape's coverage before the paint is applied, as Skia's blur mask filter: Sigma is in device pixels, so it does not scale with the canvas transform. Set it as Blur. Egami blurs with its fast blur; an axis-aligned rectangle with Normal is computed exactly from the error function, which is faster still. RectF A rectangle in float pixels, y down: the left edge at X, the top at Y. A width or height of 0 or less makes it empty. Pixel (0, 0) covers the square from (0, 0) to (1, 1), so a rectangle with whole-number edges covers whole pixels. RoundRect A rectangle with an x and y radius per corner. Radii that would overlap are scaled down together, as CSS and Skia do: every radius is multiplied by the smallest ratio of a side's length to the sum of the two radii along it, when that ratio is below 1. A radius below 0 counts as 0, and a corner with either radius 0 is square. SpriteTransform A sprite's placement in DrawAtlas(Raster, ReadOnlySpan<SpriteTransform>, ReadOnlySpan<RectF>, ReadOnlySpan<RgbaF32>, BlendMode, SamplingOptions?, RectF?, Paint?), as Skia's RSXform: a rotation with a uniform scale, then a move. A point (x, y) of the sprite, measured from its source rectangle's top-left corner, goes to (ScaleCos·x − ScaleSin·y + Tx, ScaleSin·x + ScaleCos·y + Ty). Interfaces IColorGlyphRenderer Draws color glyphs of a format Egami.Drawing does not draw itself, such as the SVG documents of an OpenType SVG table (Egami.Svg's SvgGlyphRenderer). Set on ColorGlyphRenderer, it is asked first for every glyph whose font has that format, except where the font has a COLR version 1 glyph, so the order is COLR v1, the renderer, COLR v0, sbix, CBDT, then the outline. Enums AnnotationKind What an Annotation marks, as Skia's annotations do. Antialiasing How a canvas antialiases shapes. BlurStyle How a MaskBlur keeps or removes the blurred shape's inside and outside, as Skia's blur styles. ClipOp Whether a clip keeps what is inside a shape or what is outside it. FillRule Which points a filled path covers, from how often its outline winds around them. HueMethod Which way around the hue circle an Oklch gradient goes between two stops, as CSS Color 4's hue interpolation methods. InterpolationSpace The color space a gradient's stops are mixed in. LatticeCellKind What a cell of a Lattice draws. LcdSampling How LCD text samples a glyph before filtering. LineCap How the ends of an open stroked contour look. LineJoin How a stroke turns the corner where two segments meet. MeshMode How a Mesh reads its vertices (or its indices, when it has them) as triangles. NoisePaintKind The kind of noise a NoisePaint makes. Overprint Which plates a paint prints on an ink canvas, as PDF's overprint; see Overprint. PatchKind Which surface a Patch is: its boundary only, or a full tensor-product net. PathDirection The direction a shape's outline runs, on a y-down screen. PathOp How Op(Path, PathOp, float) and Combine(IEnumerable<Path>, PathOp, float) combine the areas of two paths: Skia's five operations. PathVerb One drawing command of a Path; the comment on each says how many points it takes. PixelGeometry The order of a display's color subpixels, which LCD text edging needs to know. PixelOffset Where a canvas puts its pixel centres, for paths and unhinted text: GDI+'s PixelOffsetMode. PointMode How DrawPoints(PointMode, ReadOnlySpan<Vector2>, Stroke, Paint) reads its points. RoundRectKind What a RoundRect reduces to, so backends and the rasterizer can take a shortcut. SoftMaskKind Which value of a soft mask's drawing becomes the mask, as PDF's soft mask subtypes. StampStyle How Stamp(Path, float, float, StampStyle) places its shape along a path. TextAnchor Where text on a path is anchored at its start point, as SVG's text-anchor. TextPathSide Which side of a path text stands on. TileMode What a gradient or an image paint does past its ends or edges, as Skia's tile modes. VerticalAlign Where DrawText(string, RectF, ParagraphStyle, VerticalAlign) puts a paragraph across its lines, in a rectangle taller (or, for vertical lines, wider) than the lines. Delegates PlaceholderPainter Draws a placeholder's content where DrawTextLayout(TextLayout, Vector2, RectF?, PlaceholderPainter?) left room for it.

api/Egami.EgamiContext.html.summary: Class EgamiContext Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll Every setting that is not specific to one call: where memory comes from, how many threads an operation may use, and the safety limits. Contexts are immutable and safe to share. Change one with a with expression. public sealed record EgamiContext : IEquatable<EgamiContext> Inheritance object EgamiContext Implements IEquatable<EgamiContext> Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Extension Methods ExtendedContextExtensions.WithExtendedFormats(EgamiContext) ExtendedContextExtensions.WithFarbfeld(EgamiContext) ExtendedContextExtensions.WithPcx(EgamiContext) ExtendedContextExtensions.WithSgi(EgamiContext) ExtendedContextExtensions.WithSunRaster(EgamiContext) ExtendedContextExtensions.WithWbmp(EgamiContext) ExtendedContextExtensions.WithXbm(EgamiContext) ExtendedContextExtensions.WithXpm(EgamiContext) HeicContextExtensions.WithHeic(EgamiContext) Examples var context = EgamiContext.Default with { Limits = SafetyLimits.Default with { MaxPixels = 100_000_000 }, MaxParallelism = 4, }; Properties Default Gets the context used when a call passes none. The first read fixes it: SetDefault(EgamiContext) works only before that. public static EgamiContext Default { get; } Property Value EgamiContext DiagnosticLevel Gets the lowest level Diagnostics receives. Defaults to Warning; events below it are never built. public DiagnosticLevel DiagnosticLevel { get; init; } Property Value DiagnosticLevel Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value set is not a defined level. Diagnostics Gets the handler that receives Egami's warnings and notable decisions, or null (the default) for none, which costs nothing. It runs inline, possibly on several decode threads at once, so it must be quick and thread-safe. An exception it throws fails the call, which turns warnings into errors. Warnings a load raises arrive in Warnings order as the call ends; Info and Debug events arrive as they happen. One id is delivered at most 10 times per call, then once more as a count of the rest. public Action<EgamiDiagnostic>? Diagnostics { get; init; } Property Value Action<EgamiDiagnostic> Examples // With Microsoft.Extensions.Logging: one line at startup sends every call's warnings to the app's log, with the id as // a property to filter and count on. Egami itself has no logging dependency. EgamiContext.SetDefault(new EgamiContext { Diagnostics = d => logger.Log(d.Level.ToLogLevel(), "{Source} {Id} at {Offset}: {Message}", d.Source, d.Id, d.Offset, d.Message), }); Formats Gets the registered formats, in detection order. Defaults to PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP, QOI, PNM, TIFF, JBIG2, JPEG 2000 and TGA. public IReadOnlyList<FormatInfo> Formats { get; init; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<FormatInfo> Limits Gets the safety limits applied when reading. Defaults to Default. public SafetyLimits Limits { get; init; } Property Value SafetyLimits Exceptions ArgumentNullException The value set is null. MaxParallelism Gets the most threads one operation may use. 1 means fully sequential. Defaults to the processor count. public int MaxParallelism { get; init; } Property Value int Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value set is less than 1. Memory Gets the source of all pixel memory. Defaults to Shared. public IPixelMemorySource Memory { get; init; } Property Value IPixelMemorySource Exceptions ArgumentNullException The value set is null. Methods SetDefault(EgamiContext) Replaces Default, once, at startup, so that format plugins, memory sources and limits apply to every call that passes no context. public static void SetDefault(EgamiContext context) Parameters context EgamiContext The context to use as the default. Exceptions InvalidOperationException Default was already read or set. StartDiagnostics() Starts reporting for one call outside Egami's own loads and saves, such as a video decode or a plug-in's own entry point, with the same DiagnosticLevel filter and per-id cap. Dispose it when the call ends. public DiagnosticReporter StartDiagnostics() Returns DiagnosticReporter A reporter for the call; a shared one that does nothing when Diagnostics is null. Examples // A decoder outside Egami (a video demuxer, a format plug-in's own entry point) reports through the same handler, with the // same level filter and the same cap of 10 per id per call. Dispose the reporter when the call ends. using (DiagnosticReporter diagnostics = context.StartDiagnostics()) { if (diagnostics.IsEnabled(DiagnosticLevel.Warning)) { diagnostics.Report(DiagnosticLevel.Warning, "Avi.IndexRebuilt", "The index was missing; it was rebuilt from the frames.", offset: 4096); } diagnostics.Report(DiagnosticLevel.Info, "Mjpeg.DhtInserted", "Frames have no Huffman tables; the standard ones were used."); } WithFormat(FormatInfo) Returns a copy of this context with format registered. A format with the same name is replaced in place; otherwise the new format is detected last. public EgamiContext WithFormat(FormatInfo format) Parameters format FormatInfo The format to add. Returns EgamiContext The new context.

api/Egami.Fonts.Font.html.summary: Struct Font Namespace Egami.Fonts Assembly Egami.Fonts.dll A typeface at a size: the em in canvas units (pixels on a raster, points on a PDF page). Scales the face's font-unit metrics and turns text into a positioned GlyphRun. public readonly record struct Font : IEquatable<Font> Implements IEquatable<Font> Inherited Members ValueType.Equals(object) ValueType.GetHashCode() ValueType.ToString() object.Equals(object, object) object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Extension Methods FontExtensions.GetGlyphPath(Font, ushort) FontExtensions.GetTextPath(Font, string, Vector2) FontExtensions.ShapeOnPath(Font, string, Path, TextOnPathOptions?) Examples // A caption on a photo: white text with a dark shadow, its baseline 24 pixels above the bottom. using Raster<Rgba8> photo = Raster.Create(640, 360, new Rgba8(90, 120, 160, 255)); var font = new Font(Typeface.FromFile(FontFile), 28); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = photo.CreateCanvas()) { var origin = new Vector2(24, photo.Height - 24); canvas.DrawText("Lofoten, March", origin + new Vector2(2, 2), font, new Rgba8(0, 0, 0, 160)); canvas.DrawText("Lofoten, March", origin, font, Rgba8.White); } Remarks There is no DPI: a 12-unit font on a raster is 12 pixels per em, and the canvas transform scales it like any other drawing. Use FromPoints(Typeface, float, float) to size from points at a resolution. default(Font) has no typeface: its Typeface is null, its Scale 0, and the members that need the face (metrics, advances, shaping and measuring) throw InvalidOperationException. Create fonts with the constructor or FromPoints(Typeface, float, float). Constructors Font(Typeface, float) Initializes a font. public Font(Typeface typeface, float size) Parameters typeface Typeface The face. size float The em size in canvas units, finite and at least 0. Exceptions ArgumentNullException typeface is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException size is negative, infinite or NaN. Properties AllowSynthesis Gets whether Synthesis is applied. Defaults to true. public bool AllowSynthesis { get; init; } Property Value bool ColorGlyphs Gets whether color glyphs (COLR, sbix, CBDT) draw in color; false draws every glyph's outline in the paint. Defaults to true. public bool ColorGlyphs { get; init; } Property Value bool Edging Gets how glyph edges become pixels on a raster. Defaults to Antialias. public FontEdging Edging { get; init; } Property Value FontEdging Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is not defined. EffectiveTypeface Gets the face glyphs are drawn and measured from: Typeface, or with OpticalSizing on a face with an opsz axis it does not set, the face at opsz = Size. A PDF writer embeds this face. public Typeface EffectiveTypeface { get; } Property Value Typeface Exceptions InvalidOperationException The font is default(Font), which has no typeface. Embolden Gets how far outlines grow on every side, in canvas units at this size (pixels on a raster): 0.15 makes each stem 0.3 pixels heavier. Defaults to 0. Applied as synthetic bold is, with round joins, on top of it; advances do not change. Drawn, measured as ink and returned by glyph paths. public float Embolden { get; init; } Property Value float Examples // A little more weight without a bold face: outlines grow 0.2 pixels on each side, advances stay as they are. var heavier = new Font(face, 14) { Embolden = 0.2f }; // Darkening for thin stems only: it fades out as the face's stems grow past 1.667 pixels. var caption = new Font(face, 9) { StemDarkening = true }; using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = image.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.DrawText("Slightly heavier", new Vector2(8, 24), heavier, Rgba8.Black); canvas.DrawText("A darkened caption", new Vector2(8, 48), caption, Rgba8.Black); } Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is negative, infinite or NaN. Extents Gets the face's extents at this size, y up. public FontExtents Extents { get; } Property Value FontExtents Exceptions InvalidOperationException The font is default(Font), which has no typeface. Hinting Gets how outlines are fitted to the pixel grid on a raster. Defaults to None. public FontHinting Hinting { get; init; } Property Value FontHinting Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is not defined. HintingTarget Gets the rasterizer Full hints for and GridFitted measures with. Defaults to GdiPlus. public TrueTypeTarget HintingTarget { get; init; } Property Value TrueTypeTarget Examples // The font's own TrueType instructions, run for GDI+, with its hinted advances: glyphs on whole pixels, spacing as Windows // lays out ClearType text. Together with GDI+'s filter, sampling and gamma (1 + TextContrast/10 = 1.4), this is the closest // Egami gets to System.Drawing's ClearTypeGridFit. var label = new Font(face, 16) { Hinting = FontHinting.Full, HintingTarget = TrueTypeTarget.GdiPlus, Metrics = FontMetrics.GridFitted, Edging = FontEdging.Lcd, }; var gdiPlus = new CanvasOptions { PixelGeometry = PixelGeometry.RgbHorizontal, LcdFilter = LcdFilter.Gdi, LcdSampling = LcdSampling.Gdi, TextGamma = 1.4f, }; using (RasterCanvas<Rgb8> canvas = button.CreateCanvas(gdiPlus)) { // Measuring uses the same hinted advances, so centring is exact. float width = label.MeasureText("Start the course").Advance; canvas.DrawText("Start the course", new Vector2(MathF.Round((200 - width) / 2), 26), label, Rgba8.White); } Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is not defined. Kerning Gets whether pair kerning is applied when shaping. Defaults to true. public bool Kerning { get; init; } Property Value bool LineHeight Gets the distance from one baseline to the next at this size. public float LineHeight { get; } Property Value float Exceptions InvalidOperationException The font is default(Font), which has no typeface. Metrics Gets where advances come from: Design (the default) or GridFitted, the hinted advances at the font's size rounded to a whole number of pixels per em, with whole-pixel glyph origins when drawn. api/Egami.Fonts.FontEdging.html.summary: Enum FontEdging Namespace Egami.Fonts Assembly Egami.Fonts.dll How a glyph's edges are turned into pixels. public enum FontEdging Fields Alias = 1 One bit per pixel: a pixel is covered when its centre is inside the outline (nonzero rule). Antialias = 0 Grayscale antialiasing: each pixel covered by the share of its area inside the outline. Lcd = 2 Subpixel (LCD) antialiasing: coverage at three times the resolution along the canvas's pixel geometry, low-pass filtered and blended per color channel. Drawn only onto an opaque 8-bit RGB target with a known pixel geometry and a solid source-over paint; anything else falls back to Antialias with one diagnostic per canvas. Never for color glyphs. Examples // Small text for a screen: light hinting (vertical only), quarter-pixel origins (the default) and, for an RGB display // the image will not leave, LCD edging. var screen = new Font(face, 13) { Hinting = FontHinting.Light, Edging = FontEdging.Lcd }; using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = image.CreateCanvas(new CanvasOptions { PixelGeometry = PixelGeometry.RgbHorizontal })) { canvas.DrawText("Crisp caption", new Vector2(8, 24), screen, Rgba8.Black); // A face matched for bold italic it lacks is emboldened and slanted, unless AllowSynthesis is off. var synthetic = new Font(face, 13) { Synthesis = FontSynthesis.Bold | FontSynthesis.Italic }; canvas.DrawText("Synthetic bold italic", new Vector2(8, 48), synthetic, Rgba8.Black); }

api/Egami.Fonts.FontEmbedding.html.summary: Enum FontEmbedding Namespace Egami.Fonts Assembly Egami.Fonts.dll The embedding permissions a face declares in its OS/2 fsType field. Egami reports them and never enforces them; a caller that embeds fonts, such as a PDF writer, decides what to do. [Flags] public enum FontEmbedding Fields BitmapOnly = 512 Only bitmaps may be embedded, not outlines (bit 9). Editable = 8 The face may be embedded in documents that are edited (bit 3). api/Egami.Fonts.FontMetrics.html.title: Enum FontMetrics | Egami
api/Egami.Fonts.FontMetrics.html.summary: Enum FontMetrics Namespace Egami.Fonts Assembly Egami.Fonts.dll Where a font's advances come from. public enum FontMetrics Fields Compatible = 2 GDI's compatible widths: the advances black-and-white hinting gives, from the hdmx table when it has the size, else the rounded design advance where the LTSH table says the glyph scales linearly, else the glyph's instructions run for a monochrome rasterizer. Whole pixels, cached per face and size; faces that cannot be hinted keep their design advances, rounded. Glyph origins snap to whole pixels. Design = 0 The design advances, scaled: fractional pixels, the same at every size. GridFitted = 1 The hinted advances at a whole number of pixels per em: each glyph's right phantom point less its left after the font's instructions run for HintingTarget. Measuring and drawing both use them, and glyph origins snap to whole pixels. Faces that cannot be hinted keep their design advances, rounded. With GdiPlus these are the advances Graphics.DrawString draws with its default StringFormat. GridFittedToDesign = 3 GridFitted advances, except that a run they would make more than 2.1 pixels wider than designed keeps its design advances, rounded up to sixteenths of a pixel, as Graphics.DrawString lays out such lines with StringFormat.GenericTypographic (glyph origins still snap to whole pixels). Examples // The font's own TrueType instructions, run for GDI+, with its hinted advances: glyphs on whole pixels, spacing as Windows // lays out ClearType text. Together with GDI+'s filter, sampling and gamma (1 + TextContrast/10 = 1.4), this is the closest // Egami gets to System.Drawing's ClearTypeGridFit. var label = new Font(face, 16) { Hinting = FontHinting.Full, HintingTarget = TrueTypeTarget.GdiPlus, Metrics = FontMetrics.GridFitted, Edging = FontEdging.Lcd, }; var gdiPlus = new CanvasOptions { PixelGeometry = PixelGeometry.RgbHorizontal, LcdFilter = LcdFilter.Gdi, LcdSampling = LcdSampling.Gdi, TextGamma = 1.4f, }; using (RasterCanvas<Rgb8> canvas = button.CreateCanvas(gdiPlus)) { // Measuring uses the same hinted advances, so centring is exact. float width = label.MeasureText("Start the course").Advance; canvas.DrawText("Start the course", new Vector2(MathF.Round((200 - width) / 2), 26), label, Rgba8.White); }

api/Egami.Fonts.Layout.html.title: Namespace Egami.Fonts.Layout | Egami
api/Egami.Fonts.Layout.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Fonts.Layout Classes DecorationShape One decoration line over a decorated stretch of one text line: an underline, overline or line-through at one position and thickness for the whole stretch (the lowest underline and thickest line among its fonts, as CSS), cut where glyphs cross an underline or overline when SkipInk is Auto. LayoutRun A piece of a line: glyphs of one font and bidi level, or a placeholder, tab or break. LineBreaks Finds where lines may break: Unicode's line breaking algorithm (UAX #14, Unicode 17.0) from Egami's own tables, with CSS Text 3's word-break and line-break switches. No shaping is involved, and there are no dictionaries: Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break only at spaces and zero width spaces. LineFlow Lays a paragraph out one line at a time, each at its own width, so text can flow across columns and pages or around images; Layout(float) is built on it. Not thread-safe; make one per flow. Paragraph A paragraph of styled text, prepared once to be laid out at any width: styles resolved, bidi levels and break opportunities found, text itemized into runs and each run shaped. Immutable and safe to share between threads. ParagraphStyle How a paragraph is laid out: its default text style, direction, alignment, line breaking, line filling, hyphens, ellipsis and line limits, line box rules, tabs and writing mode. The defaults follow CSS: start-aligned, greedy filling, normal line height, tab stops every 8 spaces, horizontal lines. RichText Text with styles: a string, the StyleSpans over it (sorted, never overlapping) and the Placeholders for its object replacement characters, in order. Immutable; build one with RichTextBuilder. RichTextBuilder Builds a RichText: Push(TextStyle) a style, Append(string) text, Pop() back to the enclosing style. Styles nest: a pushed style's unset fields come from the one it is pushed on, and the result has one flat span per stretch of equal style. Strut A minimum line box every line has, from a font and a line height (CSS's strut), or with Force the exact line box, for line grids in forms and columns. TextDecoration Lines drawn with text (CSS Text Decoration 4). TextLayout A paragraph laid out at a width: its lines of glyph runs and the size of its layout box. Positions are in canvas units relative to the box's top-left corner, y down; nothing is rounded to pixels. Immutable and safe to share between threads. TextLine One line of a laid-out paragraph: the text it holds, its line box and its runs in visual order. Coordinates are the layout box's, or for a line from a LineFlow, the line's own box with its top at 0. TextStyle How a stretch of text looks. Every field is optional: an unset field takes the enclosing builder style's, then the paragraph's DefaultStyle, then Egami's default (16 pixels, black, normal line height, no decoration). Fields that change shaping (fonts, size, style, variations, language, features, letter spacing) split a paragraph into separately shaped runs; the others (colors, paints, background, decoration, shadows) never do, so a color change inside a ligature keeps the ligature. Structs Caret Where a caret is drawn: the primary segment, and at a bidi boundary, where the position touches text of both directions, a secondary segment at the other text's edge. CaretLine A caret segment across the line: vertical in horizontal layouts, horizontal in vertical ones. DecorationSegment A piece of a decoration line along a text line: its left and right x. LineBreak A place where a line may or must end. LineBreakEnumerator Enumerates line break opportunities; get one from Enumerate(ReadOnlySpan<char>, LineBreakOptions). LineBreakOptions How text may break into lines, as CSS Text 3 sets it: word-break, overflow-wrap, line-break and the content language. The default is CSS's default: Unicode's line breaking algorithm (UAX #14) with breaks before small kana, as browsers break. LineHeight The height a run asks of its line box (CSS line-height): Normal from the font's metrics, a Multiple(float) of the font size or an Absolute(float) height. The extra over the font's ascent and descent is split half above and half below. Placeholder An inline box laid out with the text, such as an icon or an image, which the caller draws: it stands for an object replacement character (U+FFFC) in the text, so bidi, line breaking and indexes treat it as one character. StyleSpan A text style over a stretch of a RichText, in UTF-16 units. TabStop An explicit tab stop. TextPosition A caret position: a UTF-16 index at a grapheme cluster boundary and the side it belongs to. TextShadow A shadow under text: the glyphs and decorations again, moved and blurred (CSS text-shadow). Interfaces ITextPaint A paint that Egami.Fonts carries for text but never reads: Egami.Drawing's Paint implements it, so gradients, images and blend modes reach text drawn from a layout without Egami.Fonts depending on the drawing package. Enums CaretMove How MoveCaret(TextPosition, CaretMove, float) moves a caret. KashidaLevel How far Kashida lengthens a word, as Word's three kashida justifications. LayoutRunKind What a LayoutRun holds. LineBreakStrictness How strictly line breaks follow Chinese and Japanese rules (CSS line-break): breaks before small kana, hyphens, iteration marks and some punctuation. LineFill How lines are filled. LineHeightKind How a LineHeight is given. OverflowWrap Whether a piece wider than its line may break anywhere (CSS overflow-wrap). PlaceholderAlignment How a Placeholder sits on its line. SelectionHeight How tall selection rectangles are. TabAlignment How text aligns on a tab stop. TextAffinity Which side of a position a caret belongs to where one index has two places: at a line wrap or a bidi boundary. TextAlign How lines align in their width (CSS text-align). TextAlignLast How the last line, and lines before a hard break, align (CSS text-align-last). TextDecorationLines Which decoration lines are drawn. TextDecorationSkipInk Whether underlines and overlines skip glyph ink. TextDecorationStyle How decoration lines are drawn. TextJustify How justified lines stretch (CSS text-justify). TextOrientation How characters stand in vertical lines (CSS text-orientation). WordBreak Where breaks may fall inside words (CSS word-break). WritingMode Whether lines run horizontally or vertically (CSS writing-mode).

api/Egami.Fonts.Shaping.TextShaper.html.title: Class TextShaper | Egami
api/Egami.Fonts.Shaping.TextShaper.html.summary: Class TextShaper Namespace Egami.Fonts.Shaping Assembly Egami.Fonts.dll OpenType text shaping in managed code: a run of text in one font becomes positioned glyphs with GSUB substitutions, GPOS positioning and the script rules HarfBuzz applies. public static class TextShaper Inheritance object TextShaper Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // One run, one font, as HarfBuzz's hb_shape: ligatures, kerning and marks from the font's GSUB and GPOS. var font = new Font(face, 24); var glyphs = new GlyphBuffer(); string text = "office"; TextShaper.ShapeRun(text, 0, text.Length, font, new RunProperties { Script = Script.Latin }, glyphs); for (int i = 0; i < glyphs.Count; i++) { ushort id = glyphs.GlyphIds[i]; int cluster = glyphs.Clusters[i]; // index in text the glyph came from GlyphPosition position = glyphs.Positions[i]; // in the font's units (pixels here) bool breakable = (glyphs.Flags[i] & GlyphFlags.UnsafeToBreak) == 0; } float width = glyphs.Advance; Remarks Stateless and thread-safe; each call needs its own GlyphBuffer. Methods Shape(string, Font, ShapingOptions?) Shapes text: splits it into lines at hard breaks, resolves each line's bidi levels, splits it into runs of one level, script, span and font (falling back per grapheme cluster as Fallback says), shapes each run as ShapeRun(ReadOnlySpan<char>, int, int, Font, RunProperties, GlyphBuffer) does and orders the runs for display. Control characters other than the breaks (a tab, for one) give no glyph. Nothing wraps. public static ShapedText Shape(string text, Font font, ShapingOptions? options = null) Parameters text string The text. font Font The font and size. options ShapingOptions The direction, language, script, features, fallback, cluster level and spans; null for Default. Returns ShapedText The shaped lines; an empty text gives one empty line. Examples // Whole text: lines at hard breaks, bidi levels, script runs, fallback fonts, runs in display order. var font = new Font(face, 24); var options = new ShapingOptions { Fallback = new FontFallback(fonts.Families) }; ShapedText shaped = TextShaper.Shape("Shalom: \u05E9\u05DC\u05D5\u05DD!", font, options); float x = 0; foreach (ShapedRun run in shaped.Lines[0].Runs) { GlyphRun glyphs = run.ToGlyphRun(new System.Numerics.Vector2(x, 0), shaped.Text); // what a canvas draws x += run.Advance; } Exceptions ArgumentNullException text is null, or font has no typeface. ArgumentOutOfRangeException A span is not inside the text, or two spans overlap. ShapeRun(ReadOnlySpan<char>, int, int, Font, RunProperties, GlyphBuffer) Shapes one run, as HarfBuzz's hb_shape: no bidi, script or font splitting; the run is one script in one direction. Clusters are UTF-16 indexes into text; the characters around the run are context for joining scripts. public static void ShapeRun(ReadOnlySpan<char> text, int start, int length, Font font, RunProperties properties, GlyphBuffer buffer) Parameters text ReadOnlySpan<char> The text the run is part of. start int The index of the run's first UTF-16 unit. length int The number of UTF-16 units in the run. font Font The font and size; positions are in its units. properties RunProperties The run's script, language, direction, features and cluster level. buffer GlyphBuffer Receives the glyphs in visual order. Exceptions ArgumentNullException buffer is null, or font has no typeface. ArgumentOutOfRangeException The run is not inside text.

api/Egami.Fonts.Shaping.html.title: Namespace Egami.Fonts.Shaping | Egami
api/Egami.Fonts.Shaping.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Fonts.Shaping Classes FontFallback Where characters the font does not map go: the caller's font families first, matched to the font's style, then a resolver. Without fallback (None, the default) shaping depends only on the fonts passed, never on the machine. GlyphBuffer A reusable buffer of shaped glyphs: glyph ids, the UTF-16 index of the text each came from, glyph flags and positions, in visual order. ShapeRun(ReadOnlySpan<char>, int, int, Font, RunProperties, GlyphBuffer) fills it; reuse one buffer for many runs to avoid allocations. OpenTypeLayout What a face's OpenType layout tables (GSUB and GPOS) offer: the scripts, language systems and features they list, and the glyphs GSUB can produce from a set of glyphs. A table whose structure is damaged is left out whole, as the shaper leaves it out. ShapedLine One line of ShapedText: its range and its runs in visual order. ShapedRun A run of a ShapedLine: one font, one bidi level, one script, one language, and its glyphs. ShapedText Text shaped by Shape(string, Font, ShapingOptions?): one ShapedLine per line between hard breaks, each with its runs in visual order. Nothing wraps. ShapingOptions How Shape(string, Font, ShapingOptions?) shapes text: the paragraph direction, the language, script and features of the whole text, the fonts that take characters the font lacks, the cluster level, and styled spans. SystemFontFallback The installed-font resolver of System: fixed families for each script on Windows, macOS and Linux (Segoe UI Emoji, Apple Color Emoji or Noto Color Emoji for emoji; the language picks Japanese, Chinese or Korean faces for Han), then any installed face that maps the cluster, found once and remembered for the process. TextShaper OpenType text shaping in managed code: a run of text in one font becomes positioned glyphs with GSUB substitutions, GPOS positioning and the script rules HarfBuzz applies. Structs FontFeature An OpenType feature setting: a feature tag, a value and the range of UTF-16 units it applies to, in HarfBuzz's model. A value of 0 turns a feature off (such as default ligatures), 1 turns it on, and higher values pick an alternate. GlyphPosition How a shaped glyph moves the pen and sits relative to it, in the units of the Font it was shaped with. RunProperties What one run of text is shaped as: its script, language, direction, features and cluster level. TextSpan A range of text with its own font, language or features, for Spans. Interfaces IFontFallbackResolver Finds a face for a grapheme cluster no listed font maps, such as SystemFontFallback. Enums ClusterLevel Which characters a glyph's cluster covers, as HarfBuzz's cluster levels. GlyphFlags What a shaped glyph says about breaking the text next to it, as HarfBuzz's glyph flags.

api/Egami.Fonts.SubsetFormat.html.title: Enum SubsetFormat | Egami
api/Egami.Fonts.SubsetFormat.html.summary: Enum SubsetFormat Namespace Egami.Fonts Assembly Egami.Fonts.dll What FontSubsetter writes. public enum SubsetFormat Fields Auto = 0 The input's own kind: TrueType for 'glyf' faces, OpenType CFF for CFF faces, bare CFF for a bare CFF face. BareCff = 3 A bare CID-keyed CFF stream with an identity charset (CID = new glyph id), as PDF embeds for CIDFontType0C. Needs CFF outlines. OpenTypeCff = 2 An OpenType font with a CFF table (.otf), as PDF embeds in FontFile3 with subtype OpenType. Needs CFF outlines. TrueType = 1 A TrueType font (.ttf), as PDF embeds in FontFile2. Needs a face with TrueType outlines. Examples // Keep only the glyphs a page uses, as a PDF writer embeds them: renumbered from 0, with the map to write the text with. GlyphRun run = new Font(face, 12).Shape("Invoice 2026-10"); FontSubset subset = FontSubsetter.Subset(face, run.Glyphs.ToArray(), new SubsetOptions { FontNamePrefix = "ABCDEF+", KeepCmap = false, }); byte[] fontFile2 = subset.Data.ToArray(); ushort first = subset.GlyphMap[run.Glyphs[0]]; // The face's embedding permissions are reported, never enforced: the writer decides. bool restricted = face.Embedding.HasFlag(FontEmbedding.Restricted);

api/Egami.Fonts.SubsetOptions.html.summary: Class SubsetOptions Namespace Egami.Fonts Assembly Egami.Fonts.dll How Subset(Typeface, IEnumerable<ushort>, SubsetOptions?) writes a subset. public sealed record SubsetOptions : IEquatable<SubsetOptions> Inheritance object SubsetOptions Implements IEquatable<SubsetOptions> Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // Keep only the glyphs a page uses, as a PDF writer embeds them: renumbered from 0, with the map to write the text with. GlyphRun run = new Font(face, 12).Shape("Invoice 2026-10"); FontSubset subset = FontSubsetter.Subset(face, run.Glyphs.ToArray(), new SubsetOptions { FontNamePrefix = "ABCDEF+", KeepCmap = false, }); byte[] fontFile2 = subset.Data.ToArray(); ushort first = subset.GlyphMap[run.Glyphs[0]]; // The face's embedding permissions are reported, never enforced: the writer decides. bool restricted = face.Embedding.HasFlag(FontEmbedding.Restricted); Properties Default Gets the default options: the input's format, dense renumbering, a character map, no extra tables, no name prefix. public static SubsetOptions Default { get; } Property Value SubsetOptions FontNamePrefix Gets the prefix put before the PostScript and CFF font names, such as the six-letter PDF subset tag "ABCDEF+". public string? FontNamePrefix { get; init; } Property Value string Format Gets the output format. Defaults to Auto. public SubsetFormat Format { get; init; } Property Value SubsetFormat KeepCmap Gets whether a character map for the kept glyphs is written (sfnt output only; PDF CIDFontType2 needs none). Defaults to true. public bool KeepCmap { get; init; } Property Value bool KeepTables Gets tables copied unchanged, such as 'GSUB'; the caller answers for glyph ids inside them. public IReadOnlyList<FontTag> KeepTables { get; init; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<FontTag> LayoutClosure Gets whether the subset can be shaped again as the full face would be: the kept glyphs gain every glyph GSUB can substitute for them (GetClosure(IEnumerable<ushort>, IEnumerable<FontTag>?) with DefaultClosureFeatures), and GSUB, GPOS and GDEF are copied unchanged. Copied layout tables hold the old glyph ids, so this needs RetainGlyphIds and sfnt output. Defaults to false, as a PDF needs only the glyphs drawn. To follow other features, pass the glyphs of GetClosure(IEnumerable<ushort>, IEnumerable<FontTag>?) with them, and keep the three tables with KeepTables. public bool LayoutClosure { get; init; } Property Value bool Examples // Keep what the text's characters can become (ligatures, contextual forms) and the layout tables, so the subset shapes // the text as the full face does; the copied tables use the old glyph ids, so the ids are kept. ushort[] glyphs = [.. "office".Select(c => face.GetGlyph(c))]; FontSubset subset = FontSubsetter.Subset(face, glyphs, new SubsetOptions { RetainGlyphIds = true, LayoutClosure = true }); GlyphRun shaped = new Font(subset.ToTypeface(), 12).Shape("office"); Remarks The tables of a variable face are copied with their variation data, so in the static subset GPOS positions and feature variations are those of the default instance, whatever Variations says. RetainGlyphIds Gets whether glyphs keep their ids, with empty glyphs in the gaps, rather than being renumbered densely in ascending order. Defaults to false. public bool RetainGlyphIds { get; init; } Property Value bool Variations Gets the position a variable face's subset is written at, applied over the face's own position, or null (the default) for the face's position. A variable face's subset is always a static font: glyf with gvar's deltas applied and rounded, hmtx from the varied metrics, OS/2 and post with MVAR's values, CFF2 written as CFF with blends resolved, and the variation tables left out, so PDF viewers draw the position rather than the default instance. public IReadOnlyList<FontVariation>? api/Egami.Fonts.TrueTypeTarget.html.summary: Enum TrueTypeTarget Namespace Egami.Fonts Assembly Egami.Fonts.dll Which rasterizer the TrueType interpreter answers for: what GETINFO tells the font and how instructions are softened. public enum TrueTypeTarget Fields FreeType = 2 A FreeType-like target: version 40 with ClearType and subpixel positioning. Gdi = 1 GDI ClearType, as measured: version 42 with ClearType, compatible widths and symmetric rendering (GETINFO 0x46C2A). GdiPlus = 0 GDI+ with ClearTypeGridFit, as measured on Windows: rasterizer version 42 with ClearType (GETINFO 0x2C2A). Examples // The font's own TrueType instructions, run for GDI+, with its hinted advances: glyphs on whole pixels, spacing as Windows // lays out ClearType text. Together with GDI+'s filter, sampling and gamma (1 + TextContrast/10 = 1.4), this is the closest // Egami gets to System.Drawing's ClearTypeGridFit. var label = new Font(face, 16) { Hinting = FontHinting.Full, HintingTarget = TrueTypeTarget.GdiPlus, Metrics = FontMetrics.GridFitted, Edging = FontEdging.Lcd, }; var gdiPlus = new CanvasOptions { PixelGeometry = PixelGeometry.RgbHorizontal, LcdFilter = LcdFilter.Gdi, LcdSampling = LcdSampling.Gdi, TextGamma = 1.4f, }; using (RasterCanvas<Rgb8> canvas = button.CreateCanvas(gdiPlus)) { // Measuring uses the same hinted advances, so centring is exact. float width = label.MeasureText("Start the course").Advance; canvas.DrawText("Start the course", new Vector2(MathF.Round((200 - width) / 2), 26), label, Rgba8.White); }

api/Egami.Fonts.Unicode.TextDirection.ht.title: Enum TextDirection | Egami
api/Egami.Fonts.Unicode.TextDirection.ht.summary: Enum TextDirection Namespace Egami.Fonts.Unicode Assembly Egami.Fonts.dll The direction of a paragraph or a run of text. public enum TextDirection Fields Auto = 0 The paragraph direction follows the first strong character (UAX #9 rules P2 and P3), left to right when there is none. LeftToRight = 1 Left to right. RightToLeft = 2 Right to left. TopToBottom = 3 Top to bottom, for vertical runs; bidi treats it as left to right. Examples // A Hebrew word inside English text: three runs, the middle one drawn right to left. string text = "abc \u05D0\u05D1\u05D2 def"; using BidiResult result = Bidi.Resolve(text, TextDirection.Auto); int paragraph = result.ParagraphLevel; // 0: the first strong character is Latin foreach (BidiRun run in result.Reorder(0, result.Length)) { Console.WriteLine($"{run.Start}+{run.Length} {(run.IsRightToLeft ? "right to left" : "left to right")}"); }

api/Egami.Fonts.Unicode.TextSegment.html.summary: Struct TextSegment Namespace Egami.Fonts.Unicode Assembly Egami.Fonts.dll A range of UTF-16 units: a grapheme cluster, a word or a run. public readonly record struct TextSegment : IEquatable<TextSegment> Implements IEquatable<TextSegment> Inherited Members ValueType.Equals(object) ValueType.GetHashCode() ValueType.ToString() object.Equals(object, object) object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Examples // A family emoji is one grapheme cluster of eight UTF-16 units; "can't" is one word. string text = "\uD83D\uDC68\u200D\uD83D\uDC69\u200D\uD83D\uDC67 can't stop"; var graphemes = new List<TextSegment>(); foreach (TextSegment grapheme in TextSegmenter.Graphemes(text)) { graphemes.Add(grapheme); } var words = new List<string>(); foreach (TextSegment word in TextSegmenter.Words(text)) { words.Add(text.Substring(word.Start, word.Length)); } bool inside = TextSegmenter.IsGraphemeBoundary(text, 2); // false: inside the family Constructors TextSegment(int, int) A range of UTF-16 units: a grapheme cluster, a word or a run. public TextSegment(int Start, int Length) Parameters Start int The index of the first UTF-16 unit. Length int The number of UTF-16 units. Examples // A family emoji is one grapheme cluster of eight UTF-16 units; "can't" is one word. string text = "\uD83D\uDC68\u200D\uD83D\uDC69\u200D\uD83D\uDC67 can't stop"; var graphemes = new List<TextSegment>(); foreach (TextSegment grapheme in TextSegmenter.Graphemes(text)) { graphemes.Add(grapheme); } var words = new List<string>(); foreach (TextSegment word in TextSegmenter.Words(text)) { words.Add(text.Substring(word.Start, word.Length)); } bool inside = TextSegmenter.IsGraphemeBoundary(text, 2); // false: inside the family Properties End Gets the index just past the segment. public int End { get; } Property Value int Length The number of UTF-16 units. public int Length { get; init; } Property Value int Start The index of the first UTF-16 unit. public int Start { get; init; } Property Value int

api/Egami.Fonts.Unicode.TextSegmenter.ht.summary: Class TextSegmenter Namespace Egami.Fonts.Unicode Assembly Egami.Fonts.dll Text boundaries from UAX #29: extended grapheme clusters (what a reader sees as one character) and words, with Unicode's default rules and no dictionaries. public static class TextSegmenter Inheritance object TextSegmenter Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A family emoji is one grapheme cluster of eight UTF-16 units; "can't" is one word. string text = "\uD83D\uDC68\u200D\uD83D\uDC69\u200D\uD83D\uDC67 can't stop"; var graphemes = new List<TextSegment>(); foreach (TextSegment grapheme in TextSegmenter.Graphemes(text)) { graphemes.Add(grapheme); } var words = new List<string>(); foreach (TextSegment word in TextSegmenter.Words(text)) { words.Add(text.Substring(word.Start, word.Length)); } bool inside = TextSegmenter.IsGraphemeBoundary(text, 2); // false: inside the family Remarks Unpaired surrogates count as one character each. Enumerators walk the text once and allocate nothing. Methods Graphemes(ReadOnlySpan<char>) Enumerates the extended grapheme clusters of a text. public static GraphemeEnumerator Graphemes(ReadOnlySpan<char> text) Parameters text ReadOnlySpan<char> The text. IsGraphemeBoundary(ReadOnlySpan<char>, int) Gets whether an index is an extended grapheme cluster boundary. public static bool IsGraphemeBoundary(ReadOnlySpan<char> text, int index) Parameters text ReadOnlySpan<char> The text. index int An index from 0 to the text's length. Returns bool true at the start and end of the text and between clusters. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException index is negative or past the end. Words(ReadOnlySpan<char>) Enumerates the segments between word boundaries: words, and the spaces, punctuation and symbols between them, each as its own segment. public static WordEnumerator Words(ReadOnlySpan<char> text) Parameters text ReadOnlySpan<char> The text. api/Egami.Fonts.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Fonts Classes BitmapColorGlyph An sbix or CBDT glyph: its image, the strike's size and where the image goes, in font units with y up, so it scales with the font; the drawing code decodes and resamples it. CffOptions What a bare CFF stream lacks and an sfnt would supply, for FromCff(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CffOptions?). CffStandardStrings The Compact Font Format's predefined data (Adobe Technical Note #5176, appendices A and B): the 391 standard strings that string ids (SIDs) below 391 name, and the Standard and Expert encodings as glyph names by code. CharacterMap One character map of a face, as stored: a cmap subtable for one (platform, encoding) pair, or a CFF font's own encoding as FreeType presents it (platform 7). Codes are the subtable's own: bytes for a Macintosh (1,0) map or a symbol font's (3,0) map, never translated to Unicode. CidSystemInfo The character collection a CID-keyed font's CIDs belong to (its CFF ROS operator), such as Adobe-Japan1-7; PDF's CIDSystemInfo dictionary carries the same three values. ColorCompositePaint Two paints composited: the source onto the backdrop with a blend or Porter-Duff mode. ColorGlyph A glyph's color description from TryGetColorGlyph(ushort, FontPalette?, out ColorGlyph?, float): a PaintColorGlyph (COLR) or a BitmapColorGlyph (sbix, CBDT). ColorGlyphPaint A paint clipped to a glyph's outline. ColorGlyphReferencePaint Another color glyph's paint graph drawn here, as COLR's PaintColrGlyph reuses it. ColorLayersPaint Paints drawn one over another, in order. ColorLine The stops of a color gradient and what happens past them. ColorLinearGradientPaint A linear gradient filling the clip: the color line runs from P0 toward P1, with lines of equal color parallel to P0–P2, as COLR defines it. ColorPaint One node of a color glyph's paint graph, in font units with y up: COLR version 1 as OpenType 1.9.1 defines it (version 0 glyphs become layers of solid glyph fills), with variable values already taken at the face's position and palette colors resolved. ColorRadialGradientPaint A gradient between two circles filling the clip. ColorSolidPaint One color filling the clip. ColorSweepGradientPaint A gradient around a center filling the clip, angles in degrees counter-clockwise from the x axis (y up). ColorTransformPaint A paint under an affine transform in font units: COLR's transform, translate, scale, rotate and skew paints, each as its matrix (row vectors, y up). FontCollection A set of faces grouped into families: the caller's own, or System for the fonts installed on the machine. Finds families by name and faces by style with the CSS Fonts Level 4 matching steps. FontFamily The faces of one family in a FontCollection, matched by style. FontLoadOptions How a font file is read: leniently with diagnostics (the default), or strictly. FontLoader Tells what font data holds and loads every face of a collection. FontPalette The palette a color font draws with: a CPAL palette by index or by the background it suits, with entries overridden, as CSS's font-palette and @font-palette-values. FontPaletteInfo One CPAL palette of a face. FontSubset A font holding only some glyphs of another, from FontSubsetter. FontSubsetter Writes fonts that hold only the glyphs a document uses, as PDF embedding and SVG export want: TrueType, OpenType CFF or bare CFF, with composite glyphs and seac accents closed over and unused CFF subroutines dropped. GlyphRun Positioned glyphs of one font, ready to draw: glyph ids, one position per glyph relative to the run's origin (the first baseline's left end, y down, in canvas units), and optionally the source text with the UTF-16 index each glyph came from, which lets a PDF writer keep text searchable. NamedInstance A named instance of a variable font, such as "Bold Condensed", from its fvar table. PaintColorGlyph A COLR glyph: its paint graph and, for version 1, the clip box the font gives. SubsetOptions How Subset(Typeface, IEnumerable<ushort>, SubsetOptions?) writes a subset. Typeface One font face: its names, style, metrics, character map, glyph outlines and kerning, read from a TrueType or OpenType font, a collection, or a bare CFF stream. Immutable and safe to share across threads, canvases and backends. VariationAxis One axis of a variable font, from its fvar table. Structs CharacterMapping A code and the glyph a CharacterMap gives it. ColorStop A stop of a color line. Font A typeface at a size: the em in canvas units (pixels on a raster, points on a PDF page). Scales the face's font-unit metrics and turns text into a positioned GlyphRun. FontExtents A face's vertical metrics and decoration positions, with y up: in font units from Extents, or in canvas units from Extents. FontMatch A matched face and the styling it lacks, from Match(FontStyle). FontNameRecord One decoded string of a font's naming table, such as the family name in one language. FontPaletteEntry One palette entry replaced, as CSS's override-colors. FontProbe The result of Probe(ReadOnlySpan<byte>). FontStyle A face's style, or the style asked for when matching: weight from 1 to 1000 (400 normal, 700 bold), width from 1 to 9 (5 normal, as OS/2 usWidthClass), and slant. FontTag A four-byte OpenType tag, such as the table tag glyf or the feature tag kern. FontVariation A position on one axis of a variable font, in the axis's own units, such as weight 650. GlyphColor A color in a color glyph: a resolved palette color, or the foreground (palette entry 0xFFFF), which takes the paint's color and keeps only this color's alpha as a factor. GlyphExtents A box around ink, such as a glyph's outline, with y up in font units or in a Font's size. GlyphTransform A glyph's placement in a transformed GlyphRun: a rotation and uniform scale, then its origin, as Skia's RSXform. A point (x, y) of the glyph, y down, goes to (ScaleCos x - ScaleSin y + Tx, ScaleSin x + ScaleCos y + Ty). TextBounds A box in canvas units with y down, such as the ink of a GlyphRun relative to its origin. TextMeasure The size of text as MeasureText(string, ShapingOptions?) lays it out, in canvas units. VerticalMetrics One set of a face's ascent, descent and line gap as stored in a table, in font units with y up. Interfaces IColorPaintVisitor Walks a color glyph's paint graph, one method per kind of node. IGlyphOutlineSink Receives a glyph outline from GetGlyphOutline(ushort, IGlyphOutlineSink), in font units with y up. Each contour starts with MoveTo(float, float) and ends with Close(); a closing line back to the start point is implied by Close() and not sent. FontEdging How a glyph's edges are turned into pixels. FontEmbedding The embedding permissions a face declares in its OS/2 fsType field. Egami reports them and never enforces them; a caller that embeds fonts, such as a PDF writer, decides what to do. FontFileKind What kind of font data some bytes hold, as Probe(ReadOnlySpan<byte>) sees it. FontHinting How glyph outlines are fitted to the pixel grid before rasterizing. FontMetrics Where a font's advances come from. FontOutlines How a face stores its glyph outlines. FontPaletteBackground Which palettes FontPalette prefers by the backgrounds CPAL says they suit. FontSlant Whether a face is upright, italic or oblique. FontSynthesis Styling a face lacks, which a matched Font asks the renderer to synthesize (drawn from 2.7.2 on). GenericFamily A generic family name, matched against fixed per-platform preference lists. OpticalSizing Whether a Font sets a variable font's optical size axis from its size. SubsetFormat What FontSubsetter writes. TrueTypeTarget Which rasterizer the TrueType interpreter answers for: what GETINFO tells the font and how instructions are softened.

api/Egami.Formats.Ani.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Formats.Ani Classes AniDetails Details only ANI has, kept in FormatDetails. Each frame's own hotspot, entry and depth are in its FormatDetails, an IcoDetails. AniFormat The Windows animated cursor format (.ani), registered in Default: a RIFF file whose frames are cursors or icons, with a display time and an order for each step. Load returns one animated raster with a frame per step, all at one size; LoadAll returns the animation once for every size its frames hold. Save writes an animated raster with AniWriterOptions. AniWriterOptions Options for writing ANI. Each frame of the raster is a step of the animation; a frame that repeats an earlier one (same pixels, same hotspot) is stored once and shown again. Every stored frame is a cursor with the entries IcoWriterOptions would write. Delays are rounded to 1/60 s, and a delay under 20 ms is written as 100 ms, as browsers play GIFs. ANI always loops. EXIF, XMP and IPTC are not written; an ICC profile goes into PNG entries.

The frames equal libaom's and dav1d's sample for sample. Containers are not read here: Egami.Video reads them and uses this decoder, and any other source of AV1 temporal units can too. public sealed class Av1StreamDecoder : IDisposable Inheritance object Av1StreamDecoder Implements IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // AV1 temporal units in stream order, here from an IVF file (Egami.Video reads WebM, Matroska, MP4 and IVF for you). using Av1StreamDecoder decoder = new(new Av1DecoderOptions { ApplyFilmGrain = true }); foreach (byte[] temporalUnit in IvfFrames("clip-av1.ivf")) { decoder.Send(temporalUnit); while (decoder.NextFrame is Av1FrameInfo next) { // A unit can show no frame (a hidden reference), one, or one per spatial layer. using YuvRaster picture = next.BitDepth == 8 ? YuvRaster.Create(next.Width, next.Height, next.Chroma, YuvColor.Bt601Limited) : YuvRaster.Create(next.Width, next.Height, next.Chroma, next.BitDepth, YuvColor.Bt601Limited); decoder.TryReceiveFrame(picture, out Av1FrameInfo info); // the picture is the caller's: change it or keep it shown++; } } Remarks Send(ReadOnlySpan<byte>) takes one temporal unit: low-overhead OBUs (section 5), each with its size field, as containers store them. It can show no frame (a hidden frame, kept as a reference), one, or with OutputAllLayers one per spatial layer; TryReceiveFrame(YuvRaster, out Av1FrameInfo) then copies each out in order. A frame shown with show_existing_frame comes out again without decoding. The decoder keeps at most eight reference frames and the frame being decoded, decodes a frame's tiles and its loop filters' rows on up to MaxParallelism threads, and checks each frame's size against the context's Limits. An instance is not thread-safe. Constructors Av1StreamDecoder(Av1DecoderOptions?, EgamiContext?) YuvRaster.Create(next.Width, next.Height, next.Chroma, YuvColor.Bt601Limited) : YuvRaster.Create(next.Width, next.Height, next.Chroma, next.BitDepth, YuvColor.Bt601Limited); decoder.TryReceiveFrame(picture, out Av1FrameInfo info); // the picture is the caller's: change it or keep it shown++; } } Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The options' operating point is not 0 to 31.
