api/Egami.Formats.Av1.Av1StreamEncoder.h.title: Class Av1StreamEncoder | Egami
api/Egami.Formats.Av1.Av1StreamEncoder.h.summary: Class Av1StreamEncoder Namespace Egami.Formats.Av1 Assembly Egami.dll Encodes an AV1 video stream (AV1 Bitstream and Decoding Process 1.0.0 with errata 1) a frame at a time: key, intra-only and inter frames, inter blocks predicted from up to seven references with every single and compound mode, inter-intra, overlapped and warped motion, and hidden frames shown later with show_existing_frame. Each frame's Av1FramePlan says what it is (its type, whether it is shown), its quality or quantizer, and which reference slots it reads and refreshes, so rate control and group-of-frames planning stay with the caller: Egami.Video drives this encoder for its containers, and any other source of frames can too. The frames decode in libaom and dav1d exactly as in Av1StreamDecoder. public sealed class Av1StreamEncoder : IDisposable Inheritance object Av1StreamEncoder Implements IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // Pictures of one size, here decoded from a clip; Egami.Video writes WebM, MP4 and IVF and plans the frames for you. using Av1StreamEncoder encoder = new(new Av1SequenceOptions { Width = pictures[0].Width, Height = pictures[0].Height }); units.Add(encoder.Encode(pictures[0], new Av1FramePlan { Kind = Av1FrameKind.Key, Quality = 60 }).Data.ToArray()); // A hidden frame from four pictures ahead goes into slot 1; the three pictures between read it as ALTREF (from the future) // and the frame before as LAST, then the hidden frame is shown when its time comes. Av1FramePlan between = new() { Quality = 60, ReferenceSlots = [0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1] }; encoder.Encode(pictures[4], new Av1FramePlan { Quality = 55, Show = false, OrderHint = 4, RefreshSlots = 0b10 }); for (int i = 1; i < 4; i++) { Av1EncodedFrame frame = encoder.Encode(pictures[i], between); // the first unit also holds the hidden frame units.Add(frame.Data.ToArray()); // an MP4 sample or a Matroska block; frame.LumaPsnr says how close it came } units.Add(encoder.ShowExisting(1).Data.ToArray()); Remarks Encode(YuvRaster, Av1FramePlan) returns low-overhead OBUs (section 5), each with its size field and without temporal delimiters, as MP4, Matroska and WebM store them: a key frame starts with the sequence header. A hidden frame's OBUs are held and lead the temporal unit of the next shown frame, so every Data that is not empty is one whole temporal unit. The encoder keeps the eight reference slots as a decoder does, decides each frame on up to MaxParallelism threads (one per tile) and checks the frame size against the context's Limits. The output does not depend on the thread count. An instance is not thread-safe. Constructors Av1StreamEncoder(Av1SequenceOptions, EgamiContext?) Starts a stream with the sequence sequence describes. public Av1StreamEncoder(Av1SequenceOptions sequence, EgamiContext? context = null) Parameters sequence Av1SequenceOptions The frame size, bit depth, chroma format, color and level, or a sequence header to reproduce. context EgamiContext The threads and limits to use; Default when null. Examples // Pictures of one size, here decoded from a clip; Egami.Video writes WebM, MP4 and IVF and plans the frames for you. using Av1StreamEncoder encoder = new(new Av1SequenceOptions { Width = pictures[0].Width, Height = pictures[0].Height }); units.Add(encoder.Encode(pictures[0], new Av1FramePlan { Kind = Av1FrameKind.Key, Quality = 60 }).Data.ToArray()); // A hidden frame from four pictures ahead goes into slot 1; the three pictures between read it as ALTREF (from the future) // and the frame before as LAST, then the hidden frame is shown when its time comes. Av1FramePlan between = new() { Quality = 60, ReferenceSlots = [0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1] }; encoder.Encode(pictures[4], new Av1FramePlan { Quality = 55, Show = false, OrderHint = 4, RefreshSlots = 0b10 }); for (int i = 1; i < 4; i++) { Av1EncodedFrame frame = encoder.Encode(pictures[i], between); // the first unit also holds the hidden frame units.Add(frame.Data.ToArray()); // an MP4 sample or a Matroska block; frame.LumaPsnr says how close it came } units.Add(encoder.ShowExisting(1).Data.ToArray()); Exceptions LimitExceededException The frame size breaks the context's safety limits. Properties Height Gets the frame height. public int Height { get; } Property Value int SequenceHeader Gets the sequence header OBU, with its size field, as an av1C box's configOBUs and a key frame's temporal unit hold it. public ReadOnlyMemory<byte> SequenceHeader { get; } Property Value ReadOnlyMemory<byte> Width Gets the frame width. public int Width { get; } Property Value int Methods Analyze(IReadOnlyList<Av1AnalysisFrame>) Runs the temporal model over frames ahead, in the order they will be coded (References says which earlier ones each predicts from): how much of each frame's content, block by block, the frames after it reuse. A frame's Av1FrameAnalysis goes in its plan (Analysis), and its Importance can set a group's base quantizer. The frames are not coded and the stream does not change; the result depends only on the pictures and references, not on the thread count. public IReadOnlyList<Av1FrameAnalysis> Analyze(IReadOnlyList<Av1AnalysisFrame> frames) Parameters frames IReadOnlyList<Av1AnalysisFrame> The frames, in coding order, at the stream's size. Returns IReadOnlyList<Av1FrameAnalysis> Each frame's analysis, in the same order. Examples // The frames ahead in coding order: a key frame, a hidden frame four pictures on, then the three between, each predicting // from the frames on both sides of it (their places in this list). IReadOnlyList<Av1FrameAnalysis> analysis = encoder.Analyze( [ new Av1AnalysisFrame { Picture = pictures[0] }, new Av1AnalysisFrame { Picture = pictures[4], References = [0] }, new Av1AnalysisFrame { Picture = pictures[1], References = [0, 1] }, new Av1AnalysisFrame { Picture = pictures[2], References = [0, 1] }, new Av1AnalysisFrame { Picture = pictures[3], References = [0, 1] }, ]); // The more the frames after them reuse the key and hidden frames, the finer their steps; each plan carries its analysis. int keyQ = (int)Math.Round(100 / Math.Sqrt(analysis[0].Importance)); encoder.Encode(pictures[0], new Av1FramePlan { Kind = Av1FrameKind.Key, QIndex = keyQ, Analysis = analysis[0] }); encoder.Encode(pictures[4], new Av1FramePlan { QIndex = 110, Show = false, OrderHint = 4, RefreshSlots = 0b10, Analysis = analysis[1] }); for (int i = 1; i < 4; i++) { encoder.Encode(pictures[i], new Av1FramePlan { QIndex = 140, Layer = 1, ReferenceSlots = [0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1], RefreshSlots = 0, Analysis = analysis[i + 1] }); } encoder.ShowExisting(1); Exceptions ArgumentException A picture is not at the stream's size, or a frame names a reference that is not before it. Dispose() Drops the reference slots and the frames held for the next temporal unit. public void Dispose() Encode(YuvRaster, Av1FramePlan) Encodes one frame as plan says and updates the reference slots. The first frame is always a key frame. public Av1EncodedFrame Encode(YuvRaster frame, Av1FramePlan plan) Parameters frame YuvRaster The picture at the stream's size, chroma format and bit depth: 8-bit samples for an 8-bit stream, else 16-bit. Its color is taken as the sequence's. plan Av1FramePlan How to code the frame. Returns Av1EncodedFrame The frame's OBUs (a whole temporal unit once a frame is shown) and what coding it cost. Exceptions ArgumentException frame does not match the stream, or the plan names an empty slot or a switch frame. ShowExisting(int) Shows the frame in a slot again (show_existing_frame), as a hidden alternate reference is shown when its time comes: a temporal unit of one frame header OBU, after any hidden frames held for it. Showing a key frame this way also refreshes every slot with it. public Av1EncodedFrame ShowExisting(int slot) Parameters slot int The slot, 0 to 7. Returns Av1EncodedFrame The temporal unit. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException slot is outside 0 to 7. ArgumentException The slot is empty or its frame cannot be shown (it was shown already, or was not showable).

api/Egami.Formats.Ccitt.CcittFax.html.summary: Class CcittFax Namespace Egami.Formats.Ccitt Assembly Egami.dll Raw CCITT fax coding as a PDF filter: Group 3 and Group 4 data (ITU-T T.4 and T.6) with PDF's CCITTFaxDecode parameters, byte-aligned Group 4 included, which a TIFF wrapper cannot express. Decode(ReadOnlySpan<byte>, CcittFaxParameters, out int, EgamiContext?) reads it and Encode(ReadOnlySpan<byte>, CcittFaxParameters) writes Group 4 and one-dimensional Group 3. To load the data as an image instead, use CcittFormat. public static class CcittFax Inheritance object CcittFax Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A PDF image with /Filter /CCITTFaxDecode: its DecodeParms become the parameters, and the result is the filter's // output, packed rows with black 0 and white 1, ready for the image's /Decode array and color space. CcittFaxParameters parameters = new() { K = -1, EncodedByteAlign = true, Columns = 301, Rows = 48 }; byte[] rows = CcittFax.Decode(stream, parameters, out int rowCount); Methods Decode(ReadOnlySpan<byte>, CcittFaxParameters, out int, EgamiContext?) Decodes CCITT fax data to packed rows, as PDF's CCITTFaxDecode filter gives them: one bit a pixel, most significant bit first, each row padded to whole bytes with 0 bits, black 0 and white 1 unless BlackIs1. public static byte[] Decode(ReadOnlySpan<byte> data, CcittFaxParameters parameters, out int rows, EgamiContext? context = null) Parameters data ReadOnlySpan<byte> The coded data, as the stream holds it after the filters before CCITTFaxDecode. parameters CcittFaxParameters The stream's DecodeParms. rows int The number of rows returned: Rows when it is above 0, else the rows decoded. context EgamiContext The context whose safety limits and diagnostics apply, or null for Default. Returns byte[] The rows, (Columns + 7) / 8 bytes each. Examples // A PDF image with /Filter /CCITTFaxDecode: its DecodeParms become the parameters, and the result is the filter's // output, packed rows with black 0 and white 1, ready for the image's /Decode array and color space. CcittFaxParameters parameters = new() { K = -1, EncodedByteAlign = true, Columns = 301, Rows = 48 }; byte[] rows = CcittFax.Decode(stream, parameters, out int rowCount); Remarks A damaged row ends decoding (after DamagedRowsBeforeError skipped rows, when it applies): the rows before it are kept, the rest are white, and a warning goes to the context's Diagnostics. Data that ends before Rows rows also warns. Exceptions ArgumentNullException parameters is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException A parameter is outside what it can mean, such as Columns below 1. CorruptDataException Not one row decodes. LimitExceededException The image breaks a safety limit. Encode(ReadOnlySpan<byte>, CcittFaxParameters) Encodes packed rows as CCITT fax data, the inverse of Decode(ReadOnlySpan<byte>, CcittFaxParameters, out int, EgamiContext?): one bit a pixel, most significant bit first, each row padded to whole bytes, black 0 and white 1 unless BlackIs1. The parameters that describe the result are the ones a PDF's DecodeParms then carries. public static byte[] Encode(ReadOnlySpan<byte> rows, CcittFaxParameters parameters) Parameters rows ReadOnlySpan<byte> The packed rows, (Columns + 7) / 8 bytes each; padding bits are ignored. parameters CcittFaxParameters The coding to write: K, EndOfLine, EndOfBlock, Columns, Rows and BlackIs1 are used. Returns byte[] The coded data. Examples // A bi-level scan as a PDF image with /Filter /CCITTFaxDecode: pack its rows (0 black, 1 white), then write Group 4. int rowBytes = (scan.Width + 7) / 8; byte[] rows = new byte[rowBytes * scan.Height]; for (int y = 0; y < scan.Height; y++) { Span<Gray8> row = scan.Row(y); for (int x = 0; x < scan.Width; x++) { if (row[x].L >= 128) { rows[(y * rowBytes) + (x >> 3)] |= (byte)(0x80 >> (x & 7)); } } } // These parameters are the image's DecodeParms: << /K -1 /Columns 301 /Rows 48 >>. CcittFaxParameters parameters = new() { K = -1, Columns = scan.Width, Rows = scan.Height }; byte[] g4 = CcittFax.Encode(rows, parameters); Remarks K below 0 writes Group 4 (ITU-T T.6), the smallest coding for scanned text; 0 writes one-dimensional Group 3 (modified Huffman rows). EndOfLine puts an EOL before each Group 3 row, and EndOfBlock ends the data with RTC or EOFB. The row count is Rows when it is above 0, else every whole row of rows. Exceptions ArgumentNullException parameters is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException A parameter is outside what it can mean, or rows holds fewer rows than Rows. NotSupportedException K above 0 (mixed Group 3) or EncodedByteAlign is asked for: neither is written.

api/Egami.Formats.Exr.ExrCompression.htm.summary: Enum ExrCompression Namespace Egami.Formats.Exr Assembly Egami.dll How an OpenEXR part's pixel data is compressed. public enum ExrCompression Fields B44 = 6 Half samples in fixed 4 × 4 blocks of 14 bytes, 32 scanlines a block. Lossy. B44A = 7 B44, with flat blocks stored in 3 bytes. Lossy. Dwaa = 8 DreamWorks' DCT compression, 32 scanlines a block. Lossy. Dwab = 9 DreamWorks' DCT compression, 256 scanlines a block. Lossy. Htj2k256 = 11 High-throughput JPEG 2000 at 256 scanlines a block, new in OpenEXR 3.4. Egami reads the header but not the pixels. Htj2k32 = 12 High-throughput JPEG 2000 at 32 scanlines a block, new in OpenEXR 3.4. Egami reads the header but not the pixels. None = 0 Not compressed. Piz = 4 A Haar wavelet and Huffman coding, 32 scanlines a block. Lossless; good on grainy photographs. Pxr24 = 5 Float samples rounded to 24 bits, then deflated, 16 scanlines a block. Lossy for float, lossless for half and uint. Rle = 1 Run-length encoding of byte differences, one scanline a block. Lossless. Zip = 3 Deflate of byte differences, 16 scanlines a block. Lossless. Zips = 2 Deflate of byte differences, one scanline a block. Lossless. Zstd = 10 Zstandard, new in OpenEXR 3.4. Egami reads the header but not the pixels. Examples // Half-float RGBA, ZIP-compressed, by default; a sRGB or other non-linear raster is linearized first. beauty.Save("copy.exr"); beauty.Save("float.exr", new ExrWriterOptions { Compression = ExrCompression.Piz, PixelType = ExrPixelType.Float });

api/Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegColorType.htm.summary: Enum JpegColorType Namespace Egami.Formats.Jpeg Assembly Egami.dll Which components a JPEG is written with. public enum JpegColorType Fields Auto = 0 Gray for gray pixel types, CMYK for CMYK pixel types, YCbCr for everything else. Cmyk = 2 Four CMYK components with an Adobe marker (transform 0), the values inverted as Photoshop writes them and every reader expects. Other pixel types are converted to ink with the plain formula. Auto picks this for CMYK pixel types. Gray = 1 One gray component, whatever the pixel type; color is converted to luma. Ycck = 3 Four YCCK components with an Adobe marker (transform 2): cyan, magenta and yellow converted to YCbCr as libjpeg converts Adobe CMYK, chroma subsampled as Subsampling says, and the inverted black at full size. Usually smaller than Cmyk. Examples using Raster photo = Raster.Load("duck.jpg", options: new JpegReaderOptions { FastUpsampling = true }); JpegDetails details = (JpegDetails)photo.Metadata.FormatDetails!; Console.WriteLine($"{details.ColorSpace}, progressive: {details.Progressive}, quality about {details.EstimatedQuality}"); foreach (JpegComponent component in details.Components) { Console.WriteLine($"Component {component.Id}: sampled {component.HorizontalSampling} × {component.VerticalSampling}"); } // Gray output, and 4:4:4 (no chroma subsampling) for sharp colored edges. photo.Save("gray.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { ColorType = JpegColorType.Gray }); photo.Save("sharp.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { Quality = 90, Subsampling = ChromaSubsampling.Subsample444 });

api/Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegTransform.htm.title: Class JpegTransform | Egami
api/Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegTransform.htm.summary: Class JpegTransform Namespace Egami.Formats.Jpeg Assembly Egami.dll Rotates, flips, crops and drops the color of JPEG files without decoding them to pixels, so nothing is lost: the quantized DCT coefficients are moved and sign-flipped block by block, as jpegtran does, and coded again. Quantization tables and chroma subsampling stay as they were. Every mode the reader takes works except lossless JPEG, which has no coefficients. public static class JpegTransform Inheritance object JpegTransform Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // Turns the photo upright by its EXIF orientation without re-encoding: no quality is lost, and the tag is reset. JpegTransform.Apply("sideways.jpg", "upright.jpg", new JpegTransformOptions { Operation = JpegTransformOperation.AutoOrient }); // Rotates, crops and drops the color in one pass; a file can be transformed in place. JpegTransformResult result = JpegTransform.Apply("upright.jpg", "upright.jpg", new JpegTransformOptions { Operation = JpegTransformOperation.Rotate90, Crop = new Rect(0, 0, 200, 120), Grayscale = true, }); Console.WriteLine($"{result.Width} × {result.Height}"); Remarks The whole image's coefficients are held while it runs (about 2 bytes per sample, 3 bytes per pixel for a 4:2:0 photo), counted against MaxTotalBytes. The result is the same for any MaxParallelism. Methods Apply(Stream, Stream, JpegTransformOptions, EgamiContext?) Transforms the JPEG in source and writes the result to destination. public static JpegTransformResult Apply(Stream source, Stream destination, JpegTransformOptions options, EgamiContext? context = null) Parameters source Stream The JPEG, read from its current position. It is not disposed. destination Stream Where the result goes. It is not disposed. options JpegTransformOptions What to do. context EgamiContext The context whose limits and diagnostics apply, or null for Default. Returns JpegTransformResult The size of the result and the warnings. Examples // Turns the photo upright by its EXIF orientation without re-encoding: no quality is lost, and the tag is reset. JpegTransform.Apply("sideways.jpg", "upright.jpg", new JpegTransformOptions { Operation = JpegTransformOperation.AutoOrient }); // Rotates, crops and drops the color in one pass; a file can be transformed in place. JpegTransformResult result = JpegTransform.Apply("upright.jpg", "upright.jpg", new JpegTransformOptions { Operation = JpegTransformOperation.Rotate90, Crop = new Rect(0, 0, 200, 120), Grayscale = true, }); Console.WriteLine($"{result.Width} × {result.Height}"); Exceptions ArgumentNullException An argument is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException Crop is empty or leaves the image. InvalidOperationException Strict and a partial MCU would move. NotSupportedException Grayscale on an RGB, CMYK or YCCK file. UnsupportedFormatException The file is lossless or hierarchical JPEG. CorruptDataException The file breaks the format's rules beyond repair. LimitExceededException The image is larger than the limits allow, or its coefficients need more memory. Apply(string, string, JpegTransformOptions, EgamiContext?) Transforms a JPEG file into another, or into itself: the result goes to a temporary file beside destinationPath that replaces it once complete, so a failure leaves the destination as it was. public static JpegTransformResult Apply(string sourcePath, string destinationPath, JpegTransformOptions options, EgamiContext? context = null) Parameters sourcePath string The JPEG file. destinationPath string The file to write; it may be sourcePath. options JpegTransformOptions What to do. context EgamiContext The context whose limits and diagnostics apply, or null for Default. JpegTransformResult result = JpegTransform.Apply("upright.jpg", "upright.jpg", new JpegTransformOptions { Operation = JpegTransformOperation.Rotate90, Crop = new Rect(0, 0, 200, 120), Grayscale = true, }); Console.WriteLine($"{result.Width} × {result.Height}"); Exceptions ArgumentNullException An argument is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException Crop is empty or leaves the image. InvalidOperationException Strict and a partial MCU would move. NotSupportedException Grayscale on an RGB, CMYK or YCCK file. api/Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegTransformEdge.title: Enum JpegTransformEdges | Egami
api/Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegTransformEdge.summary: Enum JpegTransformEdges Namespace Egami.Formats.Jpeg Assembly Egami.dll What a lossless transform does with the blocks at the right or bottom edge when the image is not a whole number of MCUs (8 or 16 pixels) across or down, so those blocks cannot move to the other side intact. public enum JpegTransformEdges Fields Keep = 2 Leaves partial MCUs where they are, unmirrored, as jpegtran does by default: every pixel is kept, but a strip up to 15 pixels wide at the edge is not turned with the rest. Strict = 1 Throws InvalidOperationException when a partial MCU would have to move, as jpegtran -perfect does, so the result is always exact and full size. Trim = 0 Drops the partial MCU from an edge that is mirrored, so the image loses up to 15 pixels there (up to 7 for gray), as jpegtran -trim does. Edges that stay in place keep every pixel. Examples // Turns the photo upright by its EXIF orientation without re-encoding: no quality is lost, and the tag is reset. JpegTransform.Apply("sideways.jpg", "upright.jpg", new JpegTransformOptions { Operation = JpegTransformOperation.AutoOrient }); // Rotates, crops and drops the color in one pass; a file can be transformed in place. JpegTransformResult result = JpegTransform.Apply("upright.jpg", "upright.jpg", new JpegTransformOptions { Operation = JpegTransformOperation.Rotate90, Crop = new Rect(0, 0, 200, 120), Grayscale = true, }); Console.WriteLine($"{result.Width} × {result.Height}");

api/Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegTransformOper.title: Enum JpegTransformOperation | Egami
api/Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegTransformOper.summary: Enum JpegTransformOperation Namespace Egami.Formats.Jpeg Assembly Egami.dll The rotation or flip a lossless JPEG transform applies, in the terms of jpegtran. public enum JpegTransformOperation Fields AutoOrient = 8 Whatever the EXIF orientation needs to show the image upright, after which the orientation is set to Normal: the lossless version of AutoOrient(). A file with no orientation, or an upright one, is copied. FlipHorizontal = 1 Mirrored left to right. FlipVertical = 2 Mirrored top to bottom. None = 0 No rotation or flip; with Crop or Grayscale only those apply. Rotate180 = 4 Turned 180°. Rotate270 = 5 Turned 270° clockwise (90° counterclockwise). Rotate90 = 3 Turned 90° clockwise. Transpose = 6 Mirrored along the top-left to bottom-right diagonal: rows become columns. Transverse = 7 Mirrored along the top-right to bottom-left diagonal. Examples // Turns the photo upright by its EXIF orientation without re-encoding: no quality is lost, and the tag is reset. JpegTransform.Apply("sideways.jpg", "upright.jpg", new JpegTransformOptions { Operation = JpegTransformOperation.AutoOrient }); // Rotates, crops and drops the color in one pass; a file can be transformed in place. JpegTransformResult result = JpegTransform.Apply("upright.jpg", "upright.jpg", new JpegTransformOptions { Operation = JpegTransformOperation.Rotate90, Crop = new Rect(0, 0, 200, 120), Grayscale = true, }); Console.WriteLine($"{result.Width} × {result.Height}");

Set, the raster is tone mapped with Bt2390 to the SDR base image, written at Quality, and Create(Raster, Raster?, GainMapOptions?) makes the map that brings the HDR raster back, written after it as KeepGainMap says. To choose the SDR rendition yourself, set GainMap of the SDR raster to Create(Raster, Raster?, GainMapOptions?)'s map and save that. A map read from the file is copied as it was stored; one an operation moved is encoded again. StripMetadata leaves it out too. Defaults to true. public bool KeepGainMap { get; init; } Property Value bool Examples // Crops, turns, flips and resizes move the gain map with the picture; saving as JPEG writes it back. using Raster photo = Raster.Load("ultrahdr.jpg"); using Raster cropped = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Crop(16, 16, 200, 150).Rotate(90)); cropped.Save("cropped.jpg"); // still Ultra HDR // Operations that change pixel values drop it (Operation.GainMapDropped), and so do formats other than JPEG // (Save.GainMapDropped); KeepGainMap = false leaves it out on purpose. cropped.Save("sdr-only.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { KeepGainMap = false }); OptimizeHuffman Gets a value indicating whether to build Huffman tables for this image in a second pass instead of using the standard ones: usually 5 to 10% smaller files, and slower. api/Egami.Formats.Jpeg.html.title: Namespace Egami.Formats.Jpeg | Egami
api/Egami.Formats.Jpeg.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Formats.Jpeg Classes JpegComponent One component of a JPEG frame and its sampling factors. JpegDetails Facts about a decoded JPEG that have no general home in RasterMetadata. Read-only facts; not written. JpegFormat The JPEG format (JFIF and EXIF files), registered in Default. JpegReaderOptions Options for reading JPEG, on top of the general ReaderOptions. JpegTransform Rotates, flips, crops and drops the color of JPEG files without decoding them to pixels, so nothing is lost: the quantized DCT coefficients are moved and sign-flipped block by block, as jpegtran does, and coded again. Quantization tables and chroma subsampling stay as they were. Every mode the reader takes works except lossless JPEG, which has no coefficients. JpegTransformOptions Options for JpegTransform: the rotation or flip, a crop, dropping color, how partial edge blocks are handled, how the result is coded and whether metadata is copied. The defaults copy the image unchanged, with optimized Huffman tables. JpegTransformResult What a lossless JPEG transform produced: the size of the result and what was repaired or left out on the way. JpegWriterOptions Options for writing JPEG. The defaults are libjpeg-turbo's cjpeg defaults: quality 75, 4:2:0 and the standard Huffman tables of T.81 Annex K, so files compare one to one. MpfData A JPEG file's Multi-Picture Format index (CIPA DC-007): the images the file holds after its primary image, such as large previews, stereo views or an HDR gain map. LoadAll(Stream, EgamiContext?, ReaderOptions?) loads each JPEG image it lists. MpfImage One image of a Multi-Picture Format file: its MP entry, with the offset resolved to the start of the file. Enums ChromaSubsampling How the chroma (Cb and Cr) components are sampled relative to luma. JpegColorSpace The color model a JPEG's components are stored in. JpegColorType Which components a JPEG is written with. JpegTransformEdges What a lossless transform does with the blocks at the right or bottom edge when the image is not a whole number of MCUs (8 or 16 pixels) across or down, so those blocks cannot move to the other side intact. JpegTransformOperation The rotation or flip a lossless JPEG transform applies, in the terms of jpegtran. MpfImageType What an image of a Multi-Picture Format file is, from its MP entry (CIPA DC-007, and the gain map type CIPA added later).

From a distance of 10 the whole image, alpha included, is coded at half size as cjxl codes it, so alpha is exact only below that. Lossless files keep alpha exact. public float AlphaDistance { get; init; } Property Value float Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is outside 0 to 25. Default Gets the default options. public static JxlWriterOptions Default { get; } Property Value JxlWriterOptions Distance Gets the Butteraugli-style distance lossy files are written at, as cjxl -d takes it: 1.0 is visually lossless, larger values give smaller files with more visible loss, 0.1 to 25. Defaults to null, which takes the distance from Quality. public float? Distance { get; init; } Property Value float? Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is outside 0.1 to 25. Effort Gets how hard the encoder works, 1 (fastest) to 7 (smallest files), on libjxl's effort scale for both kinds, so the same number gives about the same file as cjxl -e. Lossless: 1 is libjxl's fast lossless path, 2 and 3 use fixed trees, 4 and up learn the tree, and 5 and up also try local palettes and color transforms. Lossy: 1 to 3 use 8×8 DCTs and one quantization value, 4 adds finer LF and context modeling, 5 adaptive quantization, chroma from luma, Gaborish and simple block sizes, 6 the full block-size search, and 7 patches for repeated shapes such as text. api/Egami.Formats.Pnm.PnmKind.html.summary: Enum PnmKind Namespace Egami.Formats.Pnm Assembly Egami.dll Which Netpbm variant a file is, or which one to write. public enum PnmKind Fields Auto = 0 When writing: PFM for float types without alpha, PGM for other gray types, PPM for other types without alpha, PAM for types with alpha. Bitmap = 1 PBM (P1 or P4): one bit a pixel, 1 for black. FloatMap = 5 PFM (PF or Pf): 32-bit float RGB or gray in linear light, loaded as RgbF32 or GrayF32. Gray pixel types are written as Pf, the rest as PF; alpha is dropped. Graymap = 2 PGM (P2 or P5): gray. Pam = 4 PAM (P7): gray, RGB, or either with alpha. Pixmap = 3 PPM (P3 or P6): RGB. api/Egami.Formats.RecoveryMode.html.title: Enum RecoveryMode | Egami
api/Egami.Formats.RecoveryMode.html.summary: Enum RecoveryMode Namespace Egami.Formats Assembly Egami.dll How a reader handles damaged data. public enum RecoveryMode Fields Lenient = 0 Return what was decoded when the data ends early or a checksum fails after valid pixels, and note the problem in Warnings. Data that would need guessing, such as an invalid header, still throws. Strict = 1 Throw CorruptDataException on any problem. Examples EgamiContext strict = EgamiContext.Default with { Limits = SafetyLimits.Default with { MaxPixels = 25_000_000, MaxTotalBytes = 256L * 1024 * 1024 }, }; try { // Read the header first: cheap, and it rejects what you do not want before any pixel memory is used. RasterInfo info = Raster.Probe(upload, strict); if (info.Width > 8000 || info.Height > 8000) { throw new InvalidDataException("Too large."); } using Raster image = Raster.Load(upload, strict, new ReaderOptions { Recovery = RecoveryMode.Strict }); Console.WriteLine($"{info.Format.Name} {image.Width} × {image.Height}"); } catch (UnsupportedFormatException) { Console.WriteLine("Not an image format we accept."); } catch (LimitExceededException e) { Console.WriteLine($"Over the {e.LimitName} limit."); } catch (CorruptDataException e) { Console.WriteLine($"Damaged at byte {e.Offset}."); }

api/Egami.Formats.SaveKeeps.html.summary: Enum SaveKeeps Namespace Egami.Formats Assembly Egami.dll What a writer keeps of a raster, as it is about to write it, for ReportLosses(string, SaveKeeps): everything the raster has that is not named here is reported as lost. [Flags] public enum SaveKeeps Fields Alpha = 1 Alpha, or binary transparency. Cmyk = 8 CMYK inks. Comment = 1024 Text entries keyed "Comment" only. Exif = 32 The EXIF block. FloatingPoint = 4 Floating-point samples, values outside 0 to 1 included. Frames = 16 Every frame or page. GainMap = 4096 An HDR gain map (HDR Design question 11), or the caller's choice to leave it out. Icc = 256 The ICC profile. Iptc = 128 The IPTC datasets. Wide = 2 Samples deeper than 8 bits. Xmp = 64 The XMP packet. Examples /// <summary>The same RAW8 format, streaming: rows go in and out one at a time, so RasterDecoder, RasterEncoder and Transcode stream it.</summary> public static class StreamingRaw8Format { public static FormatInfo Info { get; } = Raw8Format.Info with { Reader = new Reader(), Writer = new Writer() }; private sealed class Reader : IFormatReader, IRowFormatReader { private static readonly IFormatReader Whole = Raw8Format.Info.Reader!; public RasterInfo ReadInfo(EgamiInput input, ReaderOptions options) => Whole.ReadInfo(input, options) with { Access = RasterAccess.Streamed }; public Raster<TPixel> Read<TPixel>(EgamiInput input, ReaderOptions options) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> => Whole.Read<TPixel>(input, options); public Raster Read(EgamiInput input, ReaderOptions options) => Whole.Read(input, options); // The open image reads each row when it is asked for; the decoder crops, reduces and converts after it. public RowReader Open(EgamiInput input, ReaderOptions options) { input.Skip(4); int width = (int)input.ReadUInt32BigEndian(); int height = (int)input.ReadUInt32BigEndian(); // No raster checks the size here, so check it before the row buffer is allocated. input.CheckFrameSize(width, height); return new Rows(input, width, height); } } private sealed class Rows(EgamiInput input, int width, int height) : RowReader<Rgba8> { private readonly Rgba8[] _row = new Rgba8[width]; private int _next; private bool _started; public override int Width => width; public override int Height => height; public override Metadata.RasterMetadata Metadata { get; } = new(); public override Metadata.FrameMetadata? NextFrame() { if (_started) { return null; } _started = true; return new Metadata.FrameMetadata(); } public override void ReadRow<TPixel>(int y, int x, Span<TPixel> destination) { for (; _next <= y; _next++) { input.ReadExactly(MemoryMarshal.AsBytes(_row.AsSpan())); } PixelConvert.Convert<Rgba8, TPixel>(_row.AsSpan(x, destination.Length), destination); } } private sealed class Writer : IFormatWriter, IRowFormatWriter { public void Write<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel> raster, Stream output, WriterOptions options) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> => Raw8Format.Info.Writer!.Write(raster, output, options); // Save, SaveAsync, RasterEncoder and Transcode all write through the encoder. public RowEncoder<TPixel> Start<TPixel>(Stream output, EncodeStart<TPixel> start) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> { // RAW8 keeps 8-bit RGBA and nothing else: deeper samples or metadata are reported as lost. start.ReportLosses("RAW8", SaveKeeps.Alpha); return new Encoder<TPixel>(output, start.Width, start.Height); } } private sealed class Encoder<TPixel> : RowEncoder<TPixel> where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> { private readonly Stream _output; private readonly Rgba8[] _row; public Encoder(Stream output, int width, int height) { _output = output; _row = new Rgba8[width]; Span<byte> header = stackalloc byte[12]; "RAW8"u8.CopyTo(header); BinaryPrimitives.WriteUInt32BigEndian(header[4..], (uint)width); BinaryPrimitives.WriteUInt32BigEndian(header[8..], (uint)height); output.Write(header); } public override void WriteRow(ReadOnlySpan<TPixel> row) { PixelConvert.Convert<TPixel, Rgba8>(row, _row); _output.Write(MemoryMarshal.AsBytes(_row.AsSpan())); } public override void Complete() { } } }

api/Egami.Formats.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Formats Classes EgamiInput The data a reader decodes: the caller's stream behind a pooled 64 KB buffer, with exact-read helpers. It also carries the context, limits and cancellation token for the load, and is the only way a reader allocates pixel memory. EncodeStart<TPixel> What an encode starts from: the size, metadata and options, and the whole image when Save has one. FormatInfo Describes a file format: its names, how to recognize it, and its reader and writer. HdrDecode How to read the HDR rendition of an image with a gain map, for Hdr. RasterInfo What a file's header says, read without decoding pixels. ReaderOptions Options for reading. The defaults read everything leniently. Formats with options of their own derive from it, such as JpegReaderOptions. RowEncoder<TPixel> One encode in progress: a still image's rows top-down with WriteRow(ReadOnlySpan<TPixel>), or whole frames with WriteFrame(Frame<TPixel>), then Complete(). RowReader One open image, as a format reader streams it: frames of rows at the stored size. Derive from RowReader<TNatural>, which names the natural pixel type. RowReader<TNatural> An open image whose natural pixel type is TNatural, as Load(Stream, EgamiContext?, ReaderOptions?) would give it. WriterOptions Options for writing. Each format has a subclass with its own settings; writers given this base class use their defaults. Interfaces IFormatReader Reads one file format. Readers are stateless and safe to share across threads. They read only through EgamiInput and allocate pixel memory only through CreateRaster<TPixel>(long, long, ClearMode), which checks the safety limits first, so no reader can allocate before the size has been checked. IFormatWriter Writes one file format. Writers are stateless, safe to share across threads, and never change the raster they are given. IRowFormatReader An optional interface for a format's reader: an open image that hands out rows as they are asked for, so RasterDecoder streams the format, with Region and MinimumSize applied on the way out. A reader without it still works everywhere: the decoder reads the whole image with Read(EgamiInput, ReaderOptions) and serves rows from it. Load, Probe and an incremental decode keep using IFormatReader. IRowFormatWriter An optional interface for a format's writer: an encoder that takes rows and frames one at a time. A writer that implements it streams through RasterEncoder<TPixel> and Transcode(Stream, Stream, FormatInfo, Action<RasterOps>?, ReaderOptions?, WriterOptions?, EgamiContext?), and Save(Stream, FormatInfo, WriterOptions?) and SaveAsync use it in place of Write<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel>, Stream, WriterOptions), so all of them write the same bytes. A writer without it still works everywhere: the encoder gathers the image and calls Write<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel>, Stream, WriterOptions) at the end. Enums RasterAccess How a decode produces rows, as Access reports it. RecoveryMode How a reader handles damaged data. SaveKeeps What a writer keeps of a raster, as it is about to write it, for ReportLosses(string, SaveKeeps): everything the raster has that is not named here is reported as lost. Delegates SignatureMatcher Returns whether the first bytes of a file belong to a format.

api/Egami.IPixelMemorySource.html.summary: Interface IPixelMemorySource Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll Supplies the memory behind every PixelPlane<TPixel>. Implement it to control where pixel memory comes from. Implementations must be thread-safe. public interface IPixelMemorySource Examples private sealed class CountingSource(IPixelMemorySource inner) : IPixelMemorySource { public int Blocks; public long Bytes; public int MaxBlockBytes => inner.MaxBlockBytes; public IMemoryOwner<byte> Allocate(int byteLength, ClearMode clear) { Interlocked.Increment(ref Blocks); Interlocked.Add(ref Bytes, byteLength); return inner.Allocate(byteLength, clear); // ClearMode.Zero when the caller needs zeroed memory } } Properties MaxBlockBytes Gets the largest block, in bytes, the source hands out in one piece. Planes bigger than this are split into several blocks, each holding whole rows. A single row larger than this still gets one block of its own. int MaxBlockBytes { get; } Property Value int Methods Allocate(int, ClearMode) Allocates one contiguous block of memory. IMemoryOwner<byte> Allocate(int byteLength, ClearMode clear) Parameters byteLength int The size of the block in bytes. The returned memory has exactly this length. clear ClearMode Whether to zero the block. Returns IMemoryOwner<byte> The block. Disposing it returns the memory to the source.

api/Egami.InkRaster.html.summary: Class InkRaster Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll A printed page as plates: one plane per ink of an InkSet (a disabled spot has none) plus one alpha plane, each 8 or 16 bits. A plane holds the ink as it prints over paper, 0 for none to the depth's maximum for full ink: drawing translucently leaves less ink, so the planes are premultiplied by the alpha plane, and a plate is ready to print as it is. A new raster is blank: no ink, alpha 0. public sealed class InkRaster : IDisposable Inheritance object InkRaster Implements IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A page as plates: CMYK and the spot, 8 bits each, plus alpha. Rows are written in place; a plate is also a gray raster. using InkRaster page = new(inks, 200, 100, InkDepth.Unorm8); page.Plate("PANTONE 186 C")!.Row8(10).Fill(255); // a full-tint line of the spot page.Alpha.Row8(10).Fill(255); using Raster<Gray8> spot = page.Plate("PANTONE 186 C")!.AsRaster<Gray8>(); // no copy: 0 = no ink, 255 = full ink Remarks Planar storage lets a plate come out as a Raster<TPixel> of Gray8 or Gray16 without copying (AsRaster<TPixel>()), and lets blend modes run one plane at a time. An A4 page at 300 dpi with CMYK and two spots takes 61 MB at 8 bits. Not thread-safe, like Raster. Constructors InkRaster(InkSet, int, int, InkDepth, EgamiContext?) api/Egami.Metadata.FrameBlend.html.summary: Enum FrameBlend Namespace Egami.Metadata Assembly Egami.dll How a frame is combined with what is already on the canvas. public enum FrameBlend Fields Over = 1 Alpha-blend over the existing pixels. Source = 0 Replace the pixels. Examples using Raster<Rgba8> clip = Raster.Load<Rgba8>("pan.gif"); FrameList<Rgba8> frames = clip.Frames; // Play the clip forward and then backward: append the middle frames in reverse. for (int i = frames.Count - 2; i > 0; i--) { Frame<Rgba8> copy = frames.Add(frames[i]); copy.Metadata.Delay = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(80); copy.Metadata.Disposal = FrameDisposal.None; copy.Metadata.Blend = FrameBlend.Source; } frames.RemoveAt(0); clip.Save("pan-bounce.gif");

api/Egami.Metadata.ImageOrientation.html.title: Enum ImageOrientation | Egami
api/Egami.Metadata.ImageOrientation.html.summary: Enum ImageOrientation Namespace Egami.Metadata Assembly Egami.dll How stored pixels must be turned to show the image upright: the EXIF Orientation tag (274). The value says which way the camera was held; AutoOrient applies it. public enum ImageOrientation Fields FlipHorizontal = 2 Mirrored left to right (EXIF 2). FlipVertical = 4 Mirrored top to bottom (EXIF 4). Normal = 1 Stored upright (EXIF 1). Also used when a file says nothing. Rotate180 = 3 Upside down (EXIF 3). Rotate270 = 8 Needs a 270° clockwise turn to show upright (EXIF 8). Rotate90 = 6 Needs a 90° clockwise turn to show upright (EXIF 6), as from a phone held upright. Transpose = 5 Mirrored along the top-left to bottom-right diagonal (EXIF 5). Transverse = 7 Mirrored along the top-right to bottom-left diagonal (EXIF 7). Unknown = 0 Not a valid EXIF value; treated as Normal. Readers report Normal when a file says nothing. Examples // Load returns pixels as stored. A phone photo stored sideways says so in its EXIF orientation. RasterInfo info = Raster.Probe("sideways.jpg"); Console.WriteLine(info.Orientation); // Rotate90 // AutoOrient turns the pixels upright and resets the tag. Followed by a resize, the resize runs first, on the stored image, // so only the small result is turned. using Raster photo = Raster.Load("sideways.jpg"); photo.Apply(ops => ops.AutoOrient().Fit(300, 300), Ct);

DateCreated Gets or sets when the content was created, from the date (2:55) and time (2:60): midnight UTC when there is no valid time, and null when there is no valid date. Setting writes both (CCYYMMDD and HHMMSS±HHMM); setting null removes both. public DateTimeOffset? DateCreated { get; set; } Property Value DateTimeOffset? Returns IReadOnlyList<string> The values; empty when there are none. Parse(ReadOnlySpan<byte>, SafetyLimits?) Reads IPTC-IIM datasets: tag markers 0x1C, each with a record, a dataset, a length and the value. Never throws: a block that runs past its end or past MaxMetadataBytes keeps what was read and is marked damaged. public static IptcData Parse(ReadOnlySpan<byte> iim, SafetyLimits? limits = null) Parameters iim ReadOnlySpan<byte> The datasets, without any Photoshop resource wrapper. limits SafetyLimits The limits whose MaxMetadataBytes caps the values copied. Returns bool Whether there was any. api/Egami.Metadata.html.title: Namespace Egami.Metadata | Egami
api/Egami.Metadata.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Metadata Classes ExifData A parsed EXIF block (a TIFF structure, CIPA DC-008): the tags of IFD0, the EXIF, GPS and interoperability sub-IFDs and IFD1 with its thumbnail, with typed getters for the common ones. An unedited block writes back byte for byte; after an edit it is laid out again, keeping the maker note at its old offset when it fits, since maker notes often hold offsets of their own. ExifEntry One EXIF value: its tag, TIFF type and raw bytes, with accessors that read them as text, integers or fractions. FormatDetails Format-specific details the reader found, such as the original color type or palette. Each format derives its own. FrameMetadata Metadata that belongs to one frame. IptcData Parsed IPTC-IIM datasets (IPTC-IIM 4.2), as news agencies, stock libraries and Lightroom write them next to XMP, with typed getters for the common ones. Shaped like ExifData: an unedited block writes back byte for byte; after an edit it is rebuilt in record and dataset order, record 1 first, with the coded character set (1:90) set to UTF-8 whenever a value is not plain ASCII. IptcEntry One IPTC-IIM dataset as stored: its key and its bytes. RasterMetadata Metadata that belongs to the whole raster. It is kept apart from the pixels and survives operations unless an operation makes it wrong. Metadata problems never fail a load: broken blocks are kept as bytes and noted in Warnings. TextEntry A text entry, such as a PNG text chunk or a GIF comment. XmpArray An XMP array: items in order, each a simple value (string), an XmpStruct or another XmpArray, with a language for the items of a language alternative. XmpData A parsed XMP packet: its properties by namespace URI and local name, each a simple value, an XmpArray or an XmpStruct, with typed getters and setters for what apps ask for most (Dublin Core, XMP Basic, Photoshop and TIFF properties). An unedited packet writes back byte for byte; an edited one is written as canonical RDF/XML with padding, keeping every property it does not know, qualifiers included. XmpNamespaces The namespace URIs of the XMP schemas apps use most. XmpStruct An XMP structure: named fields, each a simple value (string), an XmpArray or another XmpStruct, such as Iptc4xmpCore:CreatorContactInfo. XmpData holds its top-level properties the same way. Structs ExifFraction A rational EXIF value, such as an exposure time of 1/250 or an aperture of 28/10. ExifKey An EXIF tag: its number and the IFD it lives in. The named keys cover the tags most programs read and write. GeoPosition A position from the GPS tags of an EXIF block. IptcKey An IPTC-IIM dataset: its record and dataset numbers, as "2:25" for keywords. The named keys cover the datasets news, stock and photo software read and write; any other pair works too. Resolution Physical pixel density. XmpName An XMP property name: a namespace URI and a local name, such as dc:title. Prefixes vary between files, so Egami never matches on them; XmpNamespaces holds the URIs of the common schemas. Enums ColorSpaceHint What the raster's pixel values mean, as far as the file said. ExifIfd The image file directories (IFDs) an EXIF block holds its tags in. ExifType The TIFF data types EXIF values are stored as. FrameBlend How a frame is combined with what is already on the canvas. FrameDisposal What happens to a frame's area before the next frame is drawn. ImageOrientation How stored pixels must be turned to show the image upright: the EXIF Orientation tag (274). The value says which way the camera was held; AutoOrient applies it. ResolutionUnit The unit of a Resolution. XmpArrayKind The three kinds of XMP array.

Draws the picture on a canvas: in points from the canvas's origin (the frame's corner there), or with its frame stretched to box exactly, as Word stretches a picture to its frame. Drawing calls only the public canvas API, so a raster canvas, a PDF page, SvgCanvas or a PictureRecorder receive the same calls. It never throws on content: what it cannot draw is skipped and reported to the context's diagnostics. public void Draw(Canvas canvas, RectF? box = null, MetafileRenderOptions? options = null) Parameters canvas Canvas The canvas. box RectF? The rectangle to stretch the frame to, in the canvas's coordinates, or null. options MetafileRenderOptions Fonts, antialiasing and playback, or null for the defaults. Reads a WMF, EMF, WMZ or EMZ stream from its current position to its end. public static Metafile Load(Stream stream, MetafileLoadOptions? options = null) Parameters stream Stream The stream; it is read to its end and left open. options MetafileLoadOptions How to read it, or null for the defaults. Returns Metafile The metafile. Examples // Untrusted files: the context's limits bound the file size and what EMZ and WMZ inflate to; a record that runs past // the end is skipped with a warning, and what came before it plays. Returns Metafile The metafile. Examples // WMF, EMF and EMF+ alike, and the gzip forms WMZ and EMZ. api/Egami.MipChain.html.summary: Class MipChain Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll A chain of ever-halved copies of an image, for making many smaller sizes fast: each resize starts from the smallest level that is still at least twice the target, so a gallery of thumbnail sizes reads each source pixel about once instead of once per size. Level 0 is the source itself; each next level halves the size, rounding up, by averaging 2 × 2 blocks of premultiplied pixels. public sealed class MipChain : IDisposable Inheritance object MipChain Implements IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A responsive image set: one chain, then each width from the smallest level at least twice its size. using MipChain chain = MipChain.Build(photo); foreach (int width in (int[])[320, 240, 160, 120, 80]) { using Raster thumbnail = chain.Fit(width, width, ResampleFilter.Lanczos2); thumbnail.Save($"egret-{width}.png"); } Remarks The levels together take a third more memory than the source. Every frame of an animation gets its levels. The chain does not copy or dispose the source, which must outlive it; disposing the chain frees the levels it made. Properties Levels Gets the levels, from the source (level 0) down to 1 × 1. public IReadOnlyList<Raster> Levels { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<Raster> Exceptions ObjectDisposedException The chain has been disposed. Hocr Reads and writes hOCR, the HTML format that Tesseract, OCRopus, kraken and others write: pages (ocr_page), lines (ocr_line and its kin) and words (ocrx_word) with their bbox, x_wconf, textangle and lang. OcrResult The text an engine found in one image: lines of words, in reading order. OcrWord One recognized word. api/Egami.Operations.BlendMode.html.title: Enum BlendMode | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.BlendMode.html.summary: Enum BlendMode Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll How a source color is combined with the destination under it: the twelve Porter–Duff operators, Plus and Modulate, and the separable and non-separable blend modes of the W3C Compositing and Blending specification, plus Add and Subtract. Blend modes (Multiply to Luminosity) blend the colors where both are present, then composite source-over. The values are fixed: they never change between releases. public enum BlendMode Fields Add = 25 The sum of the colors, clamped: B = min(1, Cs + Cd) (Photoshop's Linear Dodge). Clear = 1 Both are removed: the result is transparent. Color = 29 The source's hue and saturation with the destination's luminosity: tints a gray image. ColorBurn = 20 Darkens the destination to reflect the source: B = 1 − min(1, (1 − Cd) / Cs). ColorDodge = 19 Brightens the destination to reflect the source: B = min(1, Cd / (1 − Cs)). Darken = 17 The darker of the two colors, per channel. Destination = 3 The destination is kept: d. Drawing with it changes nothing. DestinationAtop = 10 The destination on top of the source, only where the source is: s(1 − αd) + d·αs. DestinationIn = 6 The destination where the source is: d·αs. Use it to cut an image to a shape. DestinationOut = 8 The destination where the source is not: d(1 − αs). Use it to punch a shape out of an image. DestinationOver = 4 The destination covers the source: s(1 − αd) + d, drawing behind what is there. Difference = 23 The absolute difference of the colors: B = |Cd − Cs|. Exclusion = 24 Like Difference with lower contrast: B = Cs + Cd − 2·Cs·Cd. HardLight = 21 Multiplies where the source is dark and screens where it is light, as a harsh spotlight would. Hue = 27 The source's hue with the destination's saturation and luminosity. Lighten = 18 The lighter of the two colors, per channel. Luminosity = 30 The source's luminosity with the destination's hue and saturation. Modulate = 13 The product of color and of alpha: s·d. Multiply = 14 Multiplies the colors, which always darkens: B = Cs·Cd. White changes nothing; black gives black. Overlay = 16 Multiplies or screens depending on the destination, raising contrast: HardLight with the layers swapped. Plus = 12 The sum, clamped to 1, of color and of alpha: min(1, s + d) (the W3C "lighter"). Saturation = 28 The source's saturation with the destination's hue and luminosity. Screen = 15 Multiplies the inverted colors, which always lightens: B = Cs + Cd − Cs·Cd. Black changes nothing. SoftLight = 22 Darkens or lightens depending on the source, as a diffused spotlight would (the W3C formula). Source = 2 The source replaces the destination: s. SourceAtop = 9 The source on top of the destination, only where the destination is: s·αd + d(1 − αs). SourceIn = 5 The source where the destination is: s·αd. SourceOut = 7 The source where the destination is not: s(1 − αd). SourceOver = 0 The source covers the destination: s + d(1 − αs). The default, and what every 1.x DrawImage does. Subtract = 26 The source taken from the destination, clamped: B = max(0, Cd − Cs). Xor = 11 Each where the other is not: s(1 − αd) + d(1 − αs). Examples // One enum names every mode. Blend modes (Multiply to Luminosity) blend the colors, then cover what is under them. BlendMode[] darkening = [BlendMode.Multiply, BlendMode.Darken, BlendMode.ColorBurn]; BlendMode[] cutting = [BlendMode.DestinationIn, BlendMode.DestinationOut]; // shape the destination by the image's alpha Remarks Every mode works on premultiplied values; with s the source and d the destination, each with alpha αs and αd. The source's alpha is multiplied by the opacity first, so opacity 0 leaves the destination as it was for every mode except Clear, Source, DestinationAtop, Modulate and the In and Out modes, whose results depend on where the source is.

api/Egami.Operations.BlurMethod.html.title: Enum BlurMethod | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.BlurMethod.html.summary: Enum BlurMethod Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll How Blur(float, ColorSpace, BlurMethod) computes a Gaussian blur. public enum BlurMethod Fields Exact = 0 The exact Gaussian kernel, radius ceil(3σ): what Blur(float, ColorSpace) does. Its cost grows with σ. Fast = 1 Three box passes per axis with fractional end weights, whose variance equals σ² exactly (Gwosdek et al., 2011): the cost per pixel does not grow with σ, and from σ = 3 up the result is within 50 dB PSNR of Exact. Below σ = 2 it runs the exact kernel, which is as cheap there. Examples // A large, soft background blur: Fast costs the same at any sigma and is within 50 dB of the exact Gaussian from sigma 3. using Raster soft = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Blur(40, ColorSpace.Linear, BlurMethod.Fast), Ct);

api/Egami.Operations.ColorSpace.html.summary: Enum ColorSpace Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll The color space in which resizing, blurs and grayscale blend colors: the stored sRGB-encoded values, or linear light. public enum ColorSpace Fields Encoded = 0 Blends the stored sRGB-encoded values, as most libraries and browsers do. The default: faster, and what most people expect. Linear = 1 Converts to linear light, blends, and converts back. Physically correct: fine light detail on dark backgrounds keeps its brightness when reduced. Examples // Lanczos3 is sharper than the default Bicubic; Nearest keeps hard pixel edges (pixel art, masks). using Raster sharp = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Resize(200, 0, ResampleFilter.Lanczos3), Ct); // Blending in linear light keeps fine bright detail on dark backgrounds from going dim when reduced. using Raster linear = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Resize(200, 0, ResampleFilter.Mitchell, ColorSpace.Linear), Ct);

ColorFilter grade = ColorFilter.Curves(ToneCurve.FromPoints([(0, 0), (0.25f, 0.2f), (0.75f, 0.82f), (1, 1)])) .Then(ColorFilter.Saturation(1.1f)); CubeFile.Write("my-grade.cube", grade.ToLut3D(size: 33), title: "My grade"); Lut3D lut = CubeFile.Read("my-grade.cube"); raster.Apply(o => o.ApplyFilter(ColorFilter.Lerp(ColorFilter.Identity, ColorFilter.FromLut(lut), 0.7f)), Ct); // Tables can also be built from a function, and read at any color. Lut3D warm = Lut3D.FromFunction(c => new Vector3(c.X, c.Y * 0.97f, c.Z * 0.9f), size: 17); Vector3 gray = warm.Evaluate(new Vector3(0.5f), LutInterpolation.Tetrahedral); Remarks The reader is strict: every number must parse and be finite, the counts must match the sizes exactly, LUT_3D_SIZE may be at most 256 and LUT_1D_SIZE at most 65,536, and the table is checked against MaxTotalBytes before it is allocated. Anything else throws CorruptDataException naming the line. Methods Read(Stream, EgamiContext?) Reads a .cube file from a stream, which is left open. public static Lut3D Read(Stream stream, EgamiContext? context = null) Parameters stream Stream The stream, read from its current position to its end. context EgamiContext The context whose limits apply, or null for Default. Returns Lut3D The table. Exceptions ArgumentNullException stream is null. CorruptDataException The data breaks the format; the message names the line. LimitExceededException The table would exceed the context's limits. Read(string, EgamiContext?) Reads a .cube file. A 1D-only file becomes a table whose grid changes nothing, behind its 1D table as the shaper. public static Lut3D Read(string path, EgamiContext? context = null) Parameters path string The file. context EgamiContext The context whose limits apply, or null for Default. Returns Lut3D The table. Exceptions ArgumentNullException path is null. CorruptDataException The file breaks the format; the message names the line. LimitExceededException The table would exceed the context's limits. Write(Stream, Lut3D, string?) Writes a table as a .cube file to a stream, which is left open. public static void Write(Stream stream, Lut3D lut, string? title = null) Parameters stream Stream The stream. lut Lut3D The table. title string The TITLE line, or null for none. It may not hold quotes or line breaks. Exceptions ArgumentNullException stream or lut is null. ArgumentException title holds a quote or a line break. InvalidOperationException The table has a shaper whose input range differs per channel from its grid's, which a .cube file cannot hold. Write(string, Lut3D, string?) Writes a table as a .cube file: a 3D table with nine significant digits, behind its shaper as a 1D table when it has one, or an Adobe 1D-only file when the grid changes nothing. Reading the file back gives the same values. public static void Write(string path, Lut3D lut, string? title = null) Parameters path string The file, created or replaced. lut Lut3D The table. title string The TITLE line, or null for none. It may not hold quotes or line breaks. Exceptions ArgumentNullException path or lut is null. ArgumentException title holds a quote or a line break. InvalidOperationException The table has a shaper whose input range differs per channel from its grid's, which a .cube file cannot hold.

api/Egami.Operations.DistantLight.html.summary: Class DistantLight Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll A light infinitely far away, shining from one direction on every pixel, as SVG's feDistantLight. The direction toward the light is (cos Azimuth · cos Elevation, sin Azimuth · cos Elevation, sin Elevation) in the raster's coordinates (y down), which is the vector Skia's DistantLit factories take. public sealed record DistantLight : Light, IEquatable<Light>, IEquatable<DistantLight> Inheritance object Light DistantLight Implements IEquatable<Light> IEquatable<DistantLight> Inherited Members Light.Color object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // Three light sources, as SVG and Skia have them. Positions are pixels: x right, y down, z up out of the image. Light sun = new DistantLight(azimuth: 225, elevation: 40); // from the top left, 40° up Light bulb = new PointLight(new Vector3(60, 20, 80)) { Color = new Rgba8(255, 240, 210, 255) }; Light spot = new SpotLight(new Vector3(0, 0, 150), target: new Vector3(120, 60, 0), exponent: 4, coneAngle: 30); // Two ways a surface reflects: matte (N·L) or shiny (a highlight, (N·H)^shininess). LightingModel matte = LightingModel.Diffuse(kd: 1.2f); LightingModel shiny = LightingModel.Specular(ks: 1, shininess: 20); using Raster<Rgba8> map = logo.Derive(ops => ops.Lighting(sun, matte), Ct); // the light map, opaque using Raster<Rgba8> glints = logo.Derive(ops => ops.Lighting(bulb, shiny), Ct); // alpha = brightest channel using Raster<Rgba8> pool = logo.Derive(ops => ops.Lighting(spot, matte), Ct); Constructors DistantLight(float, float) Initializes a new instance of the DistantLight class. public DistantLight(float azimuth, float elevation) Parameters azimuth float The direction of the light in the image plane, in degrees clockwise from the x axis (y points down), as SVG's azimuth. elevation float The angle of the light above the image plane, in degrees, from −90 to 90; 90 shines straight down. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException azimuth is not finite, or elevation is not from −90 to 90. Properties Azimuth Gets the direction of the light in the image plane, in degrees clockwise from the x axis (y points down). public float Azimuth { get; init; } Property Value float Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is not finite. Elevation Gets the angle of the light above the image plane, in degrees. public float Elevation { get; init; } Property Value float Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is not from −90 to 90.

api/Egami.Operations.EdgeMode.html.title: Enum EdgeMode | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.EdgeMode.html.summary: Enum EdgeMode Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll How a convolution reads taps that fall past the image border. public enum EdgeMode Fields Clamp = 0 Repeats the edge pixel. The default. Mirror = 1 Reflects the image at its border, repeating the edge pixel: c b a | a b c | c b a. Transparent = 3 Reads fully transparent black, so edges fade out. Wrap = 2 Continues from the opposite edge, as if the image were tiled. Examples using Raster soft = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Blur(3), Ct); // Gaussian, sigma in pixels using Raster boxed = photo.Derive(ops => ops.BoxBlur(4), Ct); // fast, radius in pixels using Raster crisp = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Sharpen(0.8f, 1.5f), Ct); // unsharp mask: amount, sigma // Any kernel: here a 3 × 3 emboss, with edges clamped and alpha left alone. ConvolutionKernel emboss = new(3, 3, [-2, -1, 0, -1, 1, 1, 0, 1, 2]); using Raster embossed = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Convolve(emboss, EdgeMode.Clamp, preserveAlpha: true), Ct);

api/Egami.Operations.EdgeOperator.html.title: Enum EdgeOperator | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.EdgeOperator.html.summary: Enum EdgeOperator Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll The kernels Edges(EdgeOperator, bool) finds edges with. Every operator is scaled so a full black-to-white step gives 1 at its strongest pixel; stronger responses (corners, single bright pixels) clamp to 1. public enum EdgeOperator Fields Kirsch = 4 Kirsch's eight 3 × 3 compass kernels (5 on one side, −3 on the others); the strongest response is kept. Laplacian3x3 = 6 The 3 × 3 Laplacian (8 in the middle, −1 around it), as an absolute value: edges come out as thin double lines. Laplacian5x5 = 7 The 5 × 5 Laplacian (24 in the middle, −1 around it), as an absolute value. LaplacianOfGaussian = 8 The 5 × 5 Laplacian of Gaussian (16 in the middle, then −2, −1), as an absolute value: smoothed against noise. Prewitt = 2 Prewitt's 3 × 3 pair, weights 1, 1, 1 across the derivative. RobertsCross = 3 Roberts' 2 × 2 cross of diagonal differences, the pixel and the one below and to its right: the sharpest and noisiest. Robinson = 5 Robinson's eight 3 × 3 compass kernels with weights 1, 2, 1 (Sobel's, turned in 45° steps); the strongest response is kept. Scharr = 1 Scharr's 3 × 3 pair (weights 3, 10, 3), whose magnitude depends least on the edge's direction. Sobel = 0 Sobel and Feldman's 3 × 3 pair, weights 1, 2, 1 across the derivative: the usual choice. Examples using Raster edges = photo.Derive(o => o.Edges(), Ct); // Sobel, gray, 0 to 1 using Raster crisp = photo.Derive(o => o.Edges(EdgeOperator.Scharr), Ct); // rotation-steady using Raster colored = photo.Derive(o => o.Edges(EdgeOperator.Sobel, grayscale: false), Ct); // per channel using Raster lines = photo.Derive(o => o.Blur(1).Edges(EdgeOperator.Laplacian3x3), Ct); // second derivative

api/Egami.Operations.EqualizeMode.html.summary: Enum EqualizeMode Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll What Equalize(EqualizeMode, bool) equalizes. public enum EqualizeMode Fields Channels = 1 Red, green and blue, each by its own histogram, as ImageMagick's -equalize does: stronger, but it shifts colors. Luminance = 0 Lightness: L* of Lab is equalized and a* and b* are kept, so colors do not shift. The default. Examples // Spread the lightness evenly without shifting colors, or each channel on its own as ImageMagick's -equalize. using Raster<Rgba8> even = raster.Derive(o => o.Equalize(EqualizeMode.Luminance), Ct); using Raster<Rgba8> strong = raster.Derive(o => o.Equalize(EqualizeMode.Channels), Ct);

Luminance = 1 The Rec. 709 luminance of the stored (encoded) color, as ImageMagick's -shade: light is high, dark is low. Examples // A photo's luminance as the height: light areas stand up. api/Egami.Operations.Homography.html.summary: Struct Homography Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll A 3 × 3 projective matrix in double precision, for perspective transforms. It follows Matrix3x2's conventions: points are row vectors, so [x, y, 1] × H = [X, Y, W] and the point lands at (X / W, Y / W); A * B applies A first, then B. Coordinates are in pixels with the origin at the top-left corner of the top-left pixel, so pixel centers sit at +0.5. public readonly struct Homography : IEquatable<Homography> Implements IEquatable<Homography> Inherited Members object.Equals(object, object) object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Examples // The four corners of a page photographed at an angle, top-left first and clockwise... Vector2[] corners = [new(120, 60), new(560, 40), new(600, 430), new(80, 420)]; // ...go to the corners of an upright 420 × 594 (A4-shaped) canvas. Homography straighten = Homography.FromQuad(corners, new Rect(0, 0, 420, 594)); using Raster page = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Transform(straighten, new TransformOptions { Viewport = new Rect(0, 0, 420, 594) }), Ct); // Homography maps points too, and inverts. Vector2 middle = straighten.Map(new Vector2(340, 240)); bool invertible = straighten.TryInvert(out Homography back); Remarks default(Homography) is all zeros, which maps nothing; start from Identity or a factory. api/Egami.Operations.IRasterOperation.ht.title: Interface IRasterOperation | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.IRasterOperation.ht.summary: Interface IRasterOperation Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll One step of an operation chain. Built-in operations implement it, and so can callers: add one to a chain with Add(IRasterOperation). public interface IRasterOperation Examples /// <summary>Swaps red and blue, in parallel bands of rows.</summary> public sealed class SwapRedBlue : IRasterOperation { public Size OutputSize(Size input) => input; public void Run<TPixel>(OperationInput<TPixel> input) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> { input.ForEachBand((start, end) => { for (int y = start; y < end; y++) { Span<TPixel> source = input.Source.Row(y); Span<TPixel> destination = input.Destination.Row(y); for (int x = 0; x < source.Length; x++) { Vector4 v = source[x].ToScaled(); destination[x] = TPixel.FromScaled(new Vector4(v.Z, v.Y, v.X, v.W)); } } }); } } Remarks Implementations must be stateless or immutable: one instance runs on every frame and may run on several threads. Methods OutputSize(Size) Returns the frame size after this operation, so the pipeline can plan memory before any pixel changes. Size OutputSize(Size input) Parameters input Size The frame size before it. Returns Size The size after it. Return input for operations that keep the size. Exceptions ArgumentException The operation cannot apply to a frame of this size. Run<TPixel>(OperationInput<TPixel>) Runs the operation on one frame: reads Source and writes every pixel of Destination. The two can be the same plane, so an operation must handle working in place. void Run<TPixel>(OperationInput<TPixel> input) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> Parameters input OperationInput<TPixel> The planes, context and cancellation token. Type Parameters TPixel The pixel type.

api/Egami.Operations.IWarp.html.title: Interface IWarp | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.IWarp.html.summary: Interface IWarp Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll A general warp: a mapping from each output pixel back to the source point it shows. Egami samples the points with the same sampler as Transform(Homography, TransformOptions?), so every warp gets antialiasing where it shrinks the image, and edge modes. Positions are in pixels with the origin at the top-left corner of the top-left pixel, so pixel centers sit at +0.5. public interface IWarp Examples // Any mapping from output points back to source points; the sampler antialiases wherever it shrinks the image. IWarp ripple = Warp.FromFunction(p => new Vector2(p.X + (6 * MathF.Sin(p.Y / 15)), p.Y)); using Raster rippled = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Warp(ripple, new SamplingOptions { Edges = EdgeMode.Mirror }), Ct); // The same as an IWarp, mapping a whole row per call: no per-pixel delegate, so it is faster. using Raster again = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Warp(new Ripple(6, 15), new SamplingOptions { Edges = EdgeMode.Mirror }), Ct); Remarks Map(int, Size, Span<Vector2>) is called for every output row, from several threads at once, so an implementation must be stateless or immutable. The sampler finds each pixel's footprint from the points its neighbours map to, so a warp only maps points, never derivatives. Methods Map(int, Size, Span<Vector2>) Fills source with the source point of every output pixel center in row y: element x is where output point (x + 0.5, y + 0.5) comes from. A NaN coordinate marks a pixel with no source, which shows the background. void Map(int y, Size input, Span<Vector2> source) Parameters y int The output row. input Size The input size. source Span<Vector2> One point per output column. OutputSize(Size) Returns the size of the warped image for an input of input. Size OutputSize(Size input) Parameters input Size The input size. Returns Size The output size; return input for a warp that keeps the size.

api/Egami.Operations.Lut3D.html.summary: Class Lut3D Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll A 3D color lookup table: an N × N × N grid of output RGB values over the input cube, with red varying fastest, as .cube files and Hald images store it, and an optional 1D shaper per channel read before the grid (DaVinci Resolve's 1D-plus-3D .cube). ColorFilter grade = ColorFilter.Curves(ToneCurve.FromPoints([(0, 0), (0.25f, 0.2f), (0.75f, 0.82f), (1, 1)])) .Then(ColorFilter.Saturation(1.1f)); CubeFile.Write("my-grade.cube", grade.ToLut3D(size: 33), title: "My grade"); Lut3D lut = CubeFile.Read("my-grade.cube"); raster.Apply(o => o.ApplyFilter(ColorFilter.Lerp(ColorFilter.Identity, ColorFilter.FromLut(lut), 0.7f)), Ct); // Tables can also be built from a function, and read at any color. Lut3D warm = Lut3D.FromFunction(c => new Vector3(c.X, c.Y * 0.97f, c.Z * 0.9f), size: 17); Vector3 gray = warm.Evaluate(new Vector3(0.5f), LutInterpolation.Tetrahedral); Remarks Values are 32-bit floats and may lie outside 0..1; a filter clamps what it reads. Immutable and safe to share between threads. Properties DomainMax Gets the input that maps to the last grid point on each axis (DOMAIN_MAX in a .cube file). Defaults to 1. public Vector3 DomainMax { get; } Property Value Vector3 DomainMin Gets the input that maps to the first grid point on each axis (DOMAIN_MIN in a .cube file). Defaults to 0. public Vector3 DomainMin { get; } Property Value Vector3 this[int, int, int] Gets one grid point's output. public Vector3 this[int red, int green, int blue] { get; } Parameters red int The red index, 0 to Size − 1. green int The green index. blue int The blue index. Property Value Vector3 The output color. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException An index is out of range. ShaperSize Gets the number of entries in the 1D shaper read before the grid, or 0 when there is none. public int ShaperSize { get; } Property Value int Size Gets the number of grid points along each axis. public int Size { get; } Property Value int Methods Evaluate(Vector3, LutInterpolation) Returns the table's output for one color. public Vector3 Evaluate(Vector3 color, LutInterpolation interpolation = LutInterpolation.Tetrahedral) Parameters color Vector3 The input; each channel is clamped to the shaper's range, then to the domain. interpolation LutInterpolation How to read between grid points. Defaults to Tetrahedral. Returns Vector3 The output, unclamped. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException interpolation is not defined. FromFunction(Func<Vector3, Vector3>, int) Creates a table by sampling function at every grid point over 0..1. public static Lut3D FromFunction(Func<Vector3, Vector3> function, int size = 33) Parameters function Func<Vector3, Vector3> The color function; it is called only here. size int The points per axis, from 2 to 256. Defaults to 33. Returns Lut3D The table. Exceptions ArgumentNullException function is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException size is outside 2 to 256. ArgumentException The function returned a value that is not finite. FromHald(Raster) Reads a Hald CLUT image, as ImageMagick, G'MIC and RawTherapee write them: a level-L image is L³ × L³ pixels holding an L² table, red fastest, row by row. The image's own color profile is ignored, since it is a table rather than a picture. public static Lut3D FromHald(Raster hald) Parameters hald Raster The image; its first frame is read. Returns Lut3D The table. Exceptions ArgumentNullException hald is null. ArgumentException The image is not square with a side that is a cube from 8 to 4096. FromValues(int, ReadOnlySpan<Vector3>, Vector3?, Vector3?) Creates a table from its grid values, red varying fastest, then green, then blue. public static Lut3D FromValues(int size, ReadOnlySpan<Vector3> values, Vector3? domainMin = null, Vector3? domainMax = null) Parameters size int The points per axis, from 2 to 256. values ReadOnlySpan<Vector3> Exactly size³ finite colors. domainMin Vector3? The input at the first grid point, or null for 0. domainMax Vector3? The input at the last grid point, or null for 1; above domainMin on every axis. Returns Lut3D The table. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException size is outside 2 to 256. ArgumentException The value count is wrong, a value is not finite, or the domain is empty. ToHald(int) Writes the table as a Hald image of level: (level²)³ grid points in a level³ × level³ 16-bit image, for grading in an editor and loading back with FromHald(Raster). public Raster<Rgba16> ToHald(int level = 8) Parameters level int The Hald level, from 2 to 16. Defaults to 8 (a 512 × 512 image holding a 64³ table). Returns Raster<Rgba16> The image; the caller disposes it. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException level is outside 2 to 16. WithShaper(ReadOnlySpan<Vector3>, float, float) Returns this table with a 1D shaper read before it, as the first table of a 1D-plus-3D .cube file. public Lut3D WithShaper(ReadOnlySpan<Vector3> shaper, float inputMin = 0, float inputMax = 1) Parameters shaper ReadOnlySpan<Vector3> From 2 to 65,536 finite RGB entries, the first for inputMin and the last for inputMax. inputMin float The input at the shaper's first entry. Defaults to 0. inputMax float The input at its last entry, above inputMin. Defaults to 1. Returns Lut3D The table with the shaper, replacing any it had. Lut3D warm = Lut3D.FromFunction(c => new Vector3(c.X, c.Y * 0.97f, c.Z * 0.9f), size: 17); Vector3 gray = warm.Evaluate(new Vector3(0.5f), LutInterpolation.Tetrahedral);
