api/Egami.Operations.MorphologyOp.html.title: Enum MorphologyOp | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.MorphologyOp.html.summary: Enum MorphologyOp Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll The operations of Morphology(MorphologyOp, StructuringElement, int), all flat (gray-level) and per channel. public enum MorphologyOp Fields BottomHat = 6 The Close minus the image: the dark details smaller than the shape. Alpha is kept. Close = 3 Dilate, then erode: fills dark gaps and holes smaller than the shape. Never darkens a pixel. Dilate = 0 The maximum over the shape: light areas grow, dark specks vanish. Erode = 1 The minimum over the shape: light areas shrink, light specks vanish. Gradient = 4 Dilate minus erode: the outlines of shapes, as wide as the shape. Alpha is kept. Open = 2 Erode, then dilate: removes light details smaller than the shape and keeps the rest. Never brightens a pixel. TopHat = 5 The image minus its Open: the light details smaller than the shape. Alpha is kept. Examples // Close removes dark specks smaller than the shape (dust and toner dots on the paper) and keeps strokes wider than it; // Open does the opposite, for light pinholes in dark areas. using Raster<Gray8> scan = Raster.Load<Gray8>("scan.tif"); scan.Apply(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.Close, StructuringElement.Disk(1)), Ct); // The outlines of shapes, and the light details smaller than a disk. using Raster outlines = scan.Derive(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.Gradient, StructuringElement.Square(1)), Ct); using Raster details = scan.Derive(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.TopHat, StructuringElement.Disk(5)), Ct);

api/Egami.Operations.NoiseKind.html.title: Enum NoiseKind | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.NoiseKind.html.summary: Enum NoiseKind Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll The noise AddNoise(NoiseKind, float, bool, ulong) adds: ImageMagick's +noise kinds, with values on 0..1 and the amount as ImageMagick's -attenuate. At amount 1 the formulas are ImageMagick's Q16 ones. public enum NoiseKind Fields Gaussian = 0 Normal noise of standard deviation 5/64 × amount (about 20 of 255 levels at amount 1), plus a small part that grows with the value. Impulse = 2 Salt and pepper: each value becomes 0 or 1, each with probability amount / 20. Laplacian = 3 Laplacian (two-sided exponential) noise of scale 5/128 × amount: sharper peaked and heavier tailed than Gaussian. Multiplicative = 4 Normal noise proportional to the value: v × (1 + amount / 4 × N(0, 1)), so dark areas stay clean. Poisson = 5 Photon (shot) noise: a Poisson count of mean 12.5 × amount × v, scaled back, so the variance is v / (12.5 × amount). Uniform = 1 Uniform noise, ±amount / 128. Examples // Film grain: gray Gaussian noise at a third of ImageMagick's default strength; the same seed gives the same grain. photo.Apply(ops => ops.AddNoise(NoiseKind.Gaussian, 0.3f, monochrome: true, seed: 42), Ct);

Examples using Raster alpha = photo.Derive(ops => ops.AlphaToGray(), Ct); // see the transparency as gray using Raster cutout = photo.Derive(ops => ops.CopyAlpha(new Mask(matte)), Ct); // a gray image becomes the alpha using Raster onWhite = cutout.Derive(ops => ops.Flatten(Rgba8.White), Ct); // composite onto white, opaque using Raster luma = photo.Derive(ops => ops.LuminanceToAlpha(), Ct); // brightness becomes alpha ApplyFilter(ColorFilter) Runs a ColorFilter on every pixel. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A look as a value: build it once, mix it in at 70%, apply it to any image or to your own pixels. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Fix a dull scan: stretch it to the full range, clipping the darkest 2% and lightest 1%, then set the midtones. raster.Apply(o => o.Normalize().AutoGamma(), Ct); // Or stretch each channel on its own, which also removes a cast. raster.Apply(o => o.AutoLevel(linked: false), Ct); // Measured steps measure only their scope: here the sky alone is stretched. raster.Apply(o => o.Within(new Rect(0, 0, raster.Width, raster.Height / 3), sky => sky.AutoLevel()), Ct); AutoOrient() Turns the image the way its EXIF orientation says, so it looks as the camera meant, and sets the orientation to Normal. Smooths while keeping edges (Tomasi and Manduchi's bilateral filter): each neighbour counts by its distance, through a Gaussian of spatialSigma, and by how much its color differs, through a Gaussian of rangeSigma, so noise flattens and edges stay. The color difference is the root-mean-square difference of red, green and blue on 0..1, so on a gray image the sigmas mean what ImageMagick's -bilateral-blur WxW+(255·rangeSigma)+spatialSigma means. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Smooth skin or sky while keeping edges: neighbours count less the more their color differs (0.1 on the 0..1 scale). using Raster smooth = photo.Derive(ops => ops.BilateralBlur(spatialSigma: 4, rangeSigma: 0.1f), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A sigma is not positive and finite or above its limit, or radius is negative or above 100. Gamma(float) Raises red, green and blue to 1/gamma, as ImageMagick's -gamma: 2.2 brightens. See Gamma(float). public RasterOps Gamma(float gamma) Parameters gamma float The gamma, above 0. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A basic tone panel: levels with a midtone lift, a gentle S-curve, and a warm tint in the midtones. The three steps run as // one pass over the pixels. raster.Apply(o => o .Level(black: 0.04f, white: 0.96f, gamma: 1.1f) .SigmoidalContrast(4, midpoint: 0.5f) .Tint(new Rgba8(255, 200, 150, 255), 0.15f), Ct); raster.Save("duck-toned.jpg"); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException gamma is not a positive finite number. Glow(float, Rgba8, float, bool) Adds a glow around the image's alpha shape, as an editor's outer glow layer style: the alpha, blurred with Fast, spread, and filled with color, drawn behind the image. With inner the glow comes in from the shape's edges instead and is drawn on the image, inside the shape only. It is exactly the chain written by hand: a layer made with a ColorMatrix(ColorMatrix) (the color, and alpha or 1 − alpha), Blur(float, ColorSpace, BlurMethod), Arithmetic(PixelMath, float, ColorChannels) multiplying alpha by 1 / (1 − spread) and Opacity(float) for the color's alpha, then drawn with DrawImage (the image over the layer, or the layer over the image with SourceAtop). An opaque image has no edge to glow from. public RasterOps Glow(float sigma, Rgba8 color, float spread = 0, bool inner = false) Parameters sigma float The glow's blur in pixels, from 0 to 1000. color Rgba8 The glow's color, with its alpha as the glow's opacity. spread float How much the glow is hardened before it fades, from 0 (a plain blur) to just under 1 (a hard edge): the blurred alpha is divided by 1 − spread. inner bool Whether the glow is inside the shape instead of around it. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A soft yellow glow around the badge, behind it; spread hardens it before it fades. using Raster outer = logo.Derive(ops => ops.Glow(8, new Rgba8(255, 210, 0, 230), spread: 0.3f), Ct); // A white glow coming in from the badge's edges, inside it only. using Raster inner = logo.Derive(ops => ops.Glow(5, Rgba8.White, inner: true), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException sigma is outside 0..1000, or spread is outside 0 to under 1. Grayscale(LumaWeights, float, ColorSpace) Converts toward gray. By default the luma is taken from the stored, gamma-encoded values, as CSS filters do; pass Linear to weigh the colors in linear light, which keeps perceived brightness better. public RasterOps Grayscale(LumaWeights mode = LumaWeights.Rec709, float amount = 1, ColorSpace colorSpace = ColorSpace.Encoded) Parameters mode LumaWeights The luma weights. Defaults to Rec709. amount float 0 changes nothing, 1 gives full gray. colorSpace ColorSpace Where the luma is taken. Defaults to Encoded. Returns RasterOps This builder. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException An argument is out of range. HighContrast(bool, ContrastInvert, float) Skia's high-contrast accessibility filter. See HighContrast(bool, ContrastInvert, float). public RasterOps HighContrast(bool grayscale = false, ContrastInvert invert = ContrastInvert.None, float contrast = 0) Parameters grayscale bool Whether colors become gray first. invert ContrastInvert How to invert. Defaults to None. contrast float The contrast, from −1 to 1. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A two-color poster, then a check of how it reads to someone with deuteranopia. raster.Apply(o => o.Duotone(Rgba8.FromHex("#1b2a49"), Rgba8.FromHex("#f2c14e")).Posterize(4, DitherMode.Ordered), Ct); using Raster<Rgba8> preview = raster.Derive(o => o.SimulateColorBlindness(ColorVisionDeficiency.Deuteranopia), Ct); // High contrast for low vision: gray, lightness inverted so dark becomes light, and more contrast. using Raster<Rgba8> readable = raster.Derive(o => o.HighContrast(grayscale: true, ContrastInvert.Lightness, contrast: 0.3f), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException An argument is out of range. HueRotate(float) Rotates hue around the luma axis. See HueRotate(float). public RasterOps HueRotate(float degrees) Parameters degrees float The angle; 0 changes nothing. Returns RasterOps This builder. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException degrees is not finite. InnerShadow(float, float, float, Rgba8) Adds a shadow inside the image's alpha shape, as an editor's inner shadow layer style: everything outside the shape, moved by (dx, dy) rounded to whole pixels, blurred with Fast and filled with color, drawn on the image inside the shape only. Past the image's edges counts as outside, so a shape that touches an edge is shadowed from there too. It is exactly the chain written by hand: a layer made with a ColorMatrix(ColorMatrix) (the color, and 1 − alpha), Offset(int, int, EdgeMode, Rgba8) with the uncovered strips filled with the opaque color, Blur(float, ColorSpace, BlurMethod) and Opacity(float) for the color's alpha, then drawn over the image with SourceAtop. public RasterOps InnerShadow(float dx, float dy, float sigma, Rgba8 color) Parameters dx float How far the shadow moves right, in pixels (negative moves it left), at most 10000 either way. dy float How far the shadow moves down, in pixels, at most 10000 either way. sigma float The shadow's blur in pixels, from 0 (a hard shadow) to 1000. color Rgba8 The shadow's color, with its alpha as the shadow's opacity. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A shadow inside the badge, cast from up and left, as a pressed button looks. using Raster pressed = logo.Derive(ops => ops.InnerShadow(2, 3, 3, new Rgba8(0, 0, 0, 140)), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException An offset is not finite or beyond 10000 either way, or sigma is outside 0..1000. Invert(float) Replaces red, green and blue with 1 − value, blended by amount. See Invert(float). public RasterOps Invert(float amount = 1) Parameters amount float 0 changes nothing, 1 inverts fully. Returns RasterOps This builder. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException amount is outside 0..1. Kuwahara(int, float) Smooths while keeping edges, with the Kuwahara filter as ImageMagick's -kuwahara defines it: of the four (r + 1) squares that have the pixel as a corner, the one whose luma varies least gives the pixel its value, sampled at that square's middle. With sigma above 0 the image is blurred first with ImageMagick's kernel for radius x sigma (a Gaussian of σ out to the radius). The variances come from summed-area tables, so the cost does not grow with the radius. public RasterOps Kuwahara(int radius = 3, float sigma = 0) Parameters radius int The radius in pixels, from 1 to 100. sigma float The blur before, in pixels, from 0 (none) to 100. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Flattens texture into patches while keeping edges; a small blur first, as ImageMagick's -kuwahara 4x1. using Raster smooth = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Kuwahara(4, sigma: 1), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException radius is outside 1..100, or sigma is outside 0..100. LensBlur(float, LensBlurOptions?) Blurs as an out-of-focus lens does: each point spreads into the aperture's shape, a disc or a polygon of 5 to 12 blades, so small lights become discs, unlike a Gaussian's soft spots. Works in linear light by default, since a lens adds light; HighlightGain makes bright lights bloom. The cost does not grow with the radius: the blur runs by FFT on tiles. Edges repeat the edge pixel. public RasterOps LensBlur(float radius, LensBlurOptions? options = null) Parameters radius float The aperture's radius in pixels, from 0 (changes nothing) to 128. options LensBlurOptions The aperture and highlights, or null for a round aperture in linear light. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Blur the background like a wide-open lens with a six-blade aperture: bright points become hexagons. LensBlurOptions lens = new() { Blades = 6, Rotation = 15, HighlightGain = 4, HighlightThreshold = 0.8f }; photo.Apply(ops => ops.Within(new Rect(0, 0, photo.Width, photo.Height / 3), o => o.LensBlur(12, lens)), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException radius is negative, not finite or above 128, or an option is out of range: blades other than 0 or 5 to 12, a rotation that is not finite, a gain below 1 or not finite, a threshold outside 0..1, or an undefined color space. Level(float, float, float, float, float) Stretches black..white to outputBlack..outputWhite with a midtone gamma, as ImageMagick's -level and +level. See Level(float, float, float, float, float). public RasterOps Level(float black = 0, float white = 1, float gamma = 1, float outputBlack = 0, float outputWhite = 1) Parameters black float The input that becomes outputBlack, from 0 to 1. white float The input that becomes outputWhite, from 0 to 1. gamma float The midtone gamma, above 0: above 1 brightens. outputBlack float The output for black, from 0 to 1. outputWhite float The output for white, from 0 to 1. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A basic tone panel: levels with a midtone lift, a gentle S-curve, and a warm tint in the midtones. The three steps run as // one pass over the pixels. raster.Apply(o => o .Level(black: 0.04f, white: 0.96f, gamma: 1.1f) .SigmoidalContrast(4, midpoint: 0.5f) .Tint(new Rgba8(255, 200, 150, 255), 0.15f), Ct); raster.Save("duck-toned.jpg"); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A value is out of range, or black equals white. Lighting(Light, LightingModel, LightingOptions?) Lights the image as a height field with the SVG 1.1 lighting filters (feDiffuseLighting and feSpecularLighting), with Skia's parameters: the height channel (alpha by default) times SurfaceScale is a surface, its normal comes from SVG's Sobel stencils (with SVG's own stencils on the edges and corners), and the light's color is scaled by N·L (Diffuse(float)) or (N·H)^shininess (Specular(float, float)). The result is the light map (opaque for diffuse; for specular, alpha is the largest color channel), or, with Blend, the light map blended onto the image, which keeps its alpha. Light is computed on stored values, as Skia does in its working space; SVG's default of linear light is not applied. public RasterOps Lighting(Light light, LightingModel model, LightingOptions? options = null) Parameters light Light The light: DistantLight, PointLight or SpotLight, in pixel coordinates. model LightingModel How the surface reflects: Diffuse(float) or Specular(float, float); the default value is a diffuse model with kd 0, which is black. options LightingOptions The surface scale, height channel and blend; null for the defaults. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A photo's luminance as the height: light areas stand up. SurfaceScale is the height of white, in pixels. LightingOptions relief = new() { Height = HeightSource.Luminance, SurfaceScale = 6 }; using Raster lit = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Lighting(new DistantLight(300, 50), LightingModel.Diffuse(), relief), Ct); // The same light blended onto the photo instead of replacing it. using Raster shaded = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Lighting(new DistantLight(300, 50), LightingModel.Diffuse(1.3f), relief with { Blend = BlendMode.Overlay }), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentNullException light is null. LocalContrast(float, float) Brings out local detail, as ImageMagick's -local-contrast: L* is pushed away from a wide blur of itself by strength, so large-scale light changes less than detail. a* and b* are kept. public RasterOps LocalContrast(float radius = 0.1, float strength = 0.125) Parameters radius float The blur radius as a fraction of 20% of the longer side, above 0 and at most 1; the default 0.1 blurs over 2%. strength float How strongly detail is raised, 0 or more; the default 0.125 is ImageMagick's 12.5%. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Bring out detail in a flat, foggy landscape: CLAHE on 8 × 8 tiles, then ImageMagick's local contrast. raster.Apply(o => o.Clahe(tilesX: 8, tilesY: 8, clipLimit: 2).LocalContrast(radius: 0.1f, strength: 0.15f), Ct); Remarks Two lightness planes, 4 bytes a pixel each, count against MaxTotalBytes. Inside a rectangle or mask, the scope is its image. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException An argument is out of range. LuminanceToAlpha() Sets alpha to the luminance of the stored values, 0.212656 R + 0.715158 G + 0.072186 B (the Rec. 709 weights as ImageMagick derives them from the sRGB primaries), and keeps the color, exactly as ImageMagick's -alpha copy does; on a gray raster this turns the gray into alpha. A color matrix, so it fuses with neighbouring color steps. To also black out the color, as Skia's luma filter does, follow it with OnChannels(ColorChannels.Color, o => o.FillColor(Rgba8.Black)). public RasterOps LuminanceToAlpha() Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples using Raster alpha = photo.Derive(ops => ops.AlphaToGray(), Ct); // see the transparency as gray using Raster cutout = photo.Derive(ops => ops.CopyAlpha(new Mask(matte)), Ct); // a gray image becomes the alpha using Raster onWhite = cutout.Derive(ops => ops.Flatten(Rgba8.White), Ct); // composite onto white, opaque using Raster luma = photo.Derive(ops => ops.LuminanceToAlpha(), Ct); // brightness becomes alpha MakeTransparent(Rgba8, float, float) Makes pixels within tolerance of color transparent, keeping their color, by ImageMagick's -fuzz distance, so with no softness the result equals ImageMagick's -fuzz with -transparent. softness ramps alpha up over the next band of distance, for antialiased edges and green screens. public RasterOps MakeTransparent(Rgba8 color, float tolerance = 0, float softness = 0) Parameters color Rgba8 The color to remove, with its alpha (opaque for most keys). tolerance float The color distance that becomes fully transparent, from 0 (the exact color) to 1 (every color). softness float The band of distance beyond the tolerance over which alpha returns to full; 0 for a hard edge. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Remove a green screen: within 0.15 of pure green becomes transparent, and alpha ramps back over the next 0.1 for soft edges. photo.Apply(ops => ops.MakeTransparent(new Rgba8(0, 177, 64, 255), tolerance: 0.15f, softness: 0.1f), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException tolerance is outside 0..1, or softness is negative or not finite. Median(int, bool) Replaces each channel with its median over the (2r + 1) square around the pixel, as ImageMagick's -statistic Median does: removes salt-and-pepper noise while keeping edges. Works on stored values, so 8 and 16-bit results are exact; edges repeat the edge pixel. The cost per pixel does not grow with the radius on byte types. public RasterOps Median(int radius, bool includeAlpha = false) Parameters radius int The radius in pixels, from 0 (changes nothing) to 100. includeAlpha bool Whether alpha gets its own median too; by default it is kept. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Salt-and-pepper noise disappears and edges stay sharp; radius 2 is a 5 × 5 window. photo.Apply(ops => ops.Median(2), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException radius is negative or above 100. MergeDuplicates(float) Removes each frame equal to the one before it and adds its delay to the frame that stays, as ImageMagick's -layers RemoveDups: a screen recording that sat still for seconds becomes one long frame. What is on screen at every moment is unchanged. Removed frames take their metadata with them. public RasterOps MergeDuplicates(float tolerance = 0) Parameters tolerance float How far a pixel may differ and still count as equal, by ImageMagick's -fuzz distance, from 0 (the default, exact) to 1. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Shrink a screen recording: merge frames that barely change, drop frames no viewer shows, then resample to 25 fps. recording.Apply(ops => ops.MergeDuplicates(tolerance: 0.01f).DropZeroDelay().Retime(25), Ct); recording.Save("recording.gif"); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException tolerance is outside 0 to 1. Morphology(MorphologyOp, StructuringElement, int) Flat morphology: each channel's maximum (dilate) or minimum (erode) over shape around each pixel, or one of their combinations, as ImageMagick's -morphology. Works on stored values, alpha included, so 8 and 16-bit results are exact; Gradient, TopHat and BottomHat keep alpha. Edges repeat the edge pixel. Rectangles cost the same per pixel at any size; other shapes grow with their height. public RasterOps Morphology(MorphologyOp op, StructuringElement shape, int iterations = 1) Parameters op MorphologyOp The operation. shape StructuringElement The structuring element. iterations int How many times each dilation and erosion runs, 1 to 100: Open with 2 erodes twice, then dilates twice. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Close removes dark specks smaller than the shape (dust and toner dots on the paper) and keeps strokes wider than it; // Open does the opposite, for light pinholes in dark areas. using Raster<Gray8> scan = Raster.Load<Gray8>("scan.tif"); scan.Apply(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.Close, StructuringElement.Disk(1)), Ct); // The outlines of shapes, and the light details smaller than a disk. using Raster outlines = scan.Derive(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.Gradient, StructuringElement.Square(1)), Ct); using Raster details = scan.Derive(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.TopHat, StructuringElement.Disk(5)), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException op is not defined, or iterations is outside 1 to 100. MotionBlur(float, float, float, bool) Streaks the image along a direction, as a camera moving during the exposure, with ImageMagick's -motion-blur meaning: each pixel averages 2⌈radius⌉ + 1 samples one pixel apart, from itself toward angle, weighted by a Gaussian of sigma from the pixel. Samples between pixels are read bilinearly; edges repeat the edge pixel. public RasterOps MotionBlur(float radius, float sigma, float angle, bool centered = false) Parameters radius float Half the streak's length in pixels, from 0 (changes nothing) to 127. sigma float How fast the weights fall along the streak, above 0. angle float The direction in degrees, clockwise from the x axis (y points down). centered bool Whether the streak runs both ways from the pixel, instead of only toward angle. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples using Raster moving = photo.Derive(ops => ops.MotionBlur(radius: 12, sigma: 4, angle: 15), Ct); // a streak toward 15° using Raster spinning = photo.Derive(ops => ops.RotationalBlur(8), Ct); // 8° around the center using Raster zooming = photo.Derive(ops => ops.ZoomBlur(0.2f, new System.Numerics.Vector2(320, 200)), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException An argument is not finite or out of range. Normalize(bool, bool) ContrastStretch(float, float, bool, bool) at ImageMagick's -normalize points: the darkest 2% of the pixels become black and the lightest 1% white. public RasterOps Normalize(bool linked = true, bool perFrame = false) Parameters linked bool Whether the channels share one pair of points (the default) or each gets its own. perFrame bool Whether each frame is measured alone. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Fix a dull scan: stretch it to the full range, clipping the darkest 2% and lightest 1%, then set the midtones. raster.Apply(o => o.Normalize().AutoGamma(), Ct); // Or stretch each channel on its own, which also removes a cast. raster.Apply(o => o.AutoLevel(linked: false), Ct); // Measured steps measure only their scope: here the sky alone is stretched. raster.Apply(o => o.Within(new Rect(0, 0, raster.Width, raster.Height / 3), sky => sky.AutoLevel()), Ct); Offset(int, int, EdgeMode, Rgba8) Moves the image by whole pixels, right by dx and down by dy, with no resampling. What leaves one side comes in at the other with Wrap (the default, ImageMagick's -roll); with Transparent the uncovered strip is background, as Skia's Offset filter leaves it. public RasterOps Offset(int dx, int dy, EdgeMode edges = EdgeMode.Wrap, Rgba8 background = default) Parameters dx int The horizontal move, in pixels. dy int The vertical move, in pixels. edges EdgeMode What fills the uncovered strips. background Rgba8 The color of uncovered strips under Transparent. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Roll the image half way round, so its edges meet in the middle, which shows whether it tiles seamlessly. using Raster rolled = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Offset(photo.Width / 2, photo.Height / 2), Ct); // Fill a 1920 × 1080 wallpaper with copies of the duck's head. using Raster wallpaper = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Tile(1920, 1080, source: new Rect(380, 60, 160, 160)), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException edges is not defined. OilPaint(int, int) Makes the image look painted, as ImageMagick's -paint does: around each pixel, in the (2r + 1) square, pixels are sorted into levels bins by intensity, and the pixel becomes a pixel of the most common bin, unchanged. With 256 levels on 8-bit images the result is ImageMagick's exactly; fewer levels make larger, flatter strokes. Works on stored values; the histogram slides along each row, so a larger radius costs little more per pixel than the window's size. public RasterOps OilPaint(int radius = 3, int levels = 20) Parameters radius int The brush radius in pixels, from 1 to 50. levels int The number of intensity bins, from 2 to 256. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples using Raster painted = photo.Derive(ops => ops.OilPaint(radius: 4, levels: 20), Ct); using Raster magick = photo.Derive(ops => ops.OilPaint(3, levels: 256), Ct); // ImageMagick's -paint 3, pixel for pixel Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException radius is outside 1..50, or levels is outside 2..256. OnChannels(ColorChannels, Action<RasterOps>) Runs the operations build adds and keeps their result only in channels, as ImageMagick's -channel does: OnChannels(ColorChannels.Alpha, o => o.Blur(2)) softens only the alpha. Channels are the working RGBA, with a gray raster's red, green and blue its gray value. Color steps that fuse into one matrix (Brightness, ShuffleChannels, a color matrix) become that matrix with the other channels left as they are, so they cost nothing extra; other chains run once and the other channels are restored. Combines with Within in either order. public RasterOps OnChannels(ColorChannels channels, Action<RasterOps> build) Parameters channels ColorChannels The channels the result is kept in. build Action<RasterOps> Adds the operations. Each must keep the size, as in Within(Rect, Action<RasterOps>). Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Soften only the alpha; invert only the red. photo.Apply(ops => ops .OnChannels(ColorChannels.Alpha, o => o.Blur(2)) .OnChannels(ColorChannels.Red, o => o.Invert()), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException channels holds values that are not channels. ArgumentNullException build is null. ArgumentException An operation inside would change the size or the color encoding; the message names it. Opacity(float) Multiplies alpha by amount. Has no effect on pixel types without alpha. public RasterOps Opacity(float amount) Parameters amount float 0 makes the image transparent, 1 changes nothing. Returns RasterOps This builder. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException amount is outside 0..1. Pad(int, int, Rgba8, Anchor) Enlarges the canvas to width × height, placing the image at anchor and filling the new area with background. public RasterOps Pad(int width, int height, Rgba8 background = default, Anchor anchor = Anchor.Center) Parameters width int The new width, at least the image's width. height int The new height, at least the image's height. background Rgba8 The color of the new area. Defaults to transparent black. anchor Anchor Where the image sits on the new canvas. Defaults to the center, rounding toward the top left. Returns RasterOps This builder. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A size is less than 1, or smaller than the image when the chain runs (use Crop(Rect) to shrink), or anchor is not defined. Pixelate(int, Point) Pixelates: the image is cut into square cells, and every pixel of a cell becomes the cell's average, taken on premultiplied values so transparent pixels do not darken it. Cells start at origin and repeat every cellSize pixels both ways; cells cut by the image's edges average the pixels they hold. Inside Within(Rect, Action<RasterOps>) cells stay on the image's grid and average whole cells, reading past the area. public RasterOps Pixelate(int cellSize, Point origin = default) Parameters cellSize int The side of a cell in pixels, from 1 (changes nothing) to 4096. origin Point Where a cell's top-left corner falls, in the raster's coordinates; the grid repeats from there both ways. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // 12-pixel cells, each the average of what it covers. using Raster blocks = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Pixelate(12), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException cellSize is outside 1..4096. Posterize(int, DitherMode) Rounds red, green and blue to levels evenly spaced values each, as ImageMagick's -posterize, optionally dithered: ordered dithering adds a fixed 8 × 8 pattern before rounding, Floyd–Steinberg spreads each value's rounding error to its neighbours. Without dithering it is Posterize(int). public RasterOps Posterize(int levels, DitherMode dither = DitherMode.None) Parameters levels int Values per channel, from 2 to 256. dither DitherMode The dithering. Defaults to None. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A two-color poster, then a check of how it reads to someone with deuteranopia. raster.Apply(o => o.Duotone(Rgba8.FromHex("#1b2a49"), Rgba8.FromHex("#f2c14e")).Posterize(4, DitherMode.Ordered), Ct); using Raster<Rgba8> preview = raster.Derive(o => o.SimulateColorBlindness(ColorVisionDeficiency.Deuteranopia), Ct); // High contrast for low vision: gray, lightness inverted so dark becomes light, and more contrast. using Raster<Rgba8> readable = raster.Derive(o => o.HighContrast(grayscale: true, ContrastInvert.Lightness, contrast: 0.3f), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException levels is outside 2 to 256, or dither is not defined. QuadDistort(Vector2, Vector2, Vector2, Vector2, TransformOptions?) Moves the image's four corners to four points, bending it in perspective: ImageMagick's Perspective distort. Corners are pixel edges, so the top-right corner of a 100-pixel-wide image is (100, 0). public RasterOps QuadDistort(Vector2 topLeft, Vector2 topRight, Vector2 bottomRight, Vector2 bottomLeft, TransformOptions? options = null) Parameters topLeft Vector2 Where the top-left corner goes. topRight Vector2 Where the top-right corner goes. bottomRight Vector2 Where the bottom-right corner goes. bottomLeft Vector2 Where the bottom-left corner goes. options TransformOptions The filter, edges, background and viewport, or null for the defaults. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Pin the image onto a trapezoid, as if it lay on a table: its corners go to these four points (pixel edges, so the // image's own corners are (0, 0) and (640, 480)). using Raster onTable = photo.Derive(ops => ops.QuadDistort(new(200, 0), new(440, 0), new(640, 300), new(0, 300)), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentException A point is not finite, three of them lie on one line, or the viewport is empty. Quantize(PaletteOptions?) Reduces each frame to at most MaxColors colors, as a palette format would, but keeps the pixel type: an Rgba16 image stays Rgba16 with at most that many distinct values. Each frame gets its own palette (its own colors when they fit, Wu's quantizer otherwise) unless FixedPalette fixes one, and is dithered as the options say. Use ToIndexed(PaletteOptions?, int) for the indices themselves. public RasterOps Quantize(PaletteOptions? options = null) Parameters options PaletteOptions The color limit, dithering, refinement and matching, or null for Default. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A 16-color poster with Atkinson's dither; the pixel type stays as it was. photo.Apply(ops => ops.Quantize(new PaletteOptions { MaxColors = 16, Dither = DitherMode.Atkinson }), Ct); photo.Save("poster.png"); Reach(Action<RasterOps>) Returns how far a chain reads past each output pixel: the sum of its steps' reaches. Pixel-by-pixel steps (color matrices, arithmetic, color filters, blending a color, keying) reach nothing; blurs, convolutions, morphology, glows and drop shadows reach as far as their kernels and offsets. A step whose reach is unbounded or unknown (a resize, a geometric transform, a histogram step, a custom IRasterOperation) makes the whole chain's reach unknown. public static OperationReach? Reach(Action<RasterOps> build) Parameters build Action<RasterOps> Records the chain, as for Apply(Action<RasterOps>, CancellationToken); it is recorded, not run. Returns OperationReach? The reach, or null when some step's reach is unknown. Examples // How far a chain reads around each pixel: run it on a part of a picture padded by this much, and the part comes out as it // would in the whole picture. OperationReach? reach = RasterOps.Reach(ops => ops.Blur(3).Glow(4, Rgba8.White)); if (reach is OperationReach r) { Console.WriteLine($"pad by {r.X} × {r.Y}"); } // A resize reads the whole image: its reach is unknown. Assert.Null(RasterOps.Reach(ops => ops.Resize(100, 100))); Exceptions ArgumentNullException build is null. Remap(Palette, DitherMode, float) Maps every pixel onto palette, as ImageMagick's -remap: a brand palette, a display's inks, or the palette of another image. The pixel type is kept, and so is each pixel's alpha when the palette is opaque. public RasterOps Remap(Palette palette, DitherMode dither = DitherMode.FloydSteinberg, float strength = 1) Parameters palette Palette The palette. dither DitherMode How the error is spread. Defaults to FloydSteinberg. strength float How strongly, from 0 (the nearest color) to 1 (the default). Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Edit only the sky: a gray mask, white where the edit applies fully, black where it does not, soft in between. photo.Apply(ops => ops .Within(new Mask(sky), o => o.Saturation(1.3f).Contrast(1.1f)) // Or take coverage from a logo's alpha, placed on the photo, and invert the area under it. .Within(new Mask(logo, new Point(20, 20), MaskChannel.Alpha), o => o.Invert()), Ct); Remarks The mask raster must stay undisposed until the chain has run. Masking a raster with itself reads from a copy, made when the step runs. Exceptions ArgumentNullException build is null. ArgumentException The mask has no raster, or an operation inside would change the size or the color encoding. ArgumentOutOfRangeException The mask's channel is not defined. Within(Rect, Action<RasterOps>) Runs the operations build adds so that only pixels inside area change, as if the image were edited through a rectangular hole. Filters read the real pixels around the area, so a blurred rectangle has no seam and equals the whole-image blur there; flips and a 180° turn mirror the area itself. Positions inside (DrawImage, FillColor) are the raster's, as outside. Scopes nest: a rectangle inside a rectangle is their intersection. public RasterOps Within(Rect area, Action<RasterOps> build) Parameters area Rect The rectangle, in the raster's coordinates. It is clipped to the raster; one that misses it changes nothing. build Action<RasterOps> Adds the operations. Each must keep the size: a resize, crop, pad, 90° or free turn, AutoOrient, ConvertColor or ToneMap throws. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Blur a face: only pixels inside the rectangle change, and the blur reads the real pixels around it, so there is no seam. photo.Apply(ops => ops .Within(new Rect(200, 120, 160, 120), o => o.Blur(6)) .Within(new Rect(0, 0, photo.Width, 60), o => o.Brightness(0.8f).Saturation(0.5f)), Ct); // a darker band on top Exceptions ArgumentNullException build is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException area has a negative width or height. ArgumentException An operation inside would change the size or the color encoding; the message names it. ZoomBlur(float, Vector2?) Streaks the image along rays from center, as a zoom during the exposure (Photoshop's radial zoom blur): each pixel averages samples on the ray through it, spanning amount of its distance from the center, half inward and half outward, about one per pixel (at most 256). The center does not move, and a flat image stays flat. public RasterOps ZoomBlur(float amount, Vector2? center = null) Parameters amount float The streak's length as a fraction of the distance from the center, from 0 (changes nothing) to 1. center Vector2? The center in pixels, pixel centers at +0.5, or null for the image's center. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples using Raster moving = photo.Derive(ops => ops.MotionBlur(radius: 12, sigma: 4, angle: 15), Ct); // a streak toward 15° using Raster spinning = photo.Derive(ops => ops.RotationalBlur(8), Ct); // 8° around the center using Raster zooming = photo.Derive(ops => ops.ZoomBlur(0.2f, new System.Numerics.Vector2(320, 200)), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException amount is outside 0..1, or the center is not finite.

api/Egami.Operations.ResampleFilter.html.title: Enum ResampleFilter | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.ResampleFilter.html.summary: Enum ResampleFilter Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll The kernel a resize or rotation uses to blend source pixels. public enum ResampleFilter Fields Bicubic = 0 Keys cubic with a = −0.5 (Catmull-Rom): sharp, with slight ringing at hard edges. The default. Bilinear = 3 A triangle (tent) kernel: smooth and soft, with no ringing. Box = 2 Averages the source pixels each output pixel covers. Good for large reductions of flat artwork. Gaussian = 8 A Gaussian with σ = ½, exp(−2x²), out to 2 pixels, as ImageMagick's Gaussian filter: soft, with no ringing at all. Hermite = 7 The Hermite cubic (B = C = 0), 2|x|³ − 3|x|² + 1 out to 1 pixel: smooth like Bilinear when enlarging, without its corners, and no ringing. Lanczos2 = 6 A two-lobe windowed sinc, sinc(x)·sinc(x / 2) out to 2 pixels, as ImageMagick's Lanczos2: nearly as sharp as Lanczos3 with less ringing, and faster. Lanczos3 = 5 A three-lobe windowed sinc: the sharpest, with the most ringing, and the slowest. Mitchell = 4 Mitchell–Netravali with B = C = 1/3: softer than Bicubic, with less ringing. Nearest = 1 Picks the closest source pixel without blending. Exact and fastest; blocky when enlarging, aliased when shrinking. Spline = 9 The cubic B-spline (B = 1, C = 0) out to 2 pixels: the smoothest cubic, with no ringing and noticeable blur. Examples // Lanczos3 is sharper than the default Bicubic; Nearest keeps hard pixel edges (pixel art, masks). using Raster sharp = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Resize(200, 0, ResampleFilter.Lanczos3), Ct); // Blending in linear light keeps fine bright detail on dark backgrounds from going dim when reduced. using Raster linear = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Resize(200, 0, ResampleFilter.Mitchell, ColorSpace.Linear), Ct);

Examples /// <summary>Black or white per pixel: ForEachBand gives each worker a band of rows from start to end.</summary> private sealed class Threshold(float level) : IRasterOperation { public Size OutputSize(Size input) => input; public void Run<TPixel>(OperationInput<TPixel> input) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> { RowBandAction band = (start, end) => { for (int y = start; y < end; y++) { Span<TPixel> source = input.Source.Row(y), destination = input.Destination.Row(y); for (int x = 0; x < source.Length; x++) { Vector4 v = source[x].ToScaled(); float on = ((0.2126f * v.X) + (0.7152f * v.Y) + (0.0722f * v.Z)) >= level ? 1 : 0; destination[x] = TPixel.FromScaled(new Vector4(on, on, on, v.W)); } } }; input.ForEachBand(band); } }

The inverse lens model, ImageMagick's BarrelInverse distort: each output point at radius r samples the source at radius r / (a·r³ + b·r² + c·r + d), r normalized as for Barrel(double, double, double, double?, Vector2?). The size is kept. public static IWarp BarrelInverse(double a, double b, double c, double? d = null, Vector2? center = null) Parameters a double The cubic coefficient. b double The quadratic coefficient. c double The linear coefficient. d double? The constant term, or null (the default) for 1 − a − b − c. center Vector2? The center of the distortion, or null (the default) for the image's center. Returns IWarp The warp. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A coefficient or the center is not finite. DePolar(float, float, Vector2?, float, float?) Unwraps a circle into a rectangle, ImageMagick's DePolar distort, the inverse of Polar(float, float, Vector2?, float, float?): output columns are angles and rows radii from minRadius to maxRadius around the center. The output is as tall as the radii's difference and as wide as their mean circumference, rounded up. public static IWarp DePolar(float maxRadius = 0, float minRadius = 0, Vector2? center = null, float fromDegrees = -180, float? toDegrees = null) Parameters maxRadius float The outer radius; 0 (the default) for the distance from the center to the nearest edge, −1 for the farthest corner. minRadius float The inner radius, 0 or more and less than the outer. center Vector2? The center, or null (the default) for the image's center. fromDegrees float The angle of the output's left edge. toDegrees float? The angle of its right edge; null (the default) for a full circle. Returns IWarp The warp. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A radius or angle is not finite, or the radii are out of order. Implode(float) Pulls the image toward its center, ImageMagick's -implode; a negative amount pushes it out (explodes). The size is kept. public static IWarp Implode(float amount) Parameters amount float The strength: 0 changes nothing, 1 is strong. Returns IWarp The warp. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException amount is not finite. Magnifier(Rect, float, float) Magnifies the area lens by zoom, as Skia's magnifier filter does: the middle of the lens shows the zoomed image, and over the last inset pixels to the lens's edge it blends back into the surroundings with rounded corners. Outside the lens nothing moves. The size is kept. public static IWarp Magnifier(Rect lens, float zoom, float inset) Parameters lens Rect The lens, in pixels. zoom float The magnification; 1 or less changes nothing, as in Skia. inset float The width of the blending band, 0 or more; 0 gives a hard edge. Returns IWarp The warp. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The lens is empty, or the zoom or inset is out of range or not finite. Polar(float, float, Vector2?, float, float?) Wraps the image around a circle, ImageMagick's Polar distort: the source's columns become angles (0° pointing down, growing counter-clockwise on screen from fromDegrees to toDegrees) and its rows radii, the top row at minRadius and the bottom at maxRadius. The output is the square around the circle, as ImageMagick's +distort sizes it. public static IWarp Polar(float maxRadius = 0, float minRadius = 0, Vector2? center = null, float fromDegrees = -180, float? toDegrees = null) Parameters maxRadius float The outer radius; 0 (the default) for the distance from the center to the nearest edge, −1 for the farthest corner. minRadius float The inner radius, 0 or more and less than the outer. center Vector2? The center, used for the special radii; null (the default) for the image's center. fromDegrees float The angle of the source's left edge. toDegrees float? The angle of its right edge; null (the default) for a full circle. Returns IWarp The warp. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A radius or angle is not finite, or the radii are out of order. Swirl(float, Vector2?, float?) Swirls the image about its center, ImageMagick's -swirl: points turn by degrees at the center, falling to 0 at the radius with the square of the distance. The size is kept; points outside the radius stay put. public static IWarp Swirl(float degrees, Vector2? center = null, float? radius = null) Parameters degrees float The turn at the center; positive turns clockwise. center Vector2? The center, or null (the default) for ImageMagick's, the middle of the image. radius float? The radius, or null (the default) for half the image's larger side; the swirl is stretched to the image's aspect ratio. Returns IWarp The warp. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A value is not finite, or the radius is not more than 0. Wave(float, float) Shifts each column up or down along a sine wave, ImageMagick's -wave: column x moves down by |amplitude| + amplitude × sin(2πx / wavelength). The image grows by twice the amplitude in height. public static IWarp Wave(float amplitude, float wavelength) Parameters amplitude float The wave's height, in pixels. wavelength float The wave's length, in pixels, more than 0. api/Egami.Operations.WhiteBalanceMethod..summary: Enum WhiteBalanceMethod Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll How AutoWhiteBalance(WhiteBalanceMethod, bool) finds the cast to remove. public enum WhiteBalanceMethod Fields GrayWorld = 0 Gray world in Lab, as ImageMagick's -white-balance: the mean a* and b* of the image, weighted by lightness, are taken out of every pixel. The default. WhitePatch = 1 The brightest 1% of the pixels is taken to be white, and the channels are scaled in linear light so it becomes neutral. Examples // Correct a tungsten-lit photo, as a raw editor's temperature slider does. raster.Apply(o => o.WhiteBalance(temperature: 3200), Ct); // Or pick a gray card's color and make it neutral. raster.Apply(o => o.WhiteBalance(new Rgba8(182, 170, 151, 255)), Ct); // Or let the image tell: ImageMagick's gray world, or the brightest pixels as white. raster.Apply(o => o.AutoWhiteBalance(WhiteBalanceMethod.GrayWorld), Ct); raster.Apply(o => o.AutoWhiteBalance(WhiteBalanceMethod.WhitePatch), Ct);

api/Egami.Operations.html.title: Namespace Egami.Operations | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Operations Classes AnimationOverlayOptions Options for DrawAnimation(Raster, Point, AnimationOverlayOptions?). ColorFilter A function of one pixel's color, as a value: build one from a matrix, curves, a 3D table or a tone step, chain filters with Then(ColorFilter), mix two with Lerp(ColorFilter, ColorFilter, float), run one with ApplyFilter(ColorFilter) or on your own pixels with Apply<TPixel>(Span<TPixel>), and save it as a .cube file through ToLut3D(int). Like Skia's SkColorFilter, a filter sees only the pixel's own straight RGBA: no neighbours, position or image statistics, so any chain of filters runs as one pass. Compositor Blends rows of pixels with a BlendMode, for code that composites outside an operation chain: a custom IRasterOperation, a rasterizer filling spans, a layer merge. It runs the kernels DrawImage runs, so Blend<TPixel>(BlendMode, ReadOnlySpan<TPixel>, Span<TPixel>, float, ColorSpace) on a row gives the pixels DrawImage gives there. Every method works for every pixel type, allocates nothing once warm, and is safe to call from many threads at once. ConvolutionKernel A convolution kernel: an odd width and height of weights, applied as laid out (the weight at column 0, row 0 multiplies the pixel up and to the left of the center). The sum is divided by Divisor and Offset is added to the color channels. CubeFile Reads and writes .cube LUT files: the Adobe Cube LUT Specification 1.0 (a 1D or a 3D table, with TITLE, DOMAIN_MIN and DOMAIN_MAX), and DaVinci Resolve's variant with a 1D shaper before the 3D table (LUT_1D_INPUT_RANGE and LUT_3D_INPUT_RANGE). DistantLight A light infinitely far away, shining from one direction on every pixel, as SVG's feDistantLight. The direction toward the light is (cos Azimuth · cos Elevation, sin Azimuth · cos Elevation, sin Elevation) in the raster's coordinates (y down), which is the vector Skia's DistantLit factories take. DropShadowOptions The less common settings of DropShadow(float, float, float, Rgba8, DropShadowOptions?): a different vertical blur, whether the canvas grows, whether only the shadow is kept, and how the blur is computed. LensBlurOptions The aperture and highlights of LensBlur(float, LensBlurOptions?). The defaults give a round aperture in linear light with no highlight boost. Light A light for Lighting(Light, LightingModel, LightingOptions?): DistantLight, PointLight or SpotLight, the three light sources of the SVG 1.1 lighting filters (feDistantLight, fePointLight and feSpotLight), with Skia's parameters. Positions are in pixels of the raster, x to the right, y down and z up out of the image; a pixel's center is at (x + 0.5, y + 0.5), as in Skia. LightingOptions The surface and output settings of Lighting(Light, LightingModel, LightingOptions?). Lut3D A 3D color lookup table: an N × N × N grid of output RGB values over the input cube, with red varying fastest, as .cube files and Hald images store it, and an optional 1D shaper per channel read before the grid (DaVinci Resolve's 1D-plus-3D .cube). Read one with Read(string, EgamiContext?) or FromHald(Raster), and apply it with FromLut(Lut3D, LutInterpolation). OperationInput<TPixel> Everything an operation gets for one frame. PointLight A light at one point, shining in every direction, as SVG's fePointLight and Skia's PointLit factories. RasterOps Animation steps: they work on the frames of the whole animation rather than on each frame, so they run in Apply, Derive and Transcode (which then decodes the whole animation first) but not inside Within. Frames in memory are already full pictures of what is on screen, so there is no Coalesce, and the writers find each frame's changed area themselves, so there is no Optimize. SamplingOptions How a transform or warp samples the source: the filter, the color space it blends in, what samples outside the source read, and the background color. SpotLight A light at one point that shines toward a target, as SVG's feSpotLight and Skia's SpotLit factories. Light falls off away from the axis as cos(angle)^Exponent and stops at ConeAngle, with Skia's soft cone edge. ToneCurve A curve from 0..1 to 0..1 for one channel, as a photo editor's curves dialog draws it: inputs outside 0..1 are clamped first and results are clamped to 0..1. Use one in Curves(ToneCurve); the tone steps (Level, Gamma and the rest) are curves too, evaluated exactly. TransformOptions How a transform samples the source and how large its result is: SamplingOptions plus a viewport. Warp Makes warps from functions. Warps The built-in warps for Warp(IWarp, SamplingOptions?): lens correction, polar and depolar, arc, swirl, wave and implode with ImageMagick's parameter meanings, so its documentation describes them and its results are their reference, and Skia's magnifier. Positions are in pixels with pixel centers at +0.5. Structs ColorMatrix A 4 × 5 color matrix applied to straight (not premultiplied) RGBA scaled to 0..1: each output channel is m[row, 0] × R + m[row, 1] × G + m[row, 2] × B + m[row, 3] × A + m[row, 4], rows in R, G, B, A order, and results are clamped to 0..1. The factories follow the W3C Filter Effects definitions. Homography A 3 × 3 projective matrix in double precision, for perspective transforms. It follows Matrix3x2's conventions: points are row vectors, so [x, y, 1] × H = [X, Y, W] and the point lands at (X / W, Y / W); A * B applies A first, then B. Coordinates are in pixels with the origin at the top-left corner of the top-left pixel, so pixel centers sit at +0.5. LightingModel How a surface reflects light in Lighting(Light, LightingModel, LightingOptions?): Diffuse(float) (SVG's feDiffuseLighting, Lambert's N·L) or Specular(float, float) (feSpecularLighting, Phong–Blinn's (N·H)^shininess), with SVG's and Skia's constants. Mask A raster read as coverage, 0 (none) to full, placed on the image being edited: where an operation inside Within(Mask, Action<RasterOps>) applies and how strongly. The raster may have any size and pixel type; outside it coverage is 0, or full when Inverted. Its first frame is used for every frame. It must stay undisposed until the chain has run. OperationReach How far an operation chain reads past each output pixel, in whole pixels across and down: a pixel of the result can depend on input pixels up to X columns and Y rows away. A blur of σ reaches about 3σ; a color matrix reaches nothing. Reach(Action<RasterOps>) measures a chain, so code that runs one on part of a larger picture, such as a canvas layer, can include the pixels around it that the chain will read. StructuringElement The shape Morphology(MorphologyOp, StructuringElement, int) takes its maximum or minimum over: a set of cells around an origin, which sits on the pixel being computed. The factories make the shapes ImageMagick's -morphology kernels of the same names make (its Plus is Cross(int) here). The default value is the origin alone, which changes nothing. Interfaces IRasterOperation One step of an operation chain. Built-in operations implement it, and so can callers: add one to a chain with Add(IRasterOperation). IWarp A general warp: a mapping from each output pixel back to the source point it shows. Egami samples the points with the same sampler as Transform(Homography, TransformOptions?), so every warp gets antialiasing where it shrinks the image, and edge modes. Positions are in pixels with the origin at the top-left corner of the top-left pixel, so pixel centers sit at +0.5. Enums Anchor Where an image sits inside a larger area, or which part of it is kept when it is cut down. AnimationTiming How DrawAnimation(Raster, Point, AnimationOverlayOptions?) pairs the overlay's frames with the base's. BlendMode How a source color is combined with the destination under it: the twelve Porter–Duff operators, Plus and Modulate, and the separable and non-separable blend modes of the W3C Compositing and Blending specification, plus Add and Subtract. Blend modes (Multiply to Luminosity) blend the colors where both are present, then composite source-over. The values are fixed: they never change between releases. BlurMethod How Blur(float, ColorSpace, BlurMethod) computes a Gaussian blur. ChannelSource Where an output channel of ShuffleChannels(ChannelSource, ChannelSource, ChannelSource, ChannelSource) takes its value from. ColorChannel One channel of a raster's working RGBA, or its luminance, for ExtractChannel(ColorChannel). ColorChannels A set of a raster's working RGBA channels, for OnChannels(ColorChannels, Action<RasterOps>). ColorSpace The color space in which resizing, blurs and grayscale blend colors: the stored sRGB-encoded values, or linear light. ColorVisionDeficiency A color vision deficiency to simulate. Connectivity Which neighbours a flood fill spreads to. ContrastInvert How HighContrast(bool, ContrastInvert, float) inverts, as Skia's high-contrast filter does. DespillColor The screen color whose spill Despill(DespillColor, float, float) removes. EdgeMode How a convolution reads taps that fall past the image border. EdgeOperator The kernels Edges(EdgeOperator, bool) finds edges with. Every operator is scaled so a full black-to-white step gives 1 at its strongest pixel; stronger responses (corners, single bright pixels) clamp to 1. EqualizeMode What Equalize(EqualizeMode, bool) equalizes. HeightSource Which channel Lighting(Light, LightingModel, LightingOptions?) reads as the surface's height. LumaWeights The luma weights a grayscale conversion uses. LutInterpolation How a Lut3D reads between its grid points. MaskChannel Which values of a raster a Mask reads as coverage. MorphologyOp The operations of Morphology(MorphologyOp, StructuringElement, int), all flat (gray-level) and per channel. NoiseKind The noise AddNoise(NoiseKind, float, bool, ulong) adds: ImageMagick's +noise kinds, with values on 0..1 and the amount as ImageMagick's -attenuate. At amount 1 the formulas are ImageMagick's Q16 ones. PixelMath An arithmetic operation with a constant, for Arithmetic(PixelMath, float, ColorChannels): ImageMagick's -evaluate operators. ResampleFilter The kernel a resize or rotation uses to blend source pixels. StackMode How Stack(IReadOnlyList<Raster>, StackMode) combines the same channel of the same pixel across rasters. ThresholdMethod How AutoThreshold(ThresholdMethod, ThresholdMode, Rgba8?, Rgba8?, bool) and FindThreshold(ThresholdMethod, ThresholdMode) choose a level from the histogram. ThresholdMode What a threshold compares with its level. WhiteBalanceMethod How AutoWhiteBalance(WhiteBalanceMethod, bool) finds the cast to remove. Delegates RowBandAction Processes a band of rows: rows start (inclusive) to end (exclusive).

api/Egami.PixelMemoryUsage.html.summary: Class PixelMemoryUsage Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll What a PooledPixelMemorySource has handed out and not yet had back, and opt-in tracking of blocks that were never disposed. Get it from Usage; most callers want PooledPixelMemorySource.Shared.Usage. public sealed class PixelMemoryUsage Inheritance object PixelMemoryUsage Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples PixelMemoryUsage usage = PooledPixelMemorySource.Shared.Usage; usage.CaptureStackTraces = true; usage.LeakDetected += (_, leak) => Console.WriteLine($"{leak.Bytes} bytes never disposed, allocated at {leak.StackTrace}"); usage.TrackLeaks = true; RunTheCodeUnderSuspicion(); Console.WriteLine($"{usage.LiveBlocks} blocks, {usage.LiveBytes} bytes still out"); Remarks The counts are always kept, at the cost of one atomic addition per allocation and per return. Leak tracking adds a small object with a finalizer to every block allocated while it is on, so turn it on only while looking for a leak. Properties CaptureStackTraces Gets or sets whether tracked blocks record the stack trace of their allocation for LeakDetected. It makes every allocation much slower. Defaults to false. public bool CaptureStackTraces { get; set; } Property Value bool LiveBlocks Gets the number of blocks handed out and not yet disposed. public long LiveBlocks { get; } Property Value long LiveBytes Gets the bytes in blocks handed out and not yet disposed. public long LiveBytes { get; } Property Value long TrackLeaks Gets or sets whether blocks allocated from now on are tracked, so that one collected without being disposed raises LeakDetected and leaves the counts. Defaults to false. public bool TrackLeaks { get; set; } Property Value bool Events LeakDetected Occurs when a block allocated while TrackLeaks was on is collected by the garbage collector without having been disposed. Handlers run on the finalizer thread, so they must be quick, must not throw, and must not touch objects that may already be finalized. Leaks are reported here, not through Diagnostics: they belong to the memory source and are found after any call has ended. public event EventHandler<PixelMemoryLeakEventArgs>? api/Egami.Pixels.AlphaKind.html.title: Enum AlphaKind | Egami
api/Egami.Pixels.AlphaKind.html.summary: Enum AlphaKind Namespace Egami.Pixels Assembly Egami.dll How a pixel type stores alpha. public enum AlphaKind Fields None = 0 The type has no alpha channel. Every pixel is opaque. Premultiplied = 2 Premultiplied alpha: each color channel is stored already multiplied by alpha. The conversions of IPixelType<TSelf> still take and return straight values, so only code that reads the memory directly sees it. Straight = 1 Straight (not premultiplied) alpha. Examples // What a pixel type stores, for code that handles any TPixel. PixelLayoutInfo layout = Rgba16.Layout; Console.WriteLine($"{layout.ChannelOrder} {layout.ChannelType}: {layout.ChannelCount} channels, {layout.BitsPerChannel} bits each, {layout.BytesPerPixel} bytes"); bool needsAlpha = layout.Alpha != AlphaKind.None; bool eightBit = layout.ChannelType == PixelChannelType.Unorm8; bool bgrOrder = Bgr8.Layout.ChannelOrder is PixelChannelOrder.Bgr or PixelChannelOrder.Bgra;

api/Egami.Pixels.ChromaFormat.html.title: Enum ChromaFormat | Egami
api/Egami.Pixels.ChromaFormat.html.summary: Enum ChromaFormat Namespace Egami.Pixels Assembly Egami.dll How a YuvRaster stores chroma: at what resolution against luma, or not at all. public enum ChromaFormat Fields Yuv400 = 3 Luma only, with no chroma planes: a gray picture, such as a gray JPEG or monochrome AV1. Yuv410 = 5 Chroma at a quarter of the width and a quarter of the height of luma, as old codecs such as Indeo (YVU9) store it. Yuv411 = 4 Chroma at a quarter of the width and the full height of luma, as NTSC DV and some capture cards store it. Yuv420 = 0 Chroma at half the width and half the height of luma, as most video, lossy WebP and most JPEG files store it. Yuv422 = 1 Chroma at half the width and the full height of luma. Yuv444 = 2 Chroma at the full size of luma. Examples // A 1080p frame as video stores it: full-size luma, chroma at half width and height, BT.709 at limited range. using YuvRaster<byte> frame = YuvRaster.Create(1920, 1080, ChromaFormat.Yuv420, YuvColor.Bt709Limited); // 10-bit HDR planes hold samples 0 to 1023 in ushorts; an alpha plane is optional. using YuvRaster<ushort> hdr = YuvRaster.Create(3840, 2160, ChromaFormat.Yuv420, 10, YuvColor.Bt2020Limited, alpha: true); Console.WriteLine($"Chroma planes are {frame.U!.Width}×{frame.U.Height}");

api/Egami.Pixels.ChromaSiting.html.title: Enum ChromaSiting | Egami
api/Egami.Pixels.ChromaSiting.html.summary: Enum ChromaSiting Namespace Egami.Pixels Assembly Egami.dll Where each chroma sample of a subsampled picture (4:2:0, 4:2:2, 4:1:1 or 4:1:0) sits against the luma samples it covers. Conversions filter chroma to match, so colors line up with edges. Ignored for 4:4:4 and 4:0:0. public enum ChromaSiting Fields Center = 0 Centered between the luma samples it covers, both ways: JPEG, VP8 and lossy WebP. Left = 1 On the left luma column of the columns it covers and centered vertically: BT.601 and BT.709 video, MPEG-2 and later, and AV1's "vertical" position. TopLeft = 2 On the top-left luma sample of the block it covers: BT.2020 and AV1's "colocated" position. Examples // How samples turn into RGB is always stated: a preset, or the codes a video container carries (ITU-T H.273). YuvColor jpeg = YuvColor.Jpeg; // BT.601, full range, chroma centered YuvColor custom = new(YuvMatrix.Bt709, YuvRange.Full, ChromaSiting.Left); if (YuvColor.TryFromH273(matrixCoefficients: 9, fullRange: false, ChromaSiting.TopLeft, out YuvColor fromStream)) { Console.WriteLine($"{fromStream.Matrix}, {fromStream.Range}; back to code {fromStream.ToH273()}"); } // Or straight from the code points an AVIF or PNG cICP box carries. Egami.Colors.ColorCodePoints hdr10 = new(Primaries: 9, TransferCharacteristics: 16, MatrixCoefficients: 9, FullRange: false); hdr10.TryGetYuvColor(ChromaSiting.TopLeft, out YuvColor fromBox);

Rgba8 orange = new(255, 128, 0, 255); Bgr8 bgr = Bgr8.FromRgba8(orange); Gray8 gray = Gray8.FromRgba8(orange); GrayAlpha8 grayAlpha = new(gray.L, 128); Gray16 deep = Gray16.FromRgba8(orange); Rgba16 wide = new(65535, 32896, 0, 65535); Rgb16 wideOpaque = Rgb16.FromRgba16(wide); // exact: 16-bit to 16-bit never rounds GrayAlpha16 deepMask = new(deep.L, 32768); Argb8 alphaFirst = Argb8.FromRgba8(orange); // bytes A, R, G, B Alpha8 mask = Alpha8.FromRgba8(orange); // alpha only; reads back as black RgbaF16 hdr = RgbaF16.FromScaled(new Vector4(4f, 2f, 0.5f, 1f)); // half floats keep values above 1 GrayF32 depth = new(12.5f); // floats hold any value until written to an integer type Bgr565 packed = Bgr565.FromRgba8(orange); // 5-6-5 levels in one ushort; rounds to the nearest level Bgra5551 gdi16 = Bgra5551.FromRgba8(orange); // 5-5-5 levels and a 1-bit alpha, the GDI+ 16-bit ARGB layout Cmyk8 ink = Cmyk8.FromRgba8(orange); // inks by the plain formula: (0, 127, 255, 0) PremulRgba8 glass = PremulRgba8.FromRgba8(new Rgba8(255, 128, 0, 128)); // stored (128, 64, 0, 128); converts back straight RgbaF32 linear = RgbaF32.FromScaled(orange.ToScaled()); Rgba8[] row = [orange, Rgba8.Transparent]; Bgra8[] converted = new Bgra8[row.Length]; PixelConvert.Convert<Rgba8, Bgra8>(row, converted); Remarks Without a color profile, conversion uses the plain formula: red = (1 − C)(1 − K), and from RGB, K = 1 − max(R, G, B) and C = (1 − R − K) / (1 − K). It must be at least as long as source. Type Parameters TFrom The source pixel type. TTo The destination pixel type. Remarks Conversions between integer types where either side has 8-bit (or narrower packed) channels go through Rgba8, so they are exact: 8 to 16 bits multiplies by 257, and 16 to 8 bits rounds to the nearest value. Conversions between integer types wider than 8 bits go through Rgba16, also exact. All other conversions, including every one with a float or half-float side, go through red, green, blue and alpha scaled to 0..1. Converting to a gray type takes the Rec. 709 luma of the color, weighted in linear light; gray colors keep their value. Converting to a type without alpha drops alpha, and converting from one gives every pixel full alpha. Common pairs use SIMD: channel reordering between the 8-bit RGB layouts, 8 to 16 bits and back, and gray to RGB. Results are identical with and without SIMD. The spans must not overlap unless both are the same type and start at the same address. Exceptions ArgumentException destination is shorter than source.

api/Egami.Pixels.YuvMatrix.html.title: Enum YuvMatrix | Egami
api/Egami.Pixels.YuvMatrix.html.summary: Enum YuvMatrix Namespace Egami.Pixels Assembly Egami.dll The matrix between RGB and luma-chroma (Y'CbCr) values, as ITU-T H.273 names them. Shared by YCbCrColor and planar YUV images, so their coefficients never disagree. public enum YuvMatrix Fields Bt2020Ncl = 2 ITU-R BT.2020, non-constant luminance: Kr 0.2627, Kb 0.0593. UHD and HDR video. Bt601 = 0 ITU-R BT.601: Kr 0.299, Kb 0.114. JPEG, and standard-definition video. Bt709 = 1 ITU-R BT.709: Kr 0.2126, Kb 0.0722. High-definition video. Identity = 3 No matrix: Y is green, Cb blue and Cr red, as AV1 stores lossless RGB. Examples // Color values in the models apps ask for, from and to pixels, and between each other. Rgba8 orange = new(240, 128, 32, 255); HslColor hsl = HslColor.From(orange); // hue 28°, saturation 0.87, lightness 0.53 LabColor lab = ColorConvert.Convert<HslColor, LabColor>(hsl); // through XYZ OklchColor oklch = OklchColor.From(orange); YCbCrColor jpeg = YCbCrColor.From(orange); // BT.601 full range, as JPEG YCbCrColor video = YCbCrColor.From(orange, YuvMatrix.Bt709, YuvRange.Limited); // Color difference: CIEDE2000 on Lab, distance on Oklab. double deltaE = lab.DeltaE2000(LabColor.From(new Rgba8(235, 130, 40, 255))); // Whole rows at once, from any pixel type and encoding. P016 = 3 4:2:0 in two planes of little-endian 16-bit words, samples in the high bits (16, or 10 or 12 with zero low bits): Y, then U and V interleaved. api/Egami.Pixels.html.title: Namespace Egami.Pixels | Egami
api/Egami.Pixels.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Pixels Classes PixelConvert Converts spans of pixels from one pixel type to another. Structs Abgr8 A pixel with 8-bit alpha, blue, green and red channels, in that order, with straight alpha. Matches the bytes of a little-endian 32-bit RGBA value read as an integer. Alpha8 A pixel with one 8-bit alpha channel: a mask, or glyph coverage. As a color it is black with that alpha; converting a color to it keeps only the alpha, so a type without alpha gives 255. Argb8 A pixel with 8-bit alpha, red, green and blue channels, in that order, with straight alpha. Matches the byte order of big-endian ARGB buffers, such as Java's and some TIFF and PSD files. Bgr555 A 16-bit packed pixel: blue in bits 0 to 4, green in bits 5 to 9, red in bits 10 to 14, and no alpha; bit 15 is unused and written as 0. The same memory as the default 16-bit BMP, 15-bit TGA and the GDI+ 16-bit RGB 555 format. Widening and narrowing both round to the nearest value, so every value with bit 15 clear survives a round trip through Rgba8. Bgr565 A 16-bit packed pixel: blue in bits 0 to 4, green in bits 5 to 10, red in bits 11 to 15, and no alpha. The same memory as Skia's and Android's RGB 565 and the 16-bit BMP 5-6-5 bit field. Widening and narrowing both round to the nearest value, so every 16-bit value survives a round trip through Rgba8. Bgr8 A pixel with 8-bit blue, green and red channels, in that order, and no alpha. Bgra4444 A 16-bit packed pixel: blue in bits 0 to 3, green in 4 to 7, red in 8 to 11 and straight alpha in 12 to 15. The same memory as the DXGI and Vulkan B4G4R4A4 formats. Each level widens to 8 bits by multiplying by 17, and narrowing rounds to nearest. Bgra5551 A 16-bit packed pixel: blue in bits 0 to 4, green in bits 5 to 9, red in bits 10 to 14 and a 1-bit straight alpha in bit 15 (1 is opaque). The same memory as 16-bit TGA with one attribute bit, the BMP 1-5-5-5 bit field and the GDI+ 16-bit ARGB 1555 format. Color levels round to the nearest value; alpha 128 and above narrows to opaque. Every 16-bit value survives a round trip through Rgba8. Bgra8 A pixel with 8-bit blue, green, red and straight alpha channels, in that order. Cmyk16 A pixel with 16-bit cyan, magenta, yellow and black ink amounts, in that order, 0 meaning no ink. 16-bit CMYK TIFF and PSD. Cmyk8 A pixel with 8-bit cyan, magenta, yellow and black ink amounts, in that order, 0 meaning no ink. CMYK JPEG, TIFF and PSD. Gray16 A pixel with one 16-bit luminance channel and no alpha. Gray8 A pixel with one 8-bit luminance channel and no alpha. GrayAlpha16 A pixel with 16-bit luminance and straight alpha channels, in that order. GrayAlpha8 A pixel with 8-bit luminance and straight alpha channels, in that order. GrayF32 A pixel with one 32-bit float luminance channel, nominally 0 to 1, and no alpha: PFM gray maps, depth and height maps. PixelLayoutInfo Describes the memory layout of a pixel type. PremulBgra8 A pixel with 8-bit blue, green and red channels premultiplied by the alpha channel, in that order: the layout of Windows and GPU surfaces. PremulRgba8 A pixel with 8-bit red, green and blue channels premultiplied by the alpha channel, in that order: Skia's N32 premultiplied. PremulRgbaF32 A pixel with 32-bit float red, green and blue channels premultiplied by the alpha channel, in that order, for float compositing and blending. The conversions take and return straight colors; values are not clamped, except that a premultiplied pixel with zero alpha has no color. Rgb10A2 A 32-bit packed pixel: red in bits 0 to 9, green in 10 to 19, blue in 20 to 29 and straight alpha in 30 and 31. The same memory as the DXGI R10G10B10A2 and Vulkan A2B10G10R10 formats, used by 10-bit displays. Ten-bit levels round to the nearest 16-bit value and convert through Rgba16 exactly; two-bit alpha widens by multiplying. Rgb16 A pixel with 16-bit red, green and blue channels, in that order, and no alpha. Rgb8 A pixel with 8-bit red, green and blue channels, in that order, and no alpha. RgbF32 A pixel with 32-bit float red, green and blue channels, in that order, nominally 0 to 1, and no alpha. Rgba16 A pixel with 16-bit red, green, blue and straight alpha channels, in that order. Rgba8 A pixel with 8-bit red, green, blue and straight alpha channels, in that order. Egami's default working type. RgbaF16 A pixel with 16-bit float (Half) red, green, blue and straight alpha channels, in that order, nominally 0 to 1. Values outside 0..1 (HDR) are kept until written to an integer type; conversion to and from float rounds as (Half)f does: to nearest even, with values above 65,504 becoming infinity. RgbaF32 A pixel with 32-bit float red, green, blue and straight alpha channels, in that order, nominally 0 to 1. YuvColor How the samples of a YuvRaster turn into RGB: the matrix, the range and where chroma sits. Every load, wrap and conversion states one, so a picture is never read with a guessed matrix. Interfaces IPixelType<TSelf> A pixel type: an unmanaged struct holding one pixel. The conversions (ToScaled, FromScaled, ToRgba8, FromRgba8) always use sRGB-encoded values with straight (not premultiplied) alpha; Layout says how the pixel is stored, so Egami can take faster paths for layouts it knows. Types from outside Egami may use any layout, with Other for ones Egami does not know. Enums AlphaKind How a pixel type stores alpha. ChromaFormat How a YuvRaster stores chroma: at what resolution against luma, or not at all. ChromaSiting Where each chroma sample of a subsampled picture (4:2:0, 4:2:2, 4:1:1 or 4:1:0) sits against the luma samples it covers. Conversions filter chroma to match, so colors line up with edges. Ignored for 4:4:4 and 4:0:0. PixelChannelOrder The order in which a pixel type stores its channels. PixelChannelType The storage type of every channel in a pixel type. YuvMatrix The matrix between RGB and luma-chroma (Y'CbCr) values, as ITU-T H.273 names them. Shared by YCbCrColor and planar YUV images, so their coefficients never disagree. YuvPackedFormat The interleaved YUV layouts that operating system decoders, GPUs and webcams hand out, which a YuvRaster copies to and from its planes with CopyFromPacked(YuvPackedFormat, ReadOnlySpan<byte>, int, ReadOnlySpan<byte>, int) and CopyToPacked(YuvPackedFormat, Span<byte>, int, Span<byte>, int). YuvRange Whether luma-chroma values use the whole range or the video range.

api/Egami.PooledPixelMemorySource.html.summary: Class PooledPixelMemorySource Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll The default IPixelMemorySource. Small blocks are arrays rented from a shared pool; larger blocks are unmanaged memory aligned to 64 bytes, which stays off the large object heap and suits SIMD. Planes larger than MaxBlockBytes are split into several blocks of whole rows. public sealed class PooledPixelMemorySource : IPixelMemorySource Inheritance object PooledPixelMemorySource Implements IPixelMemorySource Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // Every pixel buffer comes from the context's IPixelMemorySource; wrap the pooled one to count what it hands out. CountingSource counting = new(PooledPixelMemorySource.Shared); EgamiContext context = EgamiContext.Default with { Memory = counting }; using (Raster<Rgba8> image = Raster.Create<Rgba8>(512, 512, context)) { image.Apply(ops => ops.Blur(2)); } Console.WriteLine($"{counting.Blocks} blocks, {counting.Bytes:N0} bytes"); Remarks Unmanaged blocks are kept after use, up to MaxRetainedBytes, and reused by later allocations of a similar size, because memory fresh from the operating system is slow the first time it is written. Trim() frees what is kept. Properties MaxBlockBytes Gets the largest block, in bytes, the source hands out in one piece. Planes bigger than this are split into several blocks, each holding whole rows. RetainedBytes Gets the bytes currently kept for reuse. public long RetainedBytes { get; } Property Value long Shared Gets the shared instance with the default settings. public static PooledPixelMemorySource Shared { get; } Property Value PooledPixelMemorySource Usage Gets the counts of blocks handed out and not yet disposed, and the switch for leak tracking. public PixelMemoryUsage Usage { get; } Property Value PixelMemoryUsage Methods Allocate(int, ClearMode) Allocates one contiguous block of memory. public IMemoryOwner<byte> Allocate(int byteLength, ClearMode clear) Parameters byteLength int The size of the block in bytes. api/Egami.Quantization.DitherMode.html.title: Enum DitherMode | Egami
api/Egami.Quantization.DitherMode.html.summary: Enum DitherMode Namespace Egami.Quantization Assembly Egami.dll How the error of mapping pixels to a palette is spread: error diffusion (Floyd–Steinberg and eight other published kernels, and Riemersma's Hilbert-curve walk) or an ordered pattern (Bayer 2, 4, 8 and 16, and 3 × 3). The values are fixed. public enum DitherMode Fields Atkinson = 3 Atkinson's error diffusion (Apple, 1984): spreads six eighths of the error, so flat areas keep more contrast. Bayer16x16 = 14 A 16 × 16 ordered (Bayer) pattern: the finest steps, for large palettes. Bayer2x2 = 12 A 2 × 2 ordered (Bayer) pattern: coarse, visible cross-hatching. Bayer4x4 = 13 A 4 × 4 ordered (Bayer) pattern. Burkes = 4 Burkes' error diffusion (1988): two rows, 32nds. FloydSteinberg = 0 Floyd–Steinberg error diffusion: the smoothest gradients; frames of an animation dither one row after another. JarvisJudiceNinke = 5 Jarvis, Judice and Ninke's error diffusion (1976): three rows, 48ths; smooth but slow. None = 2 No dithering: each pixel takes the nearest palette color. Ordered = 1 An 8×8 ordered (Bayer) pattern: stable between animation frames and parallel, at some cost in quality. Ordered3x3 = 15 A 3 × 3 ordered pattern. Riemersma = 11 Riemersma's dithering (1998): error diffusion along a Hilbert curve with a 16-pixel memory, so no direction shows. Sierra2 = 7 Sierra's two-row error diffusion, 16ths. Sierra3 = 6 Sierra's three-row error diffusion (1989), 32nds. SierraLite = 8 Sierra's Filter Lite: three neighbours, quarters; nearly as smooth as Floyd–Steinberg and faster. StevensonArce = 9 Stevenson and Arce's error diffusion (1985), four rows, 200ths. Stucki = 10 Stucki's error diffusion (1981): three rows, 42nds; sharper than Jarvis, Judice and Ninke. Examples using FileStream output = File.Create("duck.gif"); photo.Save(output, GifFormat.Info, new GifWriterOptions { Palette = new PaletteOptions { MaxColors = 128, Dither = DitherMode.Ordered }, // FloydSteinberg (default), Ordered or None PaletteScope = GifPaletteScope.PerFrame, // Auto (default): one table when all frames fit, else one per frame });
