api/Egami.Quantization.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Quantization Classes ErrorDiffusionKernel A custom error-diffusion kernel for Kernel: how much of each pixel's error goes to which neighbours. Row 0 of Weights is the current row, with the current pixel at column Origin; the following rows are the rows below. Only entries to the right of the current pixel on row 0, and every entry below, may be non-zero, since the rest have been mapped already. IndexedImage An image as palette indices: one byte per pixel and the palette they index, for formats and APIs that want indexed color, such as a PDF indexed image. The indices are pooled; dispose the image to return them. Palette An ordered list of up to 256 colors to map images onto: a brand palette, a display's inks, or one built from an image with Wu's quantizer. Use it as FixedPalette for the GIF, PNG, BMP and TGA writers, with Remap(Palette, DitherMode, float), or to find the nearest color yourself. PaletteOptions How formats with at most 256 colors (GIF, PNG with a palette, and indexed BMP and TGA) build their palette when an image has more colors than fit. Images with few enough colors always keep them exactly, without dithering. Palettes Ready-made palettes. Enums DitherMode How the error of mapping pixels to a palette is spread: error diffusion (Floyd–Steinberg and eight other published kernels, and Riemersma's Hilbert-curve walk) or an ordered pattern (Bayer 2, 4, 8 and 16, and 3 × 3). The values are fixed.

Signature() Returns a SHA-256 fingerprint of the pixels, as 64 lowercase hex digits: of the size, the frame count, and each frame's delay and pixels as 16-bit RGBA. Channels are combined as straight values, so a mean of semi-transparent images averages their colors and their alphas separately. The result has the first raster's pixel type and metadata. The bytes are the ones Save(Stream, FormatInfo, WriterOptions?) writes for the same pixels and options, except where a format must write differently without seeking: top-down BMP and TGA rows, and run-length TGA, which is always top-down. Options that need every pixel before the first byte (automatic palettes, PNG's Reduce, automatic alpha) throw at Create instead of quietly writing something else. public sealed class RasterEncoder<TPixel> : IDisposable where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> Type Parameters TPixel The pixel type of the rows and frames. api/Egami.Svg.html.title: Namespace Egami.Svg | Egami
api/Egami.Svg.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Svg Classes SvgAttribute An attribute of an SvgElement: its name, namespace, the prefix it was written with, and its value. SvgAttributeCollection An element's attributes, in file order. Setting, adding and removing mark the document's render tree for rebuilding. SvgCanvas A canvas that writes SVG: every drawing call becomes SVG elements, so anything drawn on a Canvas (shapes, strokes, gradients, images, text, clips, layers, recorded pictures) can be saved as a vector file that browsers, Inkscape and Egami.Svg all read. Gradients, patterns, clips, masks, images, glyph outlines and pictures are written once in defs and shared. What SVG cannot express (sweep gradients, noise and composed paints, meshes, layers with filters) is drawn by Egami into an image at FallbackScale and embedded as PNG. The output is SVG 1.1 with CSS mix-blend-mode and isolation for blend modes and layers (and SVG 2's fr for a conical gradient whose start circle has a radius). Disposing the canvas finishes the file and writes it to the stream, which is left open. An image or picture drawn several times is stored once, as it was when first drawn. SvgClip A clip path, in the coordinates of the node it clips: the union of its shapes, each with its own clip-rule. SvgComment An XML comment, kept so a save writes it back. SvgContent One item of an SvgElement's content, in file order: an element, text, a comment or a processing instruction. SvgContentList An element's content in file order: child elements, text, comments and processing instructions. Changes mark the document's render tree for rebuilding. SvgDecodeOptions Options for reading SVG through SvgFormat with Raster.Load and Raster.Probe. SvgDocument An SVG document: an editable element tree read from an .svg or .svgz file, which saves back to SVG and draws through Egami.Drawing's canvas. SvgElement An element of an SVG document's editable tree: its name and namespace, attributes and content, like XDocument's elements. Unknown elements and foreign namespaces (Inkscape's, Illustrator's metadata) are kept, so a save writes them back. SvgException Thrown when an SVG file is not well-formed XML, breaks a safety limit, or, with Strict, has anything a lenient load would skip. SvgFilter A filter, in the coordinates of the node it filters: the filter elements and CSS filter functions of its filter property, run one after the other. SvgFontOptions Where a document's text finds its fonts (question 13): the caller's Collection first, then the fonts installed on the machine unless UseSystemFonts is off, then per-character fallback through the same fonts. A server that renders untrusted files should pass its own collection and turn system fonts off, so output never depends on the machine. SvgFormat SVG and SVGZ as an Egami format: registered with WithFormat(FormatInfo), Raster.Load draws an SVG file at its own size (times Scale) and Raster.Probe gives that size without drawing. The format only reads; nothing outside the file is opened, so images it links are not drawn, and text uses the machine's fonts. For a resolver, your own fonts, a target size or a background, load an SvgDocument and call Rasterize<TPixel>(SvgRenderOptions?). SvgGlyphRenderer Draws the glyphs of an OpenType SVG table (question 20): each glyph's document is read once per font and kept, and the element glyphid is drawn in the font's units, its origin on the baseline. Set it on ColorGlyphRenderer; Rasterize<TPixel>(SvgRenderOptions?) uses it already. SvgGroup A group of nodes drawn in order: a g, svg, a, switch, a use instance or a marker. SvgImage An image: a raster drawn into a rectangle, or another SVG document drawn as a group. SvgLoadOptions How SvgDocument reads a file: what it may fetch, how strict it is, and which limits and diagnostics apply. SvgMask A mask, in the coordinates of the node it masks: content drawn into a region, used by luminance or alpha. SvgNamespaces The XML namespaces SVG files use. SvgNode A node of a document's render tree: the elements resolved for drawing, with styles applied, units in pixels, use expanded, references linked and shapes turned into paths, as resvg's usvg tree. It is immutable, so a document that is not being edited can be drawn on many threads at once. SvgPath A shape: a 2.6 Path with its fill, stroke and markers. SvgProcessingInstruction An XML processing instruction, such as <?xml-stylesheet ...?>, kept so a save writes it back. SvgRenderOptions How Rasterize<TPixel>(SvgRenderOptions?) and Draw(Canvas, RectF?, SvgRenderOptions?) draw a document. SvgResolvers Ready resolvers for Resolver. SvgSaveOptions How Save(Stream, SvgSaveOptions?) writes a document. SvgTextContent Character data in an element: text or a CDATA section, kept apart so a save writes it back the same way. SvgTextRun Text: one run of positioned glyphs in one font with one fill and stroke, drawn with DrawGlyphRun(GlyphRun, Vector2, Paint) so a PDF or SVG canvas keeps real text. A text element becomes a group of these and of the paths of its decorations. SvgWriteOptions How SvgCanvas writes SVG: text, number precision, layout, image format and fallback resolution. Enums SvgImageFormat The format SvgCanvas embeds drawn images in. SvgPaintOrder Which of a shape's fill, stroke and markers is painted first (paint-order). SvgTextMode How SvgCanvas writes text.

Default = 0 Bilinear without prefiltering. High = 2 Bicubic with prefiltering. HighQualityBicubic = 7 Bicubic with prefiltering. HighQualityBilinear = 6 Bilinear with prefiltering. Examples // DrawImage at a point draws at the image's physical size; ImageAttributes adjust its colors and tile it. using Bitmap source = new(8, 8); source.SetResolution(48, 48); // half the 96 dpi of the bitmap drawn on, so it is drawn twice as large using (Graphics s = Graphics.FromImage(source)) { s.Clear(Color.Orange); } using Bitmap bitmap = new(64, 48); using Graphics g = Graphics.FromImage(bitmap); g.DrawImage(source, 0, 0); // 16 by 16 pixels g.InterpolationMode = InterpolationMode.NearestNeighbor; using ImageAttributes attributes = new(); attributes.SetColorMatrix(new ColorMatrix { Matrix33 = 0.5f }); // half the alpha attributes.SetWrapMode(WrapMode.Tile); g.DrawImage(source, new Rectangle(20, 0, 40, 40), 0, 0, 16, 16, GraphicsUnit.Pixel, attributes);

api/Egami.SystemDrawing.Drawing2D.html.summary: Namespace Egami.SystemDrawing.Drawing2D Classes AdjustableArrowCap An arrowhead line end, its width and height in pen widths, filled or outlined, with an optional inset middle. Blend A gradient's falloff: at each position from 0 to 1, a factor from the start color (0) to the end color (1). ColorBlend A gradient's colors at positions from 0 to 1, the first at 0 and the last at 1. CustomLineCap A line end drawn from a path: the path's x axis runs across the line and its y axis along it, outward from the end, in pen widths. The stroke path is outlined; GDI+ refuses fill paths. Set it as a pen's CustomStartCap or CustomEndCap. GraphicsContainer A container BeginContainer() returned, for EndContainer(GraphicsContainer). GraphicsPath The Add builders. GraphicsPathIterator Walks a GraphicsPath by figure, by run of one point type within the current figure, or by marker, as GDI+ walks it. The iterator copies the path when it is made. GraphicsState A graphics state Save() returned, for Restore(GraphicsState). HatchBrush A brush of one of GDI+'s 53 hatch patterns: 8 by 8 tiles of a foreground color on a background, from the device origin. LinearGradientBrush A brush of colors along a line: across a rectangle at an angle (or between two points), the colors constant on lines perpendicular to it, with a Blend or preset colors, repeating beyond the rectangle. Matrix A 3 by 2 affine transform, as System.Drawing's Matrix: row vectors times the matrix, so Prepend (the default) applies a new transform before the existing one. PathData A path's points and their PathPointType types. PathGradientBrush A brush of colors from a center out to the edge of a polygon or path: the center color at the center point, the surrounding colors at the boundary's points, with a Blend or preset colors between. RegionData A region in the EMF+ region format ([MS-EMFPLUS] 2.2.1.8), after GDI+'s size and checksum, from GetRegionData(). Enums CombineMode How a region or clip combines with another. CompositingMode Whether drawing blends over what is there or replaces it. CompositingQuality How carefully blending is done. Egami blends the same way for every value. CoordinateSpace A coordinate space of a Graphics: world (before any transform), page (after the world transform) or device (pixels). DashCap How each dash ends. DashStyle A pen's dash pattern, in multiples of its width. FillMode Which points are inside a shape that crosses itself. FlushIntention Whether Flush(FlushIntention) waits for drawing to finish. Egami draws immediately, so both are the same. HatchStyle The 53 hatch patterns of HatchBrush, each an 8 by 8 tile of foreground on background, from the device origin. InterpolationMode How images are sampled when drawn at another size or angle. GDI+ and Egami.SystemDrawing default to bilinear without prefiltering. LineCap How a line ends: flat, square, round, a triangle, an anchor shape centered on the end, or a custom cap. LineJoin How two segments of a line meet. LinearGradientMode The direction of a LinearGradientBrush made from a rectangle. MatrixOrder Whether a transform is applied before the existing ones (Prepend, the default) or after them. PathPointType The type of a point of a GraphicsPath: its kind in the low bits and flags above. PenAlignment Where a pen lies along a closed shape's outline. PenType What a pen paints with: the kind of its brush. PixelOffsetMode Where pixel centers are: on whole coordinates (the default), or half a pixel off with Half and HighQuality. QualityMode A quality level, the base of the smoothing, compositing and interpolation modes. SmoothingMode Whether shapes and lines are antialiased. GDI+ and Egami.SystemDrawing default to None, aliased. WarpMode How Warp(PointF[], RectangleF, Matrix?, WarpMode, float) maps a rectangle onto four points. WrapMode How a texture or image repeats beyond its edges.

BitmapData data = bitmap.LockBits(new Rectangle(0, 0, 16, 8), ImageLockMode.ReadWrite, PixelFormat.Format32bppArgb); byte[] row = new byte[data.Stride]; for (int y = 0; y < data.Height; y++) { Marshal.Copy(data.Scan0 + (y * data.Stride), row, 0, row.Length); for (int x = 0; x < data.Width; x++) { row[(x * 4) + 2] = 255; // red } Marshal.Copy(row, 0, data.Scan0 + (y * data.Stride), row.Length); } bitmap.UnlockBits(data);

api/Egami.SystemDrawing.Imaging.PixelFor.summary: Enum PixelFormat Namespace Egami.SystemDrawing.Imaging Assembly Egami.SystemDrawing.dll The memory layout of a bitmap's pixels, with System.Drawing's values: bits 8 to 15 hold the bits a pixel, bits 0 to 7 an index, and the high bits the flags below. public enum PixelFormat Fields Alpha = 262144 The pixels hold alpha. Canonical = 2097152 The default format, 32-bit ARGB. DontCare = 0 No format; the same as Undefined. Extended = 1048576 The pixels hold 16 bits a channel. Format16bppArgb1555 = 397319 16 bits a pixel, 5 each of blue, green and red from the lowest bit and 1 bit of alpha. Bgra5551's memory. Format16bppGrayScale = 1052676 16 bits of gray a pixel. Bitmaps hold it, but drawing on one and reading its pixels throw, as in GDI+. Format16bppRgb555 = 135173 16 bits a pixel, 5 each of blue, green and red from the lowest bit; the top bit unused. Bgr555's memory. Format16bppRgb565 = 135174 16 bits a pixel, 5 of blue, 6 of green and 5 of red from the lowest bit. Bgr565's memory. Format1bppIndexed = 196865 1 bit a pixel, an index into a 2-color palette. Format24bppRgb = 137224 24 bits a pixel: blue, green and red bytes. Bgr8's memory. Format32bppArgb = 2498570 32 bits a pixel: blue, green, red and alpha bytes. Bgra8's memory; the default. Format32bppPArgb = 925707 32 bits a pixel: blue, green and red premultiplied by alpha, then alpha. PremulBgra8's memory. Format32bppRgb = 139273 32 bits a pixel: blue, green and red bytes and one unused byte. Format48bppRgb = 1060876 48 bits a pixel: blue, green and red in 16 bits each, linear light from 0 to 8192. Format4bppIndexed = 197634 4 bits a pixel, an index into a 16-color palette. Format64bppArgb = 3424269 64 bits a pixel: blue, green, red and alpha in 16 bits each, linear light from 0 to 8192. Format64bppPArgb = 1851406 64 bits a pixel: linear blue, green and red premultiplied by alpha, then alpha, in 16 bits each from 0 to 8192. Format8bppIndexed = 198659 8 bits a pixel, an index into a 256-color palette. Gdi = 131072 The pixels hold colors GDI can show. Indexed = 65536 The pixels hold indices into the bitmap's palette. Max = 15 The number of formats, one past the highest index. PAlpha = 524288 The pixels hold color premultiplied by alpha. Undefined = 0 No format. Examples // Every GDI+ pixel format, with GDI+'s conversions: 5-bit channels truncate when written and repeat their high bits when read. using Bitmap rgb555 = new(1, 1, PixelFormat.Format16bppRgb555); rgb555.SetPixel(0, 0, Color.FromArgb(10, 20, 30)); Color read = rgb555.GetPixel(0, 0); // ARGB(255, 8, 16, 24) // 48 and 64-bit formats hold linear light from 0 to 8192, as in GDI+. using Bitmap deep = new(1, 1, PixelFormat.Format48bppRgb); deep.SetPixel(0, 0, Color.FromArgb(255, 200, 100, 50)); int bits = Image.GetPixelFormatSize(deep.PixelFormat); // 48 bool alpha = Image.IsAlphaPixelFormat(PixelFormat.Format64bppArgb); // true ImageFlags flags = (ImageFlags)new Bitmap(1, 1, PixelFormat.Format32bppArgb).Flags; // HasAlpha

api/Egami.SystemDrawing.Imaging.html.summary: Namespace Egami.SystemDrawing.Imaging Classes BitmapData A locked area of a bitmap's pixels, from LockBits(Rectangle, ImageLockMode, PixelFormat): where the first row starts, the bytes from one row to the next, and the size and format of the pixels. ColorMap A color a remap table replaces, and its replacement. ColorMatrix A 5 by 5 color matrix: a color's red, green, blue, alpha and 1, as a row from 0 to 1, times the matrix, as GDI+ applies it. Starts as the identity. ColorPalette The colors an indexed bitmap's pixels point into. Palette hands out a copy: change its entries and set it back to change the bitmap's palette. Encoder An encoder setting, by the GUID GDI+ gives it: quality, compression, color depth, save flags and the rest. EncoderParameter One encoder setting and its values, passed to a save in EncoderParameters. EncoderParameters The encoder settings of one save. FrameDimension How an image's frames are counted: as pages (TIFF), as moments in time (an animated GIF) or as resolutions. ImageAttributes How images are recolored when drawn and what is drawn beyond their edges: color matrices, gamma, threshold, a color key, remap tables and an output channel per ColorAdjustType, and a wrap mode. Without a wrap mode set, nothing is drawn beyond an image, as in GDI+. ImageCodecInfo One of the codecs Save(Stream, ImageCodecInfo, EncoderParameters?) writes with, as GDI+ lists them: BMP, JPEG, GIF, TIFF and PNG encoders, and those plus EMF, WMF and ICO decoders. Egami reads many more formats than the decoders listed; the list matches GDI+'s so code that looks a codec up by its MIME type or GUID finds the same one. ImageFormat An image file format, by the GUID GDI+ gives it: what RawFormat reports and what Save(Stream, ImageFormat) writes. EncoderValue The values of the Encoder parameters that take a choice. ImageCodecFlags What an ImageCodecInfo can do. ImageFlags What an image's Flags say about it. ImageLockMode How LockBits(Rectangle, ImageLockMode, PixelFormat) may use the locked pixels. PaletteFlags What a ColorPalette's Flags say about its colors. PaletteType The fixed palettes a ColorPalette can be built from. api/Egami.SystemDrawing.RotateFlipType.h.title: Enum RotateFlipType | Egami
api/Egami.SystemDrawing.RotateFlipType.h.summary: Enum RotateFlipType Namespace Egami.SystemDrawing Assembly Egami.SystemDrawing.dll A rotation clockwise and a flip for RotateFlip(RotateFlipType). Several names mean the same transformation and share a value, as in System.Drawing. public enum RotateFlipType Fields Rotate180FlipNone = 2 Rotate 180 degrees. Rotate180FlipX = 6 Rotate 180 degrees, then flip left to right. Rotate180FlipXY = 0 Rotate 180 degrees, then flip both ways; the same as RotateNoneFlipNone. Rotate180FlipY = 4 Rotate 180 degrees, then flip top to bottom; the same as RotateNoneFlipX. Rotate270FlipNone = 3 Rotate 270 degrees. Rotate270FlipX = 7 Rotate 270 degrees, then flip left to right. Rotate270FlipXY = 1 Rotate 270 degrees, then flip both ways; the same as Rotate90FlipNone. Rotate270FlipY = 5 Rotate 270 degrees, then flip top to bottom; the same as Rotate90FlipX. Rotate90FlipNone = 1 Rotate 90 degrees. Rotate90FlipX = 5 Rotate 90 degrees, then flip left to right. Rotate90FlipXY = 3 Rotate 90 degrees, then flip both ways; the same as Rotate270FlipNone. Rotate90FlipY = 7 Rotate 90 degrees, then flip top to bottom; the same as Rotate270FlipX. RotateNoneFlipNone = 0 No change. RotateNoneFlipX = 4 Flip left to right. RotateNoneFlipXY = 2 Flip both ways; the same as Rotate180FlipNone. RotateNoneFlipY = 6 Flip top to bottom; the same as Rotate180FlipX. Examples // The same code as with System.Drawing.Common: only the using lines name Egami.SystemDrawing. using Bitmap bitmap = new(64, 32); for (int x = 0; x < 64; x++) { bitmap.SetPixel(x, 16, Color.FromArgb(255, x * 4, 0, 255 - (x * 4))); } Color middle = bitmap.GetPixel(32, 16); // ARGB(255, 128, 0, 127) bitmap.SetResolution(300, 300); bitmap.RotateFlip(RotateFlipType.Rotate90FlipNone); bitmap.Save(output, ImageFormat.Png); GraphicsUnit unit = GraphicsUnit.Inch; RectangleF bounds = bitmap.GetBounds(ref unit); // 32 by 64, in pixels

api/Egami.SystemDrawing.html.title: Namespace Egami.SystemDrawing | Egami
api/Egami.SystemDrawing.html.summary: Namespace Egami.SystemDrawing Classes Bitmap An image made of pixels, as System.Drawing's Bitmap: any of GDI+'s 14 pixel formats, with GetPixel, SetPixel, LockBits, Clone, MakeTransparent and the codecs. Pixels are kept in GDI+'s own memory layout and converted exactly as GDI+ converts them, so LockBits code and pixel values carry over. Brush What fills shapes: the base of SolidBrush and the other brushes. Brushes Solid brushes of the named web colors, one per color and thread, as System.Drawing keeps them; their color can be changed, as in System.Drawing. Graphics Draws on a bitmap, as System.Drawing's Graphics: shapes with pens and brushes, images, clipping, transforms and the page unit, with GDI+'s defaults: aliased shapes (None), pixel centers on whole coordinates, bilinear image sampling without prefiltering, transforms prepended. Get one with FromImage(Image). Icon A Windows icon: an ICO file with images at several sizes, of which the icon shows the one nearest the size asked for (32 by 32 when none is), as System.Drawing chooses it. Save(Stream) writes the file it was loaded from. Image The base of Bitmap and the metafile type: size, resolution, pixel format, palette, frames, metadata and saving, as in System.Drawing. Load one with FromFile(string) or FromStream(Stream). Pen What draws lines and outlines: a brush and a width in world units, at least one device pixel, as in GDI+. Pens One-unit pens of the named web colors, which cannot be changed or disposed. Region An area made of rectangles and shapes combined with Union(Region), Intersect(Region), Xor(Region), Exclude(Region) and Complement(Region), as System.Drawing's Region: infinite when made with no arguments. Graphics clips to one. SolidBrush A brush of one color. SystemBrushes Solid brushes of the system colors, which cannot be changed or disposed. SystemPens One-unit pens of the system colors, which cannot be changed or disposed. TextureBrush A brush that tiles an image, from the world origin, through its transform. Enums CopyPixelOperation The raster operation of CopyFromScreen(Point, Point, Size, CopyPixelOperation), which needs Windows and always throws. GraphicsUnit The unit of a measure: the world's, the display's, pixels, points, inches, document units or millimeters. RotateFlipType A rotation clockwise and a flip for RotateFlip(RotateFlipType). Several names mean the same transformation and share a value, as in System.Drawing. Delegates Graphics.DrawImageAbort Called before a DrawImage draws; returning true stops it with an ExternalException, as in GDI+. api/Egami.Video.Analysis.SceneMethod.htm.title: Enum SceneMethod | Egami
api/Egami.Video.Analysis.SceneMethod.htm.summary: Enum SceneMethod Namespace Egami.Video.Analysis Assembly Egami.Video.dll How SceneDetector scores the change between frames. public enum SceneMethod Fields Adaptive = 0 The default. The content change (luma and chroma of a 16 by 9 grid) between neighbors, kept only when it is AdaptiveRatio times the mean change of the frames around it and at least the threshold. Fast camera motion changes every frame a lot and is not taken for cuts. Reports cuts two frames after they happen. Content = 1 The content change between neighbors less the mean change of the eight frames before, against a fixed threshold: what the scenes command did before V1.4 and what ffmpeg's scene value means. Reports cuts at once. Histogram = 2 The chi-square distance between neighbors' 64-bin luma histograms, against a fixed threshold. Ignores motion within a shot, but misses cuts between shots of the same exposure. Examples // Content compares each frame with the one before, as ffmpeg's scene score does; Adaptive (the default) also weighs the // frames around it, so fast motion is not taken for a cut. Fades through black end a scene in the dark. SceneOptions options = new() { Method = SceneMethod.Content, Threshold = 0.3, MinSceneLength = MediaTime.FromSeconds(0.5), DetectFades = true, KeepSeries = true, }; MediaAnalysisResult result = MediaAnalysis.Run("shots.mkv", new MediaAnalysisOptions { Scenes = options }); SceneScore sharpest = result.SceneScores.MaxBy(s => s.Score); Console.WriteLine($"{result.Cuts.Count} cuts; the sharpest at {sharpest.Time.ToTimeSpan()}");

api/Egami.Video.Analysis.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Video.Analysis Classes AudioLevelMeter Measures sample levels per channel and over all channels: peak, RMS, DC offset, crest factor, clipped samples, how often the peak was reached, the noise floor, zero crossings and a histogram in 1 dB steps. It reports what ffmpeg's volumedetect and astats report, from any sample format. AudioLevelReport What AudioLevelMeter measured. AudioPictures Draws pictures of audio: a waveform (the min and max of each column with the RMS level shaded inside, as editors and podcast players show it) and a spectrogram (frequency over time, loudness as color). Both read the audio once with constant memory, so a three-hour file costs no more memory than a short one, and return a plain Raster<TPixel> without text; the CLI adds axes and legends. BlackDetector Finds black stretches: runs of frames where nearly every luma sample is near black, lasting at least MinDuration. It keeps ffmpeg's blackdetect measure and defaults, with the pixel threshold a fraction of the stream's own range so 8-bit and 10-bit files behave alike. BlackOptions What BlackDetector counts as black. The defaults are ffmpeg blackdetect's. ChannelLevels The sample levels of one channel, or of all channels together. Levels are in dBFS, where a full-scale sample is 0. CropDetector Finds black borders: the rectangle inside letterbox, pillarbox or windowbox bars, as ffmpeg's cropdetect does in its black mode. Rows and columns whose mean luma is at or under Limit count as border. Each frame's rectangle is rounded to Round; Report() gives the rectangle that keeps every frame's picture, the most common one, and the runs of frames that share one. CropOptions What CropDetector counts as a border. The defaults follow ffmpeg cropdetect. CropReport What CropDetector found. CropRun A run of frames that share one crop rectangle. DetectedRange A stretch of time a detector found: black, frozen, duplicated or silent. DuplicateDetector Finds repeated frames with ffmpeg mpdecimate's test, without dropping anything: a frame repeats the last kept frame when none of its 8 by 8 luma blocks differs by more than High and no more than Fraction of them differ by more than Low. A block's difference is the mean absolute difference of its samples as a share of the range, so the thresholds mean the same at every bit depth. DuplicateOptions What DuplicateDetector counts as a repeat. The defaults are ffmpeg mpdecimate's. Fade A fade to or from black (or white, when asked for) that SceneDetector found. FreezeDetector Finds frozen stretches: runs of frames that stay within Noise of the frame that starts them, lasting at least MinDuration. The measure is ffmpeg freezedetect's: the mean absolute difference over the Y, Cb and Cr planes as a fraction of the largest code value, against the same -60 dB noise floor. FreezeOptions What FreezeDetector counts as frozen. The defaults are ffmpeg freezedetect's. InterlaceDetector Tells progressive, interlaced and telecined video apart, as ffmpeg's idet does. Each frame's fields are woven three ways (with each other, and each with the other field of the frame before) and the combing of each weave compared: the weave of fields closest in time combs least. Fields that repeat the frame before's are counted, and repeats in a five-frame pattern mark 3:2 telecine. Motion is needed to decide; frames without it count as undetermined. InterlaceOptions How sure InterlaceDetector must be before it decides. The defaults are ffmpeg idet's. InterlaceReport What InterlaceDetector counted. MediaAnalysis Analyzes a file in one pass: decodes its video and audio once each and feeds every detector the options ask for, then returns what they found. The video and audio are read side by side in time order, so progress moves evenly through the file. MediaAnalysisOptions What Run(string, MediaAnalysisOptions?, MediaContext?, IProgress<MediaProgress>?, CancellationToken) looks for and where. MediaAnalysisResult What Run(string, MediaAnalysisOptions?, MediaContext?, IProgress<MediaProgress>?, CancellationToken) found. Scene A scene: a run of frames from one cut to the next, as SceneDetector finds them. SceneCut A point where a new scene starts, as SceneDetector reports it while frames come in. SceneDetector Finds the scenes of a video: where one shot cuts to the next, and where a fade or cut through black separates two. Each frame is summarized from its planes (a 16 by 9 grid of mean Y, Cb and Cr and a luma histogram) and scored against the frame before by Method; a high enough score starts a scene, unless it comes within the minimum scene length or turns out to be a flash. Feed it every frame with Add(YuvVideoFrame) and call Complete(MediaTime) at the end, or let Run(string, MediaAnalysisOptions?, MediaContext?, IProgress<MediaProgress>?, CancellationToken) do it. Memory stays flat over any length of video unless KeepSeries is set. SceneFrames Reads a picture of each scene, such as for a shot list or a storyboard. SceneOptions How SceneDetector finds scenes. The defaults suit most footage; lower the threshold to find softer cuts. SignalFrame One frame's measures from SignalMeter. SignalMeter Measures the signal, as ffmpeg's signalstats and colordetect do: the lowest, 10th percentile, mean, 90th percentile and highest code values of Y, Cb and Cr; chroma saturation; the share of pixels outside broadcast range (16 to 235 for luma, 16 to 240 for chroma, scaled to the bit depth); which range the samples really use; and whether an alpha plane is used and how. With Blur and Blockiness it also scores sharpness and coding blocks, as blurdetect and blockdetect do. SignalOptions What SignalMeter measures besides levels. The blur and blockiness settings follow ffmpeg's blurdetect and blockdetect. SignalReport What SignalMeter measured over every frame. SilenceDetector Finds silent stretches: runs of samples whose level stays under Noise for at least MinDuration. By default a stretch is silent only when every channel is, as ffmpeg's silencedetect does; PerChannel also finds each channel's own stretches. Times are exact to the sample. SilenceOptions What SilenceDetector counts as silence. The defaults are ffmpeg silencedetect's. SpectrogramOptions The size, window, scale and colors of an AudioPictures spectrogram. TestAudioFormat The rate, channels and frame size of the audio TestSources generates. TestSources Generates test video and audio: a moving test pattern with frame numbers and timecode, SMPTE color bars, solid colors and gradients, and sine tones, silence, white or pink noise and sweeps. The frames come out one at a time, so any length costs the same memory; hand them to WriteFrame(VideoFrame) and WriteAudio(AudioFrame), or to a detector. Dispose each frame. TestVideoFormat The size, rate and planes of the video TestSources generates. WaveformOptions The size, layout and colors of an AudioPictures waveform. Structs FrameValue One frame's value in a detector's series, kept when the detector's options ask for it. PlaneLevels The spread of one plane's code values. SceneFrame A scene and a frame of it, from Read(VideoReader, IEnumerable<Scene>, ScenePosition). Dispose the frame. SceneScore One frame's scene measures, kept when KeepSeries is set, to plot or tune with. Interfaces IAudioDetector A detector that listens to decoded audio one frame at a time. Feed it every frame in time order with Add(AudioFrame), then call Complete(MediaTime) once at the end; Run(string, MediaAnalysisOptions?, MediaContext?, IProgress<MediaProgress>?, CancellationToken) does both from one decode. A detector reads the samples while Add(AudioFrame) runs and keeps no reference to the frame. IVideoDetector A detector that looks at decoded pictures one at a time, such as SceneDetector. Feed it every frame in presentation order with Add(YuvVideoFrame), then call Complete(MediaTime) once at the end; Run(string, MediaAnalysisOptions?, MediaContext?, IProgress<MediaProgress>?, CancellationToken) does both for every detector from one decode, and an app with its own decode loop can do the same. A detector reads the frame while Add(YuvVideoFrame) runs and keeps no reference to it, so the caller may dispose the frame right after. Enums AlphaUse How a video's alpha plane is used. AudioPictureChannels How AudioPictures lays out the channels. ColorBarsStyle Which color bar layout ColorBars(TestVideoFormat?, MediaTime, ColorBarsStyle) draws. FadeKind Whether a fade goes out to black or in from it. FieldOrder One frame's field order, as InterlaceDetector judged it. FlashMode What SceneDetector does with a cut that comes back within the minimum scene length, as a camera flash does. FrequencyScale The frequency axis of Spectrogram(IEnumerable<AudioFrame>, MediaTime, SpectrogramOptions?, MediaContext?, CancellationToken). InterlaceVerdict What a video is, by InterlaceDetector's counts. NoiseColor The spectrum of Noise(TestAudioFormat?, MediaTime, NoiseColor, double, int). SceneMethod How SceneDetector scores the change between frames. ScenePosition Which frame of a scene Read(VideoReader, IEnumerable<Scene>, ScenePosition) reads. SceneStart How a scene starts. SignalRange Which range a video's samples really use. SpectrogramColors The colors of Spectrogram(IEnumerable<AudioFrame>, MediaTime, SpectrogramOptions?, MediaContext?, CancellationToken). WaveformScale How Waveform(IEnumerable<AudioFrame>, MediaTime, WaveformOptions?, MediaContext?, CancellationToken) scales sample values.

api/Egami.Video.Audio.Codecs.html.title: Namespace Egami.Video.Audio.Codecs | Egami
api/Egami.Video.Audio.Codecs.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Video.Audio.Codecs Classes Ac3Codec AC-3 (Dolby Digital, ATSC A/52:2018), decode only: every channel mode from 1/0 to 3/2 and dual mono, with or without the LFE, at 32, 44.1 and 48 kHz and 32 to 640 kbit/s, with coupling, rematrixing, block switching and both frame CRCs. Frames come out as planar float, 1536 samples each, in Egami.Video's channel order: a 5.1 stream as front left, front right, center, LFE, side left, side right. The stream's dynamic range control is applied in full unless DynamicRange says otherwise; dialogue normalization is not applied. Read from .ac3 files and from AC-3 tracks in MP4, Matroska, AVI and CAF. E-AC-3 (EAc3) is not decoded. Ac3DecoderOptions How the AC-3 decoder treats the stream's dynamic range control and channels. AlacCodec Apple Lossless (ALAC), translated from Apple's Apache-2.0 reference codec: decodes 16, 20, 24 and 32-bit streams of 1 to 8 channels into planar integer frames; encodes them with packets byte for byte as Apple's encoder makes them, at level 1 (normal, the default) or 0 (Apple's fast mode), 4096 samples per packet by default. Read and written in MP4 and M4A, Matroska and CAF; CodecPrivate holds the 24-byte ALACSpecificConfig. FlacCodec FLAC (RFC 9639), lossless: decodes every stream the format allows (fixed and LPC prediction, every stereo mode, block sizes up to 65535, 4 to 32 bits per sample) into planar integer frames, checking the frame CRCs and STREAMINFO's MD5; encodes at levels 0 to 8 with the reference encoder's meaning, default 5. Read and written in .flac files, Matroska and MP4. G711Codec G.711 (ITU-T G.711) μ-law and A-law, decode only: one byte per sample, expanded to 16-bit samples by the standard's tables. Read from WAV (format tags 7 and 6), AVI, AIFF-C (ulaw, alaw) and MP4/MOV. Each instance decodes both laws. Frames come out interleaved as S16. Mp3Codec MPEG audio (ISO/IEC 11172-3 and 13818-3), decode only: Layers I, II and III (MP3) of MPEG-1, MPEG-2 and MPEG-2.5, every rate from 8 to 48 kHz, mono, stereo, joint and dual channel, free-format bit rates, and the CRC-16 when frames carry it. Frames come out as planar float, one per MPEG frame (1152 samples, 576 for MPEG-2 and 2.5 Layer III, 384 for Layer I). Read from .mp3 files and from MP3 and MP2 tracks in AVI, Matroska and MP4. The decoder is translated from minimp3. OpusCodec Opus (RFC 6716 with the RFC 8251 updates). Decodes SILK, CELT and hybrid frames at every bandwidth, mono, stereo and the multichannel mapping families 0, 1 and 255 (RFC 7845), with packet loss concealment and in-band FEC. Frames come out as planar float at 48 kHz, Opus's own rate, in the canonical channel order; other rates go through a Resampler. Encodes 1 to 8 channels at 8, 12, 16, 24 or 48 kHz (mapping family 0 for mono and stereo, 1 above) in every mode, with the settings of OpusEncoderOptions; the default is 64 kbit/s per channel, variable bitrate, 20 ms frames. Both are translated from libopus 1.5.2 and match its output exactly. Ambisonic mappings (families 2 and 3) are not supported. OpusEncoderOptions How the Opus encoder codes: the bitrate and how strictly it is kept, what the audio is, the frame duration, how hard the encoder searches, the widest band and the loss protection. Every one has a default that suits music and most speech. PcmCodec Uncompressed PCM: integer samples of 8 (unsigned), 16, 24 or 32 bits, little-endian (Instance, WAV's) or big-endian (BigEndian, AIFF's and QuickTime's twos), and 32 or 64-bit float (FloatingPoint). Each instance decodes all three codec ids; it encodes its own. Decoded frames are interleaved, in the stored sample type: 24-bit samples come as S32 with ValidBits 24. VorbisCodec Vorbis I, decode only: every stream the specification allows (floors 0 and 1, residues 0 to 2, channel coupling, all block sizes), written from the Vorbis I specification and within 2^-22 of libvorbis on the test files. Frames come out as planar float in the canonical channel order (Vorbis puts center second); the first block's overlap and the end padding are trimmed. Read from Ogg, WebM, Matroska and MP4, where the track's codec private data holds the three header packets, Xiph-laced. Enums OpusApplication What the audio given to the Opus encoder is. OpusBandwidth The audio bands Opus codes, named by their upper edge. OpusRateMode How strictly the Opus encoder keeps its bitrate.

api/Egami.Video.Audio.Filters.html.title: Namespace Egami.Video.Audio.Filters | Egami
api/Egami.Video.Audio.Filters.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Video.Audio.Filters Classes AudioFade Fades the sound in or out over a stretch of the stream's time line. A fade in is silent before Start and reaches full level on the exact sample at Start plus Duration; a fade out is full level before Start and silent from its end on. Times are on the frames' own timestamps, not counted from the first sample, and are rounded to whole samples; put a Retime first to count from zero. The curves give the same gains as ffmpeg's afade with the curve each value names. Works in place. AudioFilter The base of Egami.Video's own audio filters. It takes the rate and channels from the first frame, converts every frame to F32Planar once on the way in, and queues the output. Inside an AudioFilterChain the converted frames pass from filter to filter without another copy, and filters that keep the length (gain, fades, pan) work on them in place. To write a filter of your own, implement IAudioFilter. AudioFilterChain Runs several filters on one input in a single pass: each frame is converted to F32Planar once, then handed from filter to filter in order, in place where the filter keeps the length. The chain is itself an IAudioFilter, owns the filters added to it and disposes them with itself. AudioMixer Mixes several streams into one by adding them, each times its weight, like ffmpeg's amix with normalize=0. Inputs are placed on the output by their timestamps, so one that starts later comes in at its time; a gap inside an input is silence. Inputs at another rate or with other channels are resampled with Resampler and remixed with ChannelMixer's default matrix on the way in. The sum is not divided by the number of inputs unless Normalize is set, so a voice over music keeps its level; put a limiter after it if the sum can clip. Send each input's frames with Send(int, AudioFrame) and end each with Complete(int): output waits until every input has either sent something or ended. Crossfade Joins two streams with an overlap: the end of the first fades out while the start of the second fades in, like ffmpeg's acrossfade. The output is the first stream up to its last Duration, then the overlap mixed, then the rest of the second stream, so it lasts the two lengths minus the overlap. The overlap shortens to the shorter stream's length when one is shorter. Send each input's frames with Send(int, AudioFrame) and end each with Complete(int); frames of the second input wait until the first has ended. Both inputs must have the same rate and channels. Output starts at the first input's first timestamp and runs on without gaps. Delay Delays channels by putting silence in front of them, like ffmpeg's adelay: each channel can have its own delay, for example to line up microphones or fix lip sync. The output keeps the input's timestamps and gets longer by the longest delay; Flush() hands out the tail, so no input is lost. Gain Changes the level, by a fixed gain and, optionally, an Envelope that changes over time. A change to Decibels or Factor between frames moves to the new gain over 5 ms, so it does not click. Unity gain with no envelope passes samples through unchanged. Works in place; nothing is clipped, so a gain above 0 dB can take samples past full scale until an encoder or a limiter clamps them. GainEnvelope A gain that changes over time, in decibels, for Envelope: a list of Keyframes whose values are decibels. Before the first keyframe the gain is the first value, after the last one the last value, and between two the value eases from one to the next in decibels. A value of NegativeInfinity is silence; a segment to or from it moves in linear amplitude instead, so the fade still sounds smooth. Keyframe times are the frames' own timestamps, not counted from the first sample. Pad Adds silence at the end of a stream, like ffmpeg's apad: a fixed amount, or as much as it takes for the stream to last at least a total length. The silence comes out on Flush(); the input passes through. Pan Places a mono or stereo input in a stereo output. Position pans a mono input with the constant-power law (-3 dB in each channel at the centre, like ffmpeg's pan=stereo|c0=0.7071c0|c1=0.7071c0); on a stereo input it turns one side down along the same law, scaled so the centre is unchanged. Balance turns one side down in a straight line. Swap exchanges left and right, and InvertLeft and InvertRight flip a channel's polarity. Changes to the position or balance between frames move over 5 ms. For any other channel matrix use ChannelMixer. Retime Gives a stream new timestamps, like ffmpeg's asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS: the first sample gets Start and every later one follows on at the sample rate, so gaps and jitter in the input's timestamps go away. Speed Plays a stream faster or slower with the pitch following, like a tape or ffmpeg's asetrate followed by aresample: the samples are resampled with Resampler as if they had been recorded at the rate times Factor. The output keeps the sample rate and lasts the input's length divided by the factor; it starts at the input's first timestamp. Cheaper than Tempo, which keeps the pitch. The factor is used as a fraction with a denominator up to 1000. Tempo Changes the tempo and keeps the pitch, with WSOLA (waveform similarity overlap-add, after Verhelst and Roelands, 1993): the output is built of overlapping Hann windows of the input, each taken at the place near its ideal position whose waveform best continues the window before it. The output keeps the sample rate, starts at the input's first timestamp and lasts the input's length divided by Factor, rounded to the nearest sample. A factor of 1 passes samples through. For a speed change where the pitch follows, Speed is cheaper. Trim Keeps the part of a stream between two times on its time line, like ffmpeg's atrim, cut on the exact sample. The times are the frames' own timestamps, not counted from the first sample, so put a Retime first to count from zero. The samples kept keep their timestamps; follow with Retime to start the result at zero. Interfaces IAudioFilter A streaming audio filter: frames go in through Send(AudioFrame) and come out through TryReceive(out AudioFrame?), the same shape as Resampler, decoders and encoders, so filters, the resampler and encoders plug together. Frames of any sample format go in; frames come out as F32Planar with exact timestamps. Implement it to put a filter of your own in an AudioFilterChain. Enums FadeCurve The shape of a AudioFade or Crossfade, as the gain of a fade in over its length. FadeDirection Whether a AudioFade brings the sound in or takes it out. api/Egami.Video.Audio.Resampler.html.summary: Class Resampler Namespace Egami.Video.Audio Assembly Egami.Video.dll Converts audio between any two sample rates with a polyphase windowed-sinc filter (Kaiser window). The filter's phases come from the rate ratio reduced to lowest terms; when that needs more than 1024 phases (as for unusual rates), coefficients between 1024 precomputed phases are interpolated. It works in 32-bit float and keeps time exact: the first output sample has the first input sample's timestamp and every later one follows at the output rate, so a resampled track stays in sync. Frames of any length and format go in through Send(AudioFrame); frames come out through TryReceive(out AudioFrame?), in OutputFormat and OutputLayout, so conversion and channel mixing run in the same pass. public sealed class Resampler : IDisposable Inheritance object Resampler Implements IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // 48 kHz to 44.1 kHz with the default quality (100 dB stopband); frames go in and come out like a codec's. using Resampler resampler = new(48000, 44100, ChannelLayout.Stereo, ResamplerQuality.Good); resampler.Send(tone); resampler.Flush(); long samples = 0; while (resampler.TryReceive(out AudioFrame? frame)) { using (frame) { samples += frame.SampleCount; } } Constructors Resampler(int, int, ChannelLayout, ResamplerQuality, MediaContext?) ChannelMixer Mixes one channel layout into another with a matrix: each output channel is a weighted sum of the input channels. The default matrix follows ITU-R BS.775: a speaker both layouts have passes at full level; a missing center goes to front left and right at -3 dB (0.7071); missing surrounds go to the nearest speakers left (side to back and back to side, at full level when that only renames the pair and at -3 dB when it folds a second pair in, else to the front at -3 dB); a mono output takes left and right at -3 dB and surrounds at -6 dB; LFE is dropped unless asked for. Upmixing only routes the speakers both layouts share, so no channel is made up. Channels with no position map by index. It takes any sample format, any rate from 8 to 384 kHz and any channel layout, weighting surround channels by +1.5 dB and leaving the LFE channel out. api/Egami.Video.Codecs.Av1Codec.html.summary: Class Av1Codec Namespace Egami.Video.Codecs Assembly Egami.Video.dll AV1, as WebM, Matroska, MP4, IVF and raw OBU files carry it, decoded by Egami's AV1 decoder in the Main, High and Professional profiles: 8, 10 and 12 bit, 4:0:0, 4:2:0, 4:2:2 and 4:4:4, film grain, scaled references and scalable streams, every frame equal to libaom's sample for sample. A packet is a temporal unit. Frames come out at their own size (a stream may change size at a key frame) as 8-bit planes, or 16-bit planes holding 10 or 12 bits; a monochrome stream gives 4:0:0 planes. Hidden frames give no frame; a frame shown later with show_existing_frame comes out then. Encoding goes through CreateEncoder(VideoEncoderOptions, MediaContext). public sealed class Av1Codec : VideoCodec Inheritance object VideoCodec Av1Codec Inherited Members VideoCodec.CanDecode(TrackInfo) VideoCodec.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Examples // AV1 from WebM, Matroska, MP4 or IVF reads like any other video: 10 and 12-bit streams give 16-bit planes. using (VideoReader reader = VideoReader.Open("av1.webm")) { foreach (YuvVideoFrame frame in reader.ReadFrames()) { using (frame) { Console.WriteLine($"{frame.Timestamp}: {frame.Width}x{frame.Height}, {frame.Raster.BitDepth} bit {frame.Raster.ChromaFormat}, {frame.Color}"); } } } // The frames as coded, without the film grain the stream asks for; broken units are skipped to the next key frame and // reported as Av1.CorruptFrame or Av1.MissingReference, or repeat the last good frame with Conceal. VideoReaderOptions options = new() { Decoder = new VideoDecoderOptions { ApplyFilmGrain = false }, Errors = DecodeErrorMode.Conceal, }; using VideoReader plain = VideoReader.Open("av1.webm", options); using YuvVideoFrame first = plain.ReadFrame()!; Remarks The frame's color comes from the sequence header; the container's (Color) fills only what the header leaves unspecified. Content light level and mastering display metadata OBUs give Hdr (held until the stream sends new ones; the track's Hdr before any), and an ITU-T T.35 metadata OBU with HDR10+ gives Hdr10Plus. ApplyFilmGrain turns film grain off. A track's av1C (CodecPrivate) supplies the sequence header when the first unit, or the first after a seek, has none. Broken data follows Errors and is reported through the Egami context's diagnostics as Av1.CorruptFrame (the unit's data is broken), Av1.MissingReference (a unit that needs frames from before the first key frame) or Av1.KeyframeFlagMismatch (the container's keyframe flag disagrees with the unit, which wins: a keyframe is a unit starting with a shown key frame). After a broken unit, decoding resumes at the next shown key frame; in Conceal mode the units in between show the last good frame again. Returns IVideoDecoder The decoder. Examples // The built-in codecs, for a MediaContext of your own or to create decoders directly. VideoCodec vp9 = Vp9Codec.Instance, vp8 = Vp8Codec.Instance, mjpeg = MotionJpegCodec.Instance, raw = RawVideoCodec.Instance; using IVideoDecoder decoder = vp9.CreateDecoder(track, VideoDecoderOptions.Default, MediaContext.Default); // Decoders that hand out RGB frames instead of planes. using IVideoDecoder<Rgba8> rgb = VideoCodecs.CreateDecoder<Rgba8>(track); // AV1 from WebM, Matroska, MP4 or IVF reads like any other video: 10 and 12-bit streams give 16-bit planes. using (VideoReader reader = VideoReader.Open("av1.webm")) { foreach (YuvVideoFrame frame in reader.ReadFrames()) { using (frame) { Console.WriteLine($"{frame.Timestamp}: {frame.Width}x{frame.Height}, {frame.Raster.BitDepth} bit {frame.Raster.ChromaFormat}, {frame.Color}"); } } } // The frames as coded, without the film grain the stream asks for; broken units are skipped to the next key frame and // reported as Av1.CorruptFrame or Av1.MissingReference, or repeat the last good frame with Conceal. VideoReaderOptions options = new() { Decoder = new VideoDecoderOptions { ApplyFilmGrain = false }, Errors = DecodeErrorMode.Conceal, }; using VideoReader plain = VideoReader.Open("av1.webm", options); using YuvVideoFrame first = plain.ReadFrame()!; CreateEncoder(VideoEncoderOptions, MediaContext) Creates an AV1 encoder, which codes frames with Egami's Av1StreamEncoder. 8 and 10-bit 4:2:0 planes make Main profile streams, 4:4:4 High and 12-bit or 4:2:2 Professional, coded as they are; RGB frames are converted to 8-bit 4:2:0 BT.601 limited range unless BitDepth or ChromaFormat say otherwise. By default it aims at constant quality 60 at effort 4, looks 25 frames ahead for scene cuts and for a hidden alternate reference at each group's end with a hidden frame halfway to it, both shown later with show_existing_frame, and places a keyframe at least every 10 seconds; VideoEncoderOptions chooses bitrate, constant bitrate, two passes or real time instead, and Av1 holds the expert settings. Each packet is a temporal unit; the track's av1C comes from the sequence header, which also carries the frames' color code points, and keyframes carry their static HDR metadata as metadata OBUs (HDR10+ goes into the frames that have it). Alpha is not coded: AV1 has no alpha in Matroska or MP4. The output is the same at any thread count. public override IVideoEncoder CreateEncoder(VideoEncoderOptions options, MediaContext context) Parameters options VideoEncoderOptions The picture size, frame rate and how to spend bits. context MediaContext The context. Each group's hidden alternate // reference, and a hidden frame halfway to it, are shown later with show_existing_frame. api/Egami.Video.Codecs.CodecHeaders.html.summary: Class CodecHeaders Namespace Egami.Video.Codecs Assembly Egami.Video.dll Lists what a compressed frame's header says, field by field under the codec specification's names, for tools such as egami-video info --headers and for checking an encoder's output. VP8 (RFC 6386 sections 9 and 19), VP9 (VP9 bitstream specification sections 6.2 and 6.3), AV1 (AV1 specification section 5) and FFV1 (RFC 9043 section 4) are described; later codecs add theirs to the same call. An AV1 frame header depends on the reference frames, so CodecHeaderReader reads a track's packets in order to list them whole. public static class CodecHeaders Inheritance object CodecHeaders Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples using IDemuxer demuxer = MediaFile.OpenDemuxer("clip.webm"); TrackInfo track = demuxer.Info.VideoTrack!; while (demuxer.ReadPacket() is { } packet) { using (packet) { if (packet.TrackNumber == track.Number) foreach (CodecHeaderField field in CodecHeaders.Describe(track, packet)) Console.WriteLine($"{field.Name} = {field.Value}"); // key_frame = 0, show_frame = 1, refresh_golden_frame = 0 ... } } Methods CanDescribe(TrackInfo) Returns whether Describe(TrackInfo, EncodedPacket) knows the track's codec. public static bool CanDescribe(TrackInfo track) Parameters track TrackInfo The track. Returns bool Whether its headers can be described. Describe(TrackInfo, EncodedPacket) Lists the header fields of one packet of track, in bitstream order. Lists in the header give one field per entry, named with an index (segment_prob[1]); fields the frame does not code are left out, not filled with the values they imply. For VP8, the coefficient and motion vector probability updates are given as counts (coeff_prob_updates, mv_prob_updates). For VP9, a superframe lists its index (frames_in_superframe_minus_1, frame_sizes[i]) and then each frame after a frame field with its index; each frame gives its uncompressed header, then the compressed header's tx_mode and reference mode with its probability updates as counts (coef_prob_updates and so on). A VP9 frame that takes its size from a reference is read with the track's size, which decides how many tile bits it has. For AV1, each OBU gives obu_type (with temporal_id and spatial_id when it has an extension) and obu_size, then a sequence header its coded fields, a metadata OBU metadata_type and its fields (content light level, mastering display, scalability, timecode; ITU-T T.35 as its country code and itu_t_t35_payload_bytes, the payload's length), and a frame header its start up to error_resilient_mode; the rest needs the reference frames, which CodecHeaderReader keeps. For FFV1, the configuration record's parameters come first when the track has one (version 3), then keyframe; a version 0 or 1 keyframe follows with its parameters, a version 3 frame with each slice's header and footer after a slice field with its index. public static IReadOnlyList<CodecHeaderField> Describe(TrackInfo track, EncodedPacket packet) Parameters track TrackInfo The packet's track. packet EncodedPacket The packet. Returns IReadOnlyList<CodecHeaderField> The fields; empty when the codec is not one CanDescribe(TrackInfo) knows. Exceptions CorruptDataException The header is cut off or breaks the codec's rules.

api/Egami.Video.Codecs.Ffv1Codec.html.title: Class Ffv1Codec | Egami
api/Egami.Video.Codecs.Ffv1Codec.html.summary: Class Ffv1Codec Namespace Egami.Video.Codecs Assembly Egami.Video.dll FFV1, the lossless video codec archives use (RFC 9043), as Matroska and AVI carry it: versions 0, 1 and 3, Golomb-Rice and the range coder with the default or a custom state table, YCbCr 4:2:0, 4:2:2, 4:4:4, 4:1:1, 4:1:0 and gray with or without alpha, and RGB with or without alpha, at 8 to 16 bits, every frame equal to FFmpeg's sample for sample. Frames come out as their own planes: 8-bit planes, or 16-bit planes holding 10, 12 or 16 bits, where depths 9, 11, 13, 14 and 15 sit in the next of those with their samples shifted up. RGB comes out as G, B and R planes tagged Identity. Version 2, which was experimental, and 4:4:0 streams are not decoded. public sealed class Ffv1Codec : VideoCodec Inheritance object VideoCodec Ffv1Codec Inherited Members VideoCodec.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Examples using var reader = VideoReader.Open("master.mkv"); foreach (YuvVideoFrame frame in reader.ReadFrames()) using (frame) Console.WriteLine($"{frame.Timestamp}: {frame.Raster.BitDepth} bit {frame.Raster.ChromaFormat}"); Remarks FFV1 carries no color information, so the frame's color comes from the container (Color), or is BT.601 limited range when it says nothing. Broken data follows Errors and is reported through the Egami context's diagnostics as Ffv1.SliceCrc (a slice's CRC does not match), Ffv1.ConfigCrc (the configuration record's CRC does not match), Ffv1.CorruptFrame (a slice or frame cannot be read) or Ffv1.MissingReference (a non-keyframe with no keyframe before it). In Conceal mode a damaged slice shows the last good frame there. Properties CanEncode Gets whether CreateEncoder(VideoEncoderOptions, MediaContext) is supported. public override bool CanEncode { get; } Property Value bool CodecId Gets the Matroska codec id that encoders write (CodecIds). public override string CodecId { get; } Property Value string Instance Gets the FFV1 codec. public static Ffv1Codec Instance { get; } Property Value Ffv1Codec Name Gets the codec's name, such as "Motion JPEG". public override string Name { get; } Property Value string Methods CanDecode(TrackInfo) Decodes Ffv1 tracks, and Matroska's VfwFourCC tracks whose BITMAPINFOHEADER names FFV1. public override bool CanDecode(TrackInfo track) Parameters track TrackInfo The track. Returns bool Whether this codec decodes it. CreateDecoder(VideoTrackInfo, VideoDecoderOptions?, MediaContext) Creates a decoder for a track. public override IVideoDecoder CreateDecoder(VideoTrackInfo track, VideoDecoderOptions? options, MediaContext context) Parameters track VideoTrackInfo The track, as the demuxer describes it. options VideoDecoderOptions How to decode, or null for the defaults. context MediaContext The context frames are allocated from. Returns IVideoDecoder The decoder. Examples // The built-in codecs, for a MediaContext of your own or to create decoders directly. VideoCodec vp9 = Vp9Codec.Instance, vp8 = Vp8Codec.Instance, mjpeg = MotionJpegCodec.Instance, raw = RawVideoCodec.Instance; using IVideoDecoder decoder = vp9.CreateDecoder(track, VideoDecoderOptions.Default, MediaContext.Default); // Decoders that hand out RGB frames instead of planes. using IVideoDecoder<Rgba8> rgb = VideoCodecs.CreateDecoder<Rgba8>(track); // The built-in codecs, for a MediaContext of your own or to create decoders directly. VideoCodec vp9 = Vp9Codec.Instance, vp8 = Vp8Codec.Instance, mjpeg = MotionJpegCodec.Instance, raw = RawVideoCodec.Instance; using IVideoDecoder decoder = vp9.CreateDecoder(track, VideoDecoderOptions.Default, MediaContext.Default); // Decoders that hand out RGB frames instead of planes. using IVideoDecoder<Rgba8> rgb = VideoCodecs.CreateDecoder<Rgba8>(track); CreateEncoder(VideoEncoderOptions, MediaContext) Creates an FFV1 encoder: version 3, every frame equal to its input after a decode. Frames given as planes keep their layout (4:2:0, 4:2:2, 4:4:4, 4:1:1, 4:1:0 or gray, with or without alpha, 8 to 16 bits); a 4:4:4 raster tagged Identity, and any RGB raster, is coded as RGB. The first frame sets the stream's layout, which the track then describes (its configuration record in CodecPrivate). By default every frame is a keyframe, slices end in CRCs and the range coder uses a custom state table: the profile archives use. KeyframeInterval spaces keyframes further apart, Effort picks the context model and Ffv1 holds the rest. FFV1 is lossless, so Quality is ignored and reported as Ffv1.QualityIgnored. Slices are coded in parallel, and the output is the same at any thread count. public override IVideoEncoder CreateEncoder(VideoEncoderOptions options, MediaContext context) Parameters options VideoEncoderOptions The picture size, frame rate and FFV1 settings. context MediaContext The context. Returns IVideoEncoder The encoder. Examples // FFV1 keeps every sample: RGB frames are coded as RGB and planes keep their layout and depth. The defaults are the // archival profile (version 3, every frame a keyframe, slice CRCs, the range coder with a custom table). VideoWriterOptions options = new() { Codec = VideoCodecs.Ffv1, FrameRate = new Rational(25, 1) }; using (VideoWriter writer = VideoWriter.Create("master.mkv", options)) { for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) { using Raster<Rgb8> frame = duck.Derive(ops => ops.Crop(new Rect(i * 4, i * 2, 320, 240))); writer.WriteFrame(frame); } } // Expert settings: more slices for more threads, Golomb-Rice for speed, a keyframe every 10 frames for smaller files. VideoWriterOptions fast = options with { KeyframeInterval = 10, Ffv1 = new Ffv1EncoderOptions { Slices = 16, Coder = Ffv1Coder.GolombRice, ContextModel = Ffv1ContextModel.Small }, }; // Check the archive without decoding it. bool intact = Ffv1Codec.Verify("master.mkv").IsIntact; Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException An option is out of range. Verify(Stream, MediaContext?, bool, CancellationToken) Checks an FFV1 stream's fixity without decoding pictures. See Verify(string, MediaContext?, CancellationToken). public static Ffv1VerifyResult Verify(Stream stream, MediaContext? context = null, bool leaveOpen = false, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters stream Stream The Matroska or AVI file, from its start. context MediaContext The context, or null for Default. leaveOpen bool Whether to leave stream open afterwards. cancellationToken CancellationToken Stops the check between frames. Returns Ffv1VerifyResult What was checked and every problem found. Examples // Check an archive's fixity without decoding pictures: the configuration record's CRC and every slice's. Ffv1VerifyResult result = Ffv1Codec.Verify("master.mkv"); Console.WriteLine($"{result.Frames} frames, {result.Slices} slices checked: {(result.IsIntact ? "intact" : "damaged")}"); foreach (Ffv1VerifyError error in result.Errors) { Console.WriteLine($"frame {error.Frame} at {error.Timestamp}, slice {error.Slice}: {error.Problem}"); } Exceptions UnsupportedFormatException The file has no FFV1 track. Verify(string, MediaContext?, CancellationToken) Checks an FFV1 file's fixity without decoding pictures: the configuration record's CRC, and in every frame of the first FFV1 track each slice's footer and CRC (RFC 9043 section 4.9). This is far faster than decoding, so archives can run it routinely. api/Egami.Video.Codecs.RateControlMode.h.summary: Enum RateControlMode Namespace Egami.Video.Codecs Assembly Egami.Video.dll How an encoder spends bits: on a quality, on a bitrate or on a fixed quantizer. public enum RateControlMode Fields Bitrate = 1 A target average bitrate (Bitrate) that bits are spread over by frame complexity: one pass, or two with FirstPassStats. ConstantBitrate = 2 A constant bitrate that a decoder buffer of BufferSize never runs dry on, as live streams and WebRTC want. Quality = 0 Constant quality, the default: every frame aims at Quality, so files are as large as the content needs. Best for files. Frames with alpha get a second VP9 stream for it, which WebM and Matroska carry. The output is the same at any thread count. public override IVideoEncoder CreateEncoder(VideoEncoderOptions options, MediaContext context) Parameters options VideoEncoderOptions The picture size, frame rate and how to spend bits. context MediaContext The context. Returns IVideoEncoder The encoder. Examples // VP9 in WebM at constant quality, on the same Quality and Effort scales as VP8. api/Egami.Video.Codecs.html.title: Namespace Egami.Video.Codecs | Egami
api/Egami.Video.Codecs.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Video.Codecs Classes Av1Codec AV1, as WebM, Matroska, MP4, IVF and raw OBU files carry it, decoded by Egami's AV1 decoder in the Main, High and Professional profiles: 8, 10 and 12 bit, 4:0:0, 4:2:0, 4:2:2 and 4:4:4, film grain, scaled references and scalable streams, every frame equal to libaom's sample for sample. A packet is a temporal unit. Frames come out at their own size (a stream may change size at a key frame) as 8-bit planes, or 16-bit planes holding 10 or 12 bits; a monochrome stream gives 4:0:0 planes. Hidden frames give no frame; a frame shown later with show_existing_frame comes out then. Encoding goes through CreateEncoder(VideoEncoderOptions, MediaContext). Av1EncoderOptions The AV1 settings beyond VideoEncoderOptions, for experts: quantizer limits, hidden alternate reference frames and their pyramid, golden frame spacing, the temporal filter, adaptive quantization, screen content tools, error resilience and the bit depth. Every one has a default that suits most uses. Av1Packets Helpers for AV1 packets, which hold a temporal unit of low-overhead OBUs (AV1 specification section 5, each OBU with its size field): split a unit into its frames and merge them back, and build the av1C configuration record MP4 and Matroska store for a track. CodecHeaderReader Lists the header fields of a track's packets read in order, keeping what a codec's later headers depend on. For AV1 it decodes each temporal unit with Egami's Av1StreamDecoder, so each frame header is listed whole, as the decoder read it (LastHeaders, under the specification's syntax element and variable names), in place of the start Describe(TrackInfo, EncodedPacket) gives. Other codecs give what Describe(TrackInfo, EncodedPacket) gives. CodecHeaders Lists what a compressed frame's header says, field by field under the codec specification's names, for tools such as egami-video info --headers and for checking an encoder's output. VP8 (RFC 6386 sections 9 and 19), VP9 (VP9 bitstream specification sections 6.2 and 6.3), AV1 (AV1 specification section 5) and FFV1 (RFC 9043 section 4) are described; later codecs add theirs to the same call. An AV1 frame header depends on the reference frames, so CodecHeaderReader reads a track's packets in order to list them whole. EncodeFrameOptions What one Send(VideoFrame, EncodeFrameOptions) call asks for beyond the frame. Ffv1Codec FFV1, the lossless video codec archives use (RFC 9043), as Matroska and AVI carry it: versions 0, 1 and 3, Golomb-Rice and the range coder with the default or a custom state table, YCbCr 4:2:0, 4:2:2, 4:4:4, 4:1:1, 4:1:0 and gray with or without alpha, and RGB with or without alpha, at 8 to 16 bits, every frame equal to FFmpeg's sample for sample. Frames come out as their own planes: 8-bit planes, or 16-bit planes holding 10, 12 or 16 bits, where depths 9, 11, 13, 14 and 15 sit in the next of those with their samples shifted up. RGB comes out as G, B and R planes tagged Identity. Version 2, which was experimental, and 4:4:0 streams are not decoded. Ffv1EncoderOptions FFV1's expert encoder settings (Ffv1, Ffv1). The defaults are the archival profile: version 3, the range coder with a custom state table, slice CRCs on, and a slice grid picked from the frame size. Ffv1VerifyError One problem Verify(string, MediaContext?, CancellationToken) found. Ffv1VerifyResult What Verify(string, MediaContext?, CancellationToken) found: how much it checked and every CRC that did not match. A version 3 stream with slice CRCs is checked whole; versions 0 and 1, and version 3 written without slice CRCs, have only what can be checked without decoding (the configuration record and the slice layout). FirstPassStats What the first pass of a two-pass encode learned about each frame: how hard it is to code. Pass it as FirstPassStats with Bitrate, and the second pass spreads the bits over the whole clip by it instead of guessing from the frames so far. Save(Stream) keeps it in a file, so the two passes can run apart, as FFmpeg's pass log does. MotionJpegCodec Motion JPEG: every frame a complete JPEG image, decoded and encoded by Egami's JPEG codec. Decoding fixes frames without a DHT segment, weaves interlaced field pairs, ignores junk around the image and decodes several frames at once. Frames come out as the JPEG's own YUV planes, BT.601 full range unless the container says otherwise. RawVideoCodec Uncompressed video (Uncompressed): I420, YV12, Y42B, 444P, Y800, NV12, NV21, YUY2, UYVY and v210 by FourCC (FourCC), plain planar YUV at 8 to 12 bits with optional alpha as in YUV4MPEG2, and AVI's bottom-up 24-bit BI_RGB (as VfwFourCC), whose frames come out as G, B and R planes (Identity). Decoding and encoding copy samples, so they are lossless. VideoCodec A video codec: which tracks it decodes and how to create its decoder and encoder. Register a new one with WithCodec(VideoCodec). VideoCodecs Creates decoders and encoders from the codecs registered in a MediaContext. VideoDecoderOptions How a decoder decodes. VideoEncoderOptions What an encoder makes. Vp8Codec VP8 (RFC 6386), as WebM, Matroska and IVF carry it, decoded by Egami's Vp8StreamDecoder: every frame equals libvpx's sample for sample. Frames come out as 8-bit 4:2:0 planes, BT.601 limited range unless the container says otherwise; hidden frames (alternate references) give no frame. A WebM track with alpha (HasAlpha) decodes its second VP8 stream, carried in each packet's addition 1, into the frame's alpha plane unless DecodeAlpha is off. Encoding goes through CreateEncoder(VideoEncoderOptions, MediaContext). Vp8EncoderOptions The VP8 settings beyond VideoEncoderOptions, for experts: quantizer limits, alternate reference frames, golden frame spacing, token partitions and error resilience. Every one has a default that suits most uses. Vp9Codec VP9, as WebM, Matroska and IVF carry it, decoded in all four profiles: 8, 10 and 12 bit, 4:2:0, 4:2:2, 4:4:4 and RGB, with every frame equal to libvpx's sample for sample. Frames come out at their own coded size (a stream may change size between keyframes) as 8-bit planes, or 16-bit planes holding 10 or 12 bits; hidden frames (alternate references) give no frame. A WebM track with alpha (HasAlpha) decodes its second VP9 stream, carried in each packet's addition 1, into the frame's alpha plane unless DecodeAlpha is off. 4:4:0 streams are not decoded. Encoding goes through CreateEncoder(VideoEncoderOptions, MediaContext). Vp9EncoderOptions The VP9 settings beyond VideoEncoderOptions, for experts: quantizer limits, alternate reference frames, golden frame spacing, tile columns, adaptive quantization, error resilience, the bit depth and alpha. Every one has a default that suits most uses. Structs CodecHeaderField One field of a compressed frame's header, as Describe(TrackInfo, EncodedPacket) lists it. Interfaces IVideoDecoder Turns packets into frames with a send and receive loop. One packet can give no frame yet (a codec that holds frames back) or several, so after each Send(EncodedPacket) call TryReceive(out YuvVideoFrame?) until it returns false, and at the end of the stream call Flush() and receive what is left. IVideoDecoder<TPixel> A decoder that converts its frames to TPixel pixels. See IVideoDecoder. IVideoEncoder Turns frames into packets with a send and receive loop, the mirror of IVideoDecoder. After each Send(VideoFrame) call TryReceive(out EncodedPacket?) until it returns false; at the end call Flush() and receive what is left. Enums Ffv1Coder The entropy coder FFV1 codes samples with (RFC 9043 section 4.2.3). Ffv1ContextModel How many neighbours FFV1's contexts look at. LatencyMode Whether an encoder may hold frames back to code them better, as WebCodecs' latencyMode. RateControlMode How an encoder spends bits: on a quality, on a bitrate or on a fixed quantizer.

The reader takes ID3v2.2, 2.3 and 2.4 tags (text frames into Tags, pictures as attachments with the front cover named cover.*, CHAP frames as chapters), ID3v1 and APEv2 tags at the end, and finds frames by three matching headers, so junk and false syncs are skipped. A Xing, Info or VBRI frame gives the frame count and duration, and its LAME tag the encoder delay and padding, so the audio is gapless: the first packet starts before zero and the last packet's duration stops at the source's end. Seeks are exact by default (FastSeek uses the Xing table instead). api/Egami.Video.Containers.Mp4FragmentOp.summary: Class Mp4FragmentOptions Namespace Egami.Video.Containers Assembly Egami.Video.dll How Mp4Format writes fragmented MP4 (ISO/IEC 14496-12 8.8, V4.3 Design Q1 and Q3): moov holds only the track setup, and the media follows as moof and mdat pairs, so nothing is written back and nothing waits in a temporary file.
