api/Egami.Video.Containers.html.title: Namespace Egami.Video.Containers | Egami
api/Egami.Video.Containers.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Video.Containers Classes Ac3Format Raw AC-3 and E-AC-3 (.ac3, .eac3, .ec3; ATSC A/52): sync frames back to back, with no container around them. AC-3 frames (Ac3) are read one per packet; E-AC-3 (EAc3) is passed through, an independent frame and the substreams that follow it per packet. Writing copies the packets out unchanged, so a track from MP4, Matroska, CAF or AVI can be extracted without decoding. Seeking builds a frame index in one pass. AiffFormat AIFF and AIFF-C (.aif, .aiff, .aifc; Apple's Audio Interchange File Format 1.3 and its AIFF-C draft): big-endian integer PCM, AIFF-C's little-endian (sowt), 24 and 32-bit (in24, in32), float (fl32, fl64) and G.711 (ulaw, alaw) samples. Other AIFF-C compressions (ima4, MACE, QDesign and so on) pass through undecoded with an "X_AIFC/" codec id. The NAME, AUTH, "(c) " and ANNO chunks and an ID3 chunk become Tags (ID3 pictures become attachments), MARK markers become chapters, and a CHAN chunk gives the channel layout. The writer stores integer PCM as AIFF and float as AIFF-C, the title, artist, copyright and comment in the text chunks, any other tag and cover art in an ID3 chunk, chapters as markers and the layout of more than two channels in a CHAN chunk. A non-seekable output is written through a temporary file, since AIFF's sizes come before the samples. Seeking is sample exact. Av1AnnexBFormat A raw AV1 stream in the length-delimited format of the AV1 specification's Annex B, as the AV1 conformance streams and aomenc --annexb=1 write it: each temporal unit, each frame unit in it and each OBU in that carries its length as leb128, and OBUs have no size field. Readers give each temporal unit as a packet of low-overhead OBUs with their size fields, the form every other container uses; writers turn such packets back, dropping the size fields and adding the lengths, with a temporal delimiter at the start of each unit. There are no timestamps: temporal unit n is at n frames of FrameRate. Reading a file and writing it back gives the same bytes. Not detected from the extension, which .obu files share: an Annex B file is recognized by its first temporal delimiter. Av1ObuFormat A raw AV1 stream of low-overhead OBUs (.obu; AV1 specification section 5.2), as aomenc writes with --obu and aomdec and dav1d read: each temporal unit starts with a temporal delimiter OBU, and every OBU has its size field. There is no header, index or timestamp, so temporal unit n is at n frames of FrameRate. Reading a file and writing it back gives the same bytes; the writer adds a temporal delimiter to a packet that has none. The track's size, bit depth, chroma format and av1C come from the first sequence header. AviFormat AVI, the RIFF-based container from Video for Windows, with the OpenDML extensions for files over 1 GB. Reads any AVI and writes Motion JPEG video with audio and other tracks copied through. CafFormat Apple's Core Audio Format (.caf): one audio track of PCM (integer or float, either byte order), G.711, ALAC, Opus, AAC, MP3, AC-3 or FLAC, with 64-bit chunk sizes, so no 4 GB limit. The packet table (pakt) cuts variable-size packets and gives the priming frames (CodecDelay) and the padding at the end; the magic cookie (kuki) becomes CodecPrivate; the info chunk becomes Tags; markers and regions, named from the strg chunk, become chapters; and a chan chunk gives the channel layout. Other formats pass through undecoded with an "X_CAF/" codec id. The writer streams PCM and G.711 (a data chunk sized -1 on a non-seekable output) and puts the packet table of other codecs after the samples, or before them through a temporary file when the output is not seekable. Seeking is sample exact for PCM and packet exact for the rest. ContainerFormat A container format: how to recognize it and how to open a demuxer or muxer for it. Register a new one with WithContainer(ContainerFormat). FlacFormat Native FLAC files (.flac): "fLaC", the metadata blocks and the frames. STREAMINFO gives the track; Vorbis comments become Tags (a WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE_CHANNEL_MASK comment the track's layout) and pictures become attachments, the front cover named cover.*. Frames are found by their sync code, header CRC-8 and footer CRC-16, so each packet is one whole frame; seeking uses the seek table, or one pass over the frames when there is none. The writer stores STREAMINFO, tags, cover art and padding; on a seekable stream it fills in the frame sizes, total samples and MD5 at the end and turns part of the padding into a seek table with a point every 10 seconds. IvfFormat IVF (.ivf): the bare frame container libvpx's tools and the VP8, VP9 and AV1 test vectors use. A 32-byte file header (FourCC, size, time base, frame count) and a 12-byte header per frame (size, timestamp), with no index. Reads and writes VP8 (VP80), VP9 (VP90) and AV1 (AV01) tracks; seeking scans the frame headers once. Reading a file and writing it back gives the same bytes. MatroskaFormat Matroska (RFC 9559) and its WebM subset. Both instances read either; they differ in the DocType and extension a muxer writes: Instance writes Matroska (.mkv), WebM writes WebM (.webm). Mp3Format MPEG audio files (.mp3, .mp2, .mp1, .mpa): MP3 and MP2 frames with their tags. The reader takes ID3v2.2, 2.3 and 2.4 tags (text frames into Tags, pictures as attachments with the front cover named cover.*, CHAP frames as chapters), ID3v1 and APEv2 tags at the end, and finds frames by three matching headers, so junk and false syncs are skipped. A Xing, Info or VBRI frame gives the frame count and duration, and its LAME tag the encoder delay and padding, so the audio is gapless: the first packet starts before zero and the last packet's duration stops at the source's end. Seeks are exact by default (FastSeek uses the Xing table instead). The writer stores an ID3v2.4 tag and the frames, with a Xing header and LAME-layout tag on a seekable stream, so MP3 can leave Matroska or MP4 without a re-encode. Mp4Format MP4 and QuickTime (ISO/IEC 14496-12 and 14496-14, and Apple's QuickTime File Format): .mp4, .m4v, .m4a and .mov files, flat or fragmented (CMAF, DASH segments). Reads every track: AV1, VP9, VP8, Motion JPEG, Opus, FLAC, PCM and mov_text map to their codec ids, and any other track (H.264, HEVC, AAC, timecode) is passed through so a remux keeps it. Edit lists are applied, the display matrix becomes Orientation, and tags, chapters and cover art are read. Mp4FragmentOptions How Mp4Format writes fragmented MP4 (ISO/IEC 14496-12 8.8, V4.3 Design Q1 and Q3): moov holds only the track setup, and the media follows as moof and mdat pairs, so nothing is written back and nothing waits in a temporary file. A fragment starts at the first video keyframe after Duration; audio-only files cut every Duration. Mp4SegmentOptions How Mp4SegmentWriter cuts segments and which playlists it writes. Mp4SegmentWriter Writes a file as segments for HLS and DASH (V4.3 Design Q6 and Q7): for each track a CMAF init segment (ftyp and moov) and numbered media segments (styp, sidx, moof and mdat), cut at the first video keyframe after SegmentDuration so every segment starts with one, plus an HLS multivariant playlist with a media playlist a track and a static DASH MPD. Each segment, read after its track's init segment, is valid fragmented MP4. A track is named after its kind and number: video1-init.mp4, video1-00001.m4s, video1.m3u8; the playlists are master.m3u8 and manifest.mpd. Holds the audio and video codecs Mp4Format writes, one rendition: bitrate ladders, live playlists and encryption are not written (Q8, Q9). OggFormat Ogg (.ogg, .opus, .oga), RFC 3533, with the Opus (RFC 7845), Vorbis and FLAC mappings. Pages are CRC-checked and packets rebuilt across them; timestamps come from granule positions, with Opus's pre-skip as the track's codec delay and the last page's granule position trimming the end. Seeking uses an index of granule positions built in one pass over the page headers on open. Chained files (one stream after another, as internet radio dumps are) read as one track when the codec settings stay the same, each link's TITLE a chapter; a link that changes them ends the track with an "ogg-chained-stream" warning. The writer stores Opus, Vorbis and FLAC with tags, so a WebM's Opus track remuxes to .opus without decoding. RawVideo Headerless raw video ("rawvideo"): frames of one uncompressed layout back to back, as FFmpeg's -f rawvideo reads and writes them. Nothing in the file says the size or layout, so the caller gives them as a track. WavFormat WAV (.wav): RIFF WAVE with integer or float PCM, WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE (channel mask and valid bits) and the compressed formats AVI also names, plus RF64 and BW64 for files over 4 GB (Instance) and Sony Wave64 (.w64, Wave64). Streamed files whose sizes were never filled in (0 or 0xFFFFFFFF) are read to the end. LIST/INFO and id3 tags become Tags, and cue points with their labels become chapters. The writer stores PCM and float, INFO tags and chapters as cue points, and turns a WAV file into RF64 by itself when the data passes 4 GB, as EBU Tech 3306 says (a JUNK chunk reserved after the header becomes the ds64 chunk). Seeking is sample exact. Y4mFormat YUV4MPEG2 (.y4m): uncompressed planar YUV frames behind a one-line text header, the common exchange format of video tools and codec test suites. Reads 4:2:0, 4:2:2, 4:4:4 and gray at 8, 10 and 12 bits, and 4:4:4 with alpha; writes the same. Reading a file and writing it back gives the same bytes. Interfaces IDemuxer Reads a container's tracks and packets. Packets come in file order, interleaved across tracks. IMuxer Writes packets into a container. Packets should come in timestamp order across tracks, as a demuxer returns them. Dispose() finishes the file if Finish() was not called. Enums Mp4NonSeekableLayout What Mp4Format writes to a stream that cannot seek and read back (V4.3 Design Q2). SegmentPlaylists Which playlists Mp4SegmentWriter writes with its segments (V4.3 Design Q7).

api/Egami.Video.DecodeErrorMode.html.title: Enum DecodeErrorMode | Egami
api/Egami.Video.DecodeErrorMode.html.summary: Enum DecodeErrorMode Namespace Egami.Video Assembly Egami.Video.dll What a decoder or VideoReader does with a frame it cannot decode. public enum DecodeErrorMode Fields Conceal = 2 Reports the frame and keeps going, filling what could not be read from the previous frame (VP8: the damaged macroblocks; mid-gray when there is no previous frame). Codecs with nothing to fill from (Motion JPEG) drop the frame, as in Skip. Skip = 1 Reports the frame through the Egami context's diagnostics and drops it, then, for codecs whose frames depend on earlier ones (VP8), every frame up to the next keyframe, so no wrong picture is ever shown. The default for VideoReader. Throw = 0 Throws CorruptDataException. The default for decoders made directly, so callers see every problem. Examples // How a reader decodes: which track, what a broken frame does (Skip, the default, drops it up to the next keyframe; // Conceal repeats the last good frame; Throw throws) and the codec's own options. VideoReaderOptions options = new() { TrackNumber = 1, Errors = DecodeErrorMode.Conceal, Decoder = new VideoDecoderOptions { DecodeAlpha = false }, }; using VideoReader reader = VideoReader.Open("alpha.webm", options); using YuvVideoFrame frame = reader.ReadFrame()!;

api/Egami.Video.Editing.ClipFit.html.summary: Enum ClipFit Namespace Egami.Video.Editing Assembly Egami.Video.dll How a clip whose size differs from the canvas is fitted to it. public enum ClipFit Fields Contain = 0 Scaled to fit inside the canvas with its aspect ratio kept, the rest filled with the background (letterbox or pillarbox). api/Egami.Video.Editing.TransitionKind.h.title: Enum TransitionKind | Egami
api/Egami.Video.Editing.TransitionKind.h.summary: Enum TransitionKind Namespace Egami.Video.Editing Assembly Egami.Video.dll The built-in kinds of Transition. public enum TransitionKind Fields Blur = 10 The first clip blurs out while the second blurs in, like hblur in both directions. CircleClose = 6 The first clip stays inside a circle that shrinks to the centre, like circleclose. CircleOpen = 5 The second clip shows inside a circle that grows from the centre, like circleopen. Clock = 7 The second clip shows behind a hand that sweeps clockwise from twelve o'clock, like radial. Custom = 11 An app's own ITransition. Dissolve = 2 The second clip appears pixel by pixel in a fixed noise order, like dissolve. Fade = 0 A cross-dissolve: the two clips blended by progress, like ffmpeg's xfade=fade. FadeThroughColor = 1 The first clip fades to a colour, then the second fades in from it, like fadeblack and fadewhite. Pixelize = 9 The first clip breaks up into growing blocks, then the second sharpens out of them, like pixelize. Slide = 4 The second clip slides in from the far side, pushing the first one out in Direction, like slideleft. Wipe = 3 A straight edge moves across in Direction, uncovering the second clip, like wipeleft. Zoom = 8 The first clip zooms in towards its centre while the second fades in, like zoomin. Examples // A dissolve, then a soft wipe with eased progress: each overlaps the two clips by its length, sound crossfading too. VideoEdit edit = new(new EditCanvas(320, 180, new Rational(25, 1))); edit.Track.Add(Clip.Open("intro.avi")) .Add(Clip.Open("talk.avi"), Transition.Dissolve(MediaTime.FromSeconds(0.5))) .Add(Clip.Open("outro.avi"), Transition.Wipe(TransitionDirection.Left, MediaTime.FromSeconds(0.5)) with { Softness = 0.1, Easing = Easing.EaseInOut }); EditPlan plan = edit.Render("transitions.mkv");

api/Egami.Video.Editing.html.title: Namespace Egami.Video.Editing | Egami
api/Egami.Video.Editing.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Video.Editing Classes CameraMotion How the camera moved from one frame to the next, as Analyze(string, MotionAnalysisOptions?, IProgress<MediaProgress>?, CancellationToken) measures it: a shift, a rotation and a scale per frame, in the clip's own pixels. It is pass 1 of stabilization; pass 2, Stabilize(CameraMotion, StabilizeOptions?), smooths the path and warps the frames. Save it as JSON to stabilize again with other settings without measuring again. ChromaKey A chroma key for Key(ChromaKey): pixels near Color in the CbCr plane become transparent with Egami's ChromaKey(Rgba8, float, float), then Despill(DespillColor, float, float) takes the screen's colour out of the edges and see-through pixels that are left. Clip A piece of video, with its audio, as it goes into a VideoEdit: a file or stream, or a Stack of clips. The methods return a changed copy, so they chain: Clip.Open("a.mp4").Trim(start, end).FadeIn(duration). Nothing is decoded until the edit renders. ClipStabilization A clip's stabilization, set by Stabilize(CameraMotion, StabilizeOptions?): the measured camera motion and how it is smoothed. EditCanvas The output of a VideoEdit: picture size, frame rate, how clips are fitted, the background, and the audio format every clip's audio is resampled and remixed to. When an edit has no canvas, it takes the first clip's size and frame rate. EditEffect Egami operations or an app's own effect on the frames of a VideoEdit, a Clip or a Layer, optionally only inside a time window (Between(MediaTime, MediaTime?)). Effects keep the frame size. EditPlan An edit's timeline worked out before rendering by Plan(MediaContext?): the canvas, where every clip and layer falls in whole frames, the length, and warnings about things it fixed up, such as a trim past a clip's end. EditRenderOptions How Render(string, EditRenderOptions?, IProgress<MediaProgress>?, CancellationToken) encodes. EditTrack The main track of a VideoEdit: clips that play one after another. A Transition between two clips overlaps them by its length; without one, the next clip starts on the frame after the last one ends. Layer A clip drawn over the main track of a VideoEdit inside a time window: a logo, a picture-in-picture, a lower third or a keyed presenter. It has a place, an opacity, a blend mode, fades, an optional ChromaKey and keyframed motion. Layers draw in order, the last on top. The methods return a changed copy, so they chain. MotionAnalysisOptions How Analyze(string, MotionAnalysisOptions?, IProgress<MediaProgress>?, CancellationToken) measures. PanZoomPath A pan and zoom for PanZoom(RectangleF, RectangleF, Easing): the part of the picture shown at the start and at the end, as fractions of it. PlannedClip Where one clip of the main track falls in a planned edit, in whole output frames. PlannedLayer Where one layer falls in a planned edit, in whole output frames. Slideshow Builds a VideoEdit that shows images one after another, with transitions and an optional pan and zoom. SlideshowOptions How Create(IEnumerable<string>, SlideshowOptions?) builds a slideshow. StabilizeOptions How Stabilize(CameraMotion, StabilizeOptions?) smooths the camera path and treats the edges. Stabilizer Pass 1 of two-pass stabilization: measures the camera's motion over a clip (CameraMotion). Pass 2 is Stabilize(CameraMotion, StabilizeOptions?), which smooths the camera path with a Gaussian and warps each frame onto it. Stack Builds one clip out of several shown at once: side by side, one above the other, or in a grid. A stack is an ordinary Clip, so it can be trimmed, faded or joined with a transition. StackOptions How a Stack is drawn and how long it lasts. TrackItem One clip on an EditTrack and the transition into it from the clip before. Transition How one clip on an EditTrack changes into the next. The two clips overlap by Duration, so the edit gets shorter by it; their audio crossfades over the same time, equal power by default. Make one with the static methods, such as Dissolve(MediaTime) or Wipe(TransitionDirection, MediaTime). VideoEdit An edit: clips on a main Track with transitions between them, Layers drawn over it, and Effects on the result, all fitted to one Canvas. It is a description: Plan(MediaContext?) lays out the timeline and checks it, and Render(string, EditRenderOptions?, IProgress<MediaProgress>?, CancellationToken) decodes, composes and encodes it in one pass, holding only the frames in use. Save it as JSON with ToJson(). Structs ClipFreeze A frame of a Clip held still for a time by Freeze(MediaTime, MediaTime). FrameEffectContext Where an IFrameEffect is: the frame's time and how far through its window it is. FrameMotion The camera's motion into one frame from the one before: about the frame's centre, in its pixels. Interfaces IFrameEffect An app's own effect for Of(IFrameEffect, string?), which knows each frame's time. It changes the frame in place. The same instance runs on every frame, so keep it stateless. IFrameSource An app's own frames for FromSource(IFrameSource), such as titles drawn with Egami.Drawing or generated graphics. The renderer asks for the frames in time order, once per output frame. ITransition An app's own picture transition for Custom(ITransition, MediaTime): it draws one frame of the change from one clip to the next. The two frames and the target have the canvas size. The same instance draws every frame, possibly on several threads, so keep it stateless. Enums ClipFit How a clip whose size differs from the canvas is fitted to it. LayerProperty A property of a Layer that Animate(LayerProperty, params Keyframe[]) moves over time. StabilizeEdges What Stabilize(CameraMotion, StabilizeOptions?) does with the edges a correction uncovers. StackLayout How a Stack lays out its clips. TransitionDirection Which way a Wipe edge or a Slide moves. TransitionKind The built-in kinds of Transition.

SubtitleCue One subtitle: when it shows, its text as SubtitleSpan runs, and where and how it is placed. Read from SRT, WebVTT or ASS into the same fields, so a cue converts between them; a cue that is not changed is written back to its own format exactly as it was read. SubtitleDocument A subtitle file in memory: its cues, and the styles, regions and header its format carries. Loads SRT, WebVTT, ASS and SSA into one model, saves any of SRT, WebVTT and ASS, and shifts, scales, syncs and clips the timing. A document saved in the format it was read from, unchanged, gives back the same bytes; changed cues are written in the format's canonical form, and what a target format cannot hold is reported once per kind as Subtitle.Dropped. SubtitleReaderOptions How SubtitleDocument reads a subtitle file. SubtitleRegion A WebVTT region (a REGION block): a box cues can show in, which scrolls lines up as new cues arrive. Cues name it in Region. SubtitleSpan A run of a cue's text with one look: bold, italic, color, font and so on, as SRT tags, WebVTT cue tags and ASS override tags set them. Line breaks are \n inside Text. Fields a format cannot show are dropped when it is written, and reported as Subtitle.Dropped. api/Egami.Video.TrimMode.html.title: Enum TrimMode | Egami
api/Egami.Video.TrimMode.html.summary: Enum TrimMode Namespace Egami.Video Assembly Egami.Video.dll How Trim(string, string, MediaTime, MediaTime?, TrimMode, Func<TrackInfo, bool>?, MediaContext?, IProgress<MediaProgress>?, CancellationToken) starts a cut that does not fall on a keyframe. public enum TrimMode Fields Keyframe = 1 Copies every packet: the cut starts at the video keyframe at or before the start, so it may show a few frames more than asked, as ffmpeg -ss -c copy does. Nothing is decoded. Reencode = 2 Decodes the video from the keyframe before the start and encodes every frame of the cut again, with the same codec at the quantizer the source had. Frame-exact like Smart, but slower and with a second generation of loss. Smart = 0 The default: frame-exact, with the fewest frames encoded again. The frames from the start up to the next keyframe are decoded and encoded again as a new group that starts with a keyframe and matches the stream (codec, profile, size, bit depth, chroma format, color, and for AV1 the sequence header byte for byte), at the quantizer the frames it replaces had; every packet from that keyframe on is copied byte for byte. A start on a keyframe, and Motion JPEG or uncompressed video, are a plain copy. Codecs Egami.Video cannot encode (H.264, HEVC) start at the keyframe at or before the start, as Keyframe does; a stream the encoder cannot match is encoded again whole, as Reencode does. Both say so in a MediaWarning. Examples // Frame-exact: only the frames from 0.3 s up to the next keyframe are encoded again; every other packet is copied. TrimResult result = MediaFile.Trim("show.webm", "cut.webm", MediaTime.FromSeconds(0.3), MediaTime.FromSeconds(0.8)); Console.WriteLine($"{result.Frames} frames from {result.Start.Seconds:0.000} s, {result.ReencodedFrames} encoded again"); foreach (MediaWarning warning in result.Warnings) { Console.WriteLine(warning.Message); } // No decoding at all: the cut starts at the keyframe at or before 0.3 s. api/Egami.Video.html.title: Namespace Egami.Video | Egami
api/Egami.Video.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Video Classes AttachmentInfo A file stored inside the container, such as a font for subtitles or cover art ("cover.jpg"). AudioReader Reads the audio of a file in a few lines, the twin of VideoReader: opens the container, picks the audio track, decodes it and hands out AudioFrames, converted to the sample format, rate and layout asked for (planar float by default). Codec delay and padding are trimmed, so the audio has exactly the samples the encoder was given; seeking is sample exact. AudioReaderOptions How an AudioReader reads and converts. AudioTrackInfo An audio track: a TrackInfo with the sample format. AudioWriter Writes an audio file in a few lines, the twin of VideoWriter: encodes each frame and muxes it, picking the container from the file extension. Frames may have any length and sample format; the writer resamples, mixes and converts them to what the codec takes. The rate, layout and bit depth come from the options or the first frame. AudioWriterOptions What an AudioWriter writes. ChapterInfo A chapter: where it starts and ends, and its title. CodecIds Matroska codec ids (from the Matroska codec mapping) for the codecs Egami.Video names. CodecId uses these for every container. EncodedPacket One compressed unit of a track, such as a Motion JPEG frame or a block of audio: what demuxers return, decoders take, encoders return and muxers write. The bytes may sit in a pooled buffer, which Dispose() returns. Hdr10PlusMetadata HDR10+ dynamic metadata for one frame (SMPTE ST 2094-40, application version 0 or 1), as WebM carries it in each block's BlockAdditional with BlockAddID 4 (an ITU-T T.35 payload). The values are the first processing window's, which covers the whole frame; luminances are in cd/m². Egami.Video reads and keeps it but does not tone map with it: HDR to SDR conversion uses the static metadata (Hdr). Hdr10PlusToneCurve An HDR10+ tone mapping curve for the target display: a knee point, then a Bezier curve through its anchors. MediaContext The registered containers and codecs, the safety limits for reading, and the Egami context frames are allocated from. Every entry point takes one, or uses Default. Immutable: derive a new one with with or WithContainer(ContainerFormat) and WithCodec(VideoCodec). MediaFile Entry points for media files: probe what a file holds, open a demuxer to read its packets, or create a muxer to write one. The container is detected from the file's first bytes when reading, and chosen by extension when writing. MediaInfo What a media file holds, read from its headers without decoding any frame. Returned by MediaFile.Probe. MediaLimits Limits that make readers reject hostile files early instead of allocating or looping without bound. MediaMetadata A file's tags, chapters and attachments, as a demuxer reads them and a muxer writes them. MediaWarning Something a reader or writer handled but reports, through Warnings. MovTextSample One mov_text subtitle (3GPP timed text, TS 26.245; codec MovText): its text and the style runs that make parts of it bold, italic, underlined, larger or colored. Parse a packet's bytes to read it, and write one with ToBytes(). Modifier boxes other than styles (highlight, karaoke, scroll delay, links, text box, blink, wrap) are kept as stored, so a sample read and written again keeps its bytes. PacketAddition Extra data stored with a packet (a Matroska BlockMore): an id saying what it is, and its bytes. Id 1 holds a WebM VP8 or VP9 track's alpha frame when the track has HasAlpha. PlaneScores A score per plane (Y, U, V and alpha when present) and an average. TrackInfo A track in a container: its number, kind and codec, as a demuxer reports it and a muxer takes it. Codecs are named with Matroska codec ids (CodecIds), which every container maps to and from, so a track read from AVI can be written to Matroska unchanged. TrimResult What a trim did: where the cut starts in the input, how much was copied and encoded again, and what it reported. VideoFrame A decoded picture with its time: a YuvVideoFrame as decoders hand it out (the codec's own planes), or a VideoFrame<TPixel> of RGB pixels from VideoReader.ReadFrames. Disposing the frame returns its pixel memory to the memory source it came from. VideoFrame<TPixel> A decoded picture converted to TPixel pixels, as VideoReader.ReadFrames returns it. VideoQuality Measures how close decoded video is to a reference, frame by frame or over a whole clip: PSNR and SSIM per plane, and MD5 hashes of frames and packets in the layout FFmpeg's framemd5 uses (planes one after another, rows without padding, little-endian 16-bit samples above 8 bits). VideoReader Reads the frames of a video file in a few lines: opens the container, picks the video track, decodes it and hands out frames, as the codec's planes (ReadFrames()) or as RGB rasters (ReadFrames<TPixel>()). Frame memory comes from the context's pixel memory source, pooled by default, so disposing each frame keeps memory steady over long files. VideoReaderOptions How a VideoReader reads. VideoTrackInfo A video track: a TrackInfo with the picture size, frame rate and color. VideoWriter Writes a video file from rasters in a few lines: encodes each frame and muxes it, picking the container from the file extension. The picture size comes from the first frame. Other tracks, such as audio copied from a source file, can be written alongside with WritePacket(EncodedPacket). VideoWriterOptions What a VideoWriter writes. YuvVideoFrame A decoded picture in the codec's own planar YUV layout, as decoders return it: for Motion JPEG the JPEG's Y, Cb and Cr planes at their own subsampling, with no color conversion. Structs Hdr10PlusPercentile One point of HDR10+'s distribution of each pixel's brightest component: Percentage percent of the pixels are at or below Value cd/m². Keyframe A value at a time on a stream's time line, one point of an animation such as a GainEnvelope. Easing says how the value moves on to the next keyframe. MediaProgress How far a job such as Remux(string, string, Func<TrackInfo, bool>?, MediaContext?, IProgress<MediaProgress>?, CancellationToken) has come. A job reports once its output is open, then at most every 250 ms, then once more with IsFinal set. MediaTime A point in time or a duration in a media stream: a whole number of ticks of a Rational time base. Exact for every container: AVI counts frames at the frame rate's reciprocal (for example 1001/30000 s), Matroska counts its timestamp scale in nanoseconds. TimeSpan rounds to 100 ns and drifts over long files; this type does not. MovTextStyle A style run of a mov_text subtitle (a 3GPP StyleRecord): which characters it covers and how they look. Rational An exact fraction, such as a frame rate (30000/1001) or a time base (1/1000000000). Always stored in lowest terms with a positive denominator. Enums DecodeErrorMode What a decoder or VideoReader does with a frame it cannot decode. Easing How an animated value moves from a Keyframe to the next one. FieldOrder How a video track's frames are interlaced. MovTextFace How the characters of a MovTextStyle are drawn. SeekMode How exact Seek(MediaTime, SeekMode) is. TrackKind What a track holds. TrimMode How Trim(string, string, MediaTime, MediaTime?, TrimMode, Func<TrackInfo, bool>?, MediaContext?, IProgress<MediaProgress>?, CancellationToken) starts a cut that does not fall on a keyframe.

api/Egami.YuvRaster.html.summary: Class YuvRaster Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll A picture held as separate luma (Y) and chroma (U, V) planes, plus an optional alpha plane, the way video codecs, AVIF, lossy WebP and JPEG store it. This base class is used when the sample type is not known at compile time; YuvRaster<TSample> gives the planes. Operations other than Crop and Resize run on a Raster after conversion. It is not thread-safe for writing, like a raster. api/Egami.html.title: Namespace Egami | Egami
api/Egami.html.summary: Namespace Egami Classes CorruptDataException Thrown when data matches a format but breaks its rules, such as a bad checksum, a truncated stream or an invalid table. DiagnosticReporter One call's link to Diagnostics, with the same level filter and per-id cap Egami's own readers and writers use. Get one from StartDiagnostics() at the start of a call (format plug-ins use Diagnostics) and dispose it when the call ends. When the context has no handler it is a shared instance that does nothing, so reporting costs one check. EgamiContext Every setting that is not specific to one call: where memory comes from, how many threads an operation may use, and the safety limits. Contexts are immutable and safe to share. Change one with a with expression. EgamiException The base class of every exception Egami throws for problems with image data or limits. FrameList<TPixel> The frames of a raster, all the same size and pixel type. There is always at least one. Frames added from anywhere are copied, so a frame belongs to one raster only. Frame<TPixel> One frame of a raster: a pixel plane the size of the raster plus per-frame metadata. InkCoverage How much ink an InkRaster prints, from MeasureCoverage(float). InkPlate One plane of an InkRaster: an ink's plate, or the alpha plane. Rows are read and written in place; AsRaster<TPixel>() shows the plane as a gray raster without copying. InkRaster A printed page as plates: one plane per ink of an InkSet (a disabled spot has none) plus one alpha plane, each 8 or 16 bits. A plane holds the ink as it prints over paper, 0 for none to the depth's maximum for full ink: drawing translucently leaves less ink, so the planes are premultiplied by the alpha plane, and a plate is ready to print as it is. A new raster is blank: no ink, alpha 0. InkTiffOptions How an InkRaster is saved as a separated TIFF. LimitExceededException Thrown when a SafetyLimits limit is exceeded. MipChain A chain of ever-halved copies of an image, for making many smaller sizes fast: each resize starts from the smallest level that is still at least twice the target, so a gallery of thumbnail sizes reads each source pixel about once instead of once per size. Level 0 is the source itself; each next level halves the size, rounding up, by averaging 2 × 2 blocks of premultiplied pixels. PixelMemoryLeakEventArgs Describes a pixel memory block that was collected without being disposed. PixelMemoryUsage What a PooledPixelMemorySource has handed out and not yet had back, and opt-in tracking of blocks that were never disposed. Get it from Usage; most callers want PooledPixelMemorySource.Shared.Usage. PixelPlane<TPixel> A width × height grid of pixels, stored row by row. A row is always one contiguous span, but the plane as a whole may be split into several blocks of whole rows. Planes belong to the raster or operation that hands them out, which returns their memory; user code reads and writes them but never frees them. PooledPixelMemorySource The default IPixelMemorySource. Small blocks are arrays rented from a shared pool; larger blocks are unmanaged memory aligned to 64 bytes, which stays off the large object heap and suits SIMD. Planes larger than MaxBlockBytes are split into several blocks of whole rows. ProofOptions How Proof<TPixel>(ProofOptions?) shows the plates on screen. Raster Measuring images: comparison, statistics, histograms, colors and a pixel signature. Nothing here changes a raster. RasterDecoder One open image, decoded a band of rows or a frame at a time. Opening reads the header and the metadata that comes before the image data; ReadRows<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel>) and ReadFrame<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel>) then hand out the image in any pixel type, with Region and MinimumSize applied as in Load(Stream, EgamiContext?, ReaderOptions?). RasterEncoder Creates a RasterEncoder<TPixel>, which writes an image a band of rows or a frame at a time. RasterEncoder<TPixel> An image being written a band of rows or a frame at a time, so a huge image never has to exist whole. The bytes are the ones Save(Stream, FormatInfo, WriterOptions?) writes for the same pixels and options, except where a format must write differently without seeking: top-down BMP and TGA rows, and run-length TGA, which is always top-down. Options that need every pixel before the first byte (automatic palettes, PNG's Reduce, automatic alpha) throw at Create instead of quietly writing something else. RasterList The images of a file that holds several, each its own raster with its own size, pixel type and metadata: a TIFF's pages, an icon's entries. The list owns them: disposing it disposes every raster. Raster<TPixel> An image whose pixels are of type TPixel. Pixel access is by row span. SafetyLimits Limits that protect against hostile or broken files. Readers check sizes from the header before allocating any pixel memory. The defaults let normal photos and screenshots through. Change them with a with expression. SpritePackOptions How Pack(IReadOnlyList<Raster>, SpritePackOptions?) lays sprites out. SpriteSheet A sprite sheet: many images packed into one, with the rectangle of each. Packing uses the MaxRects algorithm with the best short side fit (Jylänki, "A Thousand Ways to Pack the Bin", 2010), the images taken by height, tallest first, and then by input order, so the same inputs always give the same sheet. Sprites are never rotated. UnsupportedFormatException Thrown when no registered format matches the data, or the matching format cannot read or write. YuvConvertOptions The chroma filters for conversions between a YuvRaster and a Raster. YuvPlane<TSample> One plane of a YuvRaster<TSample>: a width × height grid of raw samples, stored row by row. A row is always one contiguous span. Samples are stored low-bit aligned: a 10-bit sample is 0 to 1023 in a ushort. YuvRaster A picture held as separate luma (Y) and chroma (U, V) planes, plus an optional alpha plane, the way video codecs, AVIF, lossy WebP and JPEG store it. This base class is used when the sample type is not known at compile time; YuvRaster<TSample> gives the planes. Convert to and from a Raster with ToRaster(YuvConvertOptions?), CopyTo<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel>, YuvConvertOptions?, CancellationToken) and FromRaster(Raster, ChromaFormat, YuvColor, bool, YuvConvertOptions?). YuvRasterInfo What Probe(Stream, EgamiContext?, ReaderOptions?) reads from a header: the image as Probe(Stream, EgamiContext?, ReaderOptions?) describes it, and the planes Load(Stream, EgamiContext?, ReaderOptions?) would give, if any. YuvRaster<TSample> A picture held as separate Y, U, V and optional alpha planes of TSample samples. See YuvRaster. Structs EgamiDiagnostic One event reported to Diagnostics, and the type of each entry in Warnings. Ids are listed in the diagnostics article and never renamed or reused. Point A position in pixels. X grows to the right and Y downward; the top-left pixel is (0, 0). Rect A rectangle of pixels: the top-left corner and a size. Size A width and height in pixels. Interfaces IPixelMemorySource Supplies the memory behind every PixelPlane<TPixel>. Implement it to control where pixel memory comes from. Implementations must be thread-safe. Enums Alignment Where a smaller image sits across the layout's direction: at the start (left or top), the center or the end. Axis The direction images are laid out in by Append(IReadOnlyList<Raster>, Axis, int, Rgba8, Alignment). ChromaDownsampling How chroma is reduced to the chroma resolution when a raster converts to a subsampled YuvRaster. ChromaUpsampling How chroma is brought up to luma resolution when a YuvRaster converts to RGB. ClearMode Says whether new pixel memory is cleared. DecodeStatus Where a RasterDecoder stands, as Status reports it. DiagnosticLevel How much an EgamiDiagnostic matters. Maps one to one onto the Debug, Information and Warning log levels. InkDepth How many bits each plane of an InkRaster stores per pixel. Delegates RowAction<TPixel> Processes one row of pixels.

articles/cli/assistants.html.title: egami for AI assistants | Egami
articles/cli/assistants.html.summary: egami for AI assistants egami mcp serves egami's commands to an AI assistant, such as Claude, GitHub Copilot or Cursor, over the Model Context Protocol. The assistant can then look at, convert, resize and edit images on your computer when you ask it to, with the same commands, options and results as the shell. It needs nothing besides the egami tool: no network, no service and no key. dotnet tool install --global Egami.Cli egami mcp --allow ~/Pictures You don't run egami mcp yourself: the assistant starts it and talks to it on standard input and output. The sections below show where each assistant takes the command. The tools Every command is a tool with the command's name, words joined by _: info, convert, resize, thumbnail, crop, rotate, flip, auto_orient, run, compare, stats, frames_split, frames_join, metadata_show, metadata_strip, metadata_copy, color, text, overlay, montage and formats. Their arguments are the command's arguments and options in snake case (--bit-depth is bit_depth), with the same descriptions as egami <command> --help, so the command reference covers them too. --jobs and --fail-fast are left out: a call works on one file per processor and keeps going past a file that fails, reporting each one. run takes its steps as a workflow object, the same JSON as a workflow file, and list_steps lists the steps and their options. Tools that write take preview: when it is true, the result also holds the first file written as a PNG picture, at most 1024 pixels on its long side, so the assistant can look at what it made. Every result is a JSON object with exitCode (as in the shell), written (the files written), output (the command's JSON, for commands with --json, or its text) and messages (warnings and errors). A usage mistake, a failed file or a safety limit marks the call as failed, so the assistant sees it and can try again; compare finding a difference is a result, not a failure. The folders egami may use A tool reads and writes only inside the folders egami may use, and refuses any other path, including one reached through a symbolic link or ..: the folders given with --allow, once per folder, and the folders the assistant has open (for example the project open in VS Code), when the assistant tells the server about them; when there are neither, the folder egami was started in. egami refuses to start in the root of a disk without --allow, because some assistants start servers there. Outputs never replace an input unless the call sets in_place. Inputs and outputs must be files: standard input and output carry the protocol, so - is refused. One call takes at most 1,000 files; --max-inputs changes that. The safety limits of --limit and EGAMI_LIMITS apply to every call, as in the shell. Claude Desktop Add egami to claude_desktop_config.json (Settings, Developer, Edit Config) and restart Claude: { "mcpServers": { "egami": { "command": "egami", "args": ["mcp", "--allow", "/Users/me/Pictures"] } } } On Windows, write the folder as C:\\Users\\me\\Pictures. Claude Desktop starts servers outside your folders, so give each folder egami may use with --allow. Claude Code claude mcp add egami -- egami mcp Claude Code starts egami in the project's folder, which egami then uses. Add --allow <folder> for others. VS Code Add egami to .vscode/mcp.json in your project. dnx runs the tool straight from NuGet, so it needs no install: { "servers": { "egami": { "type": "stdio", "command": "dnx", "args": ["Egami.Cli", "--yes", "--", "mcp"] } } } VS Code tells egami about the folders of the workspace. Other assistants take the same command and arguments in their own settings. Logging -v and -vv write what the server does (the folders it uses, each call) to standard error, which most assistants show in their server log. Standard output carries only the protocol.

articles/cli/commands.html.title: Command reference | Egami
articles/cli/commands.html.summary: Command reference Every egami command with its arguments and options, as egami <command> --help prints them. The options of all commands (-v, -vv, -q, --limit) are listed once, at the top. The egami command explains the conventions they share. Description: Convert, inspect, resize and edit images with Egami, a fully managed imaging library. Usage: egami [command] [options] Options: -v, --verbose Write information to standard error. -vv, --debug Write debugging detail to standard error. -q, --quiet Write only errors to standard error. --limit <name=value,...> Safety limits, such as pixels=100M,memory=2GB,frames=500 (names: pixels, width, height, frames, memory, metadata). EGAMI_LIMITS sets them too. --preview-formats Also read and write the formats in preview (none in this release); they may change or go in any minor release. -?, -h, --help Show help and usage information --version Show version information Commands: info <inputs> Show what images are: format, size, frames, pixel layout, orientation; with --all, their metadata. Pixels are not decoded. convert <inputs> Convert images to another format, or write them again with other settings. resize <inputs> Resize images: to a width, a height, a box, a percentage, filling or padding a box. thumbnail <inputs> Make thumbnails for the web: turned upright, shrunk (never enlarged) to fit --size (256 by default), converted to sRGB, metadata left out. crop <inputs> Crop images to a rectangle. rotate <inputs> Rotate images clockwise. A JPEG turned by a multiple of 90 degrees into a JPEG is rotated losslessly. flip <inputs> Mirror images left to right (horizontal), top to bottom (vertical) or both. A JPEG flipped into a JPEG is flipped losslessly. auto-orient, autoorient <inputs> Turn images upright from their EXIF orientation and reset it. A JPEG into a JPEG is turned losslessly. run <inputs-and-steps> Run steps over images, separated by +: 'egami run in.jpg auto-orient + resize 1200x + sharpen 0.6 + save out.webp --quality 82'. Every Egami operation is a step ('egami run --list'); save writes, and may come more than once. compare <image> <other> Compare two images: print a metric and exit with 1 when they differ more than --threshold. stats <inputs> Measure images: per-channel minimum, maximum, mean, deviation, skewness, kurtosis and entropy, as ImageMagick's identify -verbose. ocr <inputs> Read the text of images with an OCR program (Tesseract or any that writes hOCR or ALTO), as plain text, hOCR or ALTO. frames Split an animation (GIF, APNG, WebP) into still images, or join stills into one. metadata Show, strip or copy metadata: color profile, EXIF, XMP, IPTC, text and resolution. color <inputs> Convert images to another color profile (ICC, 2.1.2), tone mapping HDR to SDR where needed (2.9.1). text <inputs> Draw a caption or watermark on images, with any font and script, wrapped to fit (2.8.2 layout). overlay <inputs> Lay an image (a logo, a watermark, an SVG) on images, placed by anchor, with opacity and a blend mode. montage <inputs> Lay images out on a contact sheet: a grid of tiles, optionally labeled with their file names. formats <format> List the formats egami reads and writes, or one format's writer settings for --set. mcp Serve egami's commands as tools to an AI assistant over the Model Context Protocol, on standard input and output. Tools read and write only inside the folders the assistant opened and those given with --allow, and never replace an input unless asked. info Description: Show what images are: format, size, frames, pixel layout, orientation; with --all, their metadata. Pixels are not decoded. Usage: egami info <inputs>... [options] Arguments: <inputs> Image files, globs (*, ?, **) expanded the same way in every shell, folders with --recursive, or - for standard input. Options: -r, --recursive Take every image in folders given as inputs, at any depth. -j, --jobs <count> How many files to work on at once; 0 (the default) for one per processor. --fail-fast Stop at the first file that fails. -a, --all Also read the metadata: color profile, EXIF, XMP, IPTC, text, resolution. --json Write JSON (schema 1, see the command reference) instead of text. --preview-formats Also read and write the formats in preview (none in this release); they may change or go in any minor release. convert Description: Convert images to another format, or write them again with other settings. Usage: egami convert <inputs>... [options] Arguments: <inputs> Image files, globs (*, ?, **) expanded the same way in every shell, folders with --recursive, or - for standard input. Options: -o, --output <path> Where to write: a file, a folder, a template with {name}, {ext}, {dir}, {index} and {format}, or - for standard output. -f, --format <format> The output format by name or extension, when -o's extension does not say (and always for -o -). --quality <0-100> Lossy quality from 0 to 100 (JPEG, WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL, TIFF's JPEG). --lossless Lossless encoding (WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL). --effort <level> Encoder effort: higher is smaller and slower (WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL). --bit-depth <bits> Bits per channel to write (PNG, AVIF). --strip Leave out metadata (EXIF, XMP, IPTC, text, resolution) but keep the color profile, so colors stay right. --set <fmt.key=value> Any writer setting as fmt.key=value, such as png.compression-level=9; 'egami formats png' lists the keys. --auto-orient Turn the image upright from its EXIF orientation first. --to <profile> Convert colors to this profile while reading: srgb, display-p3, adobe-rgb, rec2020, ... or an ICC file. -r, --recursive Take every image in folders given as inputs, at any depth. -j, --jobs <count> How many files to work on at once; 0 (the default) for one per processor. --in-place Allow outputs to replace their inputs. --fail-fast Stop at the first file that fails. --preview-formats Also read and write the formats in preview (none in this release); they may change or go in any minor release. resize Description: Resize images: to a width, a height, a box, a percentage, filling or padding a box. Usage: egami resize <inputs>... [options] Arguments: <inputs> Image files, globs (*, ?, **) expanded the same way in every shell, folders with --recursive, or - for standard input. [default: 1] --blend <mode> The blend mode: normal (the default), multiply, screen, overlay, darken, lighten, ... -s, --size <size> Resize the overlay first, in the size syntax (W, xH, WxH, P%). --preview-formats Also read and write the formats in preview (none in this release); they may change or go in any minor release. montage Description: Lay images out on a contact sheet: a grid of tiles, optionally labeled with their file names. Usage: egami montage <inputs>... [options] Arguments: <inputs> The images, in order: files or globs (sorted by name). Options: -o, --output <path> (REQUIRED) The contact sheet to write. -f, --format <format> The output format, when the extension does not say. -c, --columns <count> Images per row; enough for a square sheet by default. --tile <WxH> Each image's box; images are shrunk to fit it, never enlarged. [default: 200x200] --spacing <pixels> The gap between tiles, in pixels. [default: 8] --background <color> The sheet's color (white by default). --labels Write each file's name under its image. --font <font> The label font: a file, an installed family, or sans-serif, serif or monospace. --label-size <pixels> The label size in pixels. [default: 13] --set <fmt.key=value> Writer settings as fmt.key=value. --quality <0-100> Lossy quality from 0 to 100. --preview-formats Also read and write the formats in preview (none in this release); they may change or go in any minor release. formats Description: List the formats egami reads and writes, or one format's writer settings for --set. Usage: egami formats [<format>] [options] Arguments: <format> A format name or extension, to list its writer settings. Options: --json Write JSON instead of text. --preview-formats Also read and write the formats in preview (none in this release); they may change or go in any minor release. mcp Description: Serve egami's commands as tools to an AI assistant over the Model Context Protocol, on standard input and output. Tools read and write only inside the folders the assistant opened and those given with --allow, and never replace an input unless asked. Usage: egami mcp [options] Options: --allow <folder> A folder the tools may read and write, besides the folders the assistant opened; give it once per folder. With neither, the working folder. --max-inputs <count> The most files one tool call may take; 1000 by default. [default: 1000] --preview-formats Also read and write the formats in preview (none in this release); they may change or go in any minor release.

articles/cli/index.html.title: The egami command | Egami
articles/cli/index.html.summary: The egami command egami converts, inspects, resizes and edits images from a shell or a build script, with no C# to write. It is the Egami.Cli package, a .NET tool built on Egami's public API, and reads every format Egami and its packages read: SVG, WMF, EMF and Egami.Formats.Extended's PCX, SGI, Sun raster, XBM, XPM, WBMP and Farbfeld included. It has three layers: Single commands for everyday jobs: info, convert, resize, thumbnail, crop, rotate, flip, auto-orient, compare, stats, frames, metadata, color, text, overlay, montage and formats. run, which chains any number of steps over each image. Every Egami operation is a step, and the same steps can be saved as a JSON workflow file. Batches: every command takes many files, globs and folders, and works on several at once. The command reference lists every option, and steps for run every step. egami mcp serves the same commands to an AI assistant: see egami for AI assistants. egami info photo.jpg egami convert in.png -o out.webp --quality 80 egami resize in.jpg -o out.jpg --size 800x600 egami thumbnail "photos/*.jpg" -o thumbs/{name}.webp --size 256 egami run in.jpg auto-orient + resize 1200x + sharpen 0.6 + save out.webp --quality 82 cat in.png | egami convert - -o - --format qoi > out.qoi Installing Egami.Cli is a .NET tool, so it needs the .NET 10 runtime: dotnet tool install --global Egami.Cli dnx Egami.Cli info photo.jpg runs it once without installing. The tool is built free of reflection, with the trimming and Native AOT analyzers on, so it also publishes as a standalone native program (see Native binaries). Inputs Inputs are files, globs or - for standard input. egami expands globs itself, so they work the same in bash, zsh, cmd and PowerShell: * and ? match within a name, [abc] a set, and ** any depth of folders. Quote them so the shell leaves them alone. A folder needs --recursive, and then means every image below it. Files come in sorted order, so {index} and the order of a batch never depend on the file system. Outputs -o names where to write: -o Writes out.png That file. The format comes from the extension, or --format. out/ or an existing folder out/<name>.<ext>, keeping each input's name. web/{dir}/{name}.webp A template: {name} (the input's name without extension), {ext} (its extension), {dir} (its folder below the glob's start), {index} (its position from 0, padded with {index:000}), {format} (the output format's extension). {{ and }} write braces. - Standard output. The format is --format, or the input's. With several inputs, -o must be a folder or a template that names each input. An output never replaces its input unless --in-place is given; --in-place without -o writes each file over itself. Files are written to a temporary name first and replace the target only when complete. Formats and writer settings The output format comes from the extension or --format. The common settings have flags: --quality, --lossless, --effort, --bit-depth and --strip, which leaves out EXIF, XMP, IPTC, text and resolution but keeps the color profile, so colors stay right (ImageMagick's -strip drops the profile too). A flag the format does not have is skipped with a warning. Every other writer setting is --set fmt.key=value, where the keys are the format's WriterOptions properties in kebab case: egami formats png # lists png.compression-level, png.filter, png.palette.max-colors, ... egami convert in.tif -o out.png --set png.compression-level=9 --set png.filter=paeth egami formats lists what egami reads and writes. The keys come straight from the library, so the tool never lags it. HEIC is not part of the tool, since HEVC is covered by patents. Formats Egami.Formats.Extended has in preview are read and written only with --preview-formats, which every command takes; they may change or go in any minor release, and there are none in this release. Sizes resize, thumbnail and the resize step take the size syntax, the common subset of ImageMagick's geometry: Size Means 800 800 wide, height in proportion x600 600 high, width in proportion 800x600 Fit inside 800 × 600, aspect ratio kept 50%, 50%x25% A percentage of the size 800x600! Exactly 800 × 600, aspect ratio ignored 800x600^ At least 800 × 600, aspect ratio kept (fills the box, nothing cropped) 800x600> Only shrink: images already smaller are left alone 800x600< Only enlarge --fit says how a box is filled: contain (inside it, the default), cover (filled and cropped, with --gravity choosing what stays), fill (stretched) or pad (inside, then padded with --background). --filter picks the resampling kernel (bicubic, Catmull-Rom, by default, as in the library) and --linear blends in linear light. Defaults Every command keeps the library's defaults, except thumbnail, which is the web-image shortcut: it turns the image upright from its EXIF orientation, shrinks it (never enlarges) to fit --size (256 by default), converts it to sRGB and leaves out metadata. The other commands do those only when asked: --auto-orient, --to srgb and --strip. rotate, flip and auto-orient turn a JPEG written as JPEG without decoding it, so no quality is lost, when the angle allows; --reencode decodes instead. flip has no default direction: give horizontal, vertical or both, since ImageMagick's -flip and a photo app's flip mirror opposite ways. metadata strip without --keep rewrites a JPEG without decoding it too; any other metadata edit that would write a lossy format again (JPEG, lossy WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL) asks for --reencode. Chaining steps with run egami run in.jpg auto-orient + resize 1200x + sharpen 0.6 + save out.webp --quality 82 egami run in.jpg save full.png + resize 256x256 + save thumb.webp egami run "photos/**/*.jpg" grayscale + contrast 1.2 -o gray/{dir}/{name}.jpg --jobs 8 Steps are separated by a bare +, which no shell treats specially. Each step's options follow its name: positional values fill the parameters in order, --name value sets one by name. save writes the image as it is at that point, and may come more than once; a plan without a save writes to -o. Writer flags outside a save apply to every save. --dry-run prints the steps and the files each input would write. Every single command is turned into the same kind of plan, so egami resize --size 800x and egami run resize 800x give the same bytes. A plan of steps that can stream (crop, resize and the per-pixel color steps) runs through Raster.Transcode, a band of rows at a time; anything else loads the image, runs the steps and saves. When a plan starts with a resize, the image is decoded at no less than one and a half times the result (ReaderOptions.MinimumSize), so a large JPEG is decoded at a half, a quarter or an eighth of its size and the resize filter still has real work to do. Either way the result is what the same RasterOps chain with the same reader options gives in C#. Workflow files A workflow file holds the steps of run as JSON, one object per step with the step's options as properties. It is checked against the published schema: { "egami": 1, "steps": [ { "op": "auto-orient" }, { "op": "resize", "size": "1200x", "filter": "lanczos3" }, { "op": "sharpen", "sigma": 0.6 }, { "op": "save", "format": "webp", "quality": 82, "set": { "webp.effort": 5 } } ] } egami run in.jpg resize 1200x + sharpen 0.6 --save-workflow web.json --dry-run # write the file from a command line egami run "photos/*.jpg" --workflow web.json -o web/{name}.webp A save in a workflow may give a path; one without writes to -o. Branching and conditions stay out: a script is the right tool for logic. Batches Every command takes many inputs. --jobs sets how many files run at once (one per processor by default); each image is then worked on by one core, and since Egami gives the same bytes at any core count, --jobs never changes an output. A file that fails is reported and the rest carry on; --fail-fast stops at the first. A summary goes to standard error when anything failed. Exit codes, messages and limits Code Means 0 Everything worked 1 A file failed (missing, corrupt, unwritable), or compare found a difference above --threshold 2 The command line is wrong: an unknown command, option or value 3 An input exceeded a safety limit Messages and Egami's own diagnostics go to standard error: warnings by default, -v adds information, -vv debugging detail, and -q keeps only errors. Results (info, stats, compare) go to standard output, so they can be piped. The library's safety limits apply to every input. --limit raises or lowers them, and the EGAMI_LIMITS environment variable sets them for a service: egami convert big.tif -o big.png --limit pixels=400M,memory=4GB EGAMI_LIMITS=pixels=20M,frames=100 egami thumbnail uploads/* -o thumbs/ Names: pixels (a count such as 50M, or WxH), width, height, frames, memory and metadata (bytes, such as 512MB). JSON output info --json, stats --json, compare --json, metadata show --json and formats --json write JSON for scripts. info's has a version, "schema": 1, which changes only when a field changes meaning or goes away; new fields may be added: { "schema": 1, "files": [ { "path": "photo.jpg", "format": "JPEG", "mimeType": "image/jpeg", "width": 4032, "height": 3024, "frames": 1, "images": 1, "loopCount": null, "orientation": "rotate90", "pixels": { "channels": "rgb", "channelCount": 3, "bitsPerChannel": 8, "channelType": "unorm8", "alpha": "none" }, "hasMetadata": true, "estimatedBytes": 36578304, "streams": true } ] } With --all, each file also has metadata: the blocks it holds (icc, exif, xmp, iptc, text, gain-map), the color profile's name and size, resolution, gamma, EXIF's camera, date, orientation and location, the XMP size, IPTC datasets and text entries. info never decodes pixels; --all reads the metadata, which may decode a pixel. Text in images ocr reads the text of images through an OCR program you install, such as Tesseract, run once per image as CommandOcrEngine runs it (OCR). It writes plain text to standard output by default, or text, hOCR or ALTO files by -o's extension (.txt, .hocr, .xml) or --as. egami mcp does not offer it, since it runs the program the call names. egami ocr scan.png --engine-command "tesseract {image} {output} -l {langs} --dpi {dpi} hocr" --lang eng egami ocr "scans/*.png" --engine-command "tesseract {image} {output} -l {langs} hocr" --lang eng+nor -o "text/{name}.hocr" Other tools A command egami does not know runs the program egami-<name> from the PATH with the rest of the arguments, as git does, so egami video info clip.webm starts egami-video once Egami.Video's tool is installed. Egap (documents) has its own egap tool with the same conventions. Native binaries Egami.Cli publishes as a single native program that needs no .NET runtime. It answers egami info in about 14 ms, where the dotnet tool takes about 140 ms, most of it starting the runtime: dotnet publish src/Egami.Cli -c Release -r linux-x64 -p:EgamiNativeAot=true The cli-native workflow builds and checks these for win-x64, linux-x64 and osx-arm64 on every change to the tool, and keeps them as the run's artifacts. Each release puts them on the releases page.

articles/cli/steps.html.title: Steps for run | Egami
articles/cli/steps.html.summary: Steps for run The steps egami run chains and workflow files list. Every public RasterOps method whose arguments a command line can spell is a step, named in kebab case (ContrastStretch is contrast-stretch); its options are the method's parameters. Positional values fill the parameters in order; --name value sets one by name. egami run --list <step> prints one. Step What it does adaptive-threshold Thresholds each pixel against the mean of the window around it (Bradley and Roth, 2007): a pixel is dark when its luminance is more than limit below its window's mean, so uneven lighting on a scanned page does not swallow text. add-noise Adds noise to red, green and blue (or a CMYK raster's inks), as ImageMagick's +noise with -attenuate does: film grain, sensor noise, or salt and pepper for testing filters. alpha-to-gray Makes the image a gray picture of its alpha: red, green and blue become the alpha value and alpha becomes opaque, as ImageMagick's -alpha extract does. arithmetic Applies op with value to every value of channels, on values scaled 0 to 1 and clamped back to 0..1, as ImageMagick's -evaluate defines each operator. auto-gamma Applies the Gamma that moves the image's mean to 0.5, as ImageMagick's -auto-gamma; an image whose mean is 0 or 1 is left alone. auto-level Stretches the darkest value to 0 and the lightest to 1, as ImageMagick's -auto-level. auto-orient Turns the image the way its EXIF orientation says, so it looks as the camera meant, and sets the orientation to Normal. auto-threshold Thresholds at the level method finds in the histogram, as ImageMagick's -auto-threshold; see FindThreshold. auto-white-balance Removes a color cast it measures, by method. bilateral-blur Smooths while keeping edges (Tomasi and Manduchi's bilateral filter): each neighbour counts by its distance, through a Gaussian of spatialSigma, and by how much its color differs, through a Gaussian of rangeSigma, so noise flattens and edges stay. blend-color Blends one color over every pixel by mode: Multiply tints, Screen washes out, Color colorizes. bloom Makes bright areas glow, as a camera's bloom: the parts of each channel above threshold, stretched to 0..1 and scaled by intensity, blurred in linear light with Fast and screened onto the image in linear light. blur Blurs with a Gaussian of standard deviation sigma pixels, computed by method. box-blur Replaces each pixel with the mean of the (2r + 1) square around it. brightness Multiplies red, green and blue by amount: 1 changes nothing, 0 gives black. canny-edges Finds thin edges with Canny's detector, as ImageMagick's -canny 0x{sigma}+{low × 100}%+{high × 100}% does: the luma is smoothed by a Gaussian, Canny's first differences give the gradient, pixels that are not the strongest across their edge are dropped, and hysteresis keeps pixels whose magnitude reaches high times the largest, plus those 8-connected to them that reach low times it. change-speed Plays the animation factor times as fast: every delay is divided by it, rounded to whole milliseconds. chroma-key Makes pixels whose chroma lies within similarity of color's transparent, keeping their color: a chroma key for green and blue screens. clahe Contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (Zuiderveld, 1994) on L*, as ImageMagick's -clahe: each of tilesX × tilesY tiles gets its own clipped, equalized curve, blended smoothly between tile centers, so local detail comes up without the noise of plain equalization. colorize Blends red, green and blue toward color, as ImageMagick's -colorize. contrast Scales red, green and blue around mid-gray: 1 changes nothing, 0 gives flat gray. contrast-stretch Clips the darkest black and lightest white fractions of the pixels, then stretches the rest to 0..1, as ImageMagick's -contrast-stretch. convert-color Converts the pixels from the encoding the raster is in (GetColorProfile, or the target of an earlier ConvertColor in the chain) to target, in place, and records the new encoding in the metadata: no profile for sRGB, the target's ICC profile otherwise. cover Scales the image to cover width × height with its aspect ratio kept, keeping the part at anchor. crop Keeps one rectangle of the image. deskew Straightens a scanned or photographed page: detects the tilt of its text lines (see DetectSkew) and turns the image back by it. despeckle Removes specks while keeping edges, by Crimmins' complementary hulling exactly as ImageMagick's -despeckle runs it: each color channel is nudged, a level at a time, toward neighbours that differ by two levels or more, in 16 passes along four directions. despill Removes the colored cast a green or blue screen leaves on edges, hair and see-through pixels: the screen's channel is held down to a limit taken from the other two channels. dilate The maximum over the (2rx + 1) × (2ry + 1) rectangle around each pixel, as Skia's dilate filter with those radii. displace Moves each pixel by a displacement map, as Skia's DisplacementMap and ImageMagick's -displace do: pixel (x, y) shows the source at (x + scaleX × (mx − 0.5), y + scaleY × (my − 0.5)), with mx and my the map's chosen channels from 0 to 1, so mid-gray moves nothing. draw-animation Draws an animation (or a still) onto this one at position. draw-arithmetic Draws image with the arithmetic composite (SVG's feComposite arithmetic operator, Skia's arithmetic blender): each channel of the premultiplied result is k1·S·D + k2·S + k3·D + k4, with S the image and D this raster, in 0..1. draw-image Draws the part of image inside sourceArea onto this raster with that part's top-left corner at position, combining pixels by mode as DrawImage does for the whole image. drop-shadow Adds a drop shadow, as Skia's DropShadow image filter: the image's alpha, moved by (dx, dy), blurred by a Gaussian of sigma and filled with color, with the image drawn over it source-over. drop-zero-delay Removes frames with no delay, which no viewer shows, as ImageMagick's -layers RemoveZero; when every frame has none, nothing is removed. duotone Maps luminance onto the line from shadows to highlights. edges Replaces each pixel with the strength of the edge through it: the gradient magnitude of op's kernels, scaled so a full black-to-white step gives 1, clamped to 0 to 1. emboss Embosses: blurs with a Gaussian of sigma, takes the slope toward the light at angle with a 3 × 3 Sobel stencil, scales it by depth and adds mid gray, so flat areas become 0.5 and slopes facing the light are lighter. entropy-crop Crops to the busiest part of the image: the bounding box of the 16 × 16 tiles whose luminance entropy (the Shannon entropy of the tile's 256-level histogram, over 8 bits) reaches threshold. equalize Spreads the values evenly by histogram equalization: of L* by default, keeping a* and b* so colors hold, or of each channel as ImageMagick's -equalize. erode The minimum over the (2rx + 1) × (2ry + 1) rectangle around each pixel, as Skia's erode filter with those radii. fill-color Sets every pixel in rect, or the whole image, to one color. fit Scales the image to fit inside width × height with its aspect ratio kept, so one side matches the box and the other is no larger. flatten Composites the image over background and makes it opaque, as ImageMagick's -alpha remove does. flip Mirrors the image: horizontal (left to right), vertical (top to bottom) or both. flip-horizontal Mirrors the image left to right. flip-vertical Mirrors the image top to bottom. flood-fill Fills the region connected to seed whose colors lie within tolerance of the seed's own with fill, as ImageMagick's -fuzz with -floodfill does. gamma Raises red, green and blue to 1/gamma, as ImageMagick's -gamma: 2.2 brightens. glow Adds a glow around the image's alpha shape, as an editor's outer glow layer style: the alpha, blurred with Fast, spread, and filled with color, drawn behind the image. grayscale Converts toward gray. high-contrast Skia's high-contrast accessibility filter. hue-rotate Rotates hue around the luma axis. inner-shadow Adds a shadow inside the image's alpha shape, as an editor's inner shadow layer style: everything outside the shape, moved by (dx, dy) rounded to whole pixels, blurred with Fast and filled with color, drawn on the image inside the shape only. invert Replaces red, green and blue with 1 − value, blended by amount. kuwahara Smooths while keeping edges, with the Kuwahara filter as ImageMagick's -kuwahara defines it: of the four (r + 1) squares that have the pixel as a corner, the one whose luma varies least gives the pixel its value, sampled at that square's middle. lens-blur Blurs as an out-of-focus lens does: each point spreads into the aperture's shape, a disc or a polygon of 5 to 12 blades, so small lights become discs, unlike a Gaussian's soft spots. level Stretches black..white to outputBlack..outputWhite with a midtone gamma, as ImageMagick's -level and +level. local-contrast Brings out local detail, as ImageMagick's -local-contrast: L* is pushed away from a wide blur of itself by strength, so large-scale light changes less than detail. luminance-to-alpha Sets alpha to the luminance of the stored values, 0.212656 R + 0.715158 G + 0.072186 B (the Rec. make-transparent Makes pixels within tolerance of color transparent, keeping their color, by ImageMagick's -fuzz distance, so with no softness the result equals ImageMagick's -fuzz with -transparent. median Replaces each channel with its median over the (2r + 1) square around the pixel, as ImageMagick's -statistic Median does: removes salt-and-pepper noise while keeping edges. merge-duplicates Removes each frame equal to the one before it and adds its delay to the frame that stays, as ImageMagick's -layers RemoveDups: a screen recording that sat still for seconds becomes one long frame. motion-blur Streaks the image along a direction, as a camera moving during the exposure, with ImageMagick's -motion-blur meaning: each pixel averages 2⌈radius⌉ + 1 samples one pixel apart, from itself toward angle, weighted by a Gaussian of sigma from the pixel. normalize ContrastStretch at ImageMagick's -normalize points: the darkest 2% of the pixels become black and the lightest 1% white. offset Moves the image by whole pixels, right by dx and down by dy, with no resampling. oil-paint Makes the image look painted, as ImageMagick's -paint does: around each pixel, in the (2r + 1) square, pixels are sorted into levels bins by intensity, and the pixel becomes a pixel of the most common bin, unchanged. opacity Multiplies alpha by amount. pad Enlarges the canvas to width × height, placing the image at anchor and filling the new area with background. pixelate Pixelates: the image is cut into square cells, and every pixel of a cell becomes the cell's average, taken on premultiplied values so transparent pixels do not darken it. posterize Rounds red, green and blue to levels evenly spaced values each, as ImageMagick's -posterize, optionally dithered: ordered dithering adds a fixed 8 × 8 pattern before rounding, Floyd–Steinberg spreads each value's rounding error to its neighbours. quad-distort Moves the image's four corners to four points, bending it in perspective: ImageMagick's Perspective distort. quantize Reduces each frame to at most MaxColors colors, as a palette format would, but keeps the pixel type: an Rgba16 image stays Rgba16 with at most that many distinct values. replace-color Replaces every pixel within tolerance of from with to, by ImageMagick's -fuzz distance, as ImageMagick's -fill with -opaque does. resize Resizes to a size in the size syntax (W, xH, WxH, P%, with !, ^, > or <) with a fit mode. retime Resamples the animation to framesPerSecond, as ffmpeg's fps filter: fixed ticks, each showing the frame visible when it starts, with neighbours that show the same frame merged. reverse Plays the animation backwards; each frame keeps its delay and metadata. rotate Rotates the image clockwise. rotational-blur Spins the image around center, as ImageMagick's -rotational-blur: each pixel averages samples along an arc of degrees centered on it, about one per pixel of arc (at most 256), read bilinearly. saturation Mixes each color with its luma: 1 changes nothing, 0 gives gray, above 1 oversaturates. sepia Tints toward sepia. shade Shades the image as ImageMagick's -shade does: the luminance is a height field, and each pixel becomes the Lambertian shading of its surface normal by a distant light at azimuth and elevation, a gray relief; with colored the shading multiplies the image's own colors instead, as +shade does. sharpen Sharpens with an unsharp mask: out = src + amount × (src − Blur(sigma)). shuffle-channels Rearranges the working RGBA channels: each output channel takes the input channel, or the constant, its argument names. sigmoidal-contrast Adds (or removes) contrast with ImageMagick's scaled logistic curve, which never clips. simulate-color-blindness Shows how the image looks with a color vision deficiency. skew Shears the image about its center: vertical lines lean by degreesX (x moves by y × tan) and horizontal lines by degreesY. solarize Inverts red, green and blue values above threshold, as ImageMagick's -solarize. spread Scatters pixels, as ImageMagick's -spread does: each pixel takes the value of a random pixel at most radius away (a whole-pixel offset in the disc; edges repeat the edge pixel). threshold Makes a two-color image: pixels above level take above, the others below, with alpha kept. tile Makes a new width × height canvas filled by repeating the image, or the source rectangle of it, with one copy's top-left corner at origin, as Skia's Tile filter and ImageMagick's tile: fill do. tint Pushes midtones toward color and keeps black and white, as ImageMagick's -tint. tone-map Maps HDR linear light into 0..1: pixel values are read as linear light with reference white at 1.0 (as RgbaF32, RgbaF16 and RgbF32 rasters hold PQ and HLG images converted to a linear encoding), and the tone curve brings the brightest down to 1 on max(R, G, B), which keeps hue. trim Removes the border: the rows and columns at the edges whose pixels all lie within tolerance of the border color, by ImageMagick's -fuzz distance, so the rectangle equals ImageMagick's -trim. vignette Darkens (or tints) the image toward its corners, outside an ellipse fitted to the image, with a soft edge: the shape of ImageMagick's -vignette, which blurs a drawn ellipse. white-balance Applies WhiteBalance: corrects for a light of temperature kelvin. zoom-blur Streaks the image along rays from center, as a zoom during the exposure (Photoshop's radial zoom blur): each pixel averages samples on the ray through it, spanning amount of its distance from the center, half inward and half outward, about one per
