articles/diagnostics.html.title: Diagnostics | Egami
articles/diagnostics.html.summary: Diagnostics Egami can tell an app what it recovered from, what it lost on purpose and what it decided on the caller's behalf, through one optional handler on EgamiContext. Egami has no logging dependency: the handler is a plain delegate, so one line sends the events to ILogger, Serilog or the console. // With Microsoft.Extensions.Logging: one line at startup sends every call's warnings to the app's log, with the id as // a property to filter and count on. Egami itself has no logging dependency. EgamiContext.SetDefault(new EgamiContext { Diagnostics = d => logger.Log(d.Level.ToLogLevel(), "{Source} {Id} at {Offset}: {Message}", d.Source, d.Id, d.Offset, d.Message), }); Set it once at startup; every call that passes no context then reports to the log. The handler EgamiContext.Diagnostics is an Action<EgamiDiagnostic>, null by default. With no handler, nothing is built and nothing is allocated. Each EgamiDiagnostic carries: Member What it holds Level Warning, Info or Debug, mapping onto the log levels Warning, Information and Debug Source The part of Egami that found it: Png, Tiff, Exif, Limits and so on (the id up to its first dot) Id A stable id such as Png.ChecksumMismatch, to filter and count on without parsing text Message What happened and what Egami did, as a sentence Offset The byte offset in the input, when known Frame The frame or page index, when known Ids are listed below and are never renamed or reused once shipped, like the public API. Levels. EgamiContext.DiagnosticLevel is the lowest level delivered, Warning by default. Events below it are never even formatted. // Info and Debug events are off unless asked for; below the level they are never even formatted. EgamiContext verbose = EgamiContext.Default with { Diagnostics = d => seen.Add(d), DiagnosticLevel = DiagnosticLevel.Debug, }; using Raster image = Raster.Load("duck.jpg", verbose, new ReaderOptions { MinimumSize = new Size(100, 100) }); foreach (EgamiDiagnostic d in seen) { Console.WriteLine($"{d.Level,-7} {d.Id}: {d.Message}"); } Threads. The handler runs inline, on whichever thread found the event, possibly on several decode threads at once, so it must be quick and thread-safe. Egami takes no lock around it. When Warnings arrive. The Warnings a load raises arrive as the call ends, in the order of Metadata.Warnings, on the calling thread; a RasterDecoder session sends them when it is disposed. A reader that waits for more input can take a warning back and read it again, so nothing is sent until it is final. Info and Debug events arrive as they happen. A load that throws sends no Warnings: the exception says what went wrong. Errors. An exception from the handler fails the call with that exception, which turns warnings into errors. Nothing the call allocated is leaked. // Warnings as errors: a handler that throws fails the call with its exception, and nothing the call allocated is leaked. EgamiContext strict = EgamiContext.Default with { Diagnostics = d => throw new InvalidDataException($"{d.Id}: {d.Message}"), }; try { using Raster image = Raster.Load(SampleFiles.Damaged(), strict); } catch (InvalidDataException e) { Console.WriteLine($"Rejected: {e.Message}"); } A handler that throws turns every warning into an error; RecoveryMode.Strict does the same for damage alone, without a handler. Repeats. One id is delivered at most 10 times per call, then once more as "The same problem came up N more times". Metadata.Warnings holds the same capped list, so the two always agree. A hostile file cannot flood a log. Per file. Contexts are cheap records, so a context per file, whose handler's closure carries the path, scopes the events to that file. // Per file: the handler's closure carries the path, so no correlation id is needed. Contexts are cheap records. foreach (string path in Directory.EnumerateFiles(".", "*.png")) { EgamiContext perFile = EgamiContext.Default with { Diagnostics = d => log.Add($"{path}: {d.Message}") }; using Raster image = Raster.Load(path, perFile); } Metadata.Warnings Every Warning a load raises is also in RasterMetadata.Warnings, an IReadOnlyList<EgamiDiagnostic>, with or without a handler. Info and Debug events never are. Metadata parsed on first use (XMP, IPTC, ICC) adds its warnings then, and sends them to the handler of the context the raster was loaded with. // Without a handler the same Warnings are in the metadata, each with its id. using Raster image = Raster.Load(SampleFiles.Damaged()); foreach (EgamiDiagnostic warning in image.Metadata.Warnings) { Console.WriteLine($"{warning.Id} at byte {warning.Offset}: {warning.Message}"); } bool checksumsOnly = image.Metadata.Warnings.All(w => w.Id == "Png.ChecksumMismatch"); Reporting from your own code A format plug-in notes a recovery with EgamiInput.Warn(raster, id, message), which lists it in Metadata.Warnings and sends it to the handler as Egami's own readers do; EgamiInput.Diagnostics takes its Info and Debug events. Code with no EgamiInput, such as a video demuxer, starts a DiagnosticReporter for the call with EgamiContext.StartDiagnostics(), which applies the same level filter and cap; disposing it sends the counts of capped ids. Use your own source name in ids (Avi.IndexRebuilt), never one of Egami's. // A decoder outside Egami (a video demuxer, a format plug-in's own entry point) reports through the same handler, with the // same level filter and the same cap of 10 per id per call. Dispose the reporter when the call ends. using (DiagnosticReporter diagnostics = context.StartDiagnostics()) { if (diagnostics.IsEnabled(DiagnosticLevel.Warning)) { diagnostics.Report(DiagnosticLevel.Warning, "Avi.IndexRebuilt", "The index was missing; it was rebuilt from the frames.", offset: 4096); } diagnostics.Report(DiagnosticLevel.Info, "Mjpeg.DhtInserted", "Frames have no Huffman tables; the standard ones were used."); } Logging libraries ILogger takes the mapping in the first example. Serilog's static Log is the same one line: // With Serilog's static Log: the same one line, with Serilog's level names. EgamiContext context = EgamiContext.Default with { Diagnostics = d => log.Write(d.Level == DiagnosticLevel.Warning ? "Warning" : d.Level == DiagnosticLevel.Info ? "Information" : "Debug", "{Id}: {Message}", d.Id, d.Message), }; Memory leaks are reported by PixelMemoryUsage.LeakDetected instead, because they belong to a memory source rather than a call and are found on the finalizer thread after the call has ended; see Memory and threading. Catalog Id Level Meaning Ani.ChunkPastEnd Warning An animated cursor's chunk, or a frame in its fram list, runs past the end of the file or the list; the bytes that are there were read Ani.ChunkRepeated Warning An animated cursor has a second anih header or fram list; the first was used Ani.FrameCount Warning An animated cursor's header gives a frame count its fram list contradicts; the frames in the list were used Ani.FrameDamaged Warning A frame of an animated cursor cannot be read or decoded; the steps that show it were left out Ani.HeaderSize Warning An animated cursor's anih header is not 36 bytes, or says it is not; its first 36 bytes were read Ani.IconInRawFile Warning An animated cursor's header says its frames are raw bitmaps, but a frame is an icon; it was read as one Ani.ListSize Warning An animated cursor's rate or seq chunk is not a whole number of 4-byte entries; the extra bytes were ignored Ani.RateCount Warning An animated cursor's rate chunk has a different number of entries than it has steps; steps without one use the default rate Ani.RiffSize Warning An animated cursor's RIFF header gives a size past the end of the file; the chunks that are there were read Ani.SequenceFlag Warning An animated cursor's header flag for a seq chunk disagrees with whether there is one; the chunk, if any, was used Ani.SequenceIndex Warning A step of an animated cursor shows a frame the file does not store; the step was left out Ani.SizeMissing Warning A frame of an animated cursor has no image at the size loaded; its nearest image was resized, hotspot and all Ani.StepCount Warning An animated cursor's header gives a step count its seq chunk or frames contradict; theirs was used Ani.ZeroRate Warning An animated cursor's default rate, or a step's rate, is 0; the step uses the default rate, or one jiffy (1/60 s) when that is 0 too Avif.BaseLayerOnly Warning An AVIF image is coded in layers whose later ones are inter frames, which Egami does not decode yet; its first layer was loaded Avif.ExifDamaged Warning An AVIF Exif item's TIFF header offset points past its end; the item was skipped Avif.FramesDropped Warning A frame of an AVIF sequence after the first cannot be decoded; a lenient load keeps the frames before it Avif.GainMapDropped Warning An AVIF gain map (tmap item) has metadata or an image that cannot be read, or a version Egami does not know; the image loads as SDR only Avif.MatrixApproximated Warning An AVIF image's matrix coefficients are ones libavif does not convert (reserved, constant luminance, or YCgCo at limited range); the nearest matrix it has was used Avif.MatrixUnknown Warning An AVIF image's matrix coefficients have no YuvMatrix; YuvRaster.Load marks the planes BT.601 Avif.SequenceFirstFrame Warning No longer reported: AVIF sequences decode every frame, inter frames included (Egami 1.1) Bmp.DataOffsetInHeaders Warning The pixel data offset points into the headers; the pixels are read from where the headers end Bmp.EmbeddedSizeMismatch Warning An embedded PNG or JPEG is not the size the BMP header gives Bmp.IndexOutOfRange Warning Pixels use indices past the palette; they are drawn black Bmp.PlanesInvalid Warning The header gives a plane count other than 1; it was ignored Bmp.ProfileLinked Warning The color profile is linked by file name, which Egami does not open Bmp.ProfileTruncated Warning The file ends before the embedded ICC profile; it was dropped Bmp.RowsMissing Warning The pixel data ends or is damaged; the rows not decoded are black Bmp.RunPastRow Warning RLE runs go past the end of a row; the extra pixels were dropped Ccitt.Damaged Warning A row of CCITT data is damaged and could not be skipped; the rows before it were kept and the rest are white Ccitt.RowsSkipped Warning Damaged CCITT rows were skipped to the next EOL, as DamagedRowsBeforeError allows; each repeats the row before it Ccitt.Truncated Warning The CCITT data ends before the rows its parameters give; the rest are white Color.ConvertedOnLoad Info ReaderOptions.ConvertColorTo converted the pixels; from which encoding to which Decode.FramesSelected Info ReaderOptions.Frames chose some frames; how many were read Decode.ScaleChosen Info For ReaderOptions.MinimumSize, the 1/N scale the reader decodes at and the box factor after it Detect.Format Info The format detected, and how Exif.Damaged Warning The EXIF block would not parse in full; it is kept as bytes Exr.BlocksDamaged Warning Blocks of an OpenEXR part cannot be read or decompressed; their pixels are zero Exr.ChunkTableRebuilt Warning An OpenEXR part's chunk offset table is incomplete or damaged; it was rebuilt by walking the chunks Font.BadColorGlyph Warning A glyph's color data (COLR, sbix, CBDT or SVG) is damaged, cyclic or deeper than 64 paints; the part that cannot be drawn is left out, or the glyph draws as its outline (Egami.Fonts) Font.BadContainer Warning A WOFF or WOFF2 file's header or blocks disagree with its data (a wrong length, a misplaced metadata block); the tables are still read (Egami.Fonts) Font.BadDirectory Warning A font's table directory lists a table outside the file; it was dropped or cut short (Egami.Fonts) Font.BadGlyph Warning A glyph's data cannot be read; it draws empty (Egami.Fonts) Font.BadTable Warning A font table is damaged; its documented default is used (Egami.Fonts) Font.FileSkipped Warning A file in a font folder cannot be indexed; it is left out of the collection (Egami.Fonts) Font.MissingTable Warning A font lacks a table; its documented default is used (Egami.Fonts) Font.ShapingLimit Warning A font's layout tables drove shaping past its operation or length limits, as a hostile font can; the text is shaped as far as the limits allow (Egami.Fonts) Gif.BlockTruncated Warning The file ends inside a block Gif.ColorTableMissing Warning A frame has no color table; it is drawn transparent Gif.ControlExtensionShort Warning A graphic control extension is shorter than 4 bytes Gif.DisposalUndefined Warning A frame's disposal method is undefined; it is read as none Gif.FrameOutsideScreen Warning A frame sticks out of the logical screen Gif.ImageDataShort Warning A frame's image data ends early Gif.ImageDataTruncated Warning The file ends inside a frame's image data Gif.ImageTruncated Warning The file ends inside a frame's header Gif.IndexOutOfRange Warning A frame uses indices past its color table; they are drawn transparent Gif.LzwCodeSizeOne Warning An LZW minimum code size of 1, outside the specification Gif.TrailerMissing Warning The file ends without a trailer Gif.UnknownBlock Warning An unknown block where a block introducer was expected Gif.XmpTrailerMissing Warning The XMP application extension lacks its magic trailer Heic.ExifDamaged Warning A HEIC Exif item's TIFF header offset points past its end; the item was skipped Heic.FramesDropped Warning A frame of a HEIC image sequence after the first could not be decoded; the frames before it were loaded Heic.GainMapDropped Warning A HEIC gain map (tmap item) has metadata or an image that cannot be read, or a version Egami does not know; the image loads as SDR only Heic.MatrixApproximated Warning A HEIC image's matrix coefficients are reserved or constant luminance, which heif-dec does not convert; BT.601's were used Heic.MatrixUnknown Warning A HEIC image's matrix coefficients have no YuvMatrix; YuvRaster.Load marks the planes BT.601 Heic.SequenceFirstFrame Warning A HEIC image sequence has inter frames, which Egami.Heic does not decode; its first frame was loaded Heif.ItemCount Warning A HEIF (AVIF) iinf box's entry count differs from the infe boxes it holds; the boxes found are read Heif.ItemEntryVersion Warning A HEIF (AVIF) infe box has an unknown version; the item was skipped Heif.OldItemEntry Warning A HEIF (AVIF) infe box of version 0 or 1 has no item type;
